Content Warning
This adventure contains themes of war, oppression, torture, and political violence. Before you begin, understand that player consent (including that 
of the Game Master) is vital to a safe and fun play experience for everyone. You should talk with your players before beginning the adventure and 
modify descriptions of the narrative as appropriate.

===== Page 6 =====
Campaign Background
Isger has been neglected by Cheliax and its own 
government for decades. A group of idealists and 
former soldiers, sick of the people bearing the brunt 
of the authorities’ poor decisions, founded the 
Hellbreakers League to gather like-minded rebels 
in hopes of sparking a revolution. They made little 
traction until the Godsrain, when they managed 
to locate and obtain a warshard in the town of 
Breachill.
However, Isger’s steward, Hedvend VI, was alerted 
to their activity and reported it to Abrogail Thrune. 
Queen Abrogail II, coveting the warshard and seeking 
to stamp out rebellion, sent the Order of the Rack to 
seize Breachill and scour it for her prizes.
The town withered under the subsequent public 
executions and the Hellknights’ harsh rule. Breachill’s 
cries for deliverance made it to the nation of Andoran, 
who sent a contingent of diplomats, including the 
retired general Reginald Cormoth, to entreat the 
Hellknights to stop subjugating Breachill’s citizens. 
The Hellknights responded by executing Reginald.
Outraged by the brutal and unnecessary act of 
violence, Eagle Knights of the Steel Falcons went to 
Isger and initiated the Battle of Hellknight Hill, a 
grueling fight that ended in the Eagle Knights’ victory. 
The Hellbreakers aided the Eagle Knights, and after 
the battle, they were promised aid from Andoran in 
exchange for their warshard.
A survivor of the battle, the armiger Viro Ahala, 
managed to acquire full Hellknight plate before 
fleeing the battlefield. He sought aid from the Sisters 
of the Golden Erinys, who mistook him for a full-
fledged Hellknight. Viro used the nuns’ resources to 
learn of a ritual to summon a powerful devil to exact 
revenge upon the Hellbreakers League.
Meanwhile, in the capital of Elidir, an agent 
of Illcayna Alonnor prepares to throw Isger’s 
government into chaos and arrange things so Illcayna 
can easily take over the nation. Ezio Gaeta plans 
to assassinate Hedvend at the steward’s own gala, 
distracting the authorities while Illcayna prepares to 
enact a powerful ritual to transform all of Isger into 
her undead thralls.
Ignorant to those who plot against them, the 
Hellbreakers League is reconvening in Saringallow 
to take advantage of the momentum from their 
recent victory.
About the PCs
The 1st-level PCs are low-ranking members of 
the Hellbreakers League. People of all types and 
backgrounds join the Hellbreakers League, including 
outsiders like an Eagle Knight with a bleeding heart 
or a Drumish mercenary promised a reward for 
participation. This Adventure Path caters to a wide 
range of gameplay styles with social, wilderness, and 
combat challenges.
Make sure your players read the free Player’s 
Guide to prepare for the adventure and make PCs 
appropriate for the story. Don’t forget that there’s a 
new archetype they can take at Level 2, and there’s 
also a new animal companion available on page 215.
Subsystems
This campaign makes use of several subsystems. The 
first is a reputation system that’s used throughout the 
entire campaign. In Chapter 6, several subsystems 
are used: the Victory Point system, the infiltration 
system, and the chase subsystem. Chapter 9 uses the 
research subsystem. 
Terms to Know
Cheliax: Cheliax is the patron nation of Isger and 
worships the archdevil Asmodeus.
The Goblinblood Wars: In this war, hobgoblins 
from the Chitterwood raised armies of goblins 
and set about destroying settlements nearby. Isger 
suffered greatly during this time, and the war’s effects 
still haunt its populace.
Hellbreakers League: A rebel organization dedicated 
to freeing Isger from Cheliax’s oppressive rule.
Hellknight: Hellknights are Chelaxian knights 
dedicated to law and order above all else. There 
are several different orders of Hellknights; the most 
relevant to this adventure is the Order of the Godclaw, 
which is known to worship the Godclaw pantheon. 
There are mentions of the Order of the Rack early on.
Warshard: When the god Gorum died, several 
parts of his body and weapons were strewn about the 
Universe in pieces called warshards. These items hold 
immense divine power.

Names to Know
Abrogail Thrune: Abrogail II is the ruler of Cheliax. 
She doesn’t make an appearance in this adventure, but 
her influence is felt everywhere Cheliax has a hold.
Alceo Demetrias: Cofounder of the Hellbreakers 
League, Alceo is a cleric of the goddess Milani.
Hedvend VI: Hedvend is the steward of Isger. He’s 
known to consistently prioritize Cheliax’s wants over 
Isger’s needs.
Illcayna Alonnor: Illcayna is a worshipper of the 
goddess Urgathoa, and her sole purpose is to turn Isger 
into a tribute nation to her goddess. She’s in possession 
of a warshard, which she plans to use to achieve her 
goals.
Kaltessa Iyis: Kaltessa is the mysterious, centuries-
old high priestess of the archdevil Mammon. She only 
makes a cameo in this adventure, but you might be 
seeing her again!
Phoebe Demetrias: Cofounder of the Hellbreakers 
League, Phoebe is an ex-soldier now commander of 
the rebels.
Important Locations
Chitterwood: A large forest that was mostly burned 
down during the Goblinblood Wars. It’s mostly 
occupied by goblinoids.
Elidir: The nation’s capital, home of the wealthy 
elites and Cheliax’s main supporters.
Finder’s Gulch: This town is the headquarters of 
Illcayna Alonnor and overrun with undead.
Saringallow: This small city is the base for the 
Hellbreakers League headquarters.
Relations
Isger is mostly forgotten by Cheliax, mainly retaining 
any significance due to the river running through it 
that brings lucrative shipments and trade. Cheliax 
sent limited aid during the Goblinblood Wars but 
mostly let the nation fend for itself. Once the wars 
were over, they sent nuns to perform acts of charity 
and indoctrinate civilians, for which many citizens are 
grateful. The opinions on Chelaxian rule are split, with 
more ire toward the patron nation in the countryside.

Campaign Summary
In the aftermath of the Battle of Hellknight Hill, the 
PCs travel from Breachill to Saringallow to meet with 
their superiors in the Hellbreakers League. They partake 
in several missions, learning that there’s a “Hellknight” 
seeking revenge on the League. The PCs are sent on a 
countryside mission to win over the people by aiding them 
where the government has neglected to. As they travel, 
the PCs discover evidence of “Hellknight” Viro Ahala’s 
plot against Isger—starting with the Chitterwood. Now 
knowing Viro’s plans, the PCs journey to the Chitterwood 
to entreat the goblin residents for help in stopping the 
rogue Hellknight armiger.
While the PCs dealt with things in the countryside, 
the leaders of the Hellbreakers were making plans in 
the capital. In need of backup after their identities 
are exposed, the leaders summon the PCs to take 
their place as falsified guests of Hedvend VI’s devilish 
costume gala. At the gala, the PCs meet several 
important figures, including Hellknight paralictor 
Caeto Vulaunex, who’s slated to be the head of a new 
task force to hunt down Hellbreakers. However, the 
festivities are interrupted when fake Hellbreakers 
attack the gala. The PCs deal with their impersonators 
but soon learn that someone murdered Hedvend—and 
the Hellbreakers are being blamed! Caeto asks the PCs 
to investigate as other mysterious deaths continue to 
occur. The real murderer is fellow guest Ezio Gaeta, 
a vampire and follower of Illcayna Alonnor, who has 
grand plans to transform Isger into an undead tribute 
state for Urgathoa.
Caeto takes control of Elidir, declaring martial law 
over the nation and blaming the Hellbreakers for 
Hedvend’s death. The PCs bolster a new local chapter 
of the Hellbreakers while planning to escape the city, 
but things go awry when members of the new chapter 
are captured. The PCs must rescue their new friends 
and make a daring escape from Elidir!
The PCs return to Saringallow only to learn that 
Illcayna Alonnor’s undead forces are on the move, and 
Caeto is refusing to address the issue. With no one 
else to help the citizens of Isger, the PCs return to the 
countryside to seek a solution to the undead problem. 
When they reach Gillamoor, the PCs learn that the 
town was once cursed by Illcayna so that any who died 
within the town’s grounds would rise as her undead 
thralls—and she plans to ritually cast a much more 
powerful version of the curse on the entire nation. The 
PCs must head to the town of Finder’s Gulch to defeat 
the Wight Mother once and for all.
The Hellbreakers League is more popular than 
ever after defeating Illcayna, but their increased 
profile allows Caeto to discern the location of their 
headquarters in Saringallow. The PCs barely escape 
capture and must first take the infamous Sarini Manor 
as a stronghold before planning the liberation of their 
fellow Hellbreakers.
The time has come to face Caeto himself. The PCs 
siege Saringallow with their gathered forces and allies, 
striking back to liberate their friends, reclaim their 
home, and secure their freedom at last.
ADVANCEMENT TRACK
Hellbreakers is designed for four characters.
1	
The PCs begin this adventure at 1st level.
2	
The PCs should be 2nd level after rescuing 
Rhokrag and defeating the Chelaxian loyalists.
3	
The PCs should be 3rd level after defeating the 
Sisters of the Erinys.
4	
The PCs should be 4th level after stopping Viro 
Ahala’s ritual and saving Isger.
5	
The PCs should be 5th level after infiltrating 
Hedvend’s gala.
6	
The PCs should be 6th level for solving Hedvend’s 
murder and stopping Ezio.
7	
The PCs should be 7th level for escaping Elidir.
8	
The PCs should be 8th level for defeating Illcayna 
and her undead hordes.
9	
The PCs should be 9th level for taking back 
Sarini Manor.
The PCs should reach 10th level by the end of the 
adventure.

===== Page 11 =====
When Hellknights of the Rack publicly executed 
retired Andoren general Reginald Cormoth in the 
town of Breachill for the alleged crime of “providing 
succor to dissidents against the crown of Cheliax,” they 
set alight a metaphorical powder keg that exploded 
into war with the Battle of Hellknight Hill. With the 
approach of Eagle Knight forces from Andoran into 
Isger, the Hellknights retreated into a newly fortified 
Citadel Altaerein. The ensuing siege was joined by 
rebels of the Hellbreakers League, a group of Isgeri 
citizens looking to remove the boot of Cheliax from 
their country’s neck.
While most other sieges are long, drawn-out affairs, 
the fighting at the Battle of Hellknight Hill was short 
and brutal. Many Hellknights, eager for conflict, 
ranged out of the citadel and clashed with anti-
Cheliax forces in and around Breachill. At one point, 
the diabolic dragon Kierothax perched atop Citadel 
Altaerein on behalf of the Hellknights and rained 
hellfire down upon the gathered armies.
Though both armies experienced heavy casualties, 
the forces of freedom and liberty eventually triumphed. 
They slew the dragon and routed the Hellknights, with 
the surviving Chelaxian forces fleeing southwest back 
toward Cheliax. The Eagle Knights, Hellbreakers, and 
their allies were too weary to give chase, and instead 
began the process of burying the fields of the dead, 
tending to the living wounded, and repairing damage 
to Breachill’s buildings.
Getting Started
The PCs are agents of the Hellbreakers League 
gathering in Breachill to meet a wounded Eagle Knight 
who wishes to aid the cause. Each character should

Against Hell

===== Page 12 =====
have their own reason for joining the League—perhaps 
they’re an Isgeri citizen fed up with Chelaxian rule or 
maybe they’re a mercenary who fought for the League 
in the Battle of Hellknight Hill. Each player should 
choose a background from the Hellbreakers Player’s 
Guide that ties their character to the organization. In 
any case, they have all agreed to aid this Eagle Knight 
contact, an accomplished soldier named Ethran 
Howell, in returning to the Hellbreakers headquarters 
in Saringallow.
Whether the party has met one another already (and 
possibly fought together) is up to your group, but they 
all arrive at Cayden’s Keg in Breachill on a crisp fall 
evening in Lamashan 4726 ar. As they head to this 
combination temple and alehouse, the overall mood in 
the town is celebratory.
The Aftermath of Battle
The people of Breachill, with the aid of the Eagle 
Knights and the Hellbreakers League, won a major 
victory by driving out the occupying Hellknights. 
After weeks of surviving under the iron fists of their 
oppressors, most residents are relieved to not have 
to watch their every move and word. However, as 
some Hellbreaker rebels are quick to point out: how 
free could they possibly be when their country is 
still a vassal state to Cheliax? But that’s a problem 
for another day, as the streets of Breachill fill with 
celebrants, cheering and singing even as they rebuild 
ruined homes or honor their fallen neighbors.
Nowhere are spirits as high as they are at Cayden’s 
Keg, a tavern and temple to the drunken god Cayden 
Cailean. The primary bartender and priestess Brynne 
Taithe (jovial female human cleric of Cayden Cailean 
5) has offered her healing services for free to many 
of the wounded, as well as room and board if they 
require it. Many comrades-in-arms and various local 
well-wishers congregate alongside the PCs, keeping 
the ale flowing since the battle’s end. The alehouse is 
packed with people chattering and drinking, while a 
single musician plays rousing fiddle tunes from one 
corner. A small fire crackles in the tavern’s fireplace, 
though its heat is hardly necessary to keep out the 
autumnal weather—the press of bodies does that 
particular work.
MEETING ETHRAN HOWELL
Several tavern patrons raise their mugs and loudly 
greet the PCs as they enter Cayden’s Keg. The PCs can 
ask about their contact or cast their eyes across the 
crowd; either way, they find Ethran Howell (pragmatic 
nonbinary human soldier 4) at a crowded table. The 
soldier’s left arm was gravely wounded late in the 
Battle of Hellknight Hell, leaving no choice but for 
it to be amputated, and they’ve been recuperating at 
Cayden’s Keg since then. During that time, Ethran 
decided to focus on the important work of helping to 
liberate Isger by offering their services as a soldier and 
tactician to the Hellbreakers League; the Eagle Knights 
have unofficially approved of Ethran’s decision, 
noting in the records that the veteran is on “semi-
permanent convalescence leave.” Read or paraphrase 
the following when the PCs approach Ethran.
Ethran Howell is difficult to miss in their distinctive blue, 
black, and golden breastplate decorated with a single 
golden eagle epaulet. Several townspeople crowd their 
table thanking them for their service, commiserating 
about their left arm, and buying them drinks. Ethran looks 
flattered but slightly embarrassed by the attention as they 
say to their admirers, “Fellows, I appreciate the chat and 
the drinks, but I must attend to business.” The small crowd 
disperses with a final cheer for Ethran, leaving plenty of 
space at the soldier’s table. Ethran smiles, looking a little 
relieved. “Everyone’s in high spirits, as they’re right to be. 
Would you like a drink?”
Ethran is politically aware and can explain any 
factors leading up to the Battle of Hellknight Hill 
that the players aren’t yet familiar with. If asked, they 
describe the fight with a pair of Hellknights that left 
them wounded. If any PCs also participated in the 
battle, Ethran acknowledges their contribution to the 
victory with a brief toast. Before the group can begin 
to discuss the upcoming journey, Brynne rings a bell 
mounted behind the bar to get the patrons’ attention.
The crowd hushes and the fiddler stops mid-tune as the 
clear tones of the bell ring out. Brynne leans over the bar 
counter and calls out, “Come now, friends! In the name 
of all things fun and good as our beloved Cayden Cailean 
would have it, it’s time for tonight’s contest!” Cheers erupt 
as locals excitedly whisper, wondering what the theme of

tonight’s storytelling will be. Brynne raises a frothy glass. 
“In honor of those who drove out the scum from our town, 
the theme of the evening is past battles! Tell us your 
stories, brave warriors and wily hunters, and let’s 
see who tells them best!”
NIGHT OF TALES
The head priestess of Cayden’s Keg 
regularly holds evening storytelling contests 
to both boost the mood of her customers 
and as a way to keep the alcohol flowing. 
After all, everyone loves to hear a 
good story and people usually 
stick around to hear a bunch of 
them told in succession—ordering more 
drinks in the meantime. Ethran encourages 
the PCs to participate but doesn’t pressure any of 
the characters, especially if it seems like a character’s 
history might be a sore subject. This is a good way for 
players to introduce their characters more thoroughly, 
giving a little backstory (or creating a clever fiction) to 
bring the group closer together.
As the PCs decide whether they wish to participate, 
other customers begin to tell their tales. Each one 
steps to the center of the tavern floor to speak, with 
all eyes watching and all ears listening. Most relate 
a brief story about their participation in the Battle of 
Hellknight Hill, while others spin yarns about a heroic 
hunt or a personal battle with temptation. A PC can 
enter the contest by speaking up from the center of the 
room at any point.
Each character who wants to tell a tale should 
attempt a DC 15 skill check; Performance is the 
default skill, but a character could use Deception if 
they are confabulating or Intimidation if they are 
trying to scare the audience. If the player wants to 
tell a story that directly relates to their character’s 
background, they could attempt a check using the 
Lore skill provided by that background. Other skills 
are applicable at the GM’s discretion.
On a failure, the crowd gives the character some light 
applause, but it’s clear that they’re unimpressed. On 
a success, the tavern gives a livelier response, hooting 
with delight or even openly weeping if the tale was a 
sad one. Record the result of each skill check result 
that meets or exceeds the DC. At the end of the night, 
Brynne declares the character whose story represents 
the highest of those results the winner. The assembled 
drinkers cheer loud enough to nearly bring down the 
roof as Brynne presents the winner with several mugs of 
the Keg’s finest (and most expensive) ale. Ethran bangs 
their own mug on the table in appreciation as well.
After another hour of carousing, Ethran declares 
that they’re tired and tells the PCs they’ll meet up 
again in the morning to discuss the details of the 
journey to Saringallow. Though Cayden’s Keg 
isn’t renting out rooms (they’re saved for 
those convalescing), Brynne tells the PCs they 
can find lodging at the Great Dreamhouse, a 
temple to Desna, or Wizard’s Grace, a local 
inn. They can also camp outside, near much 
of the visiting military.
Reward: If at least one PC succeeds at the 
storytelling check, award the PCs 30 XP; if 
more than half the PCs succeed, award them an 
additional 10 XP. In addition, if more than 
half the PCs succeed, Brynne thanks them 
for entertaining the tavern and gives them 
two minor healing potions before they leave, 
noting that Cayden told her they might need them “on 
the road ahead.”
NEWS FROM ELIDIR
The next morning, Breachill is abuzz with talk of news 
out of Elidir that arrived around dawn. Apparently, 
the Isgeri government placed a sizable bounty on 
“dissenters and revolutionaries” in a manner that is 
frustratingly vague. It’s obvious to anyone who reads 
the text of the decree posted outside Breachill’s town 
hall that Steward Hedvend VI (sniveling male human 
aristocrat 9) is trying to squash any anti-Chelaxian 
activities by encouraging private citizens to take 
matters into their own hands. A PC who succeeds at 
a DC 16 Society check or DC 14 Legal Lore check 
realizes that people can use this bounty to settle 
grudges with their neighbors—similar in fashion as to 
what happens during a witch hunt—while collecting 
a bit of coin.
As the PCs return to Cayden’s Keg to meet Ethran, 
they can see how this news has cast a pall over the 
town, somewhat eclipsing the celebratory mood of the 
previous evening. People in the street mutter to each 
other about how nearby towns might treat them after 
the results of the Battle of Hellknight Hill. A small 
crowd has gathered in Monument Circle near town 
hall to protest the decree and publicly decrying the 
idea of Breachill citizens turning on one another. The 
PCs should feel safe here for now.
Should they express any doubts about their safety, 
Ethran assures the PCs that no one here is likely to 
turn them in. They do note that it’ll be a different 
matter outside of Breachill. Their original plan was 
to travel south to the Conerica River and then west 
to Saringallow, but now they think it’s best to head 
directly to the Hellbreakers League headquarters, 
12
Ethran Howell

traveling southwest overland. Ethran also suggests they 
move as incognito as possible; they, for one, intend to 
hide their Eagle Knight regalia in a trunk. If any PCs 
sport obvious allegiances to the Hellbreakers League 
(or other revolutionary groups), Ethran recommends 
removing those symbols.
Setting out for Saringallow
Ethran has purchased a horse and a wagon for the 
journey. They wish to leave within the hour, giving 
the PCs an opportunity to purchase any supplies 
for the trip as they see fit. They’ll be on the road 
for about half a week, but Ethran says that they’ll 
probably have opportunities to buy more rations and 
other items on the way.
The Eagle Knight drives the wagon out of Breachill. 
The PCs can take seats in the wagon with Ethran’s 
trunk or ride or walk alongside. When the group 
sets out, the sky is gray and cloudy, presaging some 
autumnal rains. The road out of town leads west, then 
eventually turns a bit southwest, passing by farms with 
empty fields, their harvests already collected. Ethran 
makes small talk over the rumbling of the cart’s 
wheels, perhaps asking the PCs about any stories they 
told the night before, inquiring into their veracity or 
asking for more details. At the end of the first day, the 
group comes to a roadside inn where the PCs can spot 
a copy of Hedvend’s decree on a signboard outside. 
The few patrons inside mutter a bit about the country 
not being safe anymore to anyone who asks, but it 
isn’t clear whether they mean safe from Chelaxian 
intervention or from rebel activity.
During the next two days of travel, the PCs spot 
more copies of Hedvend’s decree nailed to trees and 
fence posts along the road. Ethran warns the characters 
that they should keep a low profile and not tear down 
these notices.
DRAYMOOR ROAD	
MODERATE 1
Midafternoon on the fourth day of travel out of 
Breachill, the wagon enters the small farming village 
of Draymoor.
Only a few squat buildings line the single road, which is 
muddy from a recent rain. The villagers go about their daily 
business with only a glance or two at the group. Ethran 
draws the horse alongside a general store and carefully 
climbs down to enter. “I’ll restock our supplies,” they say. 
“It should only take a few minutes. Watch the wagon, 
would you?”
Not long after Ethran heads inside, four angry-
looking individuals saunter out of Draymoor’s small 
tavern and begin to approach the wagon. Each of them 
wears hastily sewn patches depicting the flag of Cheliax 
and are armed with a light mace and a crossbow, 
though they haven’t drawn them. They accost the 
PCs with questions about where they’re coming from 
and what their business is in town. Use the Draymoor 
Road map on page 14 for this encounter.
Creatures: These locals are loyal to Cheliax’s rule 
over Isger and suspicious of all strangers. The PCs 
can try to get these loyalists to leave them alone by 
succeeding at two DC 15 Deception, Diplomacy, or 
Intimidation checks; each check can be attempted by 
a different person and they can use different skills or 
the same skill twice. If the PCs succeed, the loyalists 
are either mollified or scared off depending on the 
group’s tactics.
If the PCs fail two of these checks before they 
succeed, the loyalists get violent. Two of the loyalists 
fight with their light maces while the other two stand 
back and fire their crossbows. The loyalists try to 
remain adjacent to one another as they fight. If the 
PCs knock out two of the loyalists, the other two 
flee. The loyalists all flee if each of them is below 5 
Hit Points. During an altercation, the other village 
residents disappear indoors. Draymoor has no local 
law enforcement and the area’s sheriff won’t make her 
rounds here for another four days, so once the loyalists 
have been driven off or killed, the PCs are in no further 
danger here.

RIVER CROSSING	
SEVERE 1
A day and a half later, the group arrives at the North 
Conerica River just before dusk. They only have to 
cross the river before the home stretch to Saringallow. 
A regular ferry shuttles travelers back and forth across 
the wide river. Another large group booked passage 
several minutes before the PCs, so the party has to wait 
until the ferry returns for its last trip of the evening. A 
riverside inn can be seen on the far bank, while the side 
the PCs are on features only a small shack and dock.
While they wait, the GM should attempt a secret DC 
16 Perception check for each PC. Those who succeed 
spot a pair of silhouettes against the setting sun that 
seem to be large flying creatures approaching fast; any 
successful PCs also receive a +1 circumstance bonus 
to their initiative in the upcoming fight. Use the River 
Crossing map above for this encounter.
Creatures: Illcayna Alonnor (malevolent female 
daughter of Urgathoa 9; page 242) has been operating 
in Isger for years, and the war has given her the 
opportunity to escalate her plans to take the nation. 
As she gathers her power in Finder’s Gulch dozens of 
miles to the west, her necromantic creations sometimes 
range far from the town. A pair of undead giant bats 
recently took to the skies in search of victims, turning 
various animals across the hillside into zombies. While 
the players are unlikely to learn where these zombie 
bats came from, their appearance foreshadows the 
undead troubles that await in later chapters. The 
zombie bats fight until they are destroyed.
If it looks like the PCs are having trouble during 
this fight, Ethran can offer them some tactical advice. 
Each round, they attempt to Aid a struggling PC’s next 
Strike by attempting a Warfare Lore check with a +10 
modifier. They otherwise try to stay near the wagon to 
keep the horse calm, but they do move out of a zombie 
bat’s rotting aura if subjected to it.

The Ferry Arrives: Shortly after the PCs defeat the 
zombie giant bats, the ferry returns to their side of 
the river. Utto, the ferry operator, is concerned about 
the group’s safety and quickly ushers them and the 
wagon onto his ferry. As the vessel makes its way 
back across, Utto asks the PCs what attacked them 
and if told, he nods his head knowingly. “My cousin 
told me that the dead have been mighty restless ever 
since all that god stuff fell from the sky. She thinks it 
has something to do with that lich what lives on Lake 
Encarthan.”
A PC who succeeds at a DC 18 Society or Politics 
Lore check has heard that “that lich” Tar-Baphon has 
mostly been concentrating his recent efforts on the 
Gravelands and attempting to subjugate the orcs of 
Belkzen. A PC who succeeds at a DC 14 Religion or 
Zombie Lore check knows that undead attacks can 
happen for a number of reasons, not all of which are 
related to a sinister necromancer trying to take over 
the world.
Welcome to Hellbreakers 
Headquarters
After crossing the river on the ferry, the PCs can 
spend the night at the inn and then continue on to 
Saringallow the next morning. There are no further 
incidents, and they arrive in the midafternoon at the 
northeastern gates.
Saringallow is a large walled town on the Conerica 
River that was founded as Sarini’s Hollow by the 
Chelaxian noble Sarini family a few centuries ago. 
After a series of mysterious deaths, the townspeople 
rose up against the Sarinis and publicly hanged them, 
giving the town its more somber sobriquet. More 
details about the town’s occult history and its 
current inhabitants can be found on page 201.
Despite the town having no love for 
Chelaxian nobles, the Hellbreakers League 
must still operate with some modicum of 
secrecy here. Regardless of whether PCs 
are from Saringallow or have visited 
the town before, they know that the 
League’s headquarters is in the basement 
of an unassuming two-story house on 
the eastern side of town. Rumors hold 
that the domicile was once the home 
of an alchemist who was corrupted by 
a demonic influence. His family has since 
moved away from Saringallow, and the founders of 
the Hellbreakers League purchased the house and 
constructed a large basement in which to plan their 
revolution. Agents sometimes stay in the house, but it 
isn’t large enough to lodge the entire League.
To gain entrance, the PCs know to knock on the front 
door and announce that they are “friends of Rose.” This 
is a reference to the goddess Milani, the patron of those 
who fight against injustice and tyranny and whose 
religious symbol is a rose in a pool of blood.
A dark-haired human woman opens the door and says 
with a smile, “Afternoon! Any friends of Rose can find 
refuge here.”
This is the proper response to the phrase the PCs 
gave, a reference to Milani’s celestial domain, the 
Refuge of the Red Rose. The woman answering the 
door is Maire Phelan (jovial female human storyteller 
3), who introduces herself after waving the PCs 
inside. The house’s main room looks like a typical 
cozy residence, with a hearth on the east wall and a 
large dining table in the center. After closing the front 
door, Maire approaches a plain wooden door in the 
southern wall, which she unlocks with an iron key. 
This leads to a set of stairs descending into the beating 
heart of the Hellbreakers League.
A wide basement stretches in front of the bottom of the 
staircase, crammed with several tables, a handful of chairs, 
and maps of Isger hung on nearly every wall. The tables 
are piled with documents, ledgers, and more maps. A tall 
hobgoblin man sorts through the documents, a stern look 
on his face. A side room has been cleared of all furniture, 
and two young soldiers spar within. A second, smaller 
alcove holds a magically heated iron stove that gives off

Maire alerts the assembled group that their newest

more permanent abode. Most Hellbreakers either have 
their own residences in Saringallow or stay at an inn 
in town between missions. Maire tells the PCs they 
can go the Fiend’s Finale, which gives discount rates 
to League members (5 sp a night for a private room 
that sleeps two).
But before the PCs can sleep, Rhokrag needs them 
to do something for the organization first.
Treasure: At some point after reaching the 
Hellbreakers headquarters, Ethran gives the PCs their 
+1 greatsword for escorting them to Saringallow. 
Ethran explains that with only one arm, they won’t 
have much use for it. “My job is to teach now, anyway,” 
they say with a smile.
Warehouse Mystery
With their first official mission for the Hellbreakers 
League complete, the PCs are immediately tasked 
with another. Rhokrag explains that supplies—armor, 
weapons, ammunition, rations, and so on—are the 
fuel that keeps a revolution’s fire burning, and the 
League is in constant need. There isn’t enough room 
within the house HQ to store all such provisions, so 
the League keeps them in a warehouse at the docks 
under the name of Everbloom Imports, a fictitious 
trading company and yet another reference to Milani.
Agents posing as merchants arrive in town 
with (usually stolen) supplies, move them into the 
warehouse, and then head back out into the country 
for their next mission. This morning, a League-
affiliated vessel arrived at the docks with provisions 
from Logas. Junior Hellbreaker Gertraud Mildenhall 
(confident female halfling smuggler –1) was to meet 
them at the warehouse and inventory the goods, but 
she hasn’t returned to headquarters yet.
Rhokrag is beginning to suspect something untoward 
might have happened, as Gertraud is known for being 
quite timely. Saringallow isn’t totally free of Chelaxian 
loyalists who would jump at the chance to collect a 
generous bounty. To make matters worse, this delivery 
from Logas was meant to help provision several 
missions out in the field and the League is running low 
on weapons and ammunition. The PCs are sent to the 
warehouse to see if anything happened to Gertraud.
Unfortunately, Rhokrag’s suspicions are correct. A 
handful of Chelaxian loyalists from Logas boarded the 
ship posing as Hellbreakers and tricked a dockworker 
into telling them the location of the League’s warehouse. 
They took the ship to the warehouse, grabbed Gertraud 
when she arrived, and are holding her hostage, intending 
to capture any additional dissidents who arrive to 
increase the bounty they’ll earn.

DOCKSIDE ROW
Saringallow’s docks are located on the south side of the 
city, right on the Conerica River. Warehouses line the 
street opposite, and throughout the day, a steady stream 
of stevedores unload cargo from docked ships and into 
those buildings. Carts arrive periodically to take the goods 
to their final destinations.
The warehouse for Everbloom Imports is at the 
eastern end of the street, partially isolated from the 
other buildings. If the PCs watch it for any period of 
time, they don’t see anyone enter or leave. They might 
want to ask around the area to see if anyone’s noticed 
anything suspicious. A PC who succeeds at a DC 16 
Perception check or a DC 14 Underworld Lore check 
spots a dark-haired youth lingering about. This is 
Valerra Clive (street-smart human female urchin 0), 
one of Saringallow’s less fortunate teens who do odd 
jobs for anyone who’ll pay them. She looks hopeful 
if the PCs approach her, assuming they need her to 
run a message or hold onto something not quite legal. 
When the PCs begin asking her questions about the 
warehouse, her excitement turns to disappointment, 
and she clams up. A PC who succeeds at a DC 18 
Diplomacy or Intimidation check convinces her to 
talk; offering her at least 2 sp achieves the same result.
Once sufficiently persuaded or bribed, Valerra tells 
the PCs that she saw three shifty-looking people come 
from the west end of the street and enter the warehouse 
early this morning after forcing open the side door. 
Before noon, a woman walked down the northern 
street and took out a key to open the same door; this 
woman didn’t seem to notice anything unusual. Since 
then, no one has come out. As a result of collecting this 
information, the PCs gain a +1 circumstance bonus to 
spot the falling crates trap in area A2 (page 18) and to 
the hazard’s Reflex saving throw.
Reward: If the PCs find out that something is odd 
about the Red Refuge from Valerra Clive, award them 
10 XP.
A1. OUTSIDE EVERBLOOM IMPORTS 
WAREHOUSE
The warehouse is a large, square building with a smaller 
annex on the eastern side. Double doors the width of a 
wagon are closed with a heavy chain and sturdy padlock. A 
regular-sized door leads into the annex.
The annex door is unlocked and slightly ajar. A PC 
who succeeds at a DC 17 Perception check or DC 15 
Crafting or Carpentry Lore check can see from a faint 
splintering in the frame that it was forced open. The 
padlock is an average lock (requiring four successful 
DC 25 Thievery checks to pick), and if the PCs 
manage to open it and quietly move the chain (DC 20 
Stealth check), they can catch the loyalists in area A3 
by surprise.
A2. WAREHOUSE ANNEX	
TRIVIAL 1
This attachment to the main warehouse holds some older-
looking crates stacked up against the east wall. An open 
doorway leads onto the warehouse floor to the west.
The Hellbreakers keep old, unused crates here after 
unpacking their contents in case they’re needed to 
smuggle goods elsewhere. Many of the crates are covered 
in crumbling forged bills of lading and a layer of dust.
THE THREE LIEUTENANTS
Maire Phelan, Rhokrag, and Xerra Bluebottle 
are the three highest-ranking members of the 
Hellbreakers League apart from the founders, 
Alceo and Phoebe Demetrias. Until Chapter 4, 
the PCs will be dealing mainly with these three 
lieutenants. The following descriptions should 
help you portray these NPCs over the course of 
the Adventure Path.
Maire Phelan is in charge of recruiting new 
agents and the League’s public relations. She’s 
always pleased to see the PCs and encourages 
them to describe their heroics in greater, more 
florid detail, noting that the people of Isger will 
rally around heroes. Maire is quick to offer a 
joke or some good-natured ribbing, especially to 
somber people like Rhokrag.
Rhokrag generally gives the PCs their missions 
and tends to remain out of the public eye. He 
recognizes that many are still prejudiced against 
goblinoids since the Goblinblood Wars, but he 
believes that getting out from under the thumb 
of Cheliax will help Isger heal. Rhokrag is quite 
serious and tends to appreciate PCs who are 
similarly no-nonsense.
Xerra Bluebottle keeps the League provisioned 
and armed. They work most days at Gunty’s 
Hearty Breads across town and often bring over 
the day-old pastries that Gunty Keronna can’t 
sell, warming them on the basement stove. They 
form an instant rapport with any PC who enjoys 
cooking or baking.

the annex past a tall stack of crates (indicated by a square

FALLING CRATES	
HAZARD 3
MECHANICAL
 TRAP
Stealth DC 20 (trained)
Description A tower of precariously stacked crates is 
rigged to fall when someone steps through a trip wire.
Disable DC 17 Thievery (trained) to carefully remove the 
trip wire.
Tumble Down [reaction] Trigger A creature trips the wire; Effect 
Several heavy crates come crashing down in the 10-
foot square area marked on the map, dealing 2d10+10 
bludgeoning damage to each creature in that area (DC 
20 basic Reflex save). A creature who critically fails the 
save is knocked prone.
Stealthy Approach: If the PCs trip the trap or 
otherwise make a loud noise (such as by calling out 
for Gertraud), the loyalists on the main warehouse 
floor automatically hear the PCs coming and gain a 
+1 circumstance bonus to their initiative rolls. If more 
than half of the PCs succeed at Stealth checks against 
the Chelaxian loyalist leader’s Perception DC of 17 
and trap wasn’t triggered, the loyalists are unaware 
of the PCs’ approach and take a –1 circumstance 
penalty to their initiative rolls. If neither of the above 
situations occur, the loyalists gain neither a bonus 
nor a penalty.
A3. MAIN WAREHOUSE	
MODERATE 1
This is where the Hellbreakers League keeps the 
majority of their supplies in Saringallow.
Only a few crates occupy this large, open space. The floor 
is hard-packed dirt with the occasional scattering of straw, 
and double doors lead south to the road. A woman lies tied 
up and gagged on top of a single closed crate in the center 
of the warehouse.
The woman is Gertraud Mildenhall, one of the 
PCs’ fellow League members, who was captured by 
a group of Chelaxian loyalists earlier in the day. She 
squirms and yells a muffled warning when she sees 
the PCs enter. A PC can untie Gertraud or remove her 
gag each with a single Interact action, though she is 
effectively a noncombatant in the encounter with the 
loyalists here.
Creatures: A pair of Chelaxian loyalists, along 
with their brash leader, lurk in the warehouse to try 
to capture more dissidents and collect the bounty. 
While they were confident after capturing Gertraud, 
they become a bit hesitant when they see the party of 
PCs. They still attack when at least one PC enters the 
room, moving out from behind crates and trying to 
look intimidating. One loyalist uses a crate for cover 
while firing their crossbow, and the other loyalist and 
the leader enter in melee. The loyalists want to take the 
PCs alive for the bounty, so they nonlethally strike at 
any PC that has already been wounded, taking the –2 
circumstance penalty to the attack.
The loyalist leader zealously fights until reduced to 0 
HP. The other loyalists try to flee if they’re wounded and 
their leader has been incapacitated, though it’s likely the 
PCs are in the way of the only viable exit. If a fleeing 
loyalist has no path to freedom, they surrender instead.

GERTRAUD MILDENHALL	
CREATURE –1
Commoner (Pathfinder NPC Core 66)
Initiative Perception +3
Interrogating the Loyalists: If the PCs capture any 
of the loyalists, they admit they tricked a stevedore 
into pointing out this warehouse after arriving on a 
merchant ship from Logas that has since departed for 
Elidir. A captured loyalist holds no regret for their 
actions, referring to the PCs and their allies as “scum 
and vermin.” What the PCs do with any captives is 
up to them; since the PCs were defending themselves 
upon being attacked, they can turn any remaining 
loyalists over to the Saringallow watch—though, as 
revolutionaries, they might not want to get involved 
with the authorities. If the PCs give Valerra 5 sp, 
she’ll call the watch for them and keep an eye on any 
captured and restrained loyalists in the street while the 
PCs leave the scene.
Supply Inventory: The supposed delivery from 
Logas seems to have been a mistake or a ruse. Once 
rescued, Gertraud notes that at least the loyalists 
didn’t damage any of the League’s current supplies, 
which doesn’t amount to much. The few crates within 
the warehouse contain very basic goods: common 
suits of armor, shields, simple and martial weapons, 
and some ammunition (arrows 
and bolts, mainly). Gertraud 
matter-of-factly 
adds 
all 
weapons confiscated off the loyalists 
to the crates.
Treasure: Among the crated weapons 
is a low-grade silver melee weapon of 
the same type that one of the PCs 
uses regularly, and a whispering wire 
(page 212). Gertraud notices the PCs 
examining that weapon and insists that 
they take it for rescuing her. In addition, she 
hands another PC a masquerade scarf that has been 
passed around several Hellbreakers to aid in keeping 
a low profile, especially when securing supplies in a 
less-than-legal fashion.
Provisioning the Revolution
The next day, Rhokrag and Xerra meet with the 
agents to discuss the next steps. While they wait 
for further orders from the Demetriases, Xerra 
asks that the Hellbreakers here in Saringallow 
use the time to further provision the organization 
since their supplies from Logas were compromised. 
To that end, several groups are heading out of the 
city to raid some known Cheliax-friendly targets to 
procure armor, weapons, food, and other necessary 
materials. In the meantime, Ethran Howell will 
remain at the headquarters to continue to train a 
handful of new recruits and wait for any news from 
the League’s leaders.
As he delineates the specifics of each group’s 
mission, Rhokrag gives the following warning.
“I’m not going to lie—what we’re about to do will involve 
some law breaking. But you probably weren’t expecting 
to be upstanding Isgeri citizens when you signed up to 
be a Hellbreaker. We’re only taking what we need for the 
greater good of the country, and it’s not like those we’re 
taking from can’t afford to lose something. They’ll fight like 
that isn’t true, though, and who wouldn’t? You’re going 
to face some danger out there, mostly from hired guards 
who are just doing their jobs. Which is why, and I can’t 
stress this enough, we must refrain from killing as much as 
possible.” He briefly looks at each assembled Hellbreaker 
in turn.
“In the coming weeks and months, we’re going to 
need the people of Isger on our side. They must see us 
as fighting a good and necessary fight. Some might even 
join us! But until then, we can’t give Cheliax ammunition to

The PCs are tasked with some light river piracy. 
Rhokrag gives them directions to a spot on the North 
Conerica River that League scouts have determined 
would be a good place to ambush a passing trade 
vessel. Ships often move cargo out of Elidir bound 
for Cheliax. If a PC brings up the fact that Chelaxian 
ships pass by (and sometimes stop at) Saringallow 
all the time, Rhokrag responds, “That has a chance 
of bringing some unwanted scrutiny on the city in 
which we have our headquarters. Better we operate 
in places where such attacks could be blamed on 
bandits. For now.”
Petty Cash: Xerra gives the PCs 10 gp to buy 
anything they think they might need for the mission. 
“Better come back with more than that in supplies,” 
the halfling says with a wink.
Riverboat Ambush
The journey to the scouted ambush spot takes 
approximately two days and is relatively uneventful. 
The PCs continue to spot copies of Hedvend’s bounty 
on so-called traitors nailed up in the villages and farms 
they pass by, but no one stops them to question their 
loyalty. If the PCs took precautions to appear like 
everyday travelers, note that their thinking ahead is 
the cause of their smooth trip. Use the map to the left 
for this encounter.
B1. RIVERBANK
The PCs arrive at the designated spot—an area where 
the North Conerica River narrows a bit and passes 
by a rocky outcropping that provides excellent cover 
against ships approaching from the north—as the sun 
is setting. Most ships don’t travel much at night, so the 
PCs have time to make camp and prepare the area for 
an ambush.
Ambushing a ship, even one on a river, isn’t like 
committing highway robbery. There’s no easy way to 
stop the vessel’s passage short of completely blocking 
the river, which is well beyond the PCs’ capabilities. 
However, they should come up with some kind of plan 
that uses their party’s strengths.
Later that day, the PCs spot a potential target in 
the Night’s Prize, a trading vessel flying Chelaxian 
colors. It’s a relatively smaller boat, so it won’t have 
a lot of crew to deal with, and its hull sits low in the 
water, suggesting it’s full of cargo. The Night’s Prize 
is captained by Julenus Aedin (cutthroat male human 
privateer 1), a successful merchant who has a minor 
reputation for cruelty. No other boats are in view, 
so this is a perfect opportunity for the PCs to enact 
their plan.
Use the following examples as guidelines for how to 
adjudicate your group’s specific plan. Of course, some 
groups might simply start firing arrows and spells at 
the crew! Run the first combat from B2 with the PCs 
on the banks and the swabbies taking cover. Unless 
they have some way to stop or slow the ship, the PCs 
have 3 rounds to get aboard before the current takes 
the ship out of reach. A successful DC 12 Athletics 
check is required to Swim in the river.
Faking Distress: Tricky PCs might want to fool 
an approaching ship into stopping (or slowing 
down) long enough to be boarded. This requires a 
convincing reason (such as a false wound); each PC 
who participates in the ruse must attempt a DC 18 
Deception or Performance check. Less charismatic PCs 
can hide behind the outcropping by attempting DC 16 
Stealth checks. Anyone who fails their check takes a 
–1 circumstance penalty to their initiative roll. If all 
the PCs fail their checks, they can still attempt their 
ambush, but each member of the ship’s crew (but not 
the animated armor) gains a +1 circumstance bonus to 
the first attack roll they make against a PC.
Show of Force: The threat of violence might be 
enough to get an approaching ship to allow the

B2. NIGHT’S PRIZE LOW 1 AND MODERATE 1
This riverboat is painted mostly red with black accents, 
mirroring the colors of the Chelaxian flag that flies from its 
mast. Spiky protrusions line the gunwales. A wide door leads 
into the ship to the aft, and a hatch leads down into the hull.
The Night’s Prize is a fairly typical, if small, vessel. 
A framed portrait of Abrogail Thrune hangs over the 
door to the captain’s quarters.
Creatures: As the PCs board the Night’s Prize, 
most of the crew throw up their hands and surrender. 
They aren’t paid enough to risk their lives repelling 
attackers, and a few know about the captain’s secret 
guardian (see The Captain’s Armor). However, two 
younger swabbies are eager to prove themselves to 
the captain and brandish bottles in response to the 
PCs’ intrusion. Each of them pleads for mercy when 
reduced to 5 or fewer Hit Points.
NIGHT’S PRIZE SWABBIES (2)	
CREATURE 0
Dockhand (Pathfinder NPC Core 66)
Initiative Perception +3
The Captain’s Armor: Upon hearing the news 
about the Battle of Hellknight Hill, Captain Aedin 
spent most of the profits of his previous cargo run 
on an animated suit of armor in Elidir. This was 
mainly to protect himself from any anti-Cheliax 
rebels he believes are roaming the countryside, 
including fighting off boarders and pirates. At the 
beginning of the third round of combat with the 
swabbies or the round after both swabbies have been 
defeated, Captain Aedin appears in the doorway to 
his quarters, standing next to an intricate black suit 
of armor with no one inside. “You have 5 seconds 
to get off my damned ship,” he says, pointing his 
dagger at the PCs. No matter what the PCs reply, 
the two roll initiative.

Captain’s Armor

===== Page 23 =====
The animated armor protects the captain at all costs 
and attempts to always end its turn adjacent to him. 
Captain Aedin presses his attacks against wounded 
PCs first. The captain fights to the death, knowing 
that his animated armor has a final trick up its sleeve 
(see Sinking Ship!). If the captain is killed before the 
armor is destroyed, the armor begins acting erratically. 
It spends 1 action each turn Striding up to 10 feet in a 
random direction, though it never falls over the edge 
of the ship.
CAPTAIN JULENUS AEDIN	
CREATURE 1
Weak navigator (Pathfinder NPC Core 5, 146)
Initiative Perception +7
ANIMATED ARMOR	
CREATURE 2
Pathfinder Monster Core 18
Initiative Perception +6
SINKING SHIP!	
MODERATE 1
When the animated armor has been reduced to 0 Hit 
Points, the captain’s final failsafe is triggered. Bright 
red runes flare up on the armor as it collapses, and 
the PCs hear muffled explosions from below deck. 
Out of paranoia, when Captain Aedin purchased 
the animated armor, he magically linked its runes to 
three containers of alchemist’s fire stored within the 
hull of the ship. He planned to defuse the runes when 
the Night’s Prize reached its destination, but the PCs’ 
attack has justified their installation.
The Night’s Prize begins to simultaneously burn 
and sink. If the PCs want to salvage any supplies 
before they are destroyed or lost at the bottom of the 
river, they’ll have to act fast. This encounter uses the 
Victory Point subsystem (Pathfinder GM Core 184) 
to track how successful the PCs are during this crisis. 
Each obstacle has a threshold of Victory Points (VP) 
required to overcome it. Actions are made in phases 
where each PC can attempt a check to earn Victory 
Points toward the completion of a chosen obstacle. 
If the group’s VP total for an obstacle equals or 
exceeds the threshold of that obstacle, they overcome 
that obstacle. With the exception of the Swimming 
to Safety obstacle, the PCs can attempt any of the 
obstacles in any order, and each PC can work toward 
a different obstacle if they wish. The Subduing the 
Captain obstacle is available only if Captain Aedin 
is still alive.
The PCs have six phases before the Night’s Prize 
completely sinks. If the PCs haven’t completed the 
Swimming to Safety obstacle before then, any PC who 
didn’t contribute a VP to that obstacle’s completion 
becomes fatigued from their efforts to swim ashore.
AIDING THE CREW	
OBSTACLE
Threshold 4; Overcome DC 17 Athletics, Diplomacy, or 
Medicine; DC 15 Sailing Lore
Some of the Night’s Prize crew were injured in the 
explosions or are panicking as the ship sinks. The PCs can 
either tend to their wounds, carry them to safety, or calm 
them down.
PUTTING OUT FIRES	
OBSTACLE
Threshold 4; Overcome DC 18 Acrobatics or Survival
A multitude of fires have broken out across the ship. 
Putting them out will make other tasks easier.
Special A PC who can magically produce water can use 
the skill associated with the tradition of that magic to 
overcome this obstacle. If a phase ends and the PCs 
haven’t overcome this obstacle, each PC who hasn’t 
succeeded at a check to overcome the Swimming to 
Safety obstacle takes 1d4 fire damage.
SECURING SUPPLIES	
OBSTACLE
Threshold 2; Overcome DC 16 Athletics, Crafting, or 
Thievery; DC 15 Mercantile Lore; DC 17 Perception
Several crates of supplies—food, clothing, and alchemical 
items—are stored in the ship’s hold. The PCs must try to 
secure as much as possible for the Hellbreakers League.
Special The PCs can attempt to overcome this obstacle 
multiple times. Keep track of how many times the PCs 
overcome this obstacle for their rewards. If the PCs have 
yet to overcome the Subduing the Captain obstacle (if 
the captain is still alive), they take a –2 circumstance 
penalty to checks to overcome this obstacle as the 
captain tries to stop them from stealing his goods.
SUBDUING THE CAPTAIN	
OBSTACLE
Threshold 3; Overcome DC 17 Intimidation or attack roll
If Captain Aedin is still alive, he could prove to be a 
nuisance to the PCs.
Special A PC who casts spells can expend them to subdue 
the captain. Attempt a DC 17 spell attack roll or have the 
captain attempt a saving throw as usual for the spell. 
A failure on a saving throw grants 1 VP, while a critical 
failure grants 2. At the GM’s discretion, certain spells 
might completely subdue the captain, immediately 
overcoming this obstacle.
SWIMMING TO SAFETY	
OBSTACLE
Threshold 4; Overcome DC 15 Athletics, Nature, or Survival
Before the Night’s Prize completely sinks, the PCs must get 
off the ship and swim to shore.
Special Once the PCs decide to attempt this obstacle, 
they can’t simultaneously attempt to overcome any 
other obstacles. Once they overcome this obstacle, the 
encounter ends.

Unfortunately, however, the chaos

GLIDING RIVER SNAKES (2)	
CREATURE 0
Page 230
Initiative Perception +6
Treasure: Washed up from the remains of the Night’s 
Prize is a ring of discretion (Pathfinder Treasure Vault 
154), a greased axle (page 210), and a fine compass 
worth 10 gp.
Returning to Saringallow
Even if the PCs didn’t stop to rescue any of the Night’s 
Prize crew, some of them made it to shore. They are 
in no shape to put up a fight and, unless the PCs stop 
them, they trudge off in the direction of Elidir (or 
another nearby settlement). If asked or threatened, 
these individuals promise not to say anything about 
the PCs to any authorities. In fact, one of them is 
grateful to the PCs for dealing with Captain Aedin, 
whom they categorize as a “cruel, unfeeling man.” 
While some of the crew might be Chelaxian citizens, 
none of them have strong opinions about the current 
political situation. If any of the PCs express a sentiment 
of leaving no witnesses, remind them that they’ve been 
asked to kill only in self-defense.
It takes 2 days to return to Saringallow, though it 
might take longer if the PCs didn’t secure a method of 
transport such as a wagon for the supplies. If the PCs 
successfully overcame the Aiding the Crew obstacle 
during the Sinking Ship! encounter, those they helped 
can either aid the PCs in carrying the supplies 
or procure a cart for them. The journey is 
uneventful, especially if the characters 
play the parts of simple traveling 
citizens.
GONE MISSING
When the PCs get back to the 
Hellbreakers headquarters, they 
are debriefed by Maire, who seems 
a bit distracted. She’s pleased with 
whatever supplies the PCs return with 
and gives them a brief rundown 
of the other groups’ successes 
if asked. Afterward, Ethran 
approaches the PCs to let them 
know that there are whispers that Rhokrag 
hasn’t yet returned from his own mission. He was 
scheduled to check in the previous day and is far too 
disciplined to either miss an appointed time or neglect 
to send word if he’ll be late. If the PCs aren’t already 
concerned, Ethran suggests that they either talk to 
Maire about the possibility of Rhokrag’s capture or 
death, or track Rhokrag down themselves.
A PC who succeeds at a DC 15 Diplomacy 
check to Gather Information learns from the other 
Hellbreakers (or from Maire if they go right to the 
source) that Rhokrag had gone off on his own for 
some reconnaissance on the road to Logas, hoping 
to get some advance notice if Hellknight forces have 
regrouped enough to range further into Isger again. 
Specifically, Rhokrag had a local non-League contact 
that he was going to meet at the Waterspout Inn, a 
riverside tavern and lodging house halfway between 
Logas and Saringallow. If the PCs fail this check, they 
receive the same information from Ethran, who has 
since spoken with Maire. Later that same day, if the 
PCs haven’t already volunteered to pursue this lead, 
Maire asks them to do so.
Rhokrag’s Rescue
Unfortunately, when Rhokrag met his contact at the 
Waterspout Inn, he was betrayed. With whispers of 
insurgents and revolutionaries in Isger, the Chelaxian 
navy sent a patrol ship up the Conerica to make it 
clear to the citizens who was in charge. This vessel, 
the Witchfire, is captained by Lamperia Bane (ruthless 
female human captain 3), a steadfast military woman 
who signed her soul away to Hell only a few years 
ago in exchange for a rapid rise up the ranks. Upon 
arriving in Isger, Captain Bane began announcing that

addition, a handful of red-and-black tents have been 
erected near the riverbank behind the inn. Another 
Chelaxian banner hangs above them. It’s clear that 
Chelaxian forces have occupied the inn, but what isn’t 
clear is where they might be holding Rhokrag. Luckily,

If they watch the area from afar for a bit, they notice 
that no one enters or leaves the inn. A PC who also

movement in the windows of the inn’s first floor. A 
PC who succeeds at a DC 16 Warfare Lore check 
recognizes that camp is visible from the deck of the 
ship, and unless they are very stealthy, once they enter 
the camp, they’ll likely be spotted; any fighting within 
the camp will probably be heard from the ship.
The PCs should decide whether they want to mount 
their rescue right away or wait a little more than an 
hour until nightfall. At night, lanterns are lit inside the 
inn on the first floor, and the Chelaxian soldiers light 
torches in the camp and lanterns on the Witchfire. 
These provide light for many ancestries to see at short 
range, but outside of their radius, the cover of darkness 
could grant certain characters an edge against the 
unsuspecting loyalists. Use the Witchfire map above 
for this encounter.

C1. INN YARD
A small stone fountain, its basin empty except for several 
fallen leaves, stands just a few yards from the road. The 
two-story inn beyond it was once painted a bright blue, 
but the color has faded to gray. A sign above the front door 
reads “Waterspout Inn” with a crude image of an upward 
spray of water. A path of churned-up dirt by the fountain 
leads to an unattached stable.
The inn’s fountain has been drained for the autumn 
and winter seasons. The stable is unoccupied, apart 
from a few mice nibbling on some old hay.
As they don’t know who’s inside the inn, the 
PCs might try to create a diversion to draw out the 
occupants. To do so, a PC must succeed on a DC 12 skill 
check, depending on the nature of the ruse; Deception 
and Performance are likely the most applicable skills. 
The loyalists inside have grown bored after the brief 
excitement of capturing Rhokrag, so they’re eager to 
investigate any sounds.
C2. WATERSPOUT INN	
LOW 1
A fire burns in the hearth of this simple tavern to ward off 
the autumnal chill. A gaudily painted trident hangs above 
the fireplace. Several tables have been pushed against one 
wall, their accompanying chairs haphazardly stacked on 
top. A door leads out to the inn’s front yard and a slightly 
smaller door next to the bar leads out back. A set of stairs 
leads up to the second floor.
When Captain Bane arrived a few days ago and 
rented out the whole building, Vinzent, the inn’s 
proprietor, guiltily drank himself into a stupor as he 
knows the captain is likely to have ill intentions for 
Isger. He’s currently passed out on one of the upstairs 
room’s beds. If the PCs find and wake him, he gives 
them a warning about Captain Bane: “She consorts 
with devils, she does!” Otherwise, the rented rooms 
are empty.
Creatures: Three of the loyalists recruited by 
Captain Bane are on the first floor, occasionally 
partaking of the inn’s alcohol and playing games of 
darts. They’re waiting for the captain to finally break 
Rhokrag, giving them more targets on which to vent 
their pro-Cheliax ire. They’re cowards at heart, so if 
one of them is knocked unconscious, the other two 
try to flee through the most accessible door. This 
might mean they run out the back, alerting the camp. 
Otherwise, the recruits are used to hearing the loyalists 
carousing and don’t investigate if they hear noises 
from the inn.
CHELAXIAN LOYALISTS (3)	
CREATURE –1
Page 13
Initiative Perception +5
Innkeeper’s Aid: To alleviate his guilt in helping 
Bane, Vinzent offers the PCs a lesser bottled lightning 
and swift sparrow marvelous miniature (page 210) 
that he had in storage.
C3. SHORE CAMP	
MODERATE 1
Three tents have been erected in the narrow stretch 
between the inn and the river. Pennants with the national 
symbol of Cheliax fly from each tent, occasionally flapping 
in a cold breeze coming from off the water. A campfire 
smolders in the middle of the tents, surrounded by a couple 
of collapsible cloth camp stools.
Despite having rented out the inn’s few rooms, 
Captain Bane insists that her crew either remain on 
board the ship or set up camp outside the inn. She 
doesn’t want them “going soft” after sleeping in beds 
for a few nights. The three tents here are dyed red and 
black and each hold one sleeper.
Creatures: Two recent recruits to the Witchfire’s 
crew have been relegated to camp duty. One of the 
local loyalists is also here, eager to curry favor with 
anyone associated with the Chelaxian government. 
Though the recruits are relaxing, they’re still 
disciplined soldiers. They’re wearing their armor and 
have their weapons within arm’s reach as they sit by 
the campfire.
If they spot the PCs before combat starts, they first 
attempt to scare off the PCs. When it becomes clear 
that the PCs aren’t civilians, one recruit takes up their 
guisarme and demands the loyalist backs them up in 
melee combat, while the other recruit fires arrows 
at any other ranged combatant or spellcaster. The 
loyalist tries to flee if either of the recruits are knocked 
unconscious, but the recruits are steadfastly faithful to 
Cheliax and Captain Bane and fight until reduced to 
0 Hit Points.
By now, the recruits are used to commotions 
coming from inside the inn as other loyalists drink 
and get rowdy, so they don’t respond to any sounds of 
combat. However, if the PCs manage to sneak aboard 
the Witchfire and start a fight, the recruits will take a 
round to gather their weapons and rush onto the ship; 
the loyalist doesn’t join them.

C4A. WITCHFIRE DECK	
MODERATE 1
A short gangplank leads up from the riverbank to the deck 
of this Chelaxian vessel. Most of the planks making up the 
deck and hull have been painted black, though elaborate 
wooden scrollwork along the gunwales and across the bow 
depict curling wicks of flame, the tips of which have been 
colored a bright green. Other details around the ship have 
been painted the same color, giving an eerie effect. Doors 
lead fore and aft, and a ladder leads down into the hold. A 
Chelaxian flag flies from top the taller of the two masts.
The Witchfire’s color scheme is meant to intimidate 
enemy vessels and help the vessel move stealthily 
through the night when necessary. It’s a well-
maintained ship, thanks to Captain Bane’s strictness. 
With such a small crew, she can focus her attention 
on any one of them at any point to discipline laziness 
or incompetence.
The rigging here can be climbed with a successful 
DC 10 Athletics check.
Creatures: Two marines are on board at all times, 
keeping watch for threats from the river and scrubbing 
the deck. The marines use their familiarity with the 
ship to their advantage, climbing up into the rigging 
and attacking PCs below. Any marines the PCs 
encounter here have served with Captain Bane for a 
few years, so they know she expects them to die for 
her; they fight until brought down to 0 HP.
These marines are a little afraid to leave their posts 
but are equally worried about allowing intruders to 
interrupt Captain Bane’s interrogations. If they notice 
a fight at the camp in area C3, they wait until the 
third round of combat before rolling initiative and 
disembarking the ship. When they do so, they begin 
the fight frightened 1.

CREATURE 1

C4B. HOLD
The Witchfire’s hold is currently empty, save for a 
human-sized cage that acts as a brig and a single chest 
at the other end.
Treasure: Inside the chest is the ship’s payroll, 
consisting of 30 gp. Captain Bane leaves the chest 
unlocked, as the crew knows better than to try to steal 
the money. The last swabbie who tried was hanged 
from the boom.
C5. GALLEY
The aft doors lead into the ship’s galley, which contains its 
stores of fresh water and salted meat. Several hammocks 
hang near the ship’s fore, each covered by a thin blanket.
This area serves as the place where the crew eats and 
sleeps. The Witchfire doesn’t have a dedicated ship’s 
cook, so the recruits take turns preparing meager meals.
C6. CAPTAIN’S QUARTERS	
SEVERE 1
This spacious chamber is lavishly furnished with black 
and red velvet drapes, overstuffed chairs, a bed, and 
a mahogany desk. Several trinkets sit on shelves. The 
grandeur of the decor is marred by fresh bloodstains on the 
floor. Sitting in the center of the room is Rhokrag, barely 
conscious and tied to a wooden chair. His face is a map of 
bruises and cuts. Behind him stands a tall and imposing 
woman dressed in the uniform of the Chelaxian navy, as 
well as a grinning devil.
The captain’s quarters have been temporarily 
transformed into an interrogation room, as Captain 
Bane and her summoned devil accomplice have been 
questioning Rhokrag here for the past few days. A PC 
can free Rhokrag with a single Interact action, but

A Hellknight’s Revenge?

After rescuing Rhokrag from the Witchfire and 
returning to Saringallow, the PCs have 1 week of 
downtime for their own personal projects. This is 
an excellent time for the characters to train and 
level up, purchase or craft equipment, or rest and 
recuperate.
Some characters might want to look into the name 
“Hellknight Ahala,” but there isn’t much to find. Viro 
Ahala (vengeful male human Hellknight armiger 5; 
page 246) has little to his name, though he aims to fix 
that. A survivor of the Battle of Hellknight Hill, Viro 
yearns for vengeance against the Hellbreakers and is 
plotting their destruction with fiendish obsession.
Having learned about the Sisterhood of the Golden 
Erinys, an Isgeri monastic order fostered by the Church 
of Asmodeus, Viro approached the sisters in the name 
of the Order of the Rack and was persuasive enough 
to enlist their aid. Believing him to be a true Hellknight 
thanks to stolen armor and his confident arrogance, 
Sister Endreah (steely female human Asmodean nun 
4) brought him to a hidden monastery called the 
Lucent Mission (page 42), where he discovered a 
grand ritual to summon a devil that could give him 
the power needed to defeat the League. While the PCs 
are busy recruiting the citizens of Isger, Viro is likewise 
recruiting several other fleeing Hellknight armigers on 
his way to a series of caves in the Chitterwood where 
he can enact his ritual.
Building a Political 
Movement
At the end of the week, Rhokrag calls for an 
organization-wide meeting after receiving a message 
from the Demetriases.

Hellbreakers fill every corner of the basement headquarters 
as Rhokrag climbs onto a table and holds up a folded sheet 
of paper. “We just got word from Alceo and Phoebe, and 
they are quite pleased with our efforts so far!” A general 
murmur of satisfaction runs through the assembled. “They 
especially want to acknowledge the efforts of my 
rescuers.”
“And to tell you to stay away from boats from 
now on!” shouts Maire to some scattered laughter.
“We all make mistakes,” coughs Rhokrag. “The 
Demetriases are reporting that due in large part 
to our supply raids on various trade vessels, 
Druma has begun to limit their trade routes 
on the Conerica. Yes, this will hurt Isger’s 
economy more than Cheliax’s, but it’s a start. 
Hedvend is likely going to increase military 
patrols near the river, maybe even going so 
far as to ask for soldiers from Thrune.” The 
crowd boos. “The Demetriases are suggesting 
that we ease back on the raids for now. We need to show 
the citizens of Isger that the Hellbreakers League is more 
than a band of violent insurgents. They need to know that 
we care about the land and its people. This is OUR land. 
These are OUR people.” Another cheer rises up, louder than 
the first.
“Over the next few weeks, you’ll be going out among 
those people to spread the word of why Isgeri independence 
is so important. Talk to them. Find out what’s important to 
them and convince them it’s important to you as well. And 
if they need help, give it.”
The PCs are assigned an area of Isger south of the 
Conerica River and north of the Chitterwood that 
includes villages like Umok, Stumpfield, and Vordia, 
as well as the garrison at Wolfpoint. The PCs don’t 
need to range as far west as Logas or as far east 
as Dustpawn as another group has been assigned 
the southeast portion of Isger east of the Aspodell 
Mountains. See the map of Isger on page 176 for these 
settlements’ exact locations; you should also share this 
map with the players.
The PCs can visit these locations in any order they 
see fit, though Wolfpoint is the closest to Saringallow. 
The characters might ask about other villages and 
farms along their route; such locations are not detailed 
in this chapter, but you can describe them as being 
generally peaceful, albeit worried about the brewing 
hostilities between Andoran and Cheliax. Most Isgeri 
citizens don’t want to be caught in the middle of 
another bloody war. The PCs can make a single skill 
check during each day of travel to represent speaking 
with these townspeople and farmers to gain Reputation 
Points, as described in Countryside Travel on page 30.
There is no time limit for this portion of the 
adventure, though as the PCs help people and 
investigate unusual goings-on, they will eventually get 
a lead on Viro Ahala’s plans to get revenge against the 
Hellbreakers League.
GAINING REPUTATION POINTS
During this chapter, the PCs gain Reputation 
Points (RP), which represent the positive 
opinion and goodwill that the people of Isger 
have toward the Hellbreakers League and the 
idea of Isgeri independence. By defeating 
certain foes and solving problems, the 
PCs will gain RP automatically, but there 
will also be opportunities for skill checks 
to gain additional RP. Keep track of the 
group’s RP total, as they will be important 
in later chapters, as well as affecting how 
much the PCs will need to worry about 
Hedvend’s bounty on insurgents as the weeks progress. 
If the PCs saved the crew of the Night’s Prize in Chapter 
1, they start with 1 RP.
4 or fewer RP: If the PCs mention that they are 
affiliated with the Hellbreakers League or express open 
disdain for the Chelaxian government before they gain 
any RP at a location, attempt a DC 11 flat check. On 
a failure, at least a few people in the area still have a 
positive opinion toward Cheliax and mistrust the PCs’ 
intentions. The PCs take a –2 circumstance penalty to 
skill checks to gain Reputation Points at this location.
5–8 RP: As above, but the flat check is DC 5.
9–12 RP: As above, but the flat check is DC 5 and 
the PCs only take a –1 circumstance penalty on a 
failure.
13 or more RP: Most of the people the PCs talk to 
are receptive to the idea of throwing off the yoke of 
Chelaxian rule. You don’t need to attempt a flat check 
if the PCs openly mention their affiliation.
Reward: The first time the PCs have a total of 10 or 
more RP, award them 10 XP.
Development: When the PCs reach 10 Reputation 
Points, they’re approached by Sister Sylve (See A 
Repentant Sister on page 41).
WHAT HAVE WE HEARD?
The PCs might want to know about the places they 
are being sent before they head out of Saringallow. 
They can attempt a DC 16 Diplomacy check to Gather 
Information or a DC 16 Isger Lore or Society check 
to Recall Knowledge about each place, learning the 
information listed below on a success. Each location 
also lists an additional skill a PC can use to Recall 
Knowledge about that location.
Hellbreaker Symbol

===== Page 31 =====
30
Wolfpoint (Warfare Lore): The Wolfpoint reserve 
garrison was built before the Goblinblood Wars to 
hold soldiers and officers with the primary purpose 
of protecting the roads by the Conerica River from 
bandit activity. The wooden palisade of Wolfpoint 
isn’t impenetrable, though, having burned to the 
ground during the war. On a critical success, the PC 
has also heard that the soldiers stationed there have 
been reassigned to the Andoran border, leaving the 
garrison unoccupied.
Vordia (Religion): Vordia is a small, traditional 
Isgeri town northwest of the Aspodell Mountains. 
During the Goblinblood Wars, it suffered a fair amount 
of damage and many of its people were killed. The 
Chelaxian government helped rebuild after the war, 
creating a fair amount of goodwill with the people 
that lasts to this day. On a critical success, the PC also 
knows that the Sisterhood of the Golden Erinys has 
run an orphanage in Vordia since the war.
Umok (Gnome Lore): Umok is a gnome settlement 
nestled between the Chitterwood and the Aspodell 
Mountains. The residents have had unfortunate 
dealings with goblins in the past (not including the 
Goblinblood Wars) and have outlawed fire within 
500 yards of the village. They instead use magic and 
alchemy for cooking, warmth, and light. On a critical 
success, the PC has heard that the gnome villagers 
maintain a network of wild animals to warn them of 
a dangerous creature’s approach. They also know that 
Umok is known for raising Isgeri boarhounds (page 
215), a breed of dog with a penchant for hunting 
down extraplanar prey.
Stumpfield (Goblin Lore): Stumpfield is something 
of an oddity in Isger, as a recently established village 
of artists of both goblin and human. Located just 
north of the Chitterwood, the village and its residents 
are considered “weird but harmless” by most. On a 
critical success, the PC also knows that there is some 
tension between Stumpfield and the nearby farming 
village of Fernsby, which provides a lot of Stumpfield’s 
day-to-day goods.
Countryside Travel
Like in most countries, small roads and paths 
crisscross the whole of Isger that aren’t marked on any 
map. Most locals know how to get to the three or four 
places that are most important to them, so these roads 
lack any consistent signage. However, traveling from 
one location to another isn’t meant to be a challenge 
for the PCs; a character might even originally be from 
this area! Most residents are happy enough to point 
the party in the right direction, especially in some of 
the larger towns like Vordia. Use the map on page 
176 to chart approximate distances between locations 
and the party’s slowest Speed to determine how many 
miles they can travel in 1 day.
These journeys should be relatively uneventful, 
though if you feel the PCs are lacking in XP, a group 
of Chelaxian loyalists or Chelaxian recruits might 
attempt to bar their passage on the road. Alternatively, 
a wild animal or two might be hungry and desperate 
enough to stalk the PCs as they travel, attacking when 
they are all alone.
In addition, each day they are on the road, one PC 
can attempt a DC 18 skill check to sway the locals they 
might interact with on their journey into supporting the 
Hellbreakers League and Isgeri independence, earning 
them RP. Diplomacy is the default skill to use for these 
checks, but a PC might attempt a Deception check 
to fabricate terrible acts the Chelaxian government 
is planning, a Performance check to entertain (while 
hiding anti-Cheliax or pro-Isger sentiment within the 
performance), or an Isger Lore or Society check to 
discuss the citizens’ everyday problems and how they 
might be improved with a new government. Players 
might even propose other skills. At your discretion, the 
DC might be 1 higher or lower to represent how loyal 
the locals are to Cheliax.
Wolfpoint
The Wolfpoint reserve garrison is just south of the 
Conerica River and was built before the Goblinblood 
Wars to hold about 300 soldiers and officers, mainly 
to protect the waterway and nearby roads from 
bandit activity. The wooden palisade surrounding the 
many barracks was burned to the ground during the 
war but has since been repaired. With the tensions 
and eventual conflict at Breachill, the soldiers that 
were stationed here were reassigned elsewhere within 
Isger, leaving the garrison empty for the past several 
weeks.
As the PCs make their way toward Wolfpoint, 
they begin to hear rumors of increased bandit 
activity in the area from other travelers and farmers. 
They complain that since the soldiers at Wolfpoint 
have been stationed elsewhere, the local sheriff 
has been unable to keep a lid on highway crime. 
Many believe that a group of bandits called the 
Steel Circle has taken over Wolfpoint, but others 
insist that something more sinister now occupies 
the garrison. These people claim to have seen 
goblins within the palisade walls, lighting fires and 
preparing for another war. If pressed, they describe 
small figures with pointy ears that bear only a 
passing resemblance to goblins. In reality, the Steel 
Circle did attempt to make Wolfpoint a new semi-
