THE STEEL CIRCLE
The PCs might want to learn a little 
more about the Steel Circle before 
heading to Wolfpoint. A PC who 
succeeds at a DC 18 Society check or 
DC 16 Underworld Lore check to Recall 
Knowledge has heard of the bandit gang. 
They are a fairly large and organized 
group of thieves and robbers who operate 
throughout southern Isger. These bandits 
rove about the countryside, not staying in 
a single location long enough for law enforcement to 
track them down. On a critical success, the PC knows 
the type of places—hillside caves, hidden crevices, and 
abandoned farmhouses—the Steel Circle likes to camp 
in, gaining the result of a successful check to Gather 
Information noted below.
A PC who succeeds at a DC 18 Diplomacy check 
to Gather Information learns that the Steel Circle is 
currently camped out in an abandoned farm a mile 
southeast of Wolfpoint. On a critical success, the PC 
also hears that the bandits tried to set up in Wolfpoint, 
but something drove them off.
If the PCs approach the farm, they are spotted 
by well-hidden lookouts, who warn the Steel Circle 
leaders. Several armed bandits go out to meet the PCs 
in the middle of the fallow fields. They are led by Runa 
Bloodhammer (wary female dwarf bandit 4), whose 
first order of business is to let the PCs know that if 
they try anything against her or her people, they’ll be 
dead within seconds. The PCs are outnumbered here, 
sensing a dozen more sets of eyes upon them from the 
nearby barn and farmhouse.
Runa begins the encounter as unfriendly, though a 
PC can change her attitude with a successful DC 17 
Diplomacy check to Make an Impression. If a PC has 
a skill feat that allows them to Make an Impression 
on several people at once (such as Group Impression), 
they gain a +1 circumstance bonus to skill checks to 
change Runa’s attitude. If the PCs have 6 or more 
Reputation Points, they gain a +2 circumstance bonus 
to skill checks to change Runa’s attitude, as the Steel 
Circle are no friends of Cheliax.
Runa is willing to talk with the PCs long enough 
for them to attempt three checks to sway her. She 
asks them their business in the area and tries to 
gauge their feelings about breaking the law without 
broaching the subject directly. If the PCs increase 
Runa’s attitude to friendly, she admits that her gang 
did spend one night camped inside Wolfpoint, but 
they had terrible nightmares. While the bandits are 
hardened criminals, they were too frightened to 
remain in the garrison and set up on this farm. 
Runa snaps her fingers and proposes that if 
the PCs investigate Wolfpoint and remove 
any “curse or creature befouling the 
place,” she’ll have the Steel Circle 
help the Hellbreakers as best 
they can. If Runa’s attitude is 
helpful, she’ll also agree to donate 
some supplies to the effort.
If Runa’s attitude becomes hostile, she 
gives a sharp gesture to her fellow bandits 
and storms off. A volley of arrows rains 
down on the PCs, dealing 2d8+13 piercing damage 
to each of them with a DC 20 basic Reflex save. If 
Runa’s attitude is only indifferent or unfriendly after 
the PCs attempt three checks, she curtly tells the PCs 
to go away, warning them to not approach the farm 
again. If the PCs refuse to leave or later try to return, 
they suffer the bandits’ wrath as if Runa’s attitude is 
hostile.
Reward: For changing Runa’s attitude to friendly or 
helpful, award the PCs 30 XP.
WOLFPOINT PALISADE
LOW 2 AND MODERATE 2
When the PCs explore Wolfpoint, they find it devoid 
of life. It’s been abandoned for several weeks at most, 
but not even mice or stray wolves have attempted to 
reclaim the buildings. Living creatures just seem to 
avoid the place. This is the result of the influence of a 
drude, a shadowy fey creature whose mere presence in 
the area can invoke terrible nightmares. This particular 
drude is drawn to areas where calamity has occurred 
and uses imagery of those events in the dreams they 
cause. The drude is accompanied by several gremlins 
who delight in the chaos.
If the PCs set up camp here, their sleep is plagued 
with nightmares of bloodthirsty goblin hordes 
attacking their position, stabbing and biting them 
with sharp dogslicers and even sharper teeth. A PC 
on watch hears strange noises by the palisade like 
squawking cries and moans. This encounter takes 
place in the middle of the night, in darkness. Sleeping 
PCs likely don’t have torches or other light sources 
lit, so begin this encounter with them extinguished. 
Use the Wolfpoint Palisades map on page 32 for this 
encounter.
Creatures: A small pack of pugwampi gremlins 
have allied with the drude haunting Wolfpoint. They 
attempt to draw any PCs still awake in the night to 
Runa Bloodhammer

many of the residents feel a fair amount of goodwill 
toward Cheliax. When you attempt a flat check if the 
PCs openly discuss their allegiance to the Hellbreakers 
League (page 29), roll twice and take the worse result.
 A bustling town of several hundred people, Vordia doesn’t 
look much different from any other small settlement in the 
Isgeri countryside. The one detail that makes it stand out 
is the dozens of flags bearing either the national symbol 
of Cheliax or the religious symbol of Asmodeus flying atop 
nearly every building or from nearly every window. Despite 
this (or perhaps because of it), the residents look happy as 
they go about their day.
The town decorations should hint to the players 
that they need to keep a low profile here. They might 
not want to stay long, but it’s their mission to at least 
try to quietly sway the populace. It will benefit them to 
listen and observe to see if the residents have any issues 
with the Chelaxian government that could be a crack 
in the pleasantly maintained facade. If they spend time 
Gathering Information (DC 16), they quickly learn 
that most townspeople are concerned about the nuns 
who run the Bright Embers Orphanage. Ever since the 
town was visited by a strange Hellknight a few weeks 
ago, the nuns haven’t been seen much.
 If the PCs want to learn more about this occurrence, 
one of them must attempt a DC 16 Diplomacy check 
to Gather Information or a DC 14 Scribing Lore or 
Society check to look into the town’s public records. 
On a successful Diplomacy check, the PC learns 
that two nights ago, a group of local teens dared 
one another to sneak into the seemingly abandoned 
orphanage and were frightened off by strange noises 
coming from the second floor. On a successful Scribing 
Lore or Society check, the PC finds very recent records 
of Bright Embers’ two current orphan charges both 
finding families in neighboring towns the day after the 
Hellknight’s visit, but the names of these families are 
oddly unreadable. By simply asking around, the PCs 
learn the location of the orphanage and that it is run 
by the Sisterhood of the Golden Erinys, for whom the 
villagers have nothing but kind words.
GAINING REPUTATION POINTS
While the PCs are in Vordia, they can attempt to gain 
Reputation Points to bolster local opinion about the 
Hellbreakers League. They can, of course, use the 
organization’s name, as long as they don’t give away 
the fact that they are allied with it. With clever or fiery 
rhetoric, cautionary tales about the “true” Cheliax, or 
explanations of the good the League has accomplished, 
a PC can attempt a DC 18 Deception, Diplomacy, 
Performance, or Society check. If the PCs disparage 
the Sisterhood of the Golden Erinys without proof, 
they take a –1 circumstance penalty to this check. Use 
the same degrees of success for Countryside Travel 
(page 30).
D. BRIGHT EMBERS ORPHANAGE
The Sisterhood of the Golden Erinys ran the Bright 
Embers Orphanage for nearly two decades, starting 
by taking in orphans of the Goblinblood Wars and 
preparing them to live in a country governed by the 
rule of Asmodeus. This entailed teaching the children 
pro-Cheliax propaganda and attempting to instill 
a respect for law and order by emphasizing that the 
chaos loved by goblinkind got their parents killed, 
conveniently not mentioning that many of the war’s 
hobgoblin commanders could be as strict as some 
Hellknight orders.
This constant emotional barrage on the children’s 
minds over the years has left a psychic imprint on the 
building, causing unusual phenomena to occur within. 
Former residents have spoken about seeing doors 
slamming from across the room, hearing agonized 
cries of terror coming from the walls, feeling like 
someone unseen is watching, and so on. The Sisters 
would explain these occurrences as pranks or wild 
imaginings, and their iron will stopped the orphanage 
from becoming fully haunted. That ended with the 
arrival of Viro Ahala.
When Viro convinced Sister Endreah to help him 
with his plan, her fellow nuns went with her, leaving 
the orphanage with no staff. With no more nuns 
in Bright Embers to suppress the building’s occult 
resonance, a handful of unstable spirits have formed 
from the emotional fallout of the past decades.
As the orphanage is the only lead the PCs have to 
how the Sisters of the Golden Erinys in Vordia are 
connected to the mystery Hellknight, they’ll need 
to explore the building to find out more. If the PCs 
heard the story of the local teens, their curiosity might 
be piqued. Entering the haunted orphanage isn’t 
necessary to further the League’s reputation in Vordia, 
but they might want to return once they start hearing 
about how the strange occurrences in other villages 
might be related to the sisterhood.

town. When the PCs approach the building, read or 
paraphrase the following.
A walled yard surrounds a rectangular two-story building

D2. Entry Hall
A wide hall runs through the building. The floor is scuffed, 
and all the interior doors hang crookedly from their hinges. 
A wide staircase leads up to the second floor.
Similar to the deterioration of the front yard, the 
unkempt state of the building has been hastened by 
the now-rampant spiritual energy. The PCs hear 
footsteps all around them as if children were still 
running around. Through the open doors, the party 
can see a dining hall and kitchen to the east and a 
recreation room to the west.
D3. Dining Hall	
Trivial 2
This room features two table sets, one a bit smaller than 
the other, with accompanying small chairs to accommodate 
children. While the larger table has nothing on it, the 
smaller table is set with four plates but no utensils.
Hazard: The strict discipline of the sisterhood meant 
that meals were sedate affairs where no orphan was 
permitted to act up. This repression steeped into the 
furniture and is eager to be released now that the nuns 
have vacated. A spectral food fight breaks out when 
any creature gets close to the kids’ table (as marked 
on the map).

Faces that would normally be violent or gruesome in any

D5. Orphans’ Bedroom	
Severe 2
Two rows of small, decrepit beds line the walls of this room. 
Tattered blankets are neatly draped across the beds, and 
each bed has a small set of drawers next to it, many of 
which hang open and empty. A canine skull sits on one bed, 
next to a ratty stuffed bear.
There’s room for 12 orphans to sleep communally 
here. The orphanage hasn’t been at full capacity since 
the first few years after it was built, so often, two or 
three orphans would have this room to themselves. 
Thanks to the occult energy engulfing the building, it 
doesn’t look like anyone has slept here for years.
Hazard: The Sisters made sure that all orphans had 
the same bedtime, regardless of age. Older children 
would sometimes lie in their beds in the dark, thinking 
about new families or soothing the younger orphans 
to sleep. This unique flavor of quiet despair created 
this darkness-inducing haunt.
Creatures: The general tenor of the psychic energy in 
the orphanage has created an undead creature usually 
associated with forgotten and forlorn children, known 
as an attic whisperer. When the haunt rolls initiative, 
the canine skull on one of the beds rises up to attach 
to the rotting teddy bear. The creature is wrapped in 
a tattered sheet and begins echoing the cries of many 
of the orphans who have since grown up. This attic 
whisperer fights until destroyed.

Several sparse rooms line the hallway here, each containing 
nothing more than a simple wooden cot and a padded beam 
that is only a few inches off the ground. A red pentagram is 
painted on each wall above the beam.
These are the personal rooms of the sisters who 
ran this orphanage, though they show little of any 
inhabitants’ personality. A PC who succeeds at a DC 
13 Religion check to Recall Knowledge knows the red 
pentagram is the symbol of Asmodeus and that the 
nuns would use the beam to kneel in supplication for 
regular prayers to the Lord of Hell.
A PC who searches these rooms and succeeds at

parchment under one of the cots. It appears to be a 
draft of a letter to another sister in an unnamed town, 
explaining how these sisters are going to a place called 
the Lucent Mission for an important task that “will 
bring much glory to Asmodeus.” The final line 
explains that the recipient is being sent 
Bright Embers’ remaining orphans 
before ending in a large ink spill. 
If the PCs show the authorities 
this evidence, none of them know 
where the Lucent Mission is, but 
they thank the PCs for informing 
them of the true fate of the 
remaining orphans; the PCs gain 
1 Reputation Point.
Treasure: Left behind in one 
room is an unholy text about the 
worship of Asmodeus worth 50 gp and 
a neatly folded robes of the Erinys (page 212).
Umok
Umok was founded by gnomes several centuries 
ago as a peaceful haven for those looking to live in 
harmony with the nearby Chitterwood. Several times 
over the years, the gnome residents clashed with 
nearby goblin camps over local resources, namely 
game and wood. These conflicts came to an ugly 
head during the Goblinblood Wars, when hobgoblins 
tried to burn Umok to the ground. A visiting gnome 
champion of Cayden Cailean named Loriwyse 
Marblemug rallied the town to push back against the 
hobgoblin raiders, saving everyone. Since then, fire has 
been outlawed within 500 yards of Umok’s perimeter; 
the punishment is usually banishment, but some past 
goblin perpetrators have been executed.
The citizens of Umok use alchemy and magic to 
heat their food and light their town. They also employ 
domesticated woodland creatures to act as guards and 
lookouts in and around the town. If these animals see 
someone approaching with an open flame, they are 
trained to return to town to warn the gnomes in charge. 
Some of the larger creatures, such as wolves, try to scare 
off any such intruders, to varying degrees of success.
As the PCs approach Umok by road, they spot 
at about 500 yards from town a sign that reads in 
Common and Gnomish, “Now Entering the Umok 
Fire-Free Zone. Please Extinguish All Flames.” A 
cartoonish illustration of a fire with a big, black X 
across it has been painted underneath. Many such 
signs are around Umok, even in the surrounding 
woods. If the PCs haven’t already attempted a skill 
check to Recall Knowledge about the town, they 
might want to do so now to learn a little about the 
history behind this warning.

It is assumed that the PCs comply with the sign, 
though if they are traveling by day, they have no need 
of torches to light their way. If they don’t comply and 
approach the town carrying fire, a random PC spots a 
pair of rabbits bolting in Umok’s direction out of the 
corner of their eye. As a result of the rabbits’ warning, 
the PCs take a –2 circumstance penalty to their 
skill checks to influence the town’s people and gain 
Reputation Points, regardless of their current RP total.
When the PCs get within sight of the town, read or 
paraphrase the following.
A quaint town of cottages with peaked roofs and walls 
covered in ivy becomes visible, nestled between the 
woods and the hills. Orbs of light, twinkling in every 
color imaginable, hang in the air above each street corner. 
Smiling gnomes wave from porches and stoops, their 
clothing as brightly colored as the lights. Occasionally, a 
family of deer or a grumpy-looking badger wanders by, 
though the gnomes don’t find this at all unusual. Proud 
Isgeri boarhounds pant happily as they watch passersby, 
sometimes rolling onto their backs in hopes of a belly rub.
The town is welcome to outsiders, provided they aren’t 
carrying open flames. If the PCs discretely ask around, 
they learn that most Umok residents are neutral about 
Cheliax. The village is far enough away from most of 
Isger’s major sites that they are left to themselves. If they 
can help it, they’d rather not grab Cheliax’s attention 
with talk of rebellion. Most of the townspeople are 
more concerned about the rash of small fires that have 
been breaking out in the woods southwest of town over 
the past few weeks. Their animal-based early warning 
system has helped them ensure the fires haven’t spread, 
but they haven’t caught the perpetrator. The prevailing 
opinion around town is that goblins or hobgoblins are 
to blame. If any PC is of goblin or hobgoblin ancestry, 
the gnomes of Umok might unfairly treat them with 
suspicion.
The resident gnomes can point the PCs in the 
direction of these fires, but before they can leave town, 
there is a commotion: a badly burned goblin stumbles 
down the main street and collapses near the PCs.
A VICTIM OF HAPPENSTANCE
This unfortunate goblin is named Grizzo (hapless 
female goblin forager 1). She lives within the 
Chitterwood with her small family who aren’t a part of 
any major goblin settlement. They scrounge for berries 
and mushrooms and occasionally catch fish. Rarely do 
they interact with others outside of the forest. Grizzo 
was unknowingly rooting around the area of the 
woods near the previous fires and was attacked by the 
two hell hounds who were the fire’s cause (see below). 
She was burned by their hellfire breath but barely 
managed to escape, fleeing in the direction of town.
When Grizzo collapses in front of the PCs, she is 
unconscious with 0 Hit Points. A PC can Treat her 
Wounds, bandaging the burns and perhaps applying a 
topical salve, to help her regain consciousness. That PC 
can also attempt a DC 16 Medicine check, determining 
on a success that her burns were caused by a sustained 
direct blast of fire, perhaps from a magic spell or a 
creature that can breathe flames, rather than exposure 
to the flames of something like a forest fire.
Meanwhile, the other PCs see that gnomes are 
beginning to gather—at a safe distance—curious about 
Grizzo’s presence. Some of the gnomes begin to mutter 
accusations that she must be responsible for the recent 
fires. It isn’t too long before Ioan Marblemug (steadfast 
male gnome official 2), the town’s captain of the 
guard and descendant of Umok’s historical champion, 
approaches to assess the situation. He hears what his 
fellow citizens are saying but waits until it’s clear that 
Grizzo isn’t going to die before telling the PCs that 
“she’s got to go.” It’s clear that Ioan believes what the 
other gnomes believe about Grizzo. He explains that 
the punishment for violating Umok’s most important 
law is banishment.
When Grizzo regains consciousness, she begins 
blubbering in fear. A PC who succeeds at DC 17 
Diplomacy check calms her down enough for her to 
mutter the phrase “fire dog” over and over again. It is 
unfortunately not enough information for the PCs to 
be able to Recall Knowledge, but a PC can try to argue 
that Grizzo’s condition and her fear means that she 
likely didn’t set the fires. Getting Ioan to agree requires 
a DC 18 Diplomacy or Intimidation check or a DC 
16 Legal Lore check. On a success, Ioan begrudgingly 
allows Grizzo to remain with the town doctor while 
the PCs investigate the fires. If a PC critically fails this 
check, Ioan is adamant that Grizzo be taken out of 
Umok immediately and firmly suggests that the PCs be 
the ones to do so.
GAINING REPUTATION POINTS
While the PCs are in Umok, they can attempt to 
gain Reputation Points to bolster the townspeople’s 
opinions about the Hellbreakers League. With 
disparaging remarks about the strict order imposed 
by the Chelaxian government (and its Hellknight 
lackeys), rightful connections between devils and fire, 
or honest talk about the importance of freedom and 
nature, a PC can attempt a DC 18 Diplomacy, Nature, 
Performance, or Religion check. Use the same degrees 
of success for Countryside Travel (page 30).

FIRE!	
LOW 2
As the PCs enter the outskirts of the Chitterwood 
to investigate the fires, they spot a rising plume of 
smoke in the distance. Rushing in that direction, they 
are faced with the beginnings of a brush fire started 
by the hell hounds that could potentially be quite 
devastating. They’ll need to extinguish the flames 
before the situation grows out of control. If Grizzo 
is with the PCs, she cowers in fear of the flames and 
promptly passes out again.
This encounter uses a modified version of the 
Victory Point subsystem (GM Core 184), in which the 
PCs start with 5 Victory Points and must accumulate 
10 total Victory Points. At the end of each phase, 
after every PC has acted, they automatically lose 1 
Victory Point to represent the encroaching fire. If 
the PCs ever have 0 Victory Points, the fire can’t be 
contained (see failure below).
To put out a portion of the fire, a PC can attempt 
a DC 15 Forest Lore or DC 17 Nature or Survival 
check, gaining 1 Victory Point on a success (or 2 on a 
critical success, but losing 1 Victory Point on a critical 
failure). A spell or ability that creates at least 1 gallon 
of water automatically grants 1 Victory Point. Other 
abilities that control fire or starve a fire of oxygen can 
do the same at your discretion. A PC can also attempt 
a DC 18 Athletics check to dig part of a trench to act 
as a firebreak; successfully doing so doesn’t gain a 
Victory Point but might stop the fire from spreading. 
At the end of a phase in which a PC successfully does 
this, attempt a DC 15 flat check. On a success, the 
PCs don’t lose 1 Victory Point from the fire. If two or 
more PCs create a firebreak in the same phase, reduce 
the DC of the flat check to 11.
Success: The PCs put out the fire before it causes 
too much damage. The gnomes are grateful and the 
PCs earn 1 Reputation Point.
Failure: The fire rages out of control. Each PC 
takes 4d6 fire damage (DC 16 basic Reflex save) as 
they flee the scene. Eventually, the citizens of Umok 
and their animal friends are able to rally to put out 
the fire before it reaches town. The hell hounds are 
emboldened by the flames and gain a +2 circumstance 
bonus to their initiative rolls in the charred wood 
(page 39), and the PCs take a –1 circumstance bonus 
to skill checks to gain Reputation Points in Umok.

CHARRED WOOD	
MODERATE 2
A PC trained in Nature or Survival can trace the 
recent fire to its source, an area of the forest that 
has been almost completely turned to ash. Several 
days ago, Viro Ahala and some Sisters of the Golden 
Erinys performed a lesser version of the ritual he is 
attempting in Chapter 3, summoning a pair of hell 
hounds that has stalked the woods since. Use the 
Charred Wood map on page 38 for this encounter.
The trees have been burned down to stumps, and the 
ground is covered in charred grass in a circular area of 
the woods about one hundred feet in diameter. The heat 
has long since dissipated, but the smell of smoke remains.
Creatures: Two hell hounds, weak from their 
relatively recent summoning, consider this circle their 
lair in the mortal Universe and range out from here 
to start fires in the woods. The fiendish beasts attack 
the PCs as soon as they enter the area and fight until 
killed. If Grizzo is with the PCs, she confirms that 
these are the creatures who attacked her before she 
hides behind a burned stump.
WEAK HELL HOUNDS (2)	
CREATURE 2
Pathfinder Monster Core 7, 194
Initiative Perception +7
Presenting Evidence: If the PCs show the bodies 
of the hell hounds to Ioan Marblemug, he convinces 
the rest of Umok that the threat has been handled. 
This exonerates Grizzo, who is grateful to the PCs for 
their help. The PCs gain 1 Reputation Point. Grizzo 
is allowed to recuperate in Umok for a few more 
days before returning to her goblin friends in the 
Chitterwood. Alternatively, the PCs can bring Grizzo 
with them to Stumpfield if they haven’t yet been to 
that location.
Treasure: For solving the mystery of the Umok 
fires, Ioan Marblemug gives the PCs a pair of bracers 
of missile deflection that has been in his family for 
generations, as well as 10 gp.
Stumpfield
Before the Goblinblood Wars, the Chitterwood was 
several dozen acres larger than it is today. Those 
missing trees were either cut down or burned by the 
Isgeri military to deprive the attacking goblins of 
their homes. The ancient forest is slowly beginning 
to reclaim this land, but it will be decades or even 
a century before the new trees mature and it comes 
close to its previous size.
One section of the northern edge of the forest was 
cut down to provide lumber to expand the burgeoning 
town of Fernsby. Recently, the remaining field of 
stumps has become the home of a collective of artists 
of both human and goblin ancestries.
This artist’s colony was established by Erk 
Oilfingers (visionary male goblin painter 1) and Jett 
Saldath (focused nonbinary human sculptor 1) after 
they met and formed a fast friendship trying to capture 
the image of the same twisted tree in their respective 
mediums. By inviting artists of all kinds to live and 
work in their new town, the two hoped it would foster 
better relations between their two ancestries. They 
have yet to change the world, or even the country, 
but in the 18 months since Stumpfield was founded, 
it has built a fascinating and supportive community. 
However, there has been some friction with the 
neighboring conservative town of Fernsby, which has 
been inflamed by the actions of the gobmob snake 
Hissbite and their lackeys (page 40).
When the PCs approach Stumpfield, read or 
paraphrase the following.
The town ahead is a unique collection of homes built 
onto the sides of wagons and semi-permanent tents, 
creating an atmosphere more like a traveling festival 
than a structured settlement. Several dozen residents—
all either goblin or human—are gathered in the center 
of town around an object made of rope and wicker that 
resembles a four-legged animal. In turn, each person 
approaches the sculpture and adds something to it: a 
lump of clay to form an ear, several splashes of paint 
along the hide, or a series of colorful scarves wrapped 
around the neck. After each addition, the others 
gathered murmur in delight and approval.
The PCs arrive during Stumpfield’s monthly 
practice of “cooperative art,” where the whole town 
comes together to create something—usually a 
sculpture or a painting, but other mediums are often 
involved. A few finished cooperative art pieces can 
be found throughout the town, and each is similarly 
chaotic but nonetheless compelling. When the PCs 
make themselves known, Erk breaks off from the 
assembled townspeople, introduces himself, and 
welcomes the PCs to town. He then introduces the 
party to the other artists and says, “Since we have 
guests, let’s see if they have anything they want to 
add to this month’s collective piece…” The crowd 
nods in agreement and a few of them even clap in 
encouragement.

===== Page 41 =====
40
Each of the PCs can add something to the 
sculpture, whether from their own supplies or from 
the collections of art supplies strewn about the town 
center. When they do so, they should attempt a DC 
16 Art Lore or Performance check; you can allow 
for other skills if the players make good cases for 
them. On a failure, the Stumpfield artists show only 
mild appreciation, but on a success, a few of them 
smile and say something like “Of course, just what 
it needed!” On a critical success, the townspeople 
give a hearty cheer. If at least one character succeeds, 
the PCs gain a +1 circumstance bonus to gaining RP 
in Stumpfield (+2 circumstance bonus if at least one 
character critically succeeded).
Over the next hour, the town finishes the sculpture 
and then celebrates into the night. The PCs can meet 
as many of the artists as they like, including Jett, 
Stumpfield’s other founder. They share a bottle of wine 
with the PCs, and someone cooks a passable stew in a 
large cauldron that the whole town partakes of, with 
a random assortment of ingredients being thrown in. 
If the PCs discuss recent events in Isger (such as the 
Battle of Hellknight Hill) with anyone or ask about 
their opinion of Cheliax, most townspeople aren’t 
overly concerned. A few want to show the PCs their 
latest piece of art that expresses their views on the 
subject, but overall the artists don’t want to worry 
about the “outside world.”
However, later in the evening, Erk and Jett pull 
the PCs aside to explain a small problem the town 
is having. People are being attacked in the nearby 
town of Fernsby, and the perpetrators are rumored 
to be several goblins. Jett nervously explains that the 
villagers of Fernsby are convinced that Stumpfield is 
involved in these attacks and are threatening to stop 
selling them food and other goods. Erk insists that no 
Stumpfield goblins are as violent as Fernsby claims. 
The two ask the PCs, as a neutral party, to talk to the 
people of Fernsby and convince them not to cut off 
trade with Stumpfield.
Any Stumpfield resident can point the PCs in the 
direction of Fernsby, which is an uneventful 2-hour 
walk to the northeast.
GAINING REPUTATION POINTS
While the PCs are in Stumpfield, they can attempt to 
gain Reputation Points to bolster the artists’ opinions 
about the Hellbreakers League. With compliments 
of residents’ art, discussions of Chelaxian art and 
architectural styles, or an interpretive dance about the 
evils of imperialism, a PC can attempt a DC 18 Art 
Lore, Diplomacy, Performance, or Society check. Use 
the same rules as Countryside Travel (page 30).
E. FERNSBY
Farms and orchards surround this quaint village. Thatched-
roof cottages line the streets within the settlement proper, 
many with porches decorated with pots of flowers. In the 
center of town, a large oak tree grows in a small village 
green that has several benches. A few of the flowerbeds 
and shrubs on the green show recent signs of being 
unceremoniously dug up and destroyed.
The people of Fernsby are polite but standoffish 
toward strangers, including the PCs. If the PCs ask 
around about the recent attacks, they learn that the 
stories have been blown a little out of proportion. No 
one has been attacked, but vandals have defaced the 
village green time and again over the past two weeks. 
Many residents are fervent about the fact that the space 
is Fernsby’s pride and joy. A PC who succeeds at a DC 
15 Diplomacy check to Gather Information learns that 
a few people are convinced they saw goblins on the 
green the same nights as each incident.
If a PC inspects the latest desecration of the flowers 
and shrubs and succeeds at a DC 17 Perception or 
Survival check, they don’t spot any footprints—goblin 
or otherwise—in the churned up dirt, only a series of 
sinuous impressions. On a critical success, they also 
find a torn leaf with two identical punctures in it, as 
if from a set of fangs. With this information, a PC 
who succeeds at DC 16 Nature check can deduce that 
several large snakes recently made their way across 
the grass. No one in Fernsby has seen these snakes or 
understands why they would have snakes coming into 
their town and not attacking any people or animals.
A PC who succeeds at a DC 18 Diplomacy or 
Society check is approached by a resident named Lilli 
who tells them that during a recent walk through the 
woods, she heard a strange hissing coming up from a 
ravine. Lilli can give the PCs directions to this ravine 
(area E1). Alternatively, a PC who succeeds at a DC 18 
Survival check to Track can spot enough impressions 
to follow them to the same ravine. The PCs can also 
wait until nightfall to see if the snakes return; if they 
do so, each PC should attempt a DC 16 Stealth check 
to Hide. If more than half of them succeed, they can 
catch the goblin snakes from area E1 unaware in the 
village green (if a map is needed, one of a field or 
clearing works well). If half of them fail, the goblin 
snakes spot them and flee back to area E1, but the PCs 
can easily give chase to encounter them in the ravine.

E2. Sheltered Overhang	
Severe 2
A stone outcropping hangs over the mouth of the ravine, 
shading it from the sun and making it difficult to spot from 
the surface. A small pool of brackish rainwater occupies 
the far end of the ravine, surrounded by a dozen skeletons 
of rats, rabbits, and other small wildlife.
The walls of the ravine are 20 feet high here, and 
the area is in dim light, thanks to the shadow cast by 
the rocky overhang. The pool of water is only a few 
inches deep and looks stagnant. If anyone dares drink 
the water, it tastes foul and musty.
Creatures: When the PCs arrive, Hissbite knows 
that their plans have been foiled and immediately 
attacks. Hissbite keeps a pair of venomous vipers as 
pets, and the loyal snakes defend Hissbite to the death. 
The gobmob snake fights until reduced to 10 or fewer 
Hit Points, at which point they surrender. If the PCs 
allow them to live, Hissbite whines an apology 
for their actions and promises never to trouble 
anyone again. If the PCs haven’t yet been to 
Umok, Hissbite warns about some “real bad 
dogs” in that area.

Development: The PCs likely kill at least one goblin

Stumpfield gift the PCs a lesser healing potion.
A Repentant Sister
After Vordia’s Sisters of the Golden Erinys agreed to 
help Viro Ahala and took up residence in the Lucent 
Mission to uncover its secrets, one of them began to 
have doubts about the supposed Hellknight. Sister 
Sylve (inquisitive female human novitiate 1) kept a 
close eye on Viro as he scoured the mission’s archives, 
suspecting that he was an impostor who had not 
actually gone through the full Hellknight initiation 
ceremony. A few cleverly worded questions later, her 
suspicions were confirmed. However, before she could 
approach her superior, Sister Endreah, with proof, Viro 
found the ritual he was looking for and set back out 
into Isger to find the perfect place to enact it. Realizing 
she couldn’t confront him through proper channels, 
Sylve also slipped out of the mission to follow him, but 
was unable to pick up his trail. She’s been looking for 
other ways to deal with him since then.
When the PCs reach 10 Reputation Points for the 
first time, Sister Sylve hears of their activities in the 
Fernsby Evidence

===== Page 43 =====
42
area and seeks them out. She approaches them as 
they’re traveling or as they’re recuperating in their 
latest location for at least a day. Read or paraphrase 
the following.
A young woman wearing a red habit emblazoned with the 
symbol of a five-pointed star in golden thread approaches. 
From her posture, she seems like a tense coil ready to 
spring, but her face is devoid of any emotion. She holds up 
a hand in greeting, revealing a missing ring finger.
“Pardon me, I don’t wish to alarm,” she says. “My name 
is Sister Sylve of the Golden Erinys. Perhaps you’ve heard 
of our order? I’m aware that you may think of us as the 
enemy in your campaign to ‘free Isger,’ but you must listen 
to me. There is a dissembler named Viro Ahala falsely 
calling himself a Hellknight who has deceived my sisters. 
He took advantage of our resources to find a ritual that 
will summon a powerful devil to heed his ambitions, and I 
do not wish to see any more orphans created as the result 
of this. Unfortunately, I do not know where he intends to 
perform this ritual. My superior, Sister Endreah, might, but 
I am afraid she no longer trusts me, as she’s wholly placed 
her faith in this impostor. As much as it pains me to say, I 
think you can extract that information from her.”
Sister Sylve tells the PCs the location of the Lucent 
Mission in the Aspodell Mountains and how many 
of her sisters remain there. She asks them to not kill 
anyone, but warns them that the sisters will fight back 
against intruders. If the PCs have exorcised Bright 
Embers Orphanage, Sister Sylve plans to return there 
and reopen it.
F. LUCENT MISSION
The Lucent Mission is a small Sisterhood of the Golden 
Erinys monastery in the foothills of the northwest 
Aspodell Mountains. Various orders of the sisterhood 
use it over the course of the year, training novitiates 
before sending them to their posts in Isgeri towns. The 
building also contains an archive of Asmodean texts 
that the sisterhood has collected over the decades. It’s 
here that Viro Ahala, with the help of Sister Endreah, 
discovered the ritual he believes will grant him the 
power needed to enact his revenge.
With directions from Sister Sylve, the PCs are able 
to find the hidden trail that leads up the hills to the 
Lucent Mission. The trailhead is about half a day from 
Vordia, and ascending the path takes a few more hours. 
If the PCs left Vordia at dawn, it’s likely sunset or

F1. Mountain Trail
A rough dirt path winds up through the hills at the 
outskirts of the Aspodell Mountains. Boulders flank the 
trail, providing an obstructed view of the building ahead.
If the PCs are quiet, they can set up a small camp 
here and rest overnight without being spotted by the 
sisterhood. The sisters have no reason to patrol and do 
not fear intruders.
F2. Mission Garden	
Low 2
A low stone fence encircles a small garden in front of the 
wooden building. Two trellises are entwined with grapes 
and a few bushes bloom with autumn flowers. A pentagram 
is emblazoned in the wood above the double doors leading 
inside.
As part of their training, new sisters are tasked with 
tending this garden. The fruit and flowers here are used 
in the mission’s cooking, usually bland and simple fare. 
The grapes growing on the vines are small and bitter.
Creatures: Regardless of the time of day, two 
novitiates are here, pruning the bushes or pulling 
weeds. If the sun has already set, they do so by lantern 
light. Those not of the sisterhood are usually not 
allowed at the mission, so the novitiates attack when 
they see the PCs.

F3. Entry
This simple entryway is decorated only with a carved 
wooden plaque above the eastern door that reads “Praise 
the Bright King of Hell.”
Sisters are expected to genuflect below the plaque 
before entering the mission proper. A PC who succeeds 
at a DC 12 Religion check recognizes the plaque is 
referring to Asmodeus.
F4. Temple
Three pews occupy the space in front of an impressive 
pulpit. A massive pentagram has been neatly burned into 
the wood on the eastern wall. A hallway leads north at the 
western end of the room, while there is a door a few feet 
away in the same wall.
The sisters gather here for worship on a nightly 
basis, murmuring quiet prayers in Asmodeus’ name. 
Occasionally, the highest-ranking sister present will 
give a sermon at the pulpit, which is decorated in a 
style similar to most Chelaxian architecture.
Treasure: Among the unholy scripture found on 
the pulp, a PC who succeeds at a DC 20 Perception 
check finds a secret panel, behind which is an ebony 
statuette of Asmodeus worth 40 gp and +1 handwraps 
of mighty blows.
F5. Sisters’ Quarters
Eight identical rooms line the hall here, each containing 
a simple cot and a footlocker for the occupant’s meager 
personal belongings. The sisters don’t often stay long 
here, so the rooms contain no personal decorations.
Treasure: One footlocker contains a +1 bo staff. 
Another contains 13 gp in a leather pouch.
F6. Dining Room
At first glance, this is an unassuming dining room with a 
large table surrounded by six chairs. However, that notion 
is dispelled by the intricate scrollwork on the walls near 
the ceiling depicting hundreds of cavorting devils. There 
is a door leading further north and another leading east.
When the PCs enter this room, they hear the 
shattering of crockery and a string of curses in Diabolic

F7. Scullery 	
Moderate 2
A steel basin and an iron stove stand against the northern 
wall. A round table bears the scars and stains of hundreds 
of meal preparations. Two closed barrels occupy different 
corners.
This is the mission’s simple kitchen, where the 
sisters prepare meals for anyone staying here. One 
barrel contains fresh water, while the other contains 
ground wheat for making bread and gruel.
Creatures: Sometimes, a sister tasked with cleaning 
up after a meal will “borrow” a tome from the archive 
to summon low-level devils to perform the drudge 
work. Currently, two orts stand by the sink, scrubbing 
plates and pots, while one sister watches over them and 
keeps them on task. A small pile of broken crockery 
near the sink is the result of a clumsy ort. The sister 
orders the orts to kill the intruders, though she isn’t 
above engaging in combat herself.

F9. Mission Archive
Severe 2
Bookshelves line the eastern and western 
walls of this stuffy room filled with books and 
archived letters. A large, imposing desk made 
from ebony wood faces the only door.
The sisterhood keeps much of its most valuable 
information here in the Lucent Mission’s archive. The 
tomes and documents on the shelves are mainly texts on 
the worship of Asmodeus, treatises on the hierarchies of 
devils in Hell, and illustrated primers on various martial 
disciplines. Viro Ahala was able to discover a rare ritual

that could aid Cheliax in retaining its hold on 
Isger. She assumes the PCs are affiliated with the

Viro isn’t a real Hellknight, giving the PCs a chance to 
Demoralize her. If Sister Endreah is reduced to fewer 
than 6 Hit Points and the velavi has been defeated, she 
begrudgingly surrenders.

After investigating the Lucent Mission of the Sisterhood 
of the Golden Erinys, the PCs have learned that the false 
Hellknight Viro Ahala is planning to conduct a ritual 
somewhere in the eastern Chitterwood that could spell 
big trouble for Isger. Unfortunately, they don’t know his 
exact location, and time could be running short!
If the PCs haven’t visited the four locations in central 
Isger that they’ve been asked to help out and still need 
more XP to reach level 3, they can aid those places now. 
There is no ticking clock for Viro’s ritual, and gaining 
more Reputation Points could help the PCs leverage 
these new connections for more information. They can 
also return to Saringallow to rest, resupply, and ask 
for advice. If they do so, Rhokrag suggests they revisit 
areas near the Chitterwood (Stumpfield or Umok, for 
instance) to ask around if anyone has seen anything 
suspicious in the woods. This could be a chance for the 
PCs to gain Reputation Points in those towns if they 
haven’t already (see pages 36 and 39).
To Gather Information about Viro’s plot in 
Stumpfield or Umok, the PCs must succeed at a DC 20 
Diplomacy check. If they have at least 8 Reputation 
Points, they gain a +1 circumstance bonus to this check; 
if they have at least 12 Reputation Points, this bonus 
increases to +2. On a success, they pick up on rumors 
spread by local farmers and foresters of recently seeing 
“a figure clad in black armor” stalking through the 
woods. If a PC presses an eyewitness, they learn more 
details that confirm that the armor this figure wore is 
similar to the iconic Hellknight full plate. By following 
up on this lead, the PCs gain a +1 circumstance bonus 
to the Survival check to navigate the Chitterwood; 
if their Diplomacy check was a critical success, this 
bonus increases to +2.

Alternatively, the PCs can head directly to the

Into the Chitterwood
Despite many of the trees being cut or burned down along 
the outskirts in the aftermath of the Goblinblood Wars, 
the Chitterwood is still an imposing old-growth forest. Any 
signs of the central Isgeri farmlands are swallowed by the 
surrounding trees within only a few minutes after entering. 
The forest canopy overhead blocks much of the day’s light. 
The sounds of wildlife can be heard all around: chirping 
birds, rustling underbrush, and snapping twigs as animals 
pass by.
There are no roads into the Chitterwood, only a few 
sparse game trails widened by hunters and foresters that 
penetrate only a mile into the forest. The native goblin 
populations tend to keep to themselves, ranging only 
short distances from their caves and small villages to 
forage, which has very little impact on the surrounding 
terrain. As the PCs begin exploring the Chitterwood, 
either trying to find the spots where people mentioned 
seeing a figure in armor or searching for other signs 
of Viro, one of them should attempt a DC 20 Survival 
check to Track. On a success, after about an hour, that 
PC spots what could be heavy boot prints in the dirt; 
on a critical success, they can tell the tracks are about 
a week old. Following the prints leads them to a large 
stump that appears to have a few extinguished candle 
stubs near it. On a failure, the PCs stumble around the 
woods for a few hours and accidentally come across 
this same scene, but the devils by the stump gain a +2 
circumstance bonus to their initiative checks.
DEVILS ON THE LOOSE	
MODERATE 3
A petrified stump is the only remnant of what must have 
once been a towering tree. The brush around it has been 
cleared away, and several ritualistic candles and shards of 
crystal have been discarded by a crack in the stump that 
leads to a small underground hollow.
Approximately a week earlier, Viro Ahala and 
several other Hellknight armigers who survived the 
battle at Breachill found this stump and thought it a 
good place to practice the ritual. A PC who succeeds 
at a DC 18 Perception or Survival check discovers 
the presence of several sets of boot prints in the dirt, 
but they are unfortunately too obscured for the PC 
to deduce where the group went after moving about 
this space. If the PCs fear that they’ve missed their 
opportunity to thwart Viro, a PC who succeeds at a 
DC 16 Arcana, Occultism, or Religion check discerns 
that the magical energy lingering near this stump is the 
result of a much smaller ritual.
The PCs enter this area from the northwest. 
Because of the tree cover, this area is cast in dim light 
during the day. Use the Ritual Stump map on page 48 
for this encounter.
Creatures: Viro’s practice ritual was successful and 
summoned a small group of drudge devils that Viro 
bound to this stump. He hopes that any havoc they 
cause will be enough of a distraction to keep anyone 
hunting him (including the Hellbreakers League) busy. 
One of the four orts was empowered by the ritual to 
be a little stronger than the others, and its enhanced 
presence bolsters the group. The orts emerge from the 
hollow under the stump when the PCs approach and 
fight until destroyed, as stipulated by Viro’s orders.

THORNGRIP LOOKSEE PARTY
Once a week, the goblins of Thorngrip (see sidebar on 
page 50) put together a Looksee Party to scout around 
the town for a full day and determine whether there are 
any threats to their safety. In recent years, each Looksee 
Party has usually been led by Zagnub (cheerful nonbinary 
goblin scout 2), a trusted and well-liked member of 
the community. Zagnub enjoys the responsibility and 
keeps copious mental notes about what they see, hear, 
and smell. Recently, one of Zagnub’s Looksee Parties 
spotted Viro and his entourage and reported it back to

Thorngrip’s ruling council. Since then, the goblins have

make their way through the Chitterwood and waits to 
see what they do before confronting them.
When the PCs slay the last of the orts at the stump, 
they slowly begin to feel that they are being watched 
from the surrounding trees. A PC who succeeds at a 
DC 21 Perception check notices at least six sets of red 
eyes peering at them from the tree line to the south. 
That PC has enough time to warn their allies before a 
tall goblin steps out from the underbrush, their hands 
spread wide and away from their weapons.
Though the tall goblin is smiling and deliberately unarmed, 
their razor-sharp teeth somewhat undercut their message 
of peace. “Relax, longshanks,” they say in accented 
Common. “If we wanted to kill you, we would’ve done so. I 
be Zagnub of the Thorngrip goblins.” They gesture toward 
the steaming piles of goo that were once devils. “Devils no 
friends of yours, yes?”
The PCs immediately get the impression that the 
answer to this question is the difference between 
fighting and friendship. This adventure assumes that 
the PCs answer in the positive and perhaps even tell 
Zagnub they are looking for more devils and their 
allies to slay; with a delighted chuckle, Zagnub 
gestures for the PCs to follow them.
If the PCs lie or attempt to intimidate the goblins, 
they lose 1 Reputation Point, and the goblins hiding in 
the trees fire a volley of arrows at them before Zagnub 
disappears back into the woods. Each PC takes 2d6+4 
piercing damage (DC 18 basic Reflex save), and the 
goblins are unfriendly toward them. That said, the PCs 
can still Track the Looksee Party to Thorngrip and 
proceed to Thorngrip Pariahs (page 50).

underbrush, occasionally climbing partially up a tree 
to swing from one branch to another. If the PCs lag 
a little behind, Zagnub stops the party and waits for 
them to catch up, eagerly waving them forward. Each 
PC can attempt a DC 17 Athletics, Nature, or Survival

On the other side of the thorn wall is a bustling goblin 
town centered around the sequoia. Most of the buildings 
are small, wooden huts with thatched roofs, and a few of 
them have been built attached to the trunk of the large 
tree, with ladders and ramps leading up to them. This line

Several residents greet the returning Looksee Party, 
and some of the younger goblins stop to stare at the 
newcomers. Their parents gently guide them away, a 
few with worried looks on their own faces. “Welcome to 
Thorngrip,” says Zagnub.
Zagnub ushers the PCs through the town toward 
the base of the sequoia, where a large shrine has been 
carved into the wood. Many goblin faces have been

Brakknap (haunted male goblin oracle 4) is 
Thorngrip’s founder and often speaks with the spirits of 
goblins past to help guide the town. Brakknap has a long 
and troubled history that can be found on page 236, but 
despite the pain some humans have inflicted on him, he 
would like to see the two ancestries living in harmony. 
The goblin ancestor spirits have been perturbed lately 
by what Viro Ahala has been doing in the Chitterwood, 
but Brakknap believes that Thorngrip doesn’t have 
the strength to stop him alone, so he’s asked Zagnub’s 
Looksee Parties to be watchful for anyone else who 
might be able to help. However, Brakknap isn’t about to 
trust the PCs without good reason. Luckily for the PCs, 
tales of some of the work they’ve been doing around 
Isger has reached Thorngrip.
Before he gives them any 
information, Brakknap wants 
to hear all about the PCs from 
their mouths; he asks them who 
they are and their reasons for being in 
the Chitterwood. If any of the PCs are 
goblins or hobgoblins, Brakknap asks 
them about their histories and their 
opinions about the rest of the party, 
especially any humans. He is pleased to 
listen to any accounts of goblins and humans 
working together toward a common goal. At

If the PCs have at least 8 Reputation Points, they gain 
a +1 circumstance bonus to this check; if they have at 
least 12 Reputation Points, this bonus increases to +2. 
Brakknap’s starting attitude is indifferent; if the PCs

lightly. Though Zagnub has vouched for you by bringing

have watched other humans enter our territory whose 
motives are less worthy than yours. They are part of a 
group calling themselves the Isgeri Slayers, and they have 
made it their mission to finish what was started during the 
Goblinblood Wars.”
Brakknap looks pained, as if remembering something he 
would rather forget. “I don’t care how you do it, but drive 
them off. The chances they will find Thorngrip are small, but 
I fear what would happen if they came across any goblins.”
If the PCs agree to help Thorngrip, Brakknap tells 
them that Zagnub will point them toward where 
these Isgeri Slayers were last seen. With some remorse, 
Brakknap also says that the PCs will not be allowed 
to step inside Thorngrip again until the Isgeri Slayers 
are gone. Proceed to Isgeri Slayers on page 50 if the 
PCs are eager to get to the action, but if Brakknap is 
friendly or helpful, they can take some time to look 
around Thorngrip before they leave.

Treasure: Zagnub has taken a liking to the PCs and

DOWNTIME IN THORNGRIP
Though it’s a small town, Thorngrip has many of 
the amenities that one can find in any large city. The 
goblin residents, however, tend not to use the currency 
of the land, instead preferring to barter for goods and 
services. If the PCs want to buy items, they can procure 
common and magical items up to level 3 and alchemical 
consumables and talismans up to level 4. A PC receives 
the standard value for selling an item and can easily 
trade for an equivalent amount of items. For any 
difference in value, the goblin merchants don’t pay the 
PCs gold; instead, they give them physical items such 
as small gems or rare herbs that can later be sold or 
traded in a larger city for their correct value. If willing, 
a PC can also take an appropriate amount of food and 
drink as part of a trade. Instead of receiving currency, 
a PC who takes some downtime to Earn an Income in 
Thorngrip is instead paid in goods and services.
The artisans of Thorngrip include Ghugg (gruff 
male goblin smith 1), who sells weapons and armor 
with a goblin flair; Mirdona (inquisitive female goblin 
alchemist 1), who brews alchemical elixirs and the 
occasional bomb; Ikko (fussy nonbinary goblin 
magician 1), who fashions talismans from natural 
materials and carves runes into petrified bark; and Duz 
(experimental female goblin chef 1), who can pickle 
just about anything.
Thorngrip has no inns, as they don’t expect to have 
visitors, but there’s one house that remains empty 
for new goblin arrivals to use while they build more 
permanent abodes. Brakknap allows the PCs to use 
this house, which is close to the shrine, when they need 
to rest. If his attitude is helpful, Brakknap will cast a 
1st-rank heal on any PCs who are below half their HP 
before they rest, but he doesn’t have any magic to help 
with curses, diseases, and poisons.
Finally, if the PCs spend downtime to Craft or 
Retrain, they are allowed to use facilities within 
Thorngrip to do so at no charge. However, until they 
help out with the Isgeri Slayers, Brakknap gives them 
disappointed looks if they dawdle in town for more 
than a day.
THORNGRIP PARIAHS
On the off chance that the PCs didn’t join with the 
Looksee Party to enter Thorngrip as friends, they have 
to prove they are worthy of the goblins’ help before 
being allowed inside. If they follow the goblin scouts 
to the thorn wall, Zagnub yells at them to go away 
before passing through the thorns. It’s unlikely the 
PCs will be able to find their own way into the town 
(see Thorngrip sidebar), and after some time trying, 
Brakknap appears at the wall to confront the PCs. He 
tells them bluntly that if they wish to gain the town’s 
trust, they need to deal with the Isgeri Slayers out in 
the forest. The PCs will get a chance to tell Brakknap 
their story (and attempt to improve his attitude) once 
they do so.
The Isgeri Slayers
The hatred stoked by the Goblinblood Wars two 
decades ago has not fully dissipated in Isger. Some 
veterans of that war formed an unsanctioned group 
of rangers and foresters calling themselves the Isgeri 
Slayers. The sole purpose of this loose affiliation is to 
hunt down and kill all goblinoids within the country’s 
borders. The Isgeri Slayers spend days and sometimes 
weeks within the Chitterwood, hunting down goblins 
for sport and as an outlet for their rage.
Most goblins manage to escape these bigoted 
hunters, and more than a few larger tribes have turned 
the tables on them deep in the woods. Despite a 
relatively high rate of fatal “accidents” during these

SLAYER CAMP	
LOW 3
Five hastily erected tents surround a campfire in this small 
clearing. A handful of empty whiskey bottles have been 
pushed bottleneck-first into the dirt near the fire. A couple 
of logs have been pulled close to the tents to serve as 
makeshift chairs.
While these Isgeri Slayers have been in the 
Chitterwood before, they aren’t the most competent 
campers, largely due to their excessive drinking. The 
tents would likely collapse in a strong wind, but serve 
their purpose for the Slayers.
Creatures: Two of the Isgeri Slayers and their 
trained wolf ranged out into the woods to hunt for 
food while the remaining three stayed behind and 
continued to drink. These three are drunk enough 
that the PCs can easily creep up toward the camp 
and take them by surprise, giving the PCs a +1 
circumstance bonus to their initiative. Each of the 
drunken slayers flees, if possible, when reduced to 6 
or fewer Hit Points.
However, the PCs don’t have to attack the slayers. 
The PCs can attempt up to three DC 17 skill checks 
using any combination of Deception, Intimidation, 
and Performance to scare the slayers into leaving. 
If they succeed at two of these skill checks, they 
frighten the three drunken slayers off; a critical 
success lowers the DC of the next check by 1. If the 
PCs critically fail a single check or fail two of these 
checks, the drunken slayers grab their weapons and 
attack. An attempted Diplomacy check automatically 
fails against the inebriated slayers, who are too out of 
it to consider listening to reason, and counts against 
one of the three checks.

HUNTING PARTY	
MODERATE 3
The other two Isgeri Slayers ranged out a few miles

The Trust of Goblins
Once the PCs have taken care of the Isgeri Slayers, 
they’re met by Brakknap outside of Thorngrip, who 
ushers them inside. The resident goblins now look at 
them with admiration and respect as they pass through 
the streets. Brakknap trusts the PCs enough to reveal

The goblin oracle is waiting at the 
ancestor shrine and gives a brief smile 
before getting down to business. 
“The spirits are pleased that you are 
here on this day. This Viro Ahala you 
are searching for is doing something 
within our wood that has them 
worried, and we think you can stop 
it. However, the power he’s tapping 
into has obscured him from our ancestors’ 
sight.” His forehead crinkles a moment in 
thought. “This veil is not impenetrable. With 
your help, we can discover where the hell-human is 
performing his ritual.
“There are three sites of subtle power nearby within 
the Chitterwood. The ancestors have told me that Viro’s 
ritual has disturbed these places, making them more 
dangerous to approach than normal. Take this talisman 
to those sites. It will react to the changes in energy and, 
after being exposed to all three, it will help me to see 
Viro’s location.” Brakknap holds out a cloudy crystal on a 
leather cord. “I don’t know what you’ll find at these sites, 
but be ready for anything.”
Reward: For gaining Brakknap’s trust, 
award the PCs 30 XP.
Triangulating the 
Ritual
Brakknap describes the three locations the 
PCs need to visit and gives clear enough directions 
that the PCs should be able to find them without 
issue. The PCs can visit these three locations in any 
order and can return to Thorngrip at any point they 
need to rest. They should feel a sense of urgency 
to find Viro Ahala and stop his ritual but, for the 
moment, they don’t have a hard deadline. If the 
PCs ask Brakknap for any information about 
the locations, he will tell them the following.
The Hungry Hole: “No goblin knows who 
dug the Hungry Hole or even how deep it is, but 
we do know that it can’t be filled, no matter how much 
we throw into it. I’ve heard tales of goblins falling into 
the hole and coming out on the other side of the world. 
Those are just stories to keep young goblins away. 
Probably. The ancestors tell me, though, that it’s better 
to stay away from the edge.”
Little Tree: “For as long as I have been alive, Little 
Tree has been little. It doesn’t grow but it hasn’t died 
either. From what we understand about nature, it 
should be starved for sunlight or water by the other, 
bigger trees, but it just isn’t. The ancestors 
believe it’s fed by magic, and many find 
Little Tree’s presence very soothing.”
Moss Pond: “We call it a pond 
but it’s just a large patch of 
moss that sometimes ripples like 
water. You can walk across it if 
you want, it isn’t dangerous. You 
won’t even sink! Sometimes, 
children will take turns lying on 
the pond to feel the moss move 
under them. The ancestors say that 
it’s a connection to the very essence of the 
Chitterwood, but they can’t explain it any 
more than that.”

MODERATE 3
The Hungry Hole is less than an hour’s walk south 
of Thorngrip. When the PCs approach, read or

This clearing is devoid of all foliage in an almost perfect 
circle 40 feet in diameter. Not even the tiniest blade of 
Crystal Talisman
Hungry Hole

===== Page 55 =====
54
grass can be spotted in the dirt around a mundane-looking 
hole in the center of the clearing. The branches of the 
surrounding trees don’t encroach the space, creating a kind 
of tunnel from the ground to the sky. The edges of the hole 
shift and undulate like a ravenous mouth, daring anyone 
to approach.
The Hungry Hole is a kind of bottomless pit created 
centuries ago when a Chitterwood goblin wizard 
experimented with the extradimensional magic of 
a spacious pouch and had a predictable accident. 
Throughout the years, other goblins have thrown 
random objects within the pit; these all still exist 
somewhere within the Hungry Hole, but living things 
tossed (or that have fallen) into the pit reappeared

began corrupting the Chitterwood with his ritual. 
Now, the Hungry Hole is quite dangerous.

center to represent the Hungry Hole.

ritual has turned the Hungry Hole into a ravenous pit 
that tries to swallow the PCs whole if they approach. 
Any PC swallowed by the pit can faintly hear the 
laughter of devils and the screams of the damned, 
as if the extradimensional space within the trap 
neighbors Hell.

LITTLE TREE
MODERATE 3
Little Tree is approximately a 30-minute walk 
southeast of Thorngrip and uses the Little Tree map on 
page 54. When the PCs approach, read or paraphrase 
the following.
A sapling stands on a little hill, separate from the other 
trees. Though it’s small, the green of its leaves are lush and 
vibrant even in the autumn weather. An aura of peace and 
calm radiates from the little tree.
Little Tree is an unusual conduit of primal magic, a 
rare phenomenon that only appears deep within the 
oldest forests of Golarion. It represents the eternal 
youth of spring and while it’s a living thing, it never 
ages, gets sick, nor needs normal photosynthesis. 
However, when Viro Ahala began his ritual, this 
primal energy became warped, and all the potential 
growth Little Tree should have experienced over the 
decades has been inverted and projected outward.
Hazard: The corruption of Viro’s ritual has caused 
Little Tree’s energies to shrink nearby creatures instead 
of rejuvenating itself. A creature shrunken down by 
this trap also feels resentment and jealousy, a reflection 
of the emotions burning in Viro’s heart.

MOSS POND	
MODERATE 3
Moss Pond is less than an hour’s walk west of 
Thorngrip. Use the Moss Pond map on page 54 for 
this encounter. When the PCs approach, read or 
paraphrase the following.
The normal undergrowth of the forest gives way to a large 
patch of moss a few dozen feet in diameter. The moss 
appears to be several inches thick on the ground, with 
patches of various shades of green. The moss undulates

===== Page 57 =====
56
slightly as if floating on water, but there is no water to 
be seen.
Unlike many of the other unusual phenomena in the 
Chitterwood—which are ancient and timeless in the 
eyes of the local goblinoids—Moss Pond is a relatively 
recent addition. With the Plane of Wood’s reconnection 
to the cosmos, this once-normal, albeit large, patch of 
moss became a faint conduit to that elemental plane. 
The occasional movement across the surface of the 
moss experienced by the local goblins was caused by 
energy from the Plane of Wood seeping through to 
the mortal Universe; this energy is normally harmless. 
As Viro Ahala’s ritual attempts to draw power from 
Hell, other planar breaches in the forest are reacting, 
becoming more unstable by the moment.
Hazard: Unstable planar energy is causing sudden 
growth and subsequent decay within the moss, creating 
dangerous “spears” of plant matter. Drawn to other 
living creatures, these spears of moss strike out at nearly 
anything that comes near the pond. A creature who 
takes poison damage from a spore spear Strike has a 
brief vision of endless burning forests, an overlapping 
of landscapes from the Plane of Wood and Hell.

BRAKKNAP’S REVELATION
Once the PCs have investigated the three sites above 
and dealt with the corrupted magic caused by Viro’s 
ritual, they can return to Brakknap. He seems to know 
that they’ve completed their mission and asks to see 
the crystal he gave them.
Brakknap looks serious as he holds the leather strap 
and peers at the crystal at the end of it. He stares for 
a moment and then his eyes go wide. With a mixture of 
anger and horror he says, “The caves. The hell-human 
Viro is in the caves.” He realizes that he’s speaking 
vaguely and composes himself. “Before the founding of 
Thorngrip, my tribe was hunted by humans at the end of 
the Goblinblood Wars. We hid in a small series of caves 
near here, but we knew they would not keep us safe 
forever. My grandmother used the power of the woods 
to transform into a mighty stag and lead the humans 
away. She did not survive, but her sacrifice was not in 
vain. The survivors found this tree and the ancestors 
helped me raise the wall of thorns around it. We have 
been safe since then.”
The older goblin takes a deep breath, voice trembling 
with anger. “We named those caves Stagfall in honor of my 
grandmother. And now this hell-human Viro is using them 
for his wicked purposes! This cannot stand!”
With the magic of the eastern Chitterwood 
returning to normal, the ancestor spirits were able 
to pinpoint Viro Ahala’s location as being within the 
nearby Stagfall Caves. They tell Brakknap that the 
Hellknight has discovered tunnels that lead deeper 
than any goblins have explored and warn that he has 
many allies. Brakknap passes this information on to 
the PCs, apologizing that the ancestors can’t be more 
specific. He then hands the crystal pendant back to the 
PCs, noting that it “still has much power within it.”
Brakknap can give the PCs directions to the caves 
and even describe the first few chambers (areas G1-
G3), but has no other guidance to give. If the PCs need 
to rest before leaving Thorngrip again, they can.
Treasure: In addition to the crystal, Brakknap gifts 
the PCs a runestone with a +1 striking rune carved 
into it that is “from the town elders.”
G. Stagfall Caves
Once Viro Ahala began exploring the Chitterwood 
to find a place suitable for his ritual, he was slowly 
drawn to the tunnels the Thorngrip goblins named 
Stagfall Caves. Deeper in the caves than any goblin 
had explored is a natural nexus of magical power with 
the potential to overcharge Viro’s ritual and grant him 
the revenge he’s seeking. He, along with a coterie of 
Hellknight armigers who also fled Breachill and a 
handful of conjured devils, has explored most of the 
subterranean tunnels. They established a few defensive 
areas to protect Viro as he works toward completing 
the ritual in the caves’ rearmost chamber. If the PCs 
don’t find and stop him, he’ll succeed in a matter of 
days (though the exact timing is left vague to let the 
PCs proceed at their own pace).
The hillside that contains Stagfall Caves is a day’s 
travel through the forest southeast of Thorngrip. The 
journey is relatively uneventful, but the closer the party 
gets to the cave entrance, the more they get the sense 
that something isn’t right. There are fewer sightings and 
sounds of wild animals in the underbrush and the tree 
branches overhead, as if they’re instinctively avoiding 
the area. A PC who succeeds at a DC 20 Nature or 
Survival check spots strange patterns in the bark of trees 
and clumps of moss close to the caves that resemble 
screaming, tortured faces; this PC knows that for the 
trees to have grown that way, it would have taken 
decades if not centuries, so whatever is happening with 
Viro’s ritual seems to be warping the natural world.

===== Page 59 =====
58
The interior of the cave is in darkness except 
where noted, and most ceilings are 15 to 20 
feet high. The PCs can use any of the caverns 
they clear out as places to camp if needed, but 
they can also retreat to outside 
the cave. The conjured devils are 
under strict orders to protect the 
caves, so they don’t chase anyone past the cave 
entrance. The Hellknights, on the other hand, 
aren’t bound by any such verbal loopholes. 
They will follow any retreating PCs 
after first tending to their own wounds. 
If the PCs cause any major ruckus, the 
Hellknights might even begin searching 
the caves for the PCs, potentially 
leaving their posts.
G1. CAVE ENTRANCE
A small hill rises here deep within the Chitterwood. At certain 
angles, the trees atop it look like the antlers of a mighty stag, 
but the brush at the base of the trees is black and gnarled, 
as if existing purely out of spite. Slightly hidden behind a tall 
tree is a small cave leading into the hillside.
The cave entrance is easy to find, especially with 
Brakknap’s directions, but the tree does a good job 
of hiding it from the view of anyone not paying close 
attention. The cave entrance is small enough that 
Medium and larger creatures need to duck their heads 
to pass through; this counts as difficult terrain during 
a combat encounter.
G2. MAIN CAVE	
LOW 3
Once past the low cave entrance, the chamber opens up, 
stretching to the north and east, with alcoves in either 
direction. The rough ceiling is little more than 10 feet high, 
though it rises up a few more feet at the eastern end of the 
cave. The old remnants of a makeshift camp can be seen 
to the east.
When Brakknap’s tribe fled from their pursuers, 
they hid mostly in this part of the caves. The northern 
alcove contains a ring of stones that surrounded a fire 
years ago, apparently not having been disturbed in all 
that time. There are a few pieces of carved wood caked 
in moss near the fire pit, indistinguishable trinkets left 
behind by the goblins who sheltered here.
To the east, a pile of rocks blocks an obvious tunnel 
that leads deeper into the caves. This blockade was 
placed here by the cave’s current residents (see area 
G4), having been ordered to block the way by Viro. 
The stones aren’t packed very tightly, and the PCs 
can spend 30 minutes clearing away the stones 
enough to access the tunnel. For each PC who 
succeeds at a DC 22 Athletics check while 
doing so, this time is reduced by 5 minutes.
Creatures: A trio of conjured insidiators 
lurks in the room’s northern alcove, 
waiting for any intruders. They have 
been ordered to attack anyone who 
enters the cave from outside until told 
otherwise by Viro. The devils fight until 
killed but they don’t chase fleeing enemies, 
instead retreating to the eastern alcove 
where it’s difficult to see them from the cave 
entrance.
INSIDIATORS (3)	
CREATURE 1
Page 224
Initiative Perception +10
G3. INTERSECTION
Four tunnels lead off in all directions to and from this 
roughly circular cavern. The northeastern tunnel is a bit 
wider than the other three.
A PC who inspects the four tunnels and succeeds 
at a DC 20 Perception or DC 18 Survival check 
notices that the southern, western, and northeastern 
tunnels have seen a lot more foot traffic in the 
past week. While there is some disturbed dirt and 
stones in the southeastern tunnel, they indicate 
that two people entered the tunnel but only one 
returned. On a critical success, the PC also spots 
a bit of dried blood smeared on the cave wall near 
this end of the southeastern tunnel in area G4; two 
of Viro’s armigers explored that tunnel, which leads 
to a basilisk’s lair. One was killed and the other 
barely escaped to tell the tale. The basilisk wasn’t 
threatened enough to hunt down its fleeing prey and 
the armigers avoid that chamber.
G4. BASILISK LAIR	
MODERATE 3
A pile of nearly equally sized rocks have been piled neatly 
in the northern end of this cavern. The southern part of 
this chamber holds a small alcove that is covered with 
thick moss. The shattered remains of a stone statue of an 
armored figure lies scattered in the center of the floor.
The body here is one of the Hellknight armigers 
Viro brought with him, petrified and killed by the 
basilisk that resides in this cave.

G5. NATURAL STEPS
This tunnel opens up to the west, where a set of natural 
stone steps have been carved out by millennia of erosion. 
The occasional drop of water from the ceiling makes these 
steps slightly damp. A passageway leads north.
Each of the stone steps to the west is about 6 feet 
tall and, due to their slipperiness, requires a successful 
DC 18 Athletics check to Climb. The tunnel to the 
north narrows as it enters area G7, but not so much that 
Medium creatures need to Squeeze through. The water 
dripping from the ceiling is from a natural aquifer that 
runs north through the rock to area G10, creating the 
waterfall there. In time, the water will erode the stone 
away enough to turn these steps into a new waterfall.
Treasure: A small glint from the top of the chamber is 
noticeable with a successful DC 18 Perception check. A 
PC who climbs up to examine it finds a shining symbol.
G6. ROCKFALL	
MODERATE 3
A possible tunnel collapse filled the eastern section of this 
wide cave with tightly packed rubble. A pair of bedrolls 
have been placed on the ground along the northern wall.
Decades ago, there was a tunnel leading between 
this cave and area G9, but it collapsed. The rubble has 
settled in for so long, it would take months of work 
with heavy picks and shovels to excavate the passage.
The Hellknights here have a hooded lantern lit by 
the bedrolls. The space within 30 feet of it is in bright 
light, with dim light for an additional 30 feet.
Creatures: The bedrolls belong to the Hellknight 
armigers Viro has stationed here to monitor the 
basilisk in area G4. All of them believe Viro is a full 
Hellknight who bravely vanquished his attackers 
during the tactical retreat from Breachill. At least two 
of the armigers are on watch at all times, but when the 
PCs arrive, they are all awake and in their armor. If the 
PCs spend 10 minutes examining the skeleton in area 
G7, there’s a 50% chance that one of the armigers here 
spots them and initiates a fight.
The armigers fervently engage in battle, attempting 
to flank the toughest PC and bring them down before 
focusing on the others. However, if a different PC is 
easily hitting one of them, that Hellknight turns their 
attention to this PC. The adjutant armigers fight to the 
death, but the novice armiger tries to flee if reduced to 
4 or fewer Hit Points. If the only avenue of escape is 
through area G4, the novice surrenders instead.

G7. ANCIENT GRAVE
Passageways lead southeast, southwest, and north from 
this bean-shaped cavern. The floor here is mostly smooth 
stone, with the exception of a patch of uneven ground in 
which a humanoid skeleton is embedded. One bony arm 
reaches up toward the ceiling, as if calling for aid.
Centuries ago, when Kellids occupied most of the 
land that would become Isger, these caves were near 
a popular hunting ground. One day after a torrential 
downpour, a Kellid ranger fell through an unexpected 
sinkhole into this chamber. This Kellid died here, 
reaching for help that would not come, and their 
bones were partially preserved by the stone. A PC who 
spends 10 minutes and succeeds at a DC 18 Medicine 
or DC 16 Archaeology Lore check can determine 
the skeleton’s broken legs are the result of a fall. The 
sinkhole has since been sealed by time and shifting 
earth, but a PC who succeeds at a DC 22 Perception 
or DC 20 Survival check while examining the ceiling 
can see the barest hint of what was once a hole leading 
to the surface.
Treasure: A PC who examines the skeleton also 
finds a quiver that ironically holds two climbing bolts.
G8. GLOWING COLUMN	
LOW 3
A slightly glowing stone column connecting floor to 
ceiling is the only notable feature of this irregular-shaped 
chamber. The surface of the column is rough and full of 
millions of small divots, like pumice. Several alcoves in 
the walls have a similar texture. Tunnels lead west, east, 
and south.
The column here has absorbed some of the potential 
magic power from deeper in the cave and so gives off a 
faint, eerie glow, casting the room into dim light. Every 
so often, a flicker of this energy moves from one of 
the indentations in the stone to another, appearing as 
a translucent, glowing worm. When this occurs, the 
squares adjacent to the pillar become bright light for 
1 round.
Light of the Glow Worms: In a combat encounter, 
roll a DC 15 flat check at the start of each round. On 
a success, a glow worm appears and the DC of the 
next flat check increases by 1. On a failure, reduce the 
DC of the next flat check by 1. A PC can attempt a 
DC 17 Arcana or Nature check to Recall Knowledge 
about the column, learning of this strange property. A 
PC adjacent to the column can then Interact with it 
and attempt a DC 15 Arcana or Nature check, coaxing 
forth a glowing worm with a success; on a critical 
success, a glowing worm remains on the surface of the 
pillar for 1 minute, instead of 1 round.
Creatures: Though the magic of the column is fairly 
inconsequential, one of Viro’s Hellknight armiger 
allies became convinced that the stone harbors a 
deeper secret. She has been studying the column for 
several days, trying to discover more about the stone’s 
magical properties, but has yet to be successful. 
Recently, she borrowed a conjured pair of orts to test 
whether their fiendish forms could affect the light in
