G9. HIDDEN LEDGE
This chamber dead-ends in a pile of fallen rubble where 
perhaps a tunnel once lead south. A curving passage leads 
west and large curtains of moss hang down from various 
spots on the cave ceiling.
The tunnel to the south used to lead to area G6, 
but it collapsed long ago and is now impassable. The 
rubble has been compacted by decades of the weight 
of the hillside pressing down on it.
A PC who succeeds at a DC 20 Perception check 
while Searching the room notices that one of the 
curtains of moss hanging down from the ceiling 
conceals a small passageway going north. This hole is 
about 4 feet high and 5 feet wide and is about 10 feet 
from the ground. A successful DC 14 Athletics check 
is required to Climb the wall under it, and the passage 
is treated as difficult terrain for Medium creatures, 
while Large creatures will need to Squeeze through. 
However, this tunnel leads to a ledge in area G11 that 
might allow the PCs to get the drop on Viro, provided 
they don’t make too much noise.
G10. UNDERGROUND WATERFALL	 MODERATE 3
The sound of splashing water fills this cavern due to 
the 20-foot-tall waterfall coursing down the 
wall from the ceiling to the northwest. The 
water collects in a pool, near which a 
pair of bedrolls have been set up on 
the ground. Thick logs have been 
pulled into the cave to form a couple 
of barricades. Two tunnels exit this 
chamber to the east.
The small aquifer that runs 
above the caves comes through 
the ceiling here to form a gentle 
waterfall. The water collects in a 
pond in the northern part of the 
cave, which slowly drains into the earth. The 
bottom of the pool is lined with mossy rocks and is 
home to a tiny number of cave fish that are no more 
than an inch long.
Viro has commanded his most loyal armiger allies 
to set up a guard post in this room, thinking it’s the 
only way to get to the cave in which he performs his 
ritual. Their bedrolls lie near the northern exit, far 
enough away from the splashing waterfall to stay dry, 
and a lit hooded lantern near them lights the area with 
30 feet of bright light and 30 more feet of dim light. 
They have also dragged a few thick logs from the 
forest outside here to create a couple of makeshift but 
defensible barricades. Crossing through a square with 
one of these logs is difficult terrain, but a creature can 
use them to Take Cover. A 5-foot section of log has 
Hardness 5, 20 Hit Points, and a BT of 10, but they 
are damp enough not to be set easily alight. A broken 
section of log is no longer difficult terrain and can’t be 
used to Take Cover.
Creatures: Viro left an experienced adjutant 
Hellknight armiger in charge of the room’s defense, 
along with a novice armiger and a conjured insidiator. 
The two Hellknights are behind the northern 
barricades when the PCs enter the room, but the 
insidiator attempts to hide in the southeast alcove to 
catch intruders unaware.
The sound of the waterfall is enough to cover most 
of the sounds of combat from other rooms, but if 
the armigers do hear something from area G8, they 
remain here, as part of their orders. However, the 
adjutant armiger will send the novice armiger to 
investigate any unusual noises coming from area G11 
after 1 round, and then follow 2 rounds later if the 
novice armiger doesn’t report back. The insidiator 
doesn’t leave this chamber.

G11. RITUAL SITE
SEVERE 3
Candlelight flickers along the perimeter of this large 
chamber and the cave is infused with the scent of 
brimstone. Two men occupy the room, one in the typical 
accoutrements of a Hellknight armiger and another 
dressed in the formidable armor of a Hellknight. The 
false Hellknight stands over an ivory bowl that contains 
a bright flame in the center of the room, scattered ritual 
materials piled nearby atop a rough blanket on the stone 
floor. The air above it wavers with occult energy as he 
methodically burns a piece of parchment that has been 
inscribed with blood.
Viro Ahala chose this cave for his ritual site as it 
courses with magical energy that has gone largely 
untapped for centuries. The flame in the ivory bowl 
and the candles together provide bright light for the 
chamber. A ledge at the back of the chamber requires 
a successful DC 14 Athletics check to Climb, and 
hidden from view from the ground on this ledge is 
a tight tunnel that leads south to area G9. The 
top of the ledge is in dim light, so Viro and 
his companions are unaware of the tunnel.
Creatures: If given the opportunity to 
speak before being attacked, Viro gloats 
that the PCs are too late to stop his 
ritual in an attempt to Demoralize 
the physically most intimidating 
PC. If the PCs disable the ritual 
backlash hazard before defeating 
Viro, he becomes off-guard for 1 
round and drained 1. Viro and his 
fellow armiger won’t surrender, 
fighting to the bitter end.
Hazard: Viro Ahala has been 
performing a complicated ritual here for 
several days, one that will grant him 
only a fraction of the power of Hell, 
but enough to get his revenge on the Hellbreakers 
League. He has yet to be successful, but his attempts 
have caused the magical energy of the cave to 
become erratic. His attention to the flame within 
the ivory bowl, the focus of the ritual, has kept the 
energy in check, but the moment he becomes even 
momentarily distracted, the backlash manifests. 
Because Viro has been pouring his mental energy 
into the ritual all this time, the backlash harms only 
his enemies. If the ivory bowl is broken, the hazard 
loses 1 action. If the ivory bowl is destroyed, the 
hazard loses 2 actions.
Brakknap’s Crystal: The crystal Brakknap gave 
the PCs provides a small amount of protection and 
the ability to counter some of the ritual’s backlash. 
The PC wearing or holding the crystal, and everyone 
adjacent to them, gains a +1 status bonus to any 
Will saving throw against the hazard’s Pulse of Fear 
ability, and resistance 2 to mental damage caused 
by the ritual’s mindburn Strike. They also gain the 
following reaction.
Rebuke Hellish Healing [reaction] (primal) Trigger The ritual 
backlash hazard uses Vitality of Hell on a target within 
10 feet; Effect Attempt a DC 16 Nature or Religion check. 
On a success, Vitality of Hell is counteracted. On a 
critical success, the target of Vitality of Hell takes 1d6 
fire damage.

A Victorious Return
Once Viro Ahala has been defeated and his ritual 
stopped, the PCs can explore other parts of Stagfall 
Caves or immediately return to Thorngrip to tell 
Brakknap the good news. The goblin oracle is already 
aware of their success from the spirits of his ancestors, 
and the entire town comes out to meet the PCs as 
they step through the thorn wall. The PCs are treated 
as heroes and there’s an evening of celebration, 
especially if they need to rest for a night to tend to 
their wounds before leaving the Chitterwood. The 
PCs are especially treated well by the goblin children 
who have never met non-goblinoids before, as they 
are curious about the heroes and beg the party for 
dramatic retellings and reenactments of their defeat of 
Viro and his fiendish allies. Some children might even 
dress up as a specific PC. Food and drink is plentiful 
all throughout the night; the pickle-flavored goblin 
liquor is especially strong, and a few PCs might wake 
feeling a little worse than when they went to sleep. 
Luckily, Mirdona has surefire hangover cure, which 
also tastes of pickles.
The PCs should then return to Saringallow to 
debrief with Rhokrag and the other Hellbreakers. 
They listen with interest as the PCs recount their 
travels, with Maire taking notes for future stories. 
Rhokrag is pleased with their success, especially with 
the friendship the PCs forged with the Thorngrip 
goblins, and lets them know that the Demetriases 
want to speak with them directly. At their earliest 
convenience, the PCs should head north to Elidir, 
where the Hellbreakers League founders await.
At this point, tally the PCs’ current Reputation 
Point total. They will have the opportunity to gain (or 
lose) Reputation Points in the coming chapters, but it 
will be helpful to have a snapshot of the League’s 
reputation in Isger after the PCs’ actions; this total is 
also an extrapolation of how the other teams did in 
other areas of the country.
Fewer than 6 RP The Hellbreakers League is 
still seen as dangerous troublemakers by most 
citizens. The PCs have to travel north incognito.
7–9 RP Most people don’t believe the League 
wants to burn down every Isgeri city, but neither 
do they fully trust its members. The PCs are 
better not to draw attention to their affiliation 
for now.
10–12 RP Those who want to throw off the yoke of 
Chelaxian rule feel more comfortable speaking 
out, thanks to the efforts of the Hellbreakers 
League. The PCs won’t need to worry about the 
bounty on their capture, except in areas of deep 
Chelaxian loyalty.
13+ RP Talk of Isgeri independence is on everyone’s 
lips! The Hellbreakers League are considered the 
best chance for the future. Some citizens are still 
loyal to Steward Hedvend and Cheliax, but they 
might soon be a minority. The PCs are celebrated 
nearly everywhere they go.
Reward: For defeating Viro Ahala and stopping his 
ritual, award the PCs 40 XP. If the PCs have a total 
of at least 15 Reputation Points, award the PCs an 
additional 40 XP.
Treasure: Brakknap gifts the crystal pendant to the 
PCs, which has served its initial purpose and awakens 
into a pendant of the occult.

While the PCs were busy in the south of Isger, events 
were also unfolding in the capital, Elidir. Alceo 
Demetrias (wise male aiuvarin cleric of Milani 7) 
and Phoebe Demetrias (righteous female human 
warrior 7), the leaders of the Hellbreakers League, 
have been organizing resistance at the heart of the 
country’s critical trade route. The husband and wife 
have led numerous protests over the hardships faced 
by those outside the Conerica Straits and the Isgeri 
government’s Cheliax-centric policies. They seek to 
sow dissent against the country’s self-interested elites 
while generating support and finding recruits for the 
Hellbreakers League.
As part of their efforts, they have made tentative 
contact with a Druman trader named Quoster 
Thistlewait (opportunistic male halfling merchant 4), 
who has a strong distaste for Cheliax due to its history 
of slavery and iron grip on the Conerica River trade 
routes. He is willing to provide supplies in return for a 
lucrative trade deal when Isger is free of Cheliax.
The protests and disruptions caused by the PCs 
to the south have alarmed Hedvend VI. He’s used 
the army to crack down on gatherings, and then 
used the resulting clashes and bloodshed caused by 
his own forces to characterize the League as violent 
revolutionaries. Painting largely peaceful protests 
as vicious riots, he dubbed Alceo and Phoebe the 
Riotmongers, and placed a bounty on their heads. 
Unable to act freely, Alceo and Phoebe call for the PCs 
to come to Elidir.

and Caeto Vulaunex (self-righteous male human

Getting Started
Chapter 4 begins when the PCs are summoned by 
Rhokrag to the Hellbreakers League headquarters.
“I have something new for you all. While we’ve been 
working here, Alceo and Phoebe Demetrias have been 
trying to stir up the capital. But they’ve run into trouble—
the authorities figured out who they are, and they can’t 
work freely anymore.
“They asked me to send a few Hellbreakers I trust to get 
things done. You’ve shown your skill and smarts the last 
few months; we need you in Elidir now. Phoebe says the 
army is on high alert, and while they mostly ignore us out 
here in the hinterlands, they keep a tight grip on the capital 
and the rest of the Conerica Straits. Whatever you do, keep 
a low profile and do not get identified as League members. 
Once you get into Elidir, go to the Isgeri Circle and wait. 
Alceo and Phoebe will have someone checking for you who 
can bring you to their safe house.”
He shakes his head. “Get going. Hedvend’s throwing a 
gala in about ten days and he doesn’t know it, but you’re 
on the guest list.”
Rhokrag can’t answer many questions as the message 
purposely didn’t have much detail. He urges the PCs to 
leave immediately, as it’s a three-day journey to Elidir, 
and gives them a lifting belt for the mission. The trip 
to the capital passes uneventfully, though if your PCs 
need more Experience Points to reach 4th level, you 
can have them encounter bandits, wild animals, roving 
undead, or some other such encounter on the way.
ELIDIR’S STATUS
An open rebellion is closer than ever in Isger’s capital, 
but the army is working hard to maintain order. It’s 
not full-out martial law in the city as Hedvend tries 
to maintain some semblance of normalcy, but tensions 
are high. To reflect these competing pressures while 
in Elidir, the PCs accumulate both Uprising Points, 
which measure how successful they are in hampering 
Hedvend’s activities and recruiting Hellbreakers, 
and Suppression Points, which measure the army’s 
awareness of them and ability to quash dissent (refer 
to Victory Points in GM Core 184–185).
As the PCs reach certain thresholds, they discover 
opportunities or face additional complications. The 
points and thresholds accumulate concurrently.
Uprising Points
When the PCs’ Uprising Points reach each threshold 
for the first time, they gain the listed benefit. Each 
benefit can be used once by each PC and the PC must 
be in an area where popular support could affect 
the situation. This criteria is determined at the GM’s 
discretion; for example, it might be allowed while on 
Elidir’s streets or in the Gyve prison, but not in the 
steward’s manor.
1. Sedition (1–3 RP): While in Elidir, each PC can add +1 to 
a skill check or Perception check after they have rolled.
2. Subversion (4–6 RP): While in Elidir, each PC can add +1 
to an attack roll or saving throw after they have rolled.
3. Insurrection (7–9 RP): While in Elidir, each PC can reroll 
a check after they have rolled. They must use the second 
result, even if it’s worse. This has the fortune trait.
4. Revolution (10–12 RP): While in Elidir, each PC can roll 
a check twice and take the better result. This has the 
fortune trait.
Suppression Points
When the PCs’ Suppression Points reach each threshold, 
the effects of the government’s opposition make their 
work more difficult. The effects of each threshold are 
cumulative, but end if the PC’s Suppression Points 
total goes down, reducing the threshold. If a PC kills 
someone, they must attempt a DC 10 flat check; on a 
failure, they gain a Suppression Point.
1. Repression (1–3 SP): Outside of combat, the DC of any 
skill or Perception checks involving another humanoid 
are increased by 1.
2. Paranoia (4–6 SP): During the gala, the number of 
Influence Points to reach each threshold increases by 1.
3. Crackdown (7–9 SP): Each time the PCs go in the city 
streets, the GM rolls a DC 5 flat check; on a failure the 
PCs face the Papers, Please encounter below.
4. Martial Law (10–12 SP): Outside of combat, the DC of any 
skill or Perception checks involving another humanoid 
are increased by 1 (for a total of 2).
PAPERS, PLEASE	
MODERATE 4
Harassment by Cheliax loyalists is the status quo as 
the authorities try to quash dissent in the city. The PCs 
are approached by such loyalists looking to impress 
their superiors.

Entering the City
As the PCs approach the capital, read or paraphrase 
the following.
The Conerica River runs through the capital, bisecting the 
walled city. Ships laden with goods anchor outside huge 
river gates, waiting to enter as small sentry boats row back 
and forth delivering inspectors. Along the roads to Elidir, 
walled caravanserai teem with people, horses, wagons, and 
beasts of burden making use of the inns, stables, and trade 
facilities that facilitate the city’s lifeblood.
The PCs don’t draw any attention in the 
caravanserai outside the city walls as traders come 
and go constantly, with many travelers stopping in 
hopes of joining a caravan. Movement in and out of 
Elidir is tightly restricted, and the PCs must find a way 
past the guards without raising suspicions. The easiest 
way to do so is to join a group entering the city and 
pass through the gates right under the guards’ noses. 
Fortunately for the PCs, several people and groups are 
also looking to enter Elidir, and each has a secret that 
makes them amenable to welcoming a stranger.
Introduce the following groups, then allow each 
PC to attempt a DC 19 Diplomacy check to Gather 
Information or Perception check to learn more about 
one group of their choice. On a success, they learn the 
best skill to pose as part of the group. If a PC sneaks 
in with that group, they can use that skill instead of 
Deception or Performance to fool the guards. On a 
critical success, the PCs also learn the group’s secret. 
Doing so incentivizes the group to help any PCs that 
enter with them, giving each PC a +1 circumstance 
bonus on the subsequent check to make it past the 
guards. Reward the clever use of resources such as 
magical items, feats, and spells with bonuses or even 
an automatic success.
EINEEL HAVENMARK
Description Eineel is a mild-mannered human farmer who 
routinely brings in produce to sell at the market.
Secret Eineel is a smuggler, taking less for her services 
than official fees.
Skill Nature to Command the animals pulling her carts.
JOWARD YATLY
Description Joward is a nervous dwarven trader from 
Absalom with a shipment of wooden clockworks he’s 
been hired to deliver.
Secret Joward is actually Andoren, but fears he’ll be turned 
away due to the conflict between the countries.
Skill Crafting to demonstrate knowledge of the devices.
NORTHERN WARRIORS
Description A half-dozen partisans, led by Maurisno 
Rabesi (eager male human warrior 0), have come from 
northwest Isger to join the army to defend the nation 
from rebels and rabblerousers.
Secret The young hopeful soldiers have almost no actual 
experience with their weapons and are as likely to stab 
themselves as anyone else.
Skill Athletics to show off martial prowess.
THE MENAGERIE OF FEY FANTASTICO
Description The Menagerie is a traveling circus that has 
received permission to enter the city to put on a week’s 
worth of shows.
Secret Several of the troupe are thieves, who use the 
traveling show as cover for their activities.
Skill Acrobatics to pose as a tumbling troupe member.
Once the PCs each join a group, each PC must make 
it past the guards without raising suspicions. They 
can attempt to do so with a DC 17 check with the 
associated skill, or a DC 19 Deception or Performance 
check, with the following results.
Success The PC enters Elidir without raising any suspicions.
Failure The guards’ suspicions are raised. The PCs gain 1 
Suppression Point.
Critical Failure As failure, but the PCs gain 2 Suppression 
Points.
Sneaking In: The PCs can also attempt to enter the 
city by directly sneaking in, but the guards are on high 
alert and this may be more troublesome than blending 
in with other groups. A PC must succeed at two checks 
to enter unnoticed: a DC 19 Stealth check to approach 
unseen, and then a DC 21 Acrobatics or Athletics 
check to either scale the walls or swim through the 
river. They gain 1 Suppression Point for each failure (2 
on a critical failure).

ISGERI CIRCLE	
MODERATE 4
While the Taldans “pacified” the Isgeri in 2133, 
outbreaks of violence continued for some time. To ease 
tensions, the first Taldan governor of Isger allowed 
the Isgeri tribes to create this monument devoted to 
Urgathoa in her guise as a goddess of bounty. Attempts 
to remove it over the ensuing centuries all failed, as 
workers mysteriously grew ill when they approached. 
Most residents of the city now give it a wide berth.
Badly worn carvings of produce such as grapes, apples, 
nuts, and squashes top the ancient standing stones that 
surround a simple stone altar in this clearing.
Unable to safely venture out themselves, Alceo 
and Phoebe enlisted Sarevial (loyal male elf baker’s 
apprentice –1) to check several times each day to see 
if the PCs have arrived. Unfortunately, a guard patrol 
has grown suspicious and closes in when Sarevial 
approaches the PCs.
Creatures: In response to the protests against Cheliax, 
loyalists formed patrols to maintain security. Led by 
adiutors—mortals invested with infernal power also 
known as auxiliary devils—these patrols investigate 
any hints of subversion. They attempt to arrest Sarevial 
and the PCs for questioning. If the adiutor is slain or 
knocked unconscious, his toadies flee. Sarevial doesn’t 
participate in this combat; if you need his stats, use 
those of a commoner (NPC Core 66).
ADIUTOR
CREATURE 5
Page 222
Initiative Perception +13
TOADIES (2)
CREATURE 0
Pathfinder NPC Core 152
Initiative Perception +3
Party Preparations
Once they’ve defeated the guard patrol, Sarevial rushes 
the PCs to Alceo and Phoebe’s safe house. Alceo offers 
to tend to any wounds (via magic or Medicine) the 
PCs might have from the encounter. When everyone’s 
healed up, he gets straight to business.
Alceo takes a deep breath in his seat, Phoebe standing 
protectively behind him. “We’ve spent the past month 
stirring up discontent against Cheliax’s puppet elites 
and the city authorities. There’s been some success, but 
Hedvend’s cracked down on protests and used his own 
army’s violence against the people to frame us as rioters.”
“In some ways that’s helped us,” Phoebe interjects. 
“We’ve been hesitant to officially start a League chapter 
here, but the people are all but demanding one. They need 
someone to organize them and focus their anger, or there 
will be real riots. Unfortunately, Hedvend managed to 
identify us and spread our image around, so we’re handing 
off our operations to you.”
Alceo nods. “The immediate problem is that we were on 
the verge of arranging a deal with a Druman merchant, 
Quoster, to supply the League in return for certain trade 
rights once we’ve liberated Isger. Unfortunately, Hedvend 
outing us has spooked him. He wants proof of our abilities, 
and is demanding we show them by meeting him at 
Hedvend’s upcoming gala. You’ll have to make that meeting 
in our place and negotiate a deal that benefits both sides.”
Operating out of the safe house, the PCs must 
acquire three things before the gala at Steward 
Hedvend VI’s manor home, Reevesrest: forged 
invitations, appropriate costumes, and the lazybones 
pendant (page 211) that Quoster supplied for Alceo 
and Phoebe to identify themselves. These can be done 
in any order, and Alceo and Phoebe try to answer any 
questions the PCs have. Likely questions and their 
responses are as follows.
How were you identified? “We’re not sure,” Phoebe 
says. “Our best guess is someone we were working 
with was caught and broke in the Gyve.”
The Gyve? “It’s the prison.” Alceo’s face twists with 
disgust. “An awful place known for torturing those 
who end up there until the wardens hear what they 
want to hear.”
What can you tell us about Quoster? “He’s a halfling 
and motivated more by self-interest than concern for 
Isger. But he’s willing to help, and everything we’ve 
been able to learn about him makes us think we can 
trust him.”
Where’s the necklace? “Safely tucked away above a 
print shop called Love Sting. They make some saucy 
novels.” Phoebe grins and Alceo’s ears go pink.
CITY MAPS
Elidir is a large city, and it’s possible the PCs get 
into fights in areas that aren’t mapped (especially 
if you add some random encounters with guards). 
GMs who prefer premade maps can use flip-mats 
and flip-tiles to create suitable maps in moments. 
Some particularly useful maps are noted below.
•	 GameMastery Flip-Mat: City Square
•	 Pathfinder Flip-Mat Classics: City Streets
•	 Pathfinder Flip-Tiles: Urban Slums Expansion
•	 Pathfinder Flip-Tiles: Urban Starter Set
•	 Pathfinder Flip-Mat: City Districts Multi-Pack

What should we do about starting a League chapter? 
“The more immediate concern is Quoster and the gala. 
After that, look for recruits and sign up as many as 
you safely can. We trust you can handle it.”
After answering questions (or if asked 
what they’ll be doing), Alceo and Phoebe 
inform the PCs they plan to leave Elidir the 
morning of the gala, making a show of it to 
draw attention away from the Hellbreakers 
League’s continuing activities in the city. In 
the meantime, they’ll remain in the safe house 
and transition operations to the PCs.
OPERATION: THE INVITATION OF 
THE SEASON
The PCs need invitations to the gala! 
Fortunately for them, Alceo and Phoebe 
already did most of the legwork and 
know that a clerk at the city tax office, Orimos (petty 
nonbinary hellspawn nephilim human tax clerk 0), 
is responsible for the invites. They suggest the PCs 
approach Orimos with the truth, but warn that the 
clerk is wary of upsetting the authorities, so the PCs 
need to be subtle.
During the day, the PCs can find Orimos laboring in 
the Trade House, a bustling hive of bureaucracy filled 
with government officials, merchants, guards, and others 
coming and going with arms full of paperwork. The 
clerk is publicly officious and uninterested in discussing 
whatever trivial matter the PCs are bothering them with.
The easiest way to get them into somewhere private 
is to present them with a seemingly legitimate bit 
of paperwork, a tax problem, or other such minor 
governmental issue that they would normally discuss 
in a private office, which a PC can do with a successful 
DC 17 Accounting Lore or Legal Lore check or DC 
19 Society check. Alternatively, they can persuade 
Orimos to take them somewhere else with a successful 
DC 21 Deception check to Impersonate an official 
on a legitimate task or to Lie about their reasons for 
needing to speak with Orimos, DC 21 Diplomacy check 
to Make an Impression to make them friendly, or a 
DC 21 Intimidation check to Coerce them into a private 
conversation. On a critical failure, the PC takes a –1 
circumstance penalty to any future checks they make 
with Orimos. If at any point the PCs bring up Alceo, 
Phoebe, or the Hellbreakers League, they frighten the 
clerk and the DC of all checks to get them somewhere 
private increases by 1.
Alternatively, the PCs might stake out the office and 
follow Orimos to somewhere they can talk in private, 
such as Orimos’s home. If the PCs get Orimos to 
somewhere private and earn their trust, the PCs can 
reveal their true needs. At that point, Orimos drops 
their facade and reveals themself to be petty and eager 
to harm the elites of Cheliax and Isger, whom they 
hate for making their life difficult. They easily 
provide invitations to the PCs.
If the PCs fail to persuade Orimos to talk 
privately, the clerk sighs deeply before giving 
them one more chance. They urge whichever 
PC came closest to succeeding at their check 
to lean in, and then whispers that if the PCs’ 
concerns are urgent enough, they should put 
their money where their mouth is. 
With an appropriate bribe—3 
gp per PC—Orimos provides the 
invitations.
Reward: If the PCs acquire the invitations 
without needing to resort to a bribe, award them 
40 XP.
OPERATION: DRESS TO IMPRESS	
LOW 4
Proper attire lets the PCs fit in at the gala—and even 
bring in weapons and armor if it fits their costume. 
Alceo and Phoebe direct the PCs to Reirsumli 
Brightgate (meek male dwarf tailor 1) at his shop, the 
Silver Ribbon. Phoebe saved Reirsumli’s life during the 
Goblinblood Wars, and he owes her greatly. The PCs 
can tell him that the costumes are for Phoebe and he’ll 
happily make them for free.
The PCs must describe what they want their outfits 
to look like; give each PC a chance to describe their 
devilish garb and attempt a relevant DC 19 check 
to fully explain their vision. The PCs will also need 
costumes for any animal companions, familiars, or 
other creatures in their party as well.
Appropriate checks for costume design are Religion 
to describe a devil costume, Society to describe a 
Hellknight or other proper Chelaxian figure, or 
Crafting or Performance for a general sense of what 
they’re trying to achieve. The party needs to make a 
number of checks equal to the number of PCs, but the 
checks can be made by a single PC and the PCs can 
attempt to Aid each other. If anyone expresses concern 
about bringing larger weapons or armor into the gala, 
Reirsumli suggests dressing as a Hellknight or vordine. 
He tells the PCs to return just before the gala and he’ll 
have the costumes ready.
Whenever the PCs return, they find a well-dressed 
man with two hulking bodyguards in the shop 
confronting Reirsumli. He spotted the PCs’ outfits set 
out to be handed over and demanded them for himself!
To retrieve their costumes, the PCs must dissuade the 
noble by flattery, fear, or force. Each PC can attempt 
a DC 21 Deception or Diplomacy check to persuade 
Orimos

Use the map on page 66 for this encounter.

OPERATION: PROPER IDENTIFICATION
Before Alceo and Phoebe were identified by the 
authorities, Quoster sent them a lazybones pendant 
for them to wear as a sign of what he could provide, 
and a way of recognizing them when they finally 
met. The PCs need to collect it from where it’s being 
stored in a room above Love Sting Printing House, 
a one-elf publisher of “copper dalliances,” incredibly 
popular smutty serials with titles like The Archer All 
Aquiver, His Longsword of Love, and The Allure 
of Secret Sects, which sell for a copper apiece.
Unfortunately for the PCs, the room was 
looted by a thieves’ guild known as the Children’s 
Charity. Worse, the PCs arrive at the site just after 
an odvolos has decided that copper dalliances are a 
bad influence on the people of Elidir. Use the map on 
page 66 for this encounter.
LOVE STING PRINTING HOUSE	
MODERATE 4
Read or paraphrase the following as the PCs 
approach Love Sting Printing House.
A high-pitched voice pleads, “Please, you don’t have to 
do this! They’re just harmless entertainment!” A bruised 
elf lies crumpled in the snow in front of a shop. A trail of 
smoke wafts out the shop’s door.
Creatures: The elven man is a Calistrian devotee 
named Ievis (romantic male elf author 1), the writer, 
artist, and publisher of the copper dalliances. If 
the PCs attempt to enter the building or help him, 
a goblin calls out to the odvolos, who is torching 
unsold pamphlets inside, and attacks. The odvolos 
emerges and joins the battle, trying to prevent PCs 
from entering the building.
Hazard: The fire is spreading inside, threatening 
to destroy the entire building, including the safe 
house on the second floor. Though it’s inside, 
it’s included as part of this encounter due 
to the PCs’ need to stop it from spreading. 
Eliminating the hazard requires dousing the 
flames. Water clears a 5-foot square if the amount

SPREADING FIRE	
HAZARD 1
COMPLEX
ENVIRONMENTAL
Stealth –10; initiative modifier is +5
Description A fire engulfs a 5-foot-by-5-foot area, then 
spreads on each of its turns.
Disable DC 17 Athletics to splash the barrels of gall ink on 
the fire or DC 15 Survival to smother the flames
Spreading Flames [reaction] Trigger A creature enters the 
printing house; Effect The flames swell at the influx of 
air and deal 1d6 fire damage (DC 17 basic Reflex save). 
The fire then rolls initiative.
Routine (1 action) On its turn, the fire spreads into a 
number of additional squares equal to half the number 
of squares the fire currently occupies, with a minimum 
of 1 square. You determine the squares the fire 
spreads into—typically those with the most flammable 
materials. Any creature that ends its turn next to the 
flames takes 1d6 fire damage, and any creature within 
the flames takes 4d6 fire damage. Both of these have 
a DC 17 basic Reflex save. A creature can take damage 
from flames only once per round.
Instead of fighting the fire, PCs might try to dash 
upstairs to grab the lazybones pendant. If they do, 
they find the single, large storeroom empty and clearly 
looted. The only thing in the room is a blue 
ribbon pinned to the wall. If the PCs don’t 
make it upstairs, Ievis discovers the 
blue ribbon afterward and informs 
them that the necklace is gone.
Treasure: Ievis offers the PCs 
two unassuming face paints (page 
211) as thanks. If the PCs saved 
the shop, he also gifts them a rare 
manuscript of the banned play 
Abrogail I, which is worth 300 gp.
ABROGAIL I SCRIPT	
ITEM 4
RARE
Price 300 gp
Hands 1; Bulk L
This satirical play by Amalia Wraxton was published 
in 4710 ar. Its controversial content, depicting the 
eponymous queen as the lover of Asmodeus and a co-
conspirator in the death of Aroden, caused an uproar that 
led to violent suppression and a defiant uprising. The play 
has since been banned and can be found only among the 
secret collections of art connoisseurs. If you own a copy 
of this play, you can publicly perform parts of Abrogail I as 
a downtime activity with a successful DC 19 Performance 
check. This activity lasts four hours including setup, 
rehearsal, and attracting a crowd, and you can’t perform 
this play again in this settlement for a week.
Critical Success As success, but you gain 2 Uprising 
Points.
Success The people are roused by your performance. You 
gain 1 Uprising Point.
Failure The authorities crack down on rebellious activity, 
stopping you from performing in this settlement again 
for 1 month.
Critical Failure As failure, but the people are intimidated 
and you lose 1 Uprising Point.
Development: The PCs can now recruit Ievis to 
write copper dalliances with anti-Cheliax content to 
rally readers against the government, earning them 
2 Uprising Points. The first is called Breaking Hell 
for Her.
CHILDREN’S CHARITY
The blue ribbon was a brainchild of Tobmer Qinro, a 
petty thief who rehabilitated himself after a revelation 
that caring for Isger’s orphans was his higher 
purpose. He hoped the ribbon would become a status 
symbol and raise gold to build orphanages across the 
Love Sting Sign

===== Page 73 =====
72
country, but it largely failed. Tobmer made just enough 
to buy a small building, where he raised a handful of 
children on his own. Angry about Elidir’s stinginess, 
Tobmer took on the moniker Father Kindness 
(disillusioned male aiuvarin thief 5) and 
trained his charges to be con artists and 
thieves. He dubbed his nascent thieves’ 
guild the Children’s Charity and three 
decades later, his now-grown charges leave 
blue ribbons at the scenes of their crime as 
a (largely overlooked) message that their 
stolen prizes are what Elidir’s less fortunate 
are due.
After learning about the blue 
ribbon, a PC can attempt a DC 19 
Elidir Lore or Underworld Lore 
check or a DC 21 Society check to Recall 
Knowledge to know the ribbon’s history 
and the former orphanage’s location. If that fails, they 
can attempt a DC 19 Diplomacy check to Gather 
Information, with the following results.
Success The PC learns the origins of the blue ribbon and 
the location of the former orphanage.
Failure As success, but the PC’s inquiries make their way 
to the Children’s Charity. The thieves become wary (see 
Wariness, below).
Critical Failure As failure, but the thieves are already on 
high alert when the PCs arrive.
H. House of Found Family
The PCs can easily find the old House of Found 
Family orphanage in a rundown area of the city, 
which uses the map on page 66. Its ceilings are 10 
feet high and the walls are wooden slats with doors 
of reinforced wood. The exterior door is locked, but 
can be opened with three successful DC 20 Thievery 
checks to Pick the Lock. The interior doors are 
typically unlocked unless otherwise noted; if they’re 
locked, they can also be opened with three successful 
DC 20 Thievery checks. Only Father Kindness has 
a key—he expects his charges to be able to let 
themselves in and out without one. The windows 
are all lined with iron bars close enough together 
to keep out anything Small or larger. Wooden slat 
shutters are usually opened during the day to let in 
light, but closed at night for warmth and security. An 
everlight crystal hangs in a hooded lantern in each 
room, providing all the rooms bright illumination 
at night or when the shutters are closed, unless 
someone closes the lantern.
The PCs can spend a day staking out the 
orphanage to get a better sense of comings and 
goings. With a successful DC 19 Perception check, 
their observations reveal that there are typically 
four thieves in the building at all times (plus Father 
Kindness, but they don’t have a chance to observe 
him); on a critical success, they also realize 
that when multiple thieves come or go from 
the front door, they do so one at a time, 
with each fully descending or ascending 
the stairs before the next follows (this 
is to avoid the trap in area H1). The PC 
must also attempt a DC 19 Stealth check 
to Avoid Notice to avoid raising suspicions 
among the thieves’ guild. On a failure, the 
thieves become wary; on a critical failure, 
or if the thieves are already wary, they 
instead are on high alert.
Wariness: If the thieves are wary, 
they gain a +1 circumstance bonus to 
all initiative rolls and the PCs take a –1 
penalty to their Perception and Stealth checks if 
they try to stake out the orphanage. If the thieves 
are on high alert, in addition to the effects of 
being wary, they close the wooden shutters on the 
windows, and use Stealth for their initiatives. If the 
thieves become aware of the PCs’ presence in the 
orphanage through combat or an alarm, they go on 
high alert, which they also do if the PCs leave the 
area to recover. Once they go on high alert, they 
remain in that status throughout this adventure.
While the Children’s Charity members want to 
defend their home, they place a higher priority on 
their lives. When they’re reduced to 25% of their Hit 
Points they try to escape, either out the front entrance 
or the secret door on the second floor.
H1. FRONT ENTRANCE	
TRIVIAL 4
Stairs lead to a landing in front of a weathered door with 
a broken brass knocker hanging from a single nail. The 
plate is a cherub’s face, though it’s badly dented where 
the clapper hits its smile.
The exterior door is locked at all times.
Hazard: Father Kindness installed a trap here when 
the orphanage became a thieves’ guild headquarters. 
The thieves avoid it by only entering one at a time.

dealing 2d8+5 piercing damage to all creatures standing 
on the landing or stairs (DC 25 basic Reflex save). On 
a failure, the creature takes a –5 status penalty to its 
Speed for 1 hour; on a critical failure it’s also clumsy 1.
Reward: If the PCs bypass the trap without setting 
it off, award them 40 XP.
H2. DINING ROOM	
MODERATE 4
A wooden table runs the length of this room, its surface 
scratched and marred. Mismatched chairs line the table.
Creatures: Unless the guild is wary or on high alert, 
two members can be found here helping themselves 
to a snack. If the PCs catch them unawares, they 
shout in alarm (putting the guild on high alert), draw 
their weapons, and attack. If they can, they flee into 
the rec room (area H4), where they attempt to use 
the hazards to their advantage. If the guild is already 
wary or on high alert, these thieves are instead in the 
rec room.
CHILDREN’S CHARITY PILFERERS (2)	
CREATURE 4
Burglar (Pathfinder NPC Core 20)
Initiative Perception +10 (Stealth +12)
H3. KITCHEN
The smell of a meat stew fills this room, coming from a 
large pot hung over a fireplace in the far corner. A small 
butcher’s block table fills the center of the kitchen, and 
pots, pans, knives, and other cooking implements hang 
from the walls.
Treasure: A large amount of stolen silverware worth 
40 gp can be found here, along with a low-grade silver 
filcher’s fork.
H4. REC ROOM	
TRIVIAL 4
Several training dummies with painted faces resembling 
goblins and Isgeri army soldiers stand in this large room, 
holding wooden swords and shields. Faded paintings on the 
wall show children battling giant spiders and river bandits.
Father Kindness first entertained and then later 
trained his charges in this area.
Creatures: This room is empty if the guild is not 
wary or on high alert; otherwise the Children’s 
Charity pilferers in the dining room (area H2) 
wait here. One lurks at the foot of the stairs, just 
out of sight, waiting for anyone to enter. The other 
waits in the southeast corner, hoping to lure an 
intruder into the hazards. Their presence makes this 
a moderate encounter.
Hazards: The training dummies work as traps for 
the unwary. The Practice Guard’s Grasp is in the area 
marked T1 and the Disarming Dummy is in the area 
marked T2. The Children’s Charity members are 
familiar with the traps and don’t trigger them even 
when adjacent.

H5. ORPHANS’ DORMITORY	
LOW 4
Faded paintings on the walls of this room depict a 
mountain scene, a dark forest, a city, and a verdant field. 
Several neatly made bunk beds occupy the center of the 
chamber and fine rugs cover the floor between them. Two 
small chests sit at the head and foot of each bed.

The thieves have used this dorm since childhood. The 
rooms are otherwise largely bare of adornment other 
than the bunk beds, stolen rugs and murals depicting 
scenery around Isger. A secret door, which can be 
discovered with a successful DC 19 Perception check, 
opens to the outside where the thieves can Climb down 
the side of the building if they need to escape.
Creatures: Two thieves are in this room. If they are 
unaware of the PCs, they’re awake but relaxing in bed. 
If the guild is on high alert, they wait to ambush anyone 
who comes up the stairs. One hides in the northeastern 
corner of the room, while the other hides between the 
western bunk beds. In addition, Father Kindness waits 
just outside his room (area H8); his presence makes 
this a severe encounter. After using ranged weapons 
from hiding, the thieves attempt to flank enemies to 
use their sneak attack.

H6. STOREROOM
The shelves of this room contain bedding, cleaning 
supplies, and other such sundries. Hidden under the 
obvious items is guild equipment, which can be found 
with a successful DC 19 Perception check to Search.
Treasure: The items here include an elite disguise 
kit, 2 lesser elixirs of life, a shacklebreaker (page 212), 
and an infiltrator thieves’ toolkit.
H7. BATHROOM
The shared bathroom has two tubs fed with rainwater from 
spigots in the wall. A shelf on the back wall holds soap and 
several bottles of perfumed oils.
Hidden in the base of the tubs are several secret 
compartments, where the guild keeps its stolen money. 
A PC who Searches the room can discover it with a 
successful DC 19 Perception check.
Treasure: The hidden chambers contain stolen 
noble crests worth 30 gp.
H8. FATHER KINDNESS’S BEDROOM	MODERATE 4
Children’s drawings hang on the rough wooden walls in this 
room, contrasting with several marble busts and golden 
statuettes on the bureau. A lush bearskin rug covers the 
floor in front of a large canopy bed.
Father Kindness’s private quarters are furnished 
with stolen items from his guild’s activities and 
mementos from the orphans’ childhood. The door to 
this room remains locked at all times, and the guild 
members all know better than to attempt to enter 
without permission.
Creatures: Father Kindness is alone in this room 
unless the guild is on high alert, in which case he can 
be found outside the orphans’ dormitory. If he hears 
combat from the dormitory, he activates the trap on 
his door (if it wasn’t already activated), draws his 
weapon, and moves to the door to limit his opponents 
to fighting him one-on-one. If reduced to 25% of his 
Hit Points, he attempts to flee, but if unable, he throws 
down his weapon and cries for mercy.
Hazard: If the thieves are wary, Father Kindness 
activates the trap on the main door to blind any 
intruders.

Elidir Events
While the PCs plot rebellion, they 
face a deeply divided city inhabited 
by wealthy, self-interested elites 
who wield power under Cheliax’s 
yoke, and the downtrodden masses 
that make up the bulk of the population. 
The following events occur in no particular 
order during this part of the adventure. Use 
them to emphasize the inequity of the current 
regime and power structure in Elidir.
EVENT: A POOR DEATH
Life in Isger is difficult for those without money, and 
that’s no less true in Elidir despite the riches that pass 
through the capital. Among those down on their luck 
is Padisco (stubborn male human war veteran 3), 
an old soldier whose legs were badly injured in the 
Goblinblood War and currently survives by begging 
for coins. He’s crossing the street in front of the PCs 
when his crutches slide on a patch of ice under the 
snow, leaving him sprawled on the ground just as a 
speeding carriage approaches. If the PCs want to save 
him, they have only moments to react.
Allow PCs to determine what approach to take 
for a rescue, such as pulling Padisco to safety in the 
nick of time with a successful DC 19 Athletics check, 
redirecting the carriage with a DC 17 Driving Lore 
check, or a DC 19 Intimidation check or Nature check 
to Command an Animal. A PC could also try to stop 
the carriage with a DC 19 Crafting or Thievery check 
to jam something into the spokes of the wheel.
If no PC succeeds, the carriage tramples poor Padisco, 
leaving him at dying 2 but giving the PCs opportunities 
to save him by using Battle Medicine, alchemy, or 
magic. If any PC critically fails in their attempt, they are 
also trampled by the carriage and take 2d8 bludgeoning 
damage (DC 19 basic Reflex save).
Reward: If the PCs save Padisco’s life, award them 
30 XP and 1 Uprising Point. Padisco promises to help 
them any way he can.
EVENT: WHO’S LAUGHING NOW?	
LOW 4
A small pack of young men points and laughs as a laborer 
struggles to get an enormous daeodon to move through 
the crowded streets. As the creature stops to relieve itself, 
the group’s apparent leader stoops down and picks up 
a rock, throwing it at the beast. “Look, two piles of dung in 
the street!” he yells, as his friends laugh raucously.
The pack of awful teenagers is led by Moccoviz Azri 
(spoiled male human brat 4), the son of a rich merchant 
the PCs meet at the gala. Spotting the laborer’s 
struggles with a daeodon he’s transporting 
through the city, Moccoviz exploits 
the situation for his own amusement. 
Unfortunately for him, the stone hits the 
beast, who reacts immediately, pulling 
its lead free and charging the teens. Let 
the PCs attempt a DC 19 Perception 
check; on a success, the PC realizes the 
handler intentionally dropped the lead 
and gains a +2 circumstance bonus to 
their initiative.
Creatures: The daeodon charges the teens, 
leaving them scattered and bruised, before turning its 
attention to the PCs, who are in the wrong place at the 
wrong time. The handler laughs as the daeodon charges 
the teens, but cries out in alarm as it attacks the PCs, 
calling for them to not kill it. A PC who saw the handler 
release the beast can spend a single action, which has 
the concentrate trait, to make a DC 21 Intimidation 
check to tell him to control it. On a success, he does so 
at the end of the round, or at the end of the PC’s turn on 
a critical success, ending the combat.
ELITE DAEODON	
CREATURE 5
Pathfinder Monster Core 6, 43
Initiative Perception +14
Development: If the PCs get the handler to control 
the daeodon, he mutters an apology and departs 
with the creature before Moccoviz can take out his 
anger on him. If they kill the beast, the handler looks 
distraught, blaming them for the punishment he’ll 
face. Dirty from his fall in the street, Moccoviz says 
it’s no less than the man deserves. The humiliated teen 
grudgingly thanks the PCs and tosses 1d6 sp on the 
ground for them as he departs.
EVENT: INJUSTICE IS SERVED	
LOW 4
A sudden harsh shout—“You there! Stop! It’s the Gyve 
for you!”—booms over the noise of the streets of Elidir 
as a guard patrol moves with practiced skill through the 
parting crowds.
Justice has little place in Elidir, where the rich get 
away with all manner of behavior, and the poor face 
 Lazybones Pendant

===== Page 77 =====
76
harsh repercussions for crimes they commit to 
survive. When a starving goblin urchin tries to 
steal from the PCs, they get the chance to 
experience this state of matters firsthand 
as a guard spots her and promises harsh 
consequences in the city’s notorious 
prison.
Ozney Cacklemouth (desperate young 
female goblin urchin –1) attempts to steal 
coins from a random PC. She attempts a 
single Thievery check with a +7 modifier 
against all the PCs’ Perception DCs. In the 
unlikely event she succeeds, the PCs 
might think the guards are coming 
for them, but it’s quickly clear that 
the guards have spotted Ozney and 
plan to drag her away to the Gyve. If the PCs 
didn’t learn about the Gyve earlier, they can attempt 
a DC 17 Elidir Lore or DC 19 Society Lore check to 
Recall Knowledge to know it’s the city’s main prison, 
where suspects are tortured to get confessions and 
even minor crimes can result in forced labor (they 
can also ask the guards, who inform them it’s the 
city’s prison).
Ozney begs for forgiveness, saying she simply 
wanted a few coins to buy food, but the guards are 
unmoved. The PCs can attempt to talk the guards 
into releasing Ozney, though they’re hesitant about 
“letting a criminal go free.” Convincing them 
requires succeeding at a DC 17 Legal Lore or DC 
19 Diplomacy check to Request that the guards let 
her go, or DC 19 Intimidation check to Coerce them 
into doing so. If the PCs fail (or don’t intervene), 
the guards begin dragging the sobbing goblin away. 
The PCs can fight the guards to stop them, but 
warn them that doing so will gain them Suppression 
Points.
Creatures: The three guards fight back if the PCs 
initiate combat. Ozney hides nearby if combat breaks 
out, but if you need statistics for her, you can use the 
urchin (NPC Core 40).

offers to help if they need anything; award the

The Gala
The gala is scheduled to take place one week 
after the PCs arrive in the city. Once they 
arrive at Reevesrest, read or paraphrase 
the following.
Floating balls of red and white light 
illuminate the great room of the mansion. 
Music performed by a string quartet on a 
stage in the western wing of the room fills the air over 
the sound of conversation. Many of the assembled guests 
wear costumes to evoke Hell—elaborate pieces with horns 
and other devilish features embellish fine silk and velvet 
dresses and suits—or armored Hellknights.
A curved grand staircase with painted balusters leads 
up to a landing and a walkway that stretches across the 
room. A few figures look down from above, but a pair of 
armed guards, dressed as devils complete with a false tail 
attached to their armor, stand guard at the foot of the 
stairs, preventing most people from ascending.
The gala, filled with the elite of Elidir as well as the 
guards and servants who care for them, takes place 
over six social rounds, each taking about an hour. 
During this time, the PCs should reach a deal with 
Quoster Thistlewait using the influence subsystem 
(GM Core 187). They can also meet other important 
people in attendance. Because the PCs must maintain 
their disguises, they can’t influence the NPCs to help 
the Hellbreakers League, but can win personal favor.
Influence Rounds: Let the PCs know they have at 
least six social rounds, as the party will likely last into 
the small hours of the night, leading up to the actual 
LARGER PARTIES
You might want to reduce the number of social 
rounds for groups with more than four PCs, who 
will find it much easier to accomplish their goals. 
For groups of five PCs, you may want to have five 
influence rounds, or just four for groups of six PCs. 
Events can be spread out over the evening, with 
one or two per influence round.

I. REEVESREST MANOR
Reevesrest is fully described in Chapter 5 (page 85), 
when the PCs have free rein to explore. For now, 
the party is largely confined to the great room (area 
I2) and grounds outside. PCs who wish to explore 
can enter areas including the library, dining room, 
gallery, and garden, but are restricted from other areas 
by guards and servants, who steer them back to the 
public rooms. The upstairs is fully off limits, and two 
guards stand at the bottom of the stairs in the great 
room, preventing access.
DRAMATIS PERSONAE
Some of the gala’s guests play a larger role in Chapters 
5 and 6. Below are the most prominent, of whom 
Quoster, Caeto, and Ezio are the most important to 
the adventure; feel free to add other guests as needed.
QUOSTER THISTLEWAIT	
CREATURE 4
UNIQUE
SMALL
HALFLING
HUMANOID
Male halfling Druman trader
Perception +8
Will +10
Discovery DC 17 Mercantile Lore, DC 21 
Perception or Performance, DC 19 Society
Influence Skills DC 19 Mercantile Lore, DC 21 
Diplomacy and Society, DC 24 Crafting
Influence 0 Quoster is undeterred 
from his demands for a lucrative 
trade deal. He agrees to help the 
Hellbreakers League, but the 
concessions prove onerous and—if 
the PCs win freedom for Isger—
unpopular. Reduce the Hellbreakers

Influence 2 The PCs persuade Quoster to 
accept reasonable terms beneficial to 
both sides. The Hellbreakers League gains

Influence 4 Quoster agrees to a deal that lets

Influence 6 Quoster’s bargain benefits him 
alongside Isger—the better the country 
does, the more Quoster profits. The Hellbreakers League 
gains 3 Reputation Points and Quoster immediately 
gives the PCs the devilwing badge.
Resistances Quoster plays the fool to get ahead, but 
disdains those who don’t see the truth. PCs who 
treat him as a fool or act foolish themselves take a –2 
circumstance penalty on checks to Influence him.
Weaknesses Quoster has a strong distaste for Cheliax due 
to its history of slavery and iron grip on the Conerica 
River trade routes. PCs who frame negotiations in terms 
of how it would hurt Cheliax gain a +2 circumstance 
bonus on Influence checks.
Background Growing up in Druma, Quoster realized how 
much better his life was than most halflings. While 
he sees his wealth as his birthright, he also knows it 
protects him. He’s devoted resources to helping causes 
he deems worthy, such as the Bellflower Network, but 
prioritizes those that benefit him personally.
Appearance Quoster is dressed in over-the-top finery, 
wearing a ruffled black blouse under a red velvet coat 
with long tails and golden fastenings. His fine leather 
boots curl up at the toes. He carries a silver cane with 
a large ruby. 
Personality Quoster is a shrewd merchant, which he hides 
behind a carefully cultivated image as a fop. He 
is remorseless in business, seeking to gain every 
advantage, and justifies his cutthroat attitude by 
using his resources to help those less fortunate.

the workers that make the city’s trade economy function. 
Their competence secures their position, and earns them 
invitations to galas like this one.
Appearance Sastoli stands out among the finely dressed 
elites in the worst way possible—they’re wearing plain 
dockworker’s clothes, except for a plush sarglagon 
draped around their shoulders as a conceit to the theme. 
Personality Sastoli is blunt and out of their 
element, breaking all manner of etiquette such 
as grabbing fistfuls of appetizers from servants, 
and delights in the quiet outrage of the elites 
who can’t kick them out.
Reward: For each influence threshold the 
PCs meet, award them 40 XP.
MINOR ATTENDEES
In addition to the NPCs who the PCs can 
Influence to befriend, there are several 
other NPCs they can interact with who 
play some role in later events at the 
gala or in its aftermath.
Ambassador Vrig (cautious male 
hobgoblin diplomat 4), a former 
officer in the Ironfang Legion, was 
sent to Isger to find allies for Oprak. 
He has largely given up that hope for lost, 
realizing that Hedvend has little ability to 
make any alliances without permission from 
Cheliax. He wears an Ironfang Legion uniform 
and is a dour presence that sees the party as a 
necessary part of his job, not an enjoyable one.
Fesimwyth “Fessy” Finwinkle (anxious female 
gnome cleric of Abadar 3) found her faith following 
the Goblinblood Wars as she tried to help rebuild 
her native town of Umok. She came to Elidir 
seeking help, only to become frustrated by the 
elite’s lack of concern about the areas outside the 
Conerica Straits. Despite this, she fears the 
Hellbreakers League’s disruptions will only 
make matters worse. Fessy was sent to the 
gala as a representative of her temple, since the local 
archbanker had no interest in attending. She’s wearing 
her usual religious garb of white and gold rather than a 
costume. She isn’t comfortable at the party and stands 
off by herself, but is happy for anyone to approach her. 
She’s eager to talk, and latches on to anyone who is 
kind to her.
Lezinia (status-seeking female human wannabe diva 
1)—one name only, and often said as though followed 
by an exclamation point—is dressed as finely as anyone 
at the party, in an outfit that likely cost enough to pay 
for a small family’s food and housing for a month. Her 
dress clearly evokes a gylou (Monster Core 91), with 
the ribbon tentacles that make up her skirt showing 
off her legs to good effect. Lezinia came to Isger at 
Hedvend’s invitation after catching his eye on one of 
his trips to Cheliax. It was an opportunity she couldn’t 
turn down—she’s not talented enough to gain the same 
level of opportunity in Cheliax, but in a backwater like 
Isger? She’s a big fish in a little pond. In conversation, 
Lezinia typically steers discussion to herself, her 
talents, and her stardom. Despite her very clear self-
interest, she’s not inherently cruel or callous like 
many of the Isgeri elite.
Merpelia Carafo (inconsiderate female human 
noble 1) is a typical Elidiran elite, content 
with the way life is in Isger, and incapable of 
understanding why anyone would rebel. 
Prattling on about whatever catches 
her attention, she just can’t understand 
why so many Isgeri are upset about 
their conditions. Surely if it were 
as bad as they claim, they would 
move to Elidir or somewhere else. If 
they can’t be bothered, then they’re 
either too lazy, or just exaggerating 
for attention. Merpelia wears a fine 
golden fur made from a rare cat 
found in the Menador Mountains 
over her blue silk sari imported 
from Vudra, and jewelry made 
of gold, duskwood, and rare 
gemstones. Her outfit is not 
on theme.
Rencelos Azri (greedy male human 
war profiteer 6) is one of the richest men 
in Elidir, thanks to being one of the Isgeri 
army’s primary suppliers of arms following his 
service in the Goblinblood Wars. He’s thrilled 
by the unrest since it means more demand 
for his services. Rencelos is dressed like 
a nessari (Monster Core 89), complete 
with spiked armor, wings taken from a 
Gala Guard

drake he hunted for the occasion, and a bare chest 
that shows off his aging, but still firm, physique. His 
conversations mostly consist of laughing at those who 
are poorer than him and lamenting that his son was 
nearly killed a few days ago by some fool who let 
loose a giant boar.
Gala Events
A number of events take place during the gala between 
social rounds. They occur in the following order, 
culminating in the False Flag event, which follows the 
final social round.
EVENT: A GAME OF MANTICORE
A small group of partygoers enjoys a game of 
manticore, which involves throwing darts at targets 
set up in a playing field, and the associated gambling 
on the manor grounds.
Snow has been cleared from a strip of the lawn on the 
manor grounds. Three painted straw targets are arranged 
on the field: a halfling twenty feet away, a goblin 
forty feet away, and a human peasant sixty 
feet away.
Any PCs are welcome to join in the game or place 
wagers. Each PC can wager up to 20 gp on someone 
to win the match or before an individual throw—up 
to 1 gp that someone will hit the halfling, 3 gp that 
someone will hit the goblin, and 5 gp that someone 
will hit the human target.
Running Manticore: Each participant gets six darts, 
which they throw at targets until each has used all their 
darts. Each target is AC 18, though throwers take penalties 
due to range for farther targets (–2 and –4, respectively). 
They get 1 point for hitting the closest target, 2 for the 
next target, or 3 for the farthest; on a critical hit, they 
hit the target’s head, and get double points. A player can 
also throw two darts at the same target at the same time. 
In this case, both Strikes take the multiple attack penalty. 
Each hit from a double-throw earns double points: 2, 4, 
or 6 for a hit, or 4, 8, or 12 for a critical hit. Using magic 
is technically not allowed, but most spectators find it 
amusing that someone would resort to such tactics for a 
game and will let subtle uses slide.
The contestants: Three other partygoers participate 
in the game. You can roll for each of their 
turns with the listed attack modifier, or 
simply use their usual score if you wish to 
speed the event along.
• Ambassador Vrig (attack modifier +8; usual 
score 8) is a talented warrior, but cautious. 
He uses his own darts, which he throws one 
at a time at the nearest target.
• Colonel Rithert (attack modifier +6; usual score 
6) chafes at xir lack of combat opportunities, and 
takes the opportunity to show xir skill. Xe throws 
twice at the goblin target before double-
throwing twice at the same target.
• Rencelos Azri (attack modifier +15, 
usual score 12) is a skilled combatant, but cares 
little about winning. He throws all his darts 
two at a time at the farthest target. He laughs 
uproariously at every hit (his or other players’) 
and makes up stories about the target deserving 
it.
Social Round: A PC who participates in the game 
gains an additional social round they can use to 
Influence Colonel Rithert.
Treasure: If a PC outscores Ambassador Vrig, he 
congratulates them and offers one of his personal low-
grade silver darts as a prize. If multiple PCs outscore 
him, he offers it to the highest scorer.

One or more PCs notice a disgusted-looking servant,

Ezio threw against the wall in disgust

Ezio, he sheepishly admits it and

to the garlic in the dish, a clue to 
his true nature. Ezio then takes the 
opportunity to hobnob, granting the PCs 
he speaks with an additional social round

EVENT: FALSE FLAG	
MODERATE 4
The gala was supposed to conclude with 
Hedvend VI’s announcement, but Ezio has a 
surprise planned—an attack by guards posing 
as Hellbreakers League revolutionaries! The 
attack is not only intended to cause chaos by 
killing important Elidirans and whipping up fury 
against the Hellbreakers, it’s a distraction from Ezio’s 
simultaneous murder of Hedvend himself.
Shortly before the attacks, Ezio’s accomplice, 
Lefranek Meyal (zealous female human agent of 
Urgathoa 4), lures three guards to his side to be 
dominated and to recover the false Hellbreakers 
League flag she’s prepared for the charade. Make a 
secret DC 21 Perception check for each PC—on a 
success, the PC notices the guards left their posts, 
presumably to escort Hedvend to the party at last, 
giving them a +1 circumstance bonus to their initiative 
roll when combat begins. On a critical success, the PC 
also notices the guards return without the steward; 
due to the suspicious behavior, the PC is quickened on 
the first round of combat, and can use the extra action 
to Interact to draw a weapon or other item.
Read or paraphrase the following.
The music comes to a sudden stop as a woman’s harsh 
yell silences the party. “Enough! For too long have you 
and Hedvend been Cheliax’s lapdog and neglected our 
beautiful Isger! We shall remove your devilish taint from 
our country! It’s time for everyone here to die, in the name 
of the Hellbreakers League!” She waves an unfamiliar 
flag depicting a flaming sword piercing Asmodeus’s red 
pentagram as her masked compatriots attack.
The stunning announcement ends the gala’s 
festivities and concludes the chapter, continuing in 
Chapter 5.

free-flowing, with PCs able to pursue various leads

GALA CROWD
HAZARD 4
UNIQUE
COMPLEX
ENVIRONMENTAL
Stealth –10 (+12 initiative)
Description The panicked crowd of gala attendees reacts to 
the unexpected attack.
Disable DC 19 Intimidation, DC 21 Diplomacy, or DC 24 
Athletics to get guests to move out of harm’s way; four 
total successes across all skills are required to disable 
the hazard
AC 18; Fort +11, Ref +11
HP 60; Weaknesses area 5
Panic at the Gala [reaction] Trigger A creature rolls initiative; Effect 
The crowd stampedes, dealing 4d6 bludgeoning damage 
to anyone on the great room floor (DC 20 basic Reflex 
save), then rolls initiative.
Routine (1 action) The crowd reacts in one of the following 
ways, determined by a d12 die roll:
•	 1–2 Hunker Down: The crowd freezes in fear. It 
provides lesser cover to all creatures in the great 
room for 1 round.
•	 3–4 Run!: Determine a random direction. Each creature 
in the area must succeed at a DC 21 Fortitude save or 
be moved 10 feet in that direction. On a critical failure, 
they’re also knocked prone. This is forced movement.
•	 5–6 Hysteria: The crowd’s dread is contagious. Each 
creature in the area must attempt a DC 21 Will save or 
become frightened 1 (frightened 2 on a critical failure). 
This is an emotion, fear, and mental effect.
•	 7–8 Wailing: The cries make it hard to concentrate. 
For 1 round, any creature in the area that attempts 
an action with the concentrate trait must succeed at 
a DC 4 flat check or the action is disrupted. This is an 
auditory effect.
•	 9–10 Crushing Press: Members of the crowd shove and 
push, trying to find a way to safety. Each creature in 
the area takes 2d8+5 bludgeoning damage (DC 21 basic 
Fortitude save).
•	 11–12 Wild Dismay: The chaos is overwhelming. Each 
creature in the area must attempt a DC 21 Will save or 
become confused for 1 round. This is an emotion and 
mental effect.
Development: If any PCs are dying following the 
battle with the false Hellbreakers, immediately resolve 
recovery checks or actions to save them, though they 
won’t have time immediately to Treat Wounds or use 
other exploration activities.
DEATH NOTICE
Once everyone is in a stable condition, read or 
paraphrase the following.
The tromp of heavy boots cuts short the continuing sound 
of screams and crying, silencing everything but the moans 
of the wounded. As armor-clad guards take up positions at 
all of the exits to the room, a Hellknight in full plate mail—
Paralictor Caeto Vulaunex—moves to the top of the stairs. 
The knights look slightly battered, as if they’ve just had their 
own battle.
Caeto looks down and calls out: “Ladies and gentlemen, I 
regret to inform you that Hedvend VI, steward of all Isger, 
has been murdered!” Gasps fill the room. “You are all under 
arrest until we get to the bottom of this. Remain in this room 
for your own safety. Certain magical defenses have activated 
with the attack, so leaving the manor could be dangerous. In 
addition, the guards outside will assume anyone who tries to 
leave is complicit in this heinous crime, and they will be dealt 
with accordingly.”
It should be clear to the PCs that trying to fight their 
way out past Caeto’s forces would almost certainly be 
a fatal mistake. The PCs have about an hour to recover 
before events conspire to force them to take action. 
Fessy approaches and offers to heal them if needed 
(she has four 2nd-rank heal spells in her divine font 
and offers to cast them as the PCs need, either now or 
later during this chapter). PCs also gain access to any 
benefits they receive from becoming level 5, such as an 
alchemist’s field discovery, additional spell slots, etc.
The other guests are in shock at the events of the last 
hour. They largely huddle in small groups, whispering 
about the events and what they might mean for Isger. 
Who will rule Isger going forward is a big topic among 
the more politically inclined as Hedvend VI had no 
clear successor.

The cast of this chapter is largely the same as in Chapter

CHAPTER ORGANIZATION
This chapter follows the PCs as they investigate 
Hedvend’s murder and has two different types 
of encounters, inquiries (starting page 88 in The 
Game’s Afoot) and plot events (starting page 92 in 
The Plot Thickens). Inquiries are encounters where 
the PCs investigate and learn information about 
the murder while plot events show what else is 
happening in the manor during the investigation.

Steward Hedvend VI is dead, long unlive Steward 
Hedvend VI. In the immediate aftermath of Hedvend’s 
death, Caeto had his body moved to his bedroom 
and left to lie there in a respectful manner until his 
murder is solved and he can be properly buried. 
Unknown to Caeto, Ezio Gaeta transformed Hedvend 
into a vampire by using a unique talisman Illcayna 
created with her warshard to expedite the usual three-
day transformation process. Hedvend is partially 
under Ezio’s control and being used as a weapon to 
take out more of Elidir’s elite. However, the rapid 
transformation process has left him ravenously hungry 
and he is also feeding on random innocents in the 
mansion. When he’s not actively hunting, Hedvend 
climbs out of the manor and hides at Ezio’s command.
Caeto Vulaunex enlists the PCs’ help once a second 
body is discovered in the manor. Already impressed by 
the PCs for their fight in the great room, he knows they 
aren’t responsible for the second death because they are 
under guard at the time and concludes they are likely 
not responsible for Hedvend’s either. Caeto serves as an 
ally at this point, and PCs should be allowed to believe 
that he could, in the right circumstances, end up as a 
long-term friend in their struggle for Isger. While he is 
already privately planning how he will fill the vacuum 
left by Hedvend’s death, he remains interested in the 
investigation in the manor and checks in with the PCs 
on their progress. He can also be used to help push the 
investigation forward if needed, giving you a chance to 
lead players to hints if they appear stuck or frustrated.
Ezio Gaeta fully expected the mansion to be 
locked down after Hedvend’s murder, which he saw 
as a perfect opportunity to cause more death. He 
assumes the Hellbreakers League will take the blame 
for the night’s events, leaving him free to continue 
as Urgathoa’s agent among Isger’s new leadership. 
Ezio has multiple contingency plans ready including 
pinning the blame for the murder on Lezinia, whom 
he Dominated early in the evening. When the PCs get 
involved, he tries to befriend them so he can stay fully 
informed of their investigation and manipulate them 
as needed. He doesn’t reveal his true self until he is 
absolutely forced to.
I. Reevesrest
The steward’s home is made of fine wood, with 
reinforced doors, which are unlocked during the gala. 
The first floor is 15 feet high (except for parts of the 
great room that are open to the building’s roof, 25 feet 
up), and the second floor is 10 feet high. Most rooms 
have one or more fireplaces or braziers going to keep 
them warm against the cold Abadius weather. The 
windows are closed with wooden shutters, which are 
locked with a simple bar from the inside; from outside, 
the DC to Force them Open is 22. Magical lights 
provide bright light in the entire household. Below 
are basic descriptions of the areas; note that several of 
them have more specific details related to the mystery 
of Hedvend VI’s murder and the false Hellbreakers 
described later in the chapter.
I1: Vestibule: The dark wood of the formal entrance 
is engraved with numerous nearly invisible runes, 
which trigger magical traps. They are all deactivated 
during the gala.
I2. Great room: The stewards of Isger built the great 
room to impress visitors. The opulent chamber features 
high ceilings across much of the eastern portion of 
the room. A stage offers a place for musicians and 
other entertainers to perform. A grand staircase with 
painted balustrades leads to the second floor. The 
walls are painted with murals supposedly depicting 
Isger’s greatness.
I3. Library: The library, like the great room, is 
designed to impress visitors. Four of its walls are lined 
with shelves reaching to the ceiling, each filled with 
books. Ladders on rollers make it easy to reach the 
books on the upper shelves. The books are carefully 
curated to be acceptable to Chelaxian tastes.	
I4. Privy: Reevesrest contains several privies. The 
upstairs privies also contain bathtubs.
I5. Statue hall: This room has a statue of a stern-
looking woman wearing the amulet denoting Isger’s 
stewards. A plaque identifies her as Adraldine I, the 
first steward of Isger.
I6. Art gallery: The art gallery features valuable 
art and artifacts collected by stewards over the 
centuries. Large paintings hang on the wall showing 
scenes supposedly from Isger’s history, though 
designed to convey modern messages: the original 
Isgeri tribe surrendering to Taldor’s army, and later 
Cheliax coming to Isger’s rescue during the Even-
Tongued Conquest.
I7. Conservatory: Plants, many of them edible, 
grow in barrels in this greenhouse, which remains 
WHERE’S QUOSTER?
While Quoster is an important part of Chapter 4 
and plays a role again in Chapter 6, he has little 
to do in this chapter and is not a target of Ezio or 
Hedvend. He tries to keep his distance from the 
PCs so as not to tip off anyone to his deal with 
the Hellbreakers League and urges them to do the 
same if they approach him.

warm and moist thanks to druidic magic arranged 
by an early steward. Wide windows let in the light

I8. Kitchen: The well-stocked, well-equipped kitchen 
is designed to provide almost anything the steward or 
their guests could want at any time of day or night. A 
fire always burns here, and usually two or three chefs 
and bakers are cooking or ready to cook. That number 
increases to a half dozen during events like the gala.
I9. Storeroom: Reevesrest contains several well-
organized store rooms. On the first floor, the one 
attached to the conservatory contains gardening 
supplies, and one attached to the kitchen contains 
cooking staples (though most goods are brought in fresh 
daily). Upstairs, a larger storeroom contains linens.
I10. Dining room: A silver chandelier drips with 
crystals. The massive table is an incredible slab of black 
marble resting on an elaborate duskwood stand with 
feet carved to resemble a dragon’s. Duskwood chairs 
evoke Isger’s role in the Inner Sea, with a trading ship 
carved into the headrest and the armrests evoking the 
waves of the Conerica River.
I11. Servants’ parlor: This room serves as an 
entrance and gathering place for the manor’s servants. 
Shelves along the walls contain fine dishes, silverware 
and other such serving items.
I12. Servant’s quarters: Several servants—the 
majordomo, head chef, and chamberlain—live full-
time in the manor, staying in these small rooms. Each 
contains a bed, dresser and other personal effects.
I13. Guard post: This is the headquarters for 
the steward’s personal guard, who also take care 
of Reevesrest’s security. A table and several chairs 
let guards relax when they are not on duty but still 
required to stay available in case of emergency.
I14. Guard quarters: The heads of the steward’s 
guard live on the premises, in these rooms. Each 
contains a bed, as well as a chest containing their 
personal items.
I15: Armory: The armory contains a number of 
weapons of all types for the guards’ use.
I16. Upstairs landing: The grand staircase in the 
great room leads to the upper landing, which runs 
almost the entire length of the manor. The eastern 
portion is open so the steward and his closest guests 
can participate and be seen during events without 
having to mingle with those of lesser importance. 
Painted balustrades at about waist height for a human 
provide some minimal protection from a fall.
I17. Guest room: This impressive, opulent bedroom 
serves personal guests of the steward. It contains a large 
canopied bed and numerous dressers. Padded benches 
line the northern seating area, where guests can take 
in a view of the entire city through the floor-to-ceiling 
windows. An attached room (I17a) contains beds for a 
pair of servants or guards permitted to guests.
I18. Game room: This room offers a private, less 
formal area for the steward to relax with guests. It 
contains a game table with built-in drawer. A mounted 
cabinet on the wall contains pipes, tobacco, bottles of 
liquor, and crystal goblets.
I19. Hedvend’s bedroom: Hedvend’s bedroom is his 
primary living space. It includes a large, comfortable 
bed, dressers and chests for his clothing, and other 
personal items. Personal trophies, gifts, and other 
items celebrating him and his governorship of Isger 
hang on the walls.
I20. Private dining room: The upstairs dining room 
offers a smaller area where the steward can eat. Padded 
chairs surround a duskwood table, formal enough to 
not offend any guests here, but also more comfortable 
for a steward and their family to dine together.
I21. Private study: The private study contains 
Hedvend VI’s personal papers, including correspondence 
with other rulers and various other matters of state.

THE A-HA MOMENT!
One of the most iconic moments in a good murder 
mystery is when the intrepid detective puts 
together all the assorted clues—the seemingly 
obvious facts and innocuous observations—
to suddenly realize who the culprit is (the 
investigator class plays heavily on this very idea). 
While a novel author has free rein to create that 
moment, it might not be as obvious for players 
in a tabletop roleplaying game. Some players 
who are attuned to such stories might pick up 
on some of the clues in the ensuing pages and 
piece them together. But for those who aren’t, 
you can offer skill checks to help the PCs make 
those connections—suggested skills and DCs are 
listed with many clues. (If the PCs are having 
fun with the mystery, you could even make the 
checks secretly, noting any success, and doling 
out realizations to the players later if they get 
stuck, or at dramatic moments.)
Another option is to have Caeto stop in to check 
up on the PCs and point out something they might 
be missing, though take care not to let him steal 
the spotlight as he’s busy preparing to declare 
martial law over Isger.

I23. Boudoir: This private bedroom in the
