several months ago.
THE GAME’S AFOOT
After about an hour, a nervous-looking 
servant approaches the PCs, informing them that 
Caeto Vulaunex wishes to speak with them. If they 
agree, she escorts them upstairs to the study (area I21), 
which Caeto has appropriated for his own uses as it 
gives him privacy, but also lets him easily step out to 
look down on what’s happening in the great room. If 
the PCs refuse to accompany her, Caeto comes down 
to ask them to meet with him. If they still refuse, he 
promises the PCs that no harm will come to them 
and they are not in trouble. Read or paraphrase the 
following:
“I’m told you were responsible for stopping those 
Hellbreakers from killing everyone at the gala. That, 
along with a new development, has convinced me you 
were not involved with this slaying. Given that, and your 
obvious skill, I would like to ask you to investigate what is 
happening here. I thought there was likely one or two more 
conspirators among the partygoers who I would uncover, 
but this new development…”
His expression darkens. “Someone, or something, killed 
one of my guards. I’m convinced there’s more going on 
here. However, following Hedvend’s death, I need to 
make sure the city and country are secure. My guards are 
talented, but they are not investigators. It would appear 
you are my best option. If you agree, you will be allowed 
free movement to investigate, though you will still not be 
allowed to leave the manor grounds until these murders 
are solved and the captor killed or in custody.”
This is an opportunity for the PCs to get themselves 
out of this situation and uncover the mystery of the 
false Hellbreakers. They could even earn favor with 
the apparent new leader of Isger, which would be a 
major opportunity for the League. Once the PCs agree, 
they have four likely initial approaches to begin 
solving the mystery: the false Hellbreakers, 
the murder scene, Hedvend’s corpse, and the 
slain guard. Give players the opportunity 
to decide what to do first, but Caeto can 
suggest any or all of those if they need help 
getting started. He tells the PCs to keep him 
informed of any developments, and that he 
will try to provide anything they need 
to help them solve the crimes. The 
inquiries below detail avenues 
of investigation the PCs might 
undertake, including ones that 
develop after the four initial 
approaches.
Inquiry: False Hellbreakers
Caeto had the false Hellbreakers taken to 
the guard post (area I13). Survivors are bound hand 
and foot with good-quality manacles. Caeto gives PCs 
free rein in their investigation except that the guards 
can’t be freed. Caeto has a single scroll of talking 
corpse available, which he allows the PCs to use if all 
of the guards are dead (Fessy can cast the spell if no 
PC is able to).
The lower-level fakes, including those that attacked 
the Hellknights, were guards that Ezio magically 
dominated. A PC can Coerce them into answering 
questions with an Intimidation check against their DC 
15 Will save. If the PCs attempt to use talking corpse 
on any deceased guards, they answer willingly and 
truthfully. Each tells the same tale: Lefranek brought 
them to the private dining room, supposedly to meet 
with Hedvend on a minor matter. Instead, they found 
a red-cloaked individual there. The last thing each 
remembers was looking into the figure’s eyes and 
feeling that they needed to obey their commands.
The leader of the false Hellbreaker attack, Lefranek 
Meyal, is an Urgathoan cultist who infiltrated 
Hedvend’s guards at Illcayna’s instructions. She has 
more knowledge of the plot, though she’s unaware of 
Ezio’s identity and his role in events. Before the gala, 
she received a coded message that instructed her to 
bring her fellow guards to Hedvend’s private dining 
room. There, Ezio cast dominate on them and sent 
them to kill as many guests at the gala as they could 
with Lefranek as their willing leader.
If alive, Lefranek is largely uncooperative during any 
attempts to get information, though the PCs can try 
several different methods. PCs can attempt to Coerce 
her with a DC 19 Intimidation check, but they take

person in a red cloak, but truthfully says she doesn’t 
know who it was.

finding them less intimidating than the Hellknights, 
and nervously informs them that he saw Lefranek 
leave a supply closet during the gala. Following his tip, 
the PCs uncover a staff of the dead and an intricately 
carved onyx skull for ritual practices worth 200 gp.
Reward: If the PCs get any information from any 
of the false Hellbreakers, award them 30 XP. Award 
them an additional 30 XP if they learn of Lefranek’s 
allegiance to Urgathoa.
Inquiry: Scene of the Crime
A solid wooden door hangs off its hinges, revealing a 
stately game room. The taxidermied heads of several 
monsters look down from the walls while the smoldering 
remains of a fire burn in the ornate fireplace.
An ivory and mahogany game table fills much of the 
space, with a half dozen well-cushioned chairs arranged 
around it. One chair at the head of the table is overturned 
and speckled with blood. In front of the overturned chair, 
a hand of cards is laid out face up on the table and a single 
key sits nearby. A second hand of cards rests face down in 
front of an adjacent seat.
Hedvend VI was in his game room passing the time 
before his grand entrance to the gala when he met with 
Ezio and his demise. After killing the steward, Ezio 
locked the door and slipped out using Mist Form. He 
returned to the party downstairs, where he waited for the 
inevitable discovery. A short time later, Caeto searched 
for the steward after the false Hellbreaker attacks and 
broke the door down, discovering Hedvend’s body.
The room offers a number of clues for observant 
PCs. Some players might notice these or ask 
specifically about these topics but if not, 
point out the clues to PCs who succeed at a 
listed skill check.
•  DC 18 Games Lore, DC 20 Society: Two 
sets of cards at the table suggest Hedvend 
knew his killer and was not surprised at their 
presence.
•  DC 20 Athletics or Perception: There are 
no signs of a struggle in the room, indicating 
that Hedvend was somehow subdued or that 
he had no chance to react to the attack 
(Ezio dominated Hedvend).
•  DC 20 Medicine or Perception: There 
are a few drops of blood in one of the 
chairs, but not enough to indicate a major wound 
(Ezio drank most of the blood).
•	 DC 20 Crafting or Thievery: The key is on 
the table next to where Hedvend was sitting, 
indicating that the room was locked from the 
inside and the killer was then able to leave the 
locked room.
In addition to the clues above that PCs can see with 
no real difficulty, they can Search the room. A PC who 
succeeds at a DC 18 Perception check notices a small 
brass hourglass talisman filled with a black sand under 
the table. This was a grave time talisman that Illcayna 
created with her warshard to expedite the process of 
transforming Hedvend into Ezio’s vampire servitor. 
Ezio affixed the talisman to Hedvend’s body but it was 
inadvertently knocked off by Caeto’s men when they 
moved the steward, leaving the talisman still intact 
and Hedvend in a state of near-feral perpetual hunger.
A PC who closely examines the hourglass can 
attempt a DC 20 Nature check; on a success they 
realize the sand is actually onyx. With a successful DC 
22 Religion check to Recall Knowledge, a PC is aware 
that onyx is used in rituals to create undead. A PC can 
also attempt to Identify Magic on the talisman with a 
DC 22 Religion check; on a success, the PC understands 
the item would affect the flow of time on a body, 
likely to preserve it or accelerate its decomposition. 
Note any critical success on this check—when the PCs 
start realizing a vampire is involved in the murders, 
the PC realizes the talisman could also make it as if 
three nights had passed in an instant, the time typically 
required for a creature to be buried in the earth before 
turning into a vampire servitor.

Treasure: Underneath a table is an onyx idol of 
Urgathoa worth 10 gp. 
Reward: If the PCs discover the grave time talisman, 
award them 30 XP. Award them an additional 30 XP

Inquiry: Hedvend’s Body
Hedvend’s body was taken to his private quarters, 
where it was laid on his bed. A single Hellknight 
stands guard at the ornate double doors that lead 
into the room, but she allows the PCs to enter freely. 
Unfortunately, the PCs’ efforts to examine the body 
are doomed to failure: Hedvend’s body is missing!
Thick velvet maroon curtains cover the walls and 
a bearskin rug covers the floor of this luxurious 
grand bedroom. A glaive seemingly made of 
folded silver hangs as a trophy above the fireplace, 
where flames dance in a cold breeze. A drift of snow 
and a melting puddle both grow beneath an open 
window. Against the southern wall, a neatly made 
canopy bed shows no sign of an occupant except for a 
slight indent in the heavy quilt.
A closer examination of the scene reveals what 
appears to be a few handfuls of dirt scattered across 
the bed. PCs who investigate the dirt can attempt a 
DC 20 Nature check. On a success, they recognize it 
as freshly dug soil, likely from the manor grounds; a 
requirement for the steward’s vampiric awakening. 
Upon awakening as undead, Hedvend VI escaped 
out the window, which he left open. (A PC can 
attempt a DC 20 Nature or Survival check to realize 
the snow and puddle indicate the window was 
opened only recently).
In addition to the clues above that PCs can see 
with no real difficulty, they can Search the room. If 
their check exceeds the DC listed below, they discover 
additional clues:
•	 DC 20: The rug also has dirt on it, as if it were 
tracked into the room at some point. (If they 
choose to investigate it, see the Soiled Sheets 
Inquiry on page 91.)
•	 DC 22: Small scratches on the floor against the 
western wall indicate a secret door leading into 
the suite’s boudoir (installed decades ago to allow 
discrete assignations).
•	 DC 30: The tracks on the rug clearly were made 
by a Small creature wearing shoes. It appears 
whoever made them came in from the secret door 
in the west, moved to the bed, then turned around 
and retraced their steps.
The Hellknight guard is shocked if the PCs inform 
her that Hedvend’s body is missing and rushes in 
to verify the claim. Other than the PCs, she 
hasn’t seen anyone enter or exit since she was 
placed here to guard the body. She was unaware of 
the secret door and had no reason to think anyone 
could enter or exit Hedvend’s bedroom without 
her knowledge.
Treasure: A PC who Searched the room (DC 
20) discovers a hidden compartment with ledgers 
tracking bribes and corruption in and outside of the 
city. This ledger is worth 400 gp to the right people, 
though it might be worth even more to others. An 
astute PC also notices the glaive is a magical item, but 
the PCs won’t have the opportunity to claim 
it for themselves until Chapter 6.
Reward: If the PCs discover the tracks in 
Hedvend’s room, award them 30 XP.
Inquiry: Second Victim
One of the manor guards was searching for clues 
to Hedvend’s murder in the guest room when the 
vampire steward slipped in from outside and ripped 
out his throat before drinking as much of the guard’s 
blood as he could. When the PCs enter the room, read 
or paraphrase the following:
A small spray of blood covers the floor around a corpse in 
chain mail and the uniform of the manor guard. A frozen 
expression of shock remains on the man’s face above 
where his throat was brutally torn out.
A PC can attempt a Medicine check to examine the 
body. If their check exceeds the DC listed below, they 
learn the following:
•	 DC 18: It appears the guard’s throat was torn out 
by claws.
•	 DC 20: Based on the lack of any defensive wounds, 
the guard likely was taken by surprise.
•	 DC 22: There’s less blood than there should 
be based on the guard’s size. The spray looks 
like it came from the killing blow, but there’s a 
conspicuous lack of a pool of blood afterward.
•	 DC 25: The guard has fang marks on his neck, which 
likely were made moments after he was killed.
A PC can also attempt a DC 20 Perception check to 
examine the room. On a success, they discover the floor 
is slightly damp around the window A DC 20 Nature 
or Survival check indicates the dampness is because 
the window was opened briefly, allowing in snow that 
then melted; Hedvend moved in and out of the room by 
opening the window with telekinetic hand.

Inquiry: Private Dining Room
Fortunately for the PCs, while Ezio 
is a canny conspirator, Lefranek was 
far less capable. As she prepared for the 
false Hellbreaker attack in the private 
dining room, Lefranek left her devil 
costume and other incriminating items here. 
PCs can discover these items if they search 
this room, which is where Lefranek brought 
the guards to be dominated.
In addition to Lefranek’s discarded 
devil costume, the PCs find 12 
vertebrae fused into a column. Each 
vertebrae spins independently and is 
inscribed with several letters in Necril. The device is 
a magical wheel cipher, used by agents of Urgathoa 
to send coded messages. The most recent message 
was: “Bring the guards to a servant cloaked in our 
most sacred color. Illcayna will reward you when 
Isger is hers.”
•	 A PC who succeeds at a DC 15 Medicine check 
recognizes the vertebrae as part of a human spine.
•	 A PC who succeeds at a DC 20 Crafting or 
Society check to Recall Knowledge recognizes the 
contraption is a wheel cipher used to encode and 
decode messages.
•	 A PC who succeeds at a DC 20 Religion check to 
Recall Knowledge recognizes the wheel cipher as 
a tool used by agents of Urgathoa.
•	 A PC can attempt a DC 20 Arcana, Nature, 
Religion, or Occultism check to Identify Magic. 
Doing so gives them a +2 circumstance bonus on 
a Society check to Decipher Writing, or +4 on a 
critical success.
Finally, a PC can attempt a DC 25 Society check 
to Decipher Writing; on a success they decipher 
enough of the message to understand it included 
instructions from an Urgathoan, telling the recipient 
to bring their fellow guards to a red-cloaked man in 
the dining room, and that the plot was masterminded 
by someone named Illcayna, who seeks control of 
the country.
Treasure: Left on the table by Lefranek is a platter 
of putrid dreams (page 199) and a skeleton key.
Reward: Award the PCs 30 XP if they succeed 
on at least one check to learn about the Urgathoan 
wheel cipher. If they Decipher the Writing and learn 
the message, award them an additional 80 XP.
Inquiry: Soiled Sheets
Moderate 5
PCs who become aware of the dirty tracks in 
Hedvend’s bedroom or the boudoir might want to 
follow them, which they can attempt to do with a DC 
20 Survival check to Track (on a critical success, they 
make out enough details to determine the dirt comes 
from a Small creature wearing shoes and with a tail 
that dragged through the soil). The tracks lead from 
Hedvend’s bedroom, through the secret door into the 
boudoir, and then through the halls to the servant 
stairway in the western part of the manor, before 
ultimately leading outside through the servant’s 
entrance to the family mausoleum.
A large stone mausoleum is lit by softly 
glowing everlight crystals, which almost 
seem to sparkle in the falling snow. 
Trimmed hedges, small trees, and a few 
topiaries surround the historic resting place 
of stewards, creating a sense of serenity, 
even amid the storm.
Use the map on page 92. The winter storm imposes 
a –2 circumstance penalty to Perception checks and 
physical ranged attacks, snuffs out handheld flames, 
and makes creatures concealed if they’re more than 
30 feet away. The snow cover makes the entire area 
difficult terrain. Although it’s likely nighttime when the 
PCs investigate, the area in a 60-foot radius around the 
mausoleum is in bright light (and then dim light for 
another 60 feet) due to the crystals’ light reflecting on 
falling snow.
Creatures: Unfortunately for the PCs, Ezio’s attack 
on Hedvend activated some of the manor’s magical 
defenses. They don’t respond to manor servants but the 
PCs don’t have that protection, and three topiaries leave 
their perches and attack. They fight until destroyed.

Inquiry: The Red Cloak
The PCs might want to find the red cloak that Ezio 
wore while dominating a number of people in the 
gala. Unfortunately, he hid it in Lezinia’s closet in the 
boudoir. Unless they begin a room-by-room search, 
this is a dead end, leading to more Murders in the 
Night events and making Ezio aware the PCs know 
about the cloak and are searching for it. Should the 
PCs somehow find it ahead of Ezio’s schedule, he 
brings it up later in Lezinia Has Left the Building.
The Plot Thickens
Events don’t remain static in the mansion as the PCs 
investigate. While most of the NPCs wait anxiously, 
some wander around the mansion, falling prey to 
Hedvend—either to sate his hunger or at Ezio’s 
instructions. Ezio, meanwhile, works to obfuscate his 
role and create confusion. The events likely occur in 
generally the following order, though some might need 
to happen sooner or later depending on what the PCs do 
and your needs to keep the story engaging for players.
EVENT: EZIO GETS INVOLVED
Ezio becomes concerned when he sees Caeto summon 
the PCs at the start of the chapter, and decides he needs 
to involve himself with this unexpected complication 
to his plans. He approaches them the first time they 
descend from the second floor after their meeting with 
Caeto, likely during the False Hellbreakers or Get the 
Dirt inquiry. He plays the role of concerned guest, 
asking PCs for information about what’s happening. 
If the PCs successfully influenced him at all during 
the previous chapter, he offers to help them again, 
suggesting he could facilitate any discussions with 
other guests thanks to his connections or anything 
else the PCs need. He attempts to keep tabs on the 
PCs throughout the course of this chapter, steering 
them in directions he wants while disrupting their 
investigation as much as possible. He doesn’t take the 
risk of attempting to Dominate them, however.
EVENT: MURDERS IN THE NIGHT
Hedvend strikes again, killing another person in the 
mansion. This event occurs multiple times over the 
course of the night, repeating every hour or so until 
the PCs discover the murderer(s), adding urgency to 
the PCs’ investigation and possibly narrowing their 
pool of suspects. In terms of gameplay, the event likely 
follows every 1–2 completed inquiries. While several 
of the targets are selected to weaken Isger, others are 
random victims of Hedvend’s hunger. Ezio’s targets 
are killed in the following order, interspersed with 
unfortunate guards and servants. The location and 
circumstances of the deaths are included below, while 
the guards and servants can be found in any room 
with access to outside.
•	 Merpelia Carafo, whom Ezio targets to end her 
support of Isger’s army, is murdered in the gallery.
•	 Ambassador Vrig, targeted to prevent any chance 
of an alliance with Oprak, is killed in the library.
•	 Sastoli Brunc, whose command of the docks

The first time a named target is killed, the PCs can 
attempt a DC 21 Isger Lore check or DC 23 Society 
check to Recall Knowledge to realize the death would 
be an additional blow to Isger’s government. For each 
subsequent named target, reduce the DC by 1. They 
can attempt the same check, at the current DC, after 
each guard or servant’s death to realize that they don’t 
seem to fit the pattern, and could have simply been in 
the wrong place at the wrong time.
A PC who wants to learn more about a victim’s 
actions or behavior in their final moments can attempt 
a Diplomacy check to Gather Information. The DC 
for an unnamed servant or guard is 20, with a success 
revealing they were acting normally and doing their 
job. The DC for a named victim begins at 25, and goes 
down by 1 for each subsequent victim. On a success, 
PCs can learn that the victim was last seen speaking 
with Ezio. On a critical success, PCs learn that they 
seemed to be having an intense conversation with a 
lot of direct eye contact, before the victim seemed 
to just turn and wander away. See Event: The Alibi 
Attack (below) and The Jig Is Up (page 94) for Ezio’s 
reactions if they confront him.
After Ambassador Vrig’s death, and each subsequent 
death, a PC can attempt a DC 20 Architecture Lore or 
DC 22 Crafting check to Recall Knowledge to realize 
the each death is occurring in a room with a window 
to the outside, or in a room that has a chimney.
Development: If the PCs realize all the deaths are in 
rooms with access to outside, they can warn guests to 
avoid them. This prevents any further reoccurrences 
of this event.
Reward: If the PCs learn any of the deaths are 
intended to harm the Isgeri government, award them 
30 XP. If they learn of Ezio’s conversations with any 
of the victims, award them an additional 30 XP. If the 
PCs warn gala guests to stay out of rooms with access 
to the outdoors, award them 80 XP.
EVENT: THE ALIBI ATTACK
It’s possible the PCs become suspicious of Ezio early in 
this chapter, likely if they discover he was seen talking 
with a named victim of Hedvend in a Murders in the 
Night event. If they attempt to question or confront 
him, he triggers this event. Allow the PCs to have a 
brief interaction with Ezio, who rejects any allegations 
of culpability in the night’s events. Even as he talks to 
the PCs, he telepathically commands Hedvend to go to 
the servants’ parlor (area I11) and kill the first creature 
he sees there (if the PCs happen to be in the servants’ 
parlor, the killing takes place outside the upstairs 
storeroom). The PCs’ questioning is then interrupted 
either by a scream if they’re near the murder scene or 
the panicked arrival of a servant.
Unlike most of the murders Ezio orchestrates, 
the hurried nature of this one leaves a witness: the 
unfortunate Otton Nettlebrush. He babbles that 
something was trying to eat the human woman who 
now lies dead and bleeding on the floor. A PC can 
attempt to calm him down with a DC 20 Diplomacy 
or Medicine or a DC 22 Intimidation check. If they 
succeed, Otton tearfully admits it looked like Hedvend 
before it scrambled outside when he screamed (either 
through the door or, if the attack occurred upstairs, 
through the window).
Development: If the PCs return to the conversation 
with Ezio, he attempts to lead them to the conclusion 
that he can’t be responsible since there was another 
killing while he was in their presence without outright 
saying so. If the PCs press the issue, he triggers Event: 
Lezinia Has Left the Building (page 94), and the 
mystery moves into its end game.
EVENT: EXTERMINATE THE PESTS	
LOW 5
As the PCs’ investigation progresses, they increasingly 
threaten Ezio’s plan and he decides to eliminate them. 
This event should occur sometime after he approaches 
the PCs for the first time, likely after they have 
completed one or two more inquiries and might have 
discovered signs that point to a vampire in Reevesrest 
but not yet be certain of its presence. It can take place 
anywhere in the manor, but you might want to choose 
an area where the PCs haven’t spent much time (and 
haven’t had a fight before), such as the conservatory, 
downstairs dining room, gallery, or library.
Hazard: Ezio summons creatures of the night from 
the city environs, directing them to kill the PCs. The 
creatures, which are represented as a hazard, enter the 
building through the foundations and chimneys and 
make their way to the PCs. The hazard occupies the 
entire room where this encounter occurs.

EVENT: FESSY’S FEAR
LOW 5
Ezio’s contingency plan involves implicating Lezinia, 
but he’s cunning enough to also try to remove a 
potential threat to himself and source of support for 
the PCs: Fessy. He sends the dominated Chelaxian 
diva to suggest that Fessy find somewhere safe to rest 
and refresh. Lezinia also provides her with a scroll to 
summon a celestial that she claims she acquired in 
Cheliax in case of devil attack. In truth the scroll is from 
Ezio, and it’s tainted by Illcayna’s warshard. The scared 
gnome cleric hides in the private dining room, where 
she locks the door and falls into an exhausted sleep.
This event ideally occurs if the PCs look for Fessy to 
help heal them following a battle. A servant informs 
them that she went to the private dining room on 
the second floor (area I20) a short while ago. If the 
PCs don’t need Fessy’s help, this event occurs after 
Exterminate the Pests but before Colonel Rithert’s 
murder by Hedvend. A servant timidly approaches the 
PCs to express concern about Fessy after seeing her go 
into the private dining room and never emerge.
The door is locked, but a PC can open it with three 
successful DC 20 Thievery checks or Force it Open 
with a successful DC 20 Athletics check. In either 
case, the noise startles Fessy awake and she quickly 
casts from the scroll, summoning a gnokesh just as 
the PCs open the door.
Creatures: Filled with battle lust by the warshard-
tainted scroll, the gnokesh takes the PCs for threats 
and attacks, castigating them as devil worshippers. 
It continues fighting until slain, despite not being 
sustained, and ignores any attempts to appeal to 
its true nature or attempts to stop or 
Dismiss it.

The Jig Is Up
By the time they have completed all the inquiries, 
the PCs should have a strong suspicion of vampiric 
activity. They likely know that Hedvend was killed 
by a vampire, turned into one himself, and killed a 
number of people in the last few hours. Some PCs 
might prioritize finding Hedvend, but Ezio tries to 
turn their attention to Lezinia.

CREATURE 7
Pathfinder Monster Core 7, page 223
Initiative Perception +14; darkvision
Suspicious Diva: Following the 
fight, Caeto orders the terrified 
singer back to the boudoir and 
declares that no one may enter or

A 
concerned-looking 
Ezio approaches the PC, with whom he

If Ezio is aware the PCs learned about the red 
cloak he wore earlier in the evening (which he hid in 
Lezinia’s closet), he suggests they search her room If 
the PCs follow his advice, a guard insists they can’t 
enter without Caeto accompanying him. Caeto joins 
them at their request.
This scene concludes with Lezinia—under Ezio’s 
control—ultimately confessing to killing Hedvend, 
but how exactly that plays out depends on the PCs’ 
actions. If they come in and accuse her, she confesses 
immediately. If they instead want to search the 
room, she petulantly allows it. A DC 10 Perception 
check to search the room reveals a red cloak balled 
up around several magical items in the back of 
Lezinia’s closet; on a critical success, the PC realizes 
there were a number of places it could have been 
hidden that would have made it far more difficult 
to find.
Once the PCs accuse her—or if they go to leave 
without doing so—Lezinia confesses in dramatic 
fashion. Read or paraphrase the following:
“Fine,” Lezinia suddenly declares. “You caught me! I did it! 
I killed that miserable old man! He promised me he would 
marry me and make me queen of Isger. That’s what tonight 
was supposed to be about, our engagement! But then he 
said he wasn’t going to do it; when he still wouldn’t agree 
to marry me, I killed him! I don’t know what happened 
afterward!” She breaks down in sobs.
Because the confession is pure fantasy, Lezinia has 
few other details she’s able to give the PCs and can’t 
say how she supposedly killed Hedvend. She 
claims she took the items because he owed 
them to her and wrapped it in the first 
cloak she found.
If a PC is suspicious, they can attempt a 
DC 20 Perception check to Sense Motive. 
On a success, they know Lezinia isn’t acting 
normally, while a critical success reveals she’s 
certainly being magically controlled.
Regardless of the PCs’ reactions, 
Caeto is suspicious of the unexpected 
confession and Lezinia’s ability to pull 
off such a calculated murder. He 
insists the PCs find some way to 
test if she is a vampire, but if they 
don’t have any other options, he 
says they should go get a leftover 
caramelized garlic tart from 
the kitchen and test her with that. 
The reference to garlic calls back to the No Thank You 
Bite event in Chapter 4 (page 81), pointing to Ezio’s 
true status as a vampire; GMs might want to remind 
players of that moment if they’ve forgotten, but give 
them a chance to make the connection themselves first. 
Alternatively, Caeto could question why they suspected 
Lezinia, also directing them back toward Ezio.
Lezinia fails whatever test the PCs attempt to 
determine whether she’s a vampire, but she continues 
to proclaim her guilt. A PC can convince her that she’s 
not a vampire or a murderer with a DC 20 Diplomacy 
or Intimidation check. If they are successful, Lezinia 
is confused about why she confessed. She admits that 
nothing she said is true; she and Hedvend were in a 
relationship but he hadn’t promised her anything, but 
can’t explain anything else.
Treasure: If the PCs persuade Lezinia that she was 
not the killer, she rewards them with 200 gp in jewelry 
gifted to her by Hedvend and the greater whispering 
wire (page 212) and oil of revelation that were 
wrapped with the cloak.
Reward: Award the PCs 30 XP if they persuade 
Lezinia that she is not a murderer. Award an additional 
80 XP if they put the pieces together and realize Ezio’s 
guilt after this inquiry.
Inquiry: Hunting for Hedvend VI	
Severe 5
Once the PCs realize a vampiric Hedvend is stalking 
the mansion, their first inclination might be to try 
to find him, either by setting up a trap for him or 
hunting him down. Caeto gives them free rein to do 
either, though declines to participate. He expresses 
Lezinia

===== Page 97 =====
96
confidence in the PCs’ abilities while at the same time 
remaining busy making sure the attack in the manor 
isn’t a prelude to a full-scale surprise Hellbreaker 
attack on Elidir.
Setting a Trap: Following the Murders in the 
Night event, if the PCs learn that Hedvend is killing 
people important to the Isgeri government and 
that his killings all occur in rooms with access to 
the outdoors, they have all the information they 
need to set a trap; all they require is bait. They 
can determine who would make sense to use as a 
stalking horse with a successful DC 20 Diplomacy 
check to Gather Information or Society check to 
Recall Knowledge—a success reveals that any of the 
still-living named victims from the Murders in the 
Night event would serve well in that role, as would 
Rencelos Azri. A critical success reveals that Fessy 
would also be an option.
The next challenge is persuading the bait to play 
the role. A PC can do so with a successful DC 20 
Deception check to try to trick them into going alone 
into the PC’s ambush site, a DC 22 Diplomacy check 
to try to persuade them, or a DC 24 Intimidation 
check to try to make them. If the PCs attempt to get 
Fessy to be the bait, she automatically agrees to help.
Once they have a potential victim, the PCs can 
choose any Reevesrest location they want for the 
ambush other than the great room, which remains 
crowded. Allow them to make any preparations they 
want. Once they’re ready, they can attempt a DC 6 
flat check every 15 minutes; on a success, Hedvend 
enters the room and attacks.
Pursuing the Killer: The PCs might want to look 
for Hedvend’s tracks once they realize he’s likely 
hiding outside between murders in the manor but 
the snowstorm outside makes this difficult. If they 
persevere, the PCs can track him to the roof of the 
mausoleum with a successful DC 25 Survival check to 
Track. If they’re successful, the conditions are likely 
to make this a more difficult fight. Although it’s likely 
still nighttime, the area in a 60-foot radius around 
the mausoleum is in bright light (and then dim light 
for another 60 feet) due to the everlight crystals’ light 
reflecting on falling snow. The winter storm imposes 
a –2 circumstance penalty to Perception checks and 
physical ranged attacks, snuffs handheld flames (such 
as from a torch or candle), and makes creatures 
concealed if they’re more than 30 feet away. The 
snow cover makes the entire area difficult terrain.
Ezio’s Involvement: By the time the PCs face 
Hedvend, Ezio is fully aware of the threat they 
pose to him and, more importantly, Illcayna’s plans. 
Considering the secluded nature of this encounter, he 
sees it as an opportunity to eliminate the PCs and 
blame it on Hedvend. If you feel that Ezio wouldn’t 
have reason to think the PCs are suspicious of him by 
the time they face Hedvend, he’ll instead face them 
one-on-one later in the evening.
The PCs might be more concerned with Ezio than 
Hedvend once they realize that he’s the original killer 
and manipulating events around he gala. They can 
choose where and how to stage any confrontation, 
making any necessary preparations. If the PCs 
confront him, Ezio initially denies any responsibility 
but finally acknowledges he’s lost once the PCs lay 
out all their evidence.
If the PCs confront Ezio before hunting down 
Hedvend, Ezio smiles and compliments the PCs on 
their investigative work, acknowledging that he 
would likely have gotten away with it if it weren’t 
for them. “Let the devil worshippers and the rebels 
fight,” he says. “In the end when they fall, our undead 
army will grow fat with their blood and bodies, and 
we will reclaim this land for the Pallid Princess! No 
more will our resources go to feed others. Isger will 
be for Isger and Urgathoa!”
Creatures: Hedvend VI, consumed with hunger, 
fights until destroyed. If the PCs used an NPC as bait 
to set a trap, that character flees at the start of the 
first round of combat. Ezio rolls initiative at the start 
of the second round of combat and joins the fight at 
his initiative spot in that round. He enters through 
a door from the manor interior, using his Change 
Shape ability if necessary. Fully cognizant that he will 
be exposed if he doesn’t kill all the PCs and expecting 
that his Cloud of Plague ability will preserve his 
unlife, Ezio fights until reduced to 0 HP. If Ezio isn’t 
involved in this fight, it becomes a trivial encounter.
Ezio fights until reduced to 0 HP, and fully expects 
to be able to revive with Cloud of Plague. If Hedvend 
VI hasn’t been destroyed, Ezio summons the vampire 
steward to aid him. Roll initiative for Hedvend VI, 
who arrives in 1d3 rounds; if the battle takes place in

Hedvend VI channels a spell into his claw Strike to 
deliver a combined attack. He Casts a Spell that requires 
a spell attack roll. The effects of the spell don’t occur 
immediately but are imbued into his attack instead.

spell. This counts as two attacks for his multiple attack 
penalty, but he doesn’t apply the penalty until after he’s

grants his Strike the arcane trait, making it magical. 
After he uses Spellstrike, he can’t do so again until he 
recharges his Spellstrike as a single action, which has 
the concentrate trait. He also recharge his Spellstrike 
when he Drinks Blood.
EZIO GAETA	
CREATURE 7
Page 240
Initiative Perception +16
Epilogue
Following their victory, the PCs discover a skeletal 
encryption ring Ezio used to send coded messages to 
his agents hidden as part of his costume. The discovery 
allows them to decrypt the wheel cipher they found 
among Lefranek’s items (if they haven’t already), 
revealing for certain that an Urgathoan faction has 
gotten involved in the battle for Isger, though there’s 
no information about where they’re based or what 
their next plan is.
Caeto thanks the PCs for solving Hedvend’s murder 
and uncovering Ezio’s perfidy. He promises he will 
do everything he can in his power to build a better 
country that works for all its citizens. The PCs can 
tell he is sincere about this. He tells them he hopes 
they’ll be part of his efforts and allows everyone to 
depart for home.
Treasure: Caeto gives the PCs an imposing shield 
(page 213) and dreamcrusher (page 213) as a reward 
for their work.

Following the PCs’ victory over Ezio and the 
transformed Hedvend VI, they’re able to regroup with 
their fellow Hellbreakers and celebrate their successful 
mission in recruiting Quoster. Unfortunately, they wake 
the next morning to learn of disaster: Caeto Vulaunex 
has declared martial law and is locking down the city 
so he can “catch the Hellbreaker assassins and bring 
them to justice.” The Hellbreakers are now trapped in 
enemy territory and framed for murder! They must 
find a way to escape the city before they’re hunted 
down. Fortunately, they’ve made allies in Elidir, and 
the combination of Hedvend’s assassination and 
Caeto’s crackdown has the city up in arms and ripe for 
recruiting new Hellbreakers!
This chapter lasts roughly three weeks, to the end 
of Abadius. There’s largely little time-specific pressure 
on the PCs; if they fail a mission, they can generally 
retreat and then try again, but doing so will likely 
increase their Suppression Points.
Part 1: The Chains That Bind
The day after the gala, the PCs hear a knock on the 
door of their safe house. They open it to find Quoster, 
who slips in followed by two human employees laden 
with goods. He comes bearing the grim news of the 
city’s lockdown along with an offer for the PCs (and 
any items he promised them during their first meeting), 
but also a request for their help.

merchant says, “but we’ve already agreed to work 
together and we need to work even more closely now that 
the city’s locked down. I don’t want the Hellknight to find 
you—bad for business, bad for surviving. I can help you

Quoster gives the group a staff of phantasms. If the 
PCs immediately agree to help, Quoster is touched and 
also gives them a ring of fair assessment (page 212).
MISSION: JAILBREAK
When the PCs arrive at the Gyve, they find a group 
of outraged citizens protesting the crackdown and 
preventing Siadrius’s captors from bringing him into 
the Moil, the labor camp that surrounds the prison. The 
army is slow to respond as it locks down the city, giving 
the PCs a chance to free Siadrius without having to enter 
the prison itself. Read or paraphrase the following.
Towering iron gates open into a courtyard, where prisoners 
arrive to be led through the dark stone walls that lead 
into the labor camp known as the Moil. In the 
center of the camp, the Gyve rises above the 
walls. Made of black stone, the prison is a blot 
on the skyline, a dreadful, ominous presence 
among the cheerfully painted wooden homes 
and businesses of Elidir. Small barred windows 
can be seen on the second floor and in the 
fourth-floor tower, about 40 feet up.
An angry crowd spilled into the 
courtyard, known as Purgatory, when 
the outer gates were opened to allow in 
Siadrius’s captors. The volatile crowd 
is currently preventing the guards from 
closing the outer gates or opening the interior 
ones. Blocked and badly outnumbered by the 
crowd, the guards are still trying to decide on a course 
of action when the PCs arrive. Siadrius is shackled 
hand and foot, and bound to a pole held by two 
guards in front of the interior gate.

Development: The mob is thrilled by the PCs’ 
resistance to the guards and, as the battle concludes, 
begins chanting slogans, such as “Isger for Isger,” “Send 
the devils back to Cheliax,” and “Hellbreakers!” If the 
players or PCs have discussed or used any slogans among 
themselves, having the crowd spontaneously chant that 
would help convey the PCs’ growing influence and 
importance to the Hellbreakers League. At this point, it’s 
up to the PCs to decide what to do—they can abandon 
the mob to its own devices, try to get it to disperse for 
the protesters’ own safety, or recruit members for their 
own chapter of the Hellbreakers League as Alceo and 
Phoebe tasked them to do when they first arrived.
Attempting to break up the mob before it gets out 
of hand requires a DC 22 skill check using the basic 
Victory Point mechanic (GM Core 184) to measure the 
PCs’ success. Determine how a PC wants to engage the 
mob and what skill makes the most sense; each PC has 
one chance to influence the crowd. Some likely choices 
include Athletics to bodily separate people from the 
whole; Diplomacy to reason with them; Intimidation 
to scare them away; or Society to explain the danger 
they face with the protest. If the PCs leave the mob to 
its own devices and flee with Siadrius, they receive 0 
Victory Points.
0 	
Victory Points: The mob continues to protest after 
the PCs leave until they are brutally put down 
by Caeto’s forces. Word of the slaughter quickly 
spreads, and the PCs lose 2 Uprising Points.
1–2 	 Victory Points: The PCs persuade a few protesters 
to take their requested action, but can’t control 
most of the mob. They gain 0 Uprising Points.
3–4 	Victory Points: Most of the mob heeds the PCs and 
follows their directions, though a few protesters 
continue to decry Caeto’s crackdown. They gain 1 
Uprising Points.
5+	 Victory Points: The PCs quickly persuade the 
protesters to do as instructed, bolstering their 
reputation. They gain 2 Uprising Points and increase 
the Hellbreakers League’s Reputation Points by 1.
Part 2: Raising Hell
Once the PCs return to the safe house, Quoster is 
elated that they saved Siadrius.
“I can’t think you all enough, I... Siadrius means more to me 
than you’ll ever know. If what you did at the gala wasn’t 
enough, this only proves I’m making the right choice by 
supporting the Hellbreakers League. Stay here, rest and 
recover, and I’ll get us all out of Elidir as quickly as possible.”
Siadrius, as a way of thanks, says even with his 
current legal troubles, he has enough friends in the 
city that he can buy (or sell) anything the PCs might 
need, letting them shop safely during this part of the 
adventure. He says he’ll contact a friend, Jenvirick 
(excitable female nephilim halfling antiques collector 
3), whom he trusts to serve as an intermediary, and 
will send her to the PCs’ safe house.
WHO ARE THE ROOKIE HELLBREAKERS?
The number of Hellbreakers who join the PCs 
isn’t specified and mostly serve as background 
characters. You can reintroduce NPCs the PCs 
met in the city to fill out the ranks, including 
any of those they entered the city with, such as: 
Sarevial, the elf apprentice they met shortly after 
entering Elidir (page 68); Padisco, the wounded 
veteran (page 75); Ozney, if they didn’t let the 
authorities take her to prison (page 76); and 
Father Kindness and the Children’s Charity (page 
72). Otton Nettlebrush, the servant from the 
manor (page 81), definitely joins. He appears in 
one of the early uprisings that Jenvirick suggests, 
but is later captured and reveals the PCs’ locations 
after being tortured in the Gyve. Feel free to flesh 
out additional Hellbreaker recruits and give them 
backgrounds that emphasize the iniquity in Isger. 
Creating connections with NPCs during the earlier 
part of the chapter will increase the impact of 
their eventual arrest and attempts to free them.

Jenvirick arrives shortly after the PCs have had a 
chance to rest and recover from the fight at the Moil. 
The daughter of Goblinblood War veterans, 
she’s tired of watching her parents and her 
country be taken advantage of. While she’s 
always been excitable (as well as a bit of 
a conspiracy theorist), Siadrius’s request 
to work with the Hellbreakers has ignited 
her into a full-blown radical. She soon 
approaches the PCs about starting a 
local chapter of the Hellbreakers League. 
The exact timing for this request is up to 
you—it might work well immediately 
after she returns from a first shopping 
expedition for the PCs, but could be 
sooner if they don’t immediately have any 
goods they want to buy or sell.
Jenvirick serves as an important NPC in this 
section. She pushes the PCs to start a chapter 
of the Hellbreakers League in the city and offers 
them missions to advance their cause.
Jenvirick nearly thrums with excitement, shifting her 
weight from foot to foot as if she’s only barely holding 
herself back from rushing into action. “I can do more than 
just shop. I joined the protests before Hedvend—” She 
stops to spit on the ground as she mentions the now-dead 
steward. “—cracked down on the Riotmongers. I’ve heard 
about what the Hellbreakers League is doing in the south, 
and Siadrius told me how you rescued him. The time is 
now! Elidir is ready for its own chapter. That protest at 
the Moil proves it. We just need leaders! And you showed 
you can lead! Let me join, let me help! I have so many 
ideas!”
If the PCs agree, Jenvirick claps her hands. When 
they’re ready, she spills out ideas for missions the 
PCs can undertake. Her ideas make up the following 
encounters: The Manor Job (page 101), The Army 
Job (page 102), and The Talisman Job (page 103), 
which the PCs can do in whatever order they 
chose. After they complete the second of Jenvirick’s 
missions, Quoster approaches them about The Dock 
Job uprising (page 104). If the PCs feel they’re low on 
Uprising Points, they can also attempt the Propaganda 
mission (page 105). This section of the adventure lasts 
about 2–3 weeks, giving PCs time to rest, craft, or 
shop between missions. You could even have missions 
overlap to convey a sense of time passing—especially 
with perhaps one or two obstacles from the Talisman 
Job happening around other uprisings, though you 
should make sure doing it this way won’t confuse 
your players.
If the PCs rebuff her, Jenvirick is disappointed, 
but continues to press them over the following days, 
arguing that the League has been a positive 
force for other areas of Isger and that 
Elidir deserves the same. If they still refuse, 
she decides to take matters into her own 
hands, slowly bringing more and more 
revolutionaries into the safe house 
and holding meetings right under 
the PCs’ noses—such meetings lead 
to wilder and wilder ideas that the 
PCs should be able to immediately 
tell would result in mass casualties. 
If the PCs don’t quickly take a 
leadership role, they become aware 
that the unauthorized Hellbreakers 
League is trying to incite misbehavior 
and provoking Caeto to increase his efforts 
against them. From here, the PCs’ Suppression 
Points increase by 1 per day. After three days, 
Quoster approaches the PCs to share his 
concerns about the high-profile actions being 
attributed to the League and their repercussions, and 
urges the PCs to take leadership of the group.
MISSION: THE MANOR JOB
Jenvirick approaches with a familiar halfling. “This is Otton 
Nettlebrush. I heard him talking with another League 
member and, well, you should hear what he has to say!”
Otton mumbles to himself nervously and shifts his feet 
for a moment before he begins. “Right... Jenvirick says I 
should tell you that I served in Reevesrest until Hedvend 
got exactly what he deserved. After that, Vulaunex sacked 
most of the staff, just left a few guards and servants. But 
here’s the thing: that manor has a lot of valuables in it. 
Coins, of course, but also artwork, rare books, even that 
glaive that hangs in the steward’s room—the older servants 
used to say it was some sort of ancient magical weapon 
that stewards have kept since they defeated the original 
Isgeri.”
Vibrating with excitement, Jenvirick interrupts. “So that 
gave me an idea! We could go loot it. Then we use the 
money to help the city’s needy, which should bring them 
to our side!”
Caeto remains ensconced in the Chelaxian Quarter, 
also known as the Devil’s Acre—the walled area 
of the city that houses the Chelaxian elite—leaving 
Reevesrest largely empty other than a few guards and 
servants to maintain it. The PCs, who already know 
the manor’s layout, have a golden opportunity to sneak 
back in and loot the place. Jenvirick suggests some of 
Jenvirick

===== Page 103 =====
102
the treasure could help fund the nascent chapter of the 
Hellbreakers League, but the rest could be distributed 
to the needy to earn favor for the rebellion.
To succeed at this mission, the PCs need to sneak 
past the guards and quietly enter the home. This 
uprising is a skill challenge using the Victory Points 
mechanic (GM Core 184). This is a two-step challenge 
over about 8 hours that can be done day or night. 
Each PC can attempt one check per step and a PC 
who uses an appropriate non-cantrip spell can earn 
an automatic success, or a critical success if it’s the 
highest rank spell they can cast.
In the first part of the challenge, the PCs must avoid 
both human and animal guards. They can attempt 
to do so with a DC 22 check using Acrobatics to 
go over and around gates and guards, Deception 
to Impersonate a new servant or guard, Nature to 
Command an Animal, Stealth to avoid being seen, or 
Perception to Spot approaching patrols.
0–1	  Victory Points: The PCs are spotted, and fail to get 
past the guards.
2–3 	Victory Points: The PCs make it past the guards, 
but raise suspicions. They suffer a –1 circumstance 
penalty to any skill checks in the second part of this 
challenge.
4 	
Victory Points: The PCs slip into the manor grounds 
completely undetected.
If the PCs have enough VP to proceed to the second 
part of the challenge, they must break into the manor 
and bypass locks and magical traps set to secure the 
location. They can do so with a DC 22 check using 
Athletics to Force Open a door or window, or a DC 
22 Arcana, Crafting, Occultism, Religion, or Thievery 
check to bypass the magical security.
0–1 	Victory Points: The PCs fail to get into the manor 
and need to retreat.
2–3 	Victory Points: The PCs get into the manor, but 
can’t access all of its valuables.
4 	
Victory Points: The PCs strip the manor of 
everything that’s not nailed down.
If the PCs fail at either challenge, they escape 
unscathed and can try again on another day. Each 
failed attempt gains the PCs 1 Suppression Point, but 
also reduces the DCs in both parts of the challenge by 1 
as they gain familiarity with the security (this reduction 
is cumulative if the PCs make multiple attempts).
Treasure: If the PCs strip the manor of all its valuables, 
they claim a token of salt and earth (page 212) as well 
as the glaive in Hedvend’s room, an ancient Isgeri 
weapon called Lifebloom (page 214). In addition, they 
earn 2 Uprising Points as the Hellbreakers distribute 
Hedvend’s wealth to those who need it. If they couldn’t 
access all of the valuables, they get the two treasures 
and only gain 1 Uprising Point.
Reward: If the PCs successfully get into the manor 
and get any valuables, award them 10 XP.
MISSION: THE ARMY JOB
An evil grin crosses Jenvirick’s face. “I have an idea!” she 
says excitedly. “I was looking for something to eat earlier 
and I accidentally snapped at Sarevial because I wanted 
some bread. People get cranky when they’re hungry, and 
they don’t always make the best choices. What if we 
did that to the army? Who knows if Vulaunex has fully 
wrapped his greedy fists around the army’s hilt, but I bet 
we can make things uncomfortable there!”
Jenvirick suggests the PCs take advantage of the 
confusion around Caeto’s takeover to disrupt 
the Isgeri army’s operations. If they impersonate 
Chelaxian couriers, they could send supplies or even 
forces to the wrong places, creating shortages and 
opportunities for other activities. Doing so requires 
the PCs to create false orders and infiltrate Isger’s Fist, 
the army headquarters, which takes an entire day.
The PCs must first falsify documents, which they 
can attempt to do with a DC 22 Society check to 
Create a Forgery or a DC 22 Crafting check to create 
the paper, inks, and seals associated with the army’s 
written orders. This check should be made secretly. 
The PCs then must deliver the orders, which requires 
a DC 22 Deception or Performance check. If the PCs 
successfully influenced Colonel Rithert in Chapter 4 
(page 78) and xe survived the gala, reduce each DC 
by 1.
If the PCs succeed at both checks, they disrupt 
the army’s supply lines, reducing their number of 
Suppression Points by 2; if they critically succeeded 
at one of the checks, they instead reduce the number 
by 3, or by 4 if they critically succeed at both checks. 
If they fail at either check, they aren’t able to deliver 
the false orders, but can attempt to do so again. If they 
critically fail at one of the checks, they raise suspicions 
and gain 1 Suppression Point. If they critically fail at 
both checks, they gain 2 Suppression Points and can’t 
attempt this uprising again.
Reward: If the PCs successfully complete the Army 
Job, award them 10 XP.

The PCs have had a couple of interactions with the 
Azri family, who represent the very worst Isger has 
to offer: unparalleled wealth, less concern for the 
common person than the dirt on their exquisite 
custom shoes, and fewer scruples than a devil from 
the Hells. Unfortunately, their status and connections 
as one of the primary providers of weapons and 
supplies to the Isgeri army have largely made them 
untouchable as does their immense amount of private 
security. Framing the Azris as Hellbreakers would 
force Caeto to arrest them, even if only to acquit 
them. While they might be able to buy their freedom, 
the charges would be serious enough that they would 
be imprisoned, which would in turn interfere with 
the army’s weapon supply.
Jenvirick lays out an elaborate heist for the PCs, 
which involves spreading rumors about a shipment 
of talismans from Druma intended for Elidir’s army 
that have disappeared. Next, the PCs must find a way 
to connect the talismans to the Azris by posing as 
thieves who offer to sell them to the corrupt nobles. 
The PCs can then slip word to the army, claiming 
the Azris were the ones who stole the supposed 
shipment in the first place with plans to sell them 
to the Hellbreakers League. Once all those hooks 
are baited, it’s simply a matter of luring both sides 
to the same location and getting away unseen and 
untouched. This uprising uses the Infiltration system 
from GM Core 196.

MISSION: THE DOCK JOB
LOW OR MODERATE 6
This uprising occurs after the PCs complete two of the 
previous uprisings. Quoster approaches the PCs and 
says he’s having trouble persuading the authorities 
to let him leave the city. Fortunately, Jenvirick has an 
idea: she suggests the PCs to stage a robbery to pile 
on pressure.
Quoster runs his hands through his hair, looking haggard. 
“I still think I can get you out with my goods, but the 
authorities are being stubborn devils. They’re refusing to 
let me leave, and I need some leverage.”
Jenvirick lets out a squeak: “Oh, I have an idea! What if 
you stage a robbery down at the docks and intentionally 
get spotted so there’s no chance it’s overlooked? Then 
Quoster can use that to emphasize that his goods aren’t 
safe here!”
It’s not important that the PCs actually steal 
anything, but Quoster needs them to be spotted so 
he can point to the threat of thieves as a reason he 
should be allowed to move his goods out of Elidir lest 
Caeto risk him kicking up enough of a fuss to cause an 
international squabble. Quoster suggests going at night 
when the docks are largely empty other than security 
patrols, which typically consist of a few guards. He 
urges the PCs to avoid killing anyone, since that could 
backfire and make Caeto tighten his grip.
If the PCs successfully influenced Sastoli Brunc in 
Chapter 4 (page 78) and he survived the gala, Quoster 
suggests they try to enlist his aid. A PC who goes to the 
docks to talk to him can attempt a DC 20 Diplomacy 
check to Request his help. On a success, he informs 
the PCs about what a typical guard patrol consists of, 
including the spells the watchmage has prepared and 
the presence of the hell hound. On a critical success, 
Sastoli agrees to divert some resources away from 
where the PCs plan to stage the robbery; remove 
one dock guard from the encounter, reducing it from 
moderate to low.
This encounter uses the map to the left. If the PCs 
want to scope out the scene ahead of time, they can do 
so easily. Once they’re ready to proceed, allow them to 
set up where they would like. At least one PC needs to

PCs who wish to be caught robbing the docks attempt

MISSION: PROPAGANDA
This uprising is an optional event for if the PCs are 
lacking Uprising Points. The city is being beaten down 
by Caeto’s brutal crackdown on rebellious elements, 
but the Hellbreakers can turn public sentiment further 
against him through this uprising. First, the PCs must 
attempt to create anti-Cheliax propaganda with a 
DC 22 Crafting or appropriate Lore check. If the PCs 
received the Abrogail I script from Ievis (page 71), 
they automatically succeed.
Next, the PCs must bring their propaganda to the 
public. They can do this quietly or loudly, each with 
their own risks and benefits. If the PCs choose to take 
the quiet approach, they can wait until night and 
sneakily distribute their materials with a DC 24 Stealth 
or Thievery check. If they choose the loud approach, 
they stage a public forum protesting Caeto’s rule and 
rousing a mob with a DC 24 Diplomacy, Intimidation, 
or Performance check.
On a success, the PCs gain 1 Uprising Point (2 if they 
went loud). On a failure, they gain no Uprising Points. 
On a critical failure, they draw attention from guards 
and are confronted (2 guards for quiet, 4 for loud).

CREATURE 4
Elite watch officer (Pathfinder NPC Core 5, 113)

Part 3: The Great Escape
After the PCs have attempted all of Jenvirick’s missions, 
they move on to Part 3 of this chapter. About three 
weeks after the gala, as Abadius draws to a close, the 
PCs receive word that Quoster is finally being allowed 
to leave and they should meet him at the docks along 
with everything they wish to take with them out of 
the city.
The timing is serendipitous, as the PCs’ departure 
comes minutes before the headquarters is raided by the 
Isgeri army. Unrealized by anyone, Otton Nettlebrush 
was captured some time ago. He finally broke under 
torture at the Gyve and revealed the Hellbreakers’ 
location. Jenvirick is barely able to escape, and rushes 
to bring word to the PCs.
Quoster urges his men to quickly finish the preparations, 
carefully having them arrange crates on the ship to create 
a hiding place where they can smuggle multiple people 
out of Elidir. Their work is interrupted as a guard calls out, 
“Boss, there’s someone coming!”
As everyone tenses, a solitary figure limps into the 
warehouse. It’s Jenvirick, but she’s clearly been in a fight. 
She holds one arm carefully against her chest with the 
other, cradling it to prevent the injured limb from being 
jarred. Her hair is matted with blood, and one eye is swollen 
closed. “It’s the army, they found us! They attacked us 
moments after you left,” she says, clearly in pain. “I barely 
escaped. Everyone else has been captured—they’ve all been 
taken to the Gyve!” Her voice cracks with a sob as the final 
word escapes her lips.
The PCs likely have questions for her, which Jenvirick 
struggles to answer as best she can. She doesn’t know 
how the authorities found their headquarters, but they 
came in force and addressed them as Hellbreakers, 
so they clearly knew what they were walking into. 
She tells the PCs that the other revolutionaries are 
almost certainly in the prison by now—she didn’t 
know what else to do, so she hid until she knew it 
was safe to come find the PCs. She urges the PCs to

===== Page 107 =====
106
break them out of prison; otherwise, they’ll likely be 
publicly executed, which would all but end any hope 
of rebellion in the capital. If the PCs agree, read or 
paraphrase the following.
“I don’t think you can just assault the Gyve—that would be 
suicide. Even if you got in, you’d never get out again. But 
I have an idea! One of my parents’ friends fought in the 
Wars, and he was always talking about the chaos that all 
the goblins’ bombs caused. If we had some explosives, that 
could give you an easy way in and out of the prison! And 
maybe we set up some around the city, cause chaos—away 
from people, of course. Then the army has to deal with that 
and can’t come after you.”
Jenvirick’s heard rumors that a veterans home run 
by Rencelos Azri doubles as a secret workshop where 
he has munitions made to sell to the army. If there’s 
anywhere that might have enough explosives to make 
her plan work that’s without drawing the army’s 
immediate ire, that would be it. Once the PCs get the 
supplies, they can set them up in the city to create 
distractions at the proper time. Then, after they get in 
and out of the prison, they’ll need to steal the army’s 
mounts—that will both let them escape quickly and 
prevent the army from following. The PCs might have 
a chance to rest after Prepare the Path (page 108), but 
warn them that once they enter the prison, they likely 
won’t get to rest until they escape the city.
Refusal: If the PCs refuse to help, Quoster frowns 
but agrees that he’ll still help them leave the city. 
However, that attempt is foiled when they arrive at the 
gates and find that they’ve been closed—Caeto isn’t 
allowing anyone to leave the city until he’s executed 
the captured Hellbreakers.
J. MISSION: UP IN ARMS
After the Goblinblood Wars, Rencelos Azri opened 
a veteran’s home called Soldier’s Aegis for members 
of his company. In the beginning, this was a genuine 
act of charity for those who’d aided him throughout 
the war. In time, however, he began having them 
craft magical munitions for him to sell to the highest 
bidder. Soldier’s Aegis slowly transformed from respite 
home to a magical arms workshop staffed by veterans 
known as skirmancers.
Soldier’s Aegis’s walls are wooden slats, and the 
doors are wood. It has magical lights in each room 
that provide dim light unless one of the skirmancers is 
in the room, in which case it provides bright light. The 
windows are closed with wooden shutters, but can be 
Forced Open with a successful DC 22 Athletics check. 
The windows are big enough for a Small creature 
to enter, but Medium or larger creatures need to 
Squeeze through. Use the map above for the following 
encounters.
J1. Vestibule	
Trivial 6
A painting of Rencelos Azri in military attire hangs on 
the wall opposite the door in this finely paneled wooden 
foyer. By the door, a coat rack holds several warm jackets, 
and a small bucket holds water and a rag to wipe dirt off 
muddy boots.
The door from the outer courtyard to the vestibule 
is locked. A PC can Pick the Lock with three successful 
DC 22 Thievery checks.
Hazard: The door to the courtyard is warded with 
a magical trap.

J2. Lounge
Several thickly padded chairs and side tables are scattered 
around this comfortable room. Magical light illuminates the 
corners where bookcases along the walls hold a number of 
titles. A dozen bottles of wine fill a rack, which also holds 
crystal goblets.
The Azris take care of the skirmancers whose

maintained this lounge for them to relax when they’re 
not working. A small bathroom connects to the lounge

Creatures: If the Azris weren’t taken to the Gyve at

J3. Arcane Smithy	
Trivial 6
The acrid smell of magic and alchemy permeates the air. A 
spellbook floats in a silver ritual circle with arcane runes 
of power set in the floor of this wooden room. Shelves 
hold various magical loci and other crafting elements, all 
carefully stored and labeled.
The skirmancers use this room, with its protective 
warding circle, for their magical crafting. While 
activated, the circle prevents anything from crossing. 
Creatures in the circle gain a +2 status bonus to AC 
against any attacks made from outside the area. In 
addition, a creature that attempts to enter the circle 
must make a DC 22 Will save. On a failure, the circle 
stops their movement (though they can still attempt 
any other actions that were part of an activity as long 
as they meet the requirements, such as a Strike that 
is part of a Sudden Charge). On a critical failure, 
the entire activity ends and the creature becomes 
stunned 1. A creature cannot be summoned inside the 
circle, and a creature with the magical or summoned 
trait that tries to enter the circle treats the results of its 
save as one degree worse.
Creatures: A skirmancer is working here in the 
warding circle. They remain in the circle, hoping its 
magic will protect them, and they respond to any 
intruders with deadly intent. If the Azris are in the 
lounge, the skirmancer rushes in to help them if they 
hear combat. The skirmancer surrenders if reduced to 
10 Hit Points or fewer.

K. MISSION: BREAK THE FETTERS
Once the PCs finish their preparations, they can begin 
their assault on the Gyve at any time. The prison uses 
the map on page 108 and is made of well-maintained 
masonry (Hardness 14, HP 56 [BT 28], Climb DC 22), 
with 10-foot-high ceilings. Its doors and portcullises 
are wood (Hardness 10, HP 40 [BT 20]) and are locked 
unless otherwise noted. They require two successes 
on a DC 22 Thievery check to Pick the Lock or can 
be Forced Open with a DC 27 Athletics check. The 
windows are barred with iron, but have been poorly 
maintained while the government has used its limited 
resources on other priorities—they have Hardness 
10, HP 40 (BT 20), and can be Forced Open with a 
successful DC 24 Athletics check. Torches on the first 
floor provide bright light throughout the area. The rest 
of the prison is in darkness unless indicated otherwise.
If the PCs wish to know more about the prison, 
they can attempt a DC 20 Society check to Recall 
Knowledge or a DC 22 Diplomacy check to Gather 
Information. On a success, they learn that prisoners 
are kept on the upper floors, while a torture chamber 
is in the basement. On a critical success, they learn 
specifics about the prison: Give them a map of the first, 
second, and third floor, though don’t let them know 
where the secret entrance to area K5 is.
Jenvirick strongly recommends the PCs blow a 
hole in the surrounding walls of the prison to enter, 
which they can do with supplies they’ve acquired 
from Soldier’s Aegis. Allow them to pick a spot on the 
outer walls where they want to set a bomb. When it 
explodes, it blows a 5-foot-wide gap the PCs can use 
to enter directly into the Moil (area K2), and from 
there the Gyve. If they have Volcanic Diversion Points, 
they can spend 1 to create an additional 5-foot hole in 
the Gyve’s outer wall, or in the prison itself.
Some PCs might want to try a stealthier approach. 
One option—which Jenvirick strongly recommends 
against—is to get themselves arrested. They can do 
this very easily via street patrol (use the Papers, Please 
encounter on page 65). This would bring them into 
the prison via Purgatory and then the main entrance 
to the Descent, but the guards would take any 
armor, weapons, and magic items unless they were 
successfully concealed with Stealth or magic. They 
could also attempt to get a man on the inside through 
a hefty bribe of 300+ gp or an extremely difficult 
Diplomacy check (DC 30), but this might take time 
they can’t afford.
If a PC wants to impersonate a guard, warn them 
through a NPC that the guards have a daily code 
phrase that they use to identify themselves. The phrase 
on the day the PCs break in is “It’s colder than a rime 
dragon’s breath,” and the PCs must find a guard and 
get the code out of them with a DC 27 Diplomacy 
check or a DC 29 Intimidation check.
K1. Purgatory	
Trivial 6
The grim gates of the prison await those doomed.
The entranceway to the prison grounds acts as an 
airlock—the interior and exterior gates are never 
opened at the same time. By Caeto’s orders, the 
prison is under lockdown until the Hellbreakers 
have been executed. Three guards are stationed here, 
with keys for both gates, but they’ll only open them 
for guards with the pass phrase. The gates to the 
north and south of this area are iron, with Hardness 
18, and 72 HP (Broken Threshold 36), and the DC 
to Force them Open is 27.
Creatures: The guards only open the gates if they 
hear the proper pass phrase. Otherwise, if the PCs 
enter this area, they attack. They fight until reduced 
to 10 HP, at which point they attempt to surrender 
or flee. If the guards hear a disturbance in the Moil 
(such as an explosive entrance by the PCs), they rush 
to investigate, likely encountering the PCs in area K2.
CONTENT WARNING
The Gyve is intentionally a horrible place, a 
prison designed to cause suffering and includes 
mention of torture. Before you begin, understand 
that player consent (including that of the Game 
Master) is vital to a safe and fun play experience 
for everyone. You should talk with your players 
before beginning the adventure and modify 
descriptions of the narrative as appropriate.

K2. Moil
Makeshift buildings and canvas canopies lean against 
the walls of this courtyard. Large piles of wood and 
other raw materials sit next to them, scattered about the 
yard for use by the prisoners of the Gyve. Old, rusted 
manacles lie broken on the ground, remnants of the 
courtyard’s past.
The former slave auction attached to the prison was 
transformed into a labor camp after the Emancipation 
Edict in 4722 ar. Debtors and minor criminals are 
sentenced to work here, earning coppers to pay off 
their obligations by crafting supplies used by the army. 
This area is open to the sky and might have lighting 
based on the time of day the PCs attack. The prisoners 
are locked inside, so the area is empty (either because 
it’s night or because of Caeto’s lockdown orders) with 
nothing of note or value.
K3. Guard Tower	
Low 6
This stone tower rises 10 feet above the prison walls. Two 
bull’s-eye lanterns are mounted on the walls, and a ballista 
points in toward the prison grounds.
Twin towers to the east and west of the Moil house 
guards who watch for escapees. A ladder on the first 
floor (K3a) goes up to a trapdoor. If the guards see 
someone enter the first floor of the tower, they lock 
the trapdoor. The range of fire from the top of the 
tower (K3b) effectively includes the tower’s entire 
half of the court yard, but prevents the guards 
from targeting enemies on the far side of the prison 
grounds.
Creatures: Three guards are stationed in this area, 
day or night, and don’t leave the tower under any 
circumstances. If they see PCs in the Moil, they shoot 
at them from this location, with the artillerists using 
their actions to operate the ballista (Guns & Gears 
74) and the sniper using his own weapons. If it’s night, 
the sniper turns the lanterns to keep the PCs in light. 
If the PCs enter the tower, the guards switch to melee 
combat. They fight until reduced to 10 HP, at which 
point they attempt to surrender or flee.

K7. Storeroom
Closed chests line the walls of this room beneath shelves

K8. Holding Cell A
Dirty straw covers the floor of this room, piled in places

Prisoners sentenced to labor in the Moil sleep in this 
shared cell when they aren’t working. This room has 
no torches; if the PCs arrive during the day, the light 
coming in through the barred windows leaves the 
entire area in dim light, otherwise it’s dark.
A dozen people of various ages and ancestries are 
incarcerated here at the time of the PCs’ arrest. If the 
PCs free them, decrease their number of Suppression

recapturing them. The PCs can also attempt to recruit

solid wooden doors that line this hallway of dark stone. 
Occasional moans, sobs and other noises—even unhinged 
laughter—drift out from inside the cells. The stench of 
misery fills this area along with the miasma of unwashed 
bodies and excreta.
This outer hallway of the cell block is unlit and 
in darkness. A few candles burn low in the inner 
“courtyard,” leaving that area in dim light, a very 
small privilege for the better-behaved inmates that 
are kept in those cells. Two slightly larger cells in the 
western wall have one small window each—they’re 
typically given to prisoners who inform on their fellow 
inmates to the guards. The panel in each cell door can 
be opened to allow guards (or PCs) to look in.
Creatures: If the PCs successfully completed the 
Talisman Job, the Azris have been imprisoned here. 
As they’ve mostly been arrest for the optics, their cell 
doors are kept unlocked and they’re free to roam the 
floor as a special privilege. When the PCs enter, the 
Azris recognize them from previous encounters and 
attack in a rage! The pair focus on a single target at 
a time and protect each other’s backs. If the Azris 
weren’t arrested, the PCs can free their companions 
without issue.
WHO’S THERE?
The two Hellbreakers being held in area K13 aren’t 
named. If the PCs have formed a connection with 
any of the recruits, they might work well here, but 
be careful to consider whether that might be too 
upsetting.

K12. Warden’s Tower	
Moderate 6
This hexagonal chamber is finely appointed, with a rug 
covering the dark stone floor and simple ink drawings 
hanging on the wall between the barred windows. A large 
wooden desk stands in the middle of the room, covered 
in papers. One large, throne-like chair stands behind the 
desk and three smaller ones in front of it, two of them with 
leather straps on the arms and legs.
The warden rules the prison as a personal kingdom 
from this office. The smaller chairs are for her 
subordinates or, occasionally, prisoners who are 
restrained and brought here for interviews. The area 
is lit with everlight crystals, so it’s always bright light 
here.
Creatures: Warden Irkazer (relentless female 
human warden 8) runs the prison from this tower. 
She works day and night and can be found here at 
any time. She attacks any PCs who enter, fighting to 
the death.

K13. Oubliette
Low 6
A damp chill pervades this round, subterranean chamber. 
Water drips from the black stone, a constant trickle that 
seems somehow amplified into strange echoes, and almost 
instantly begins to feel monotonous. Rusty shackles hang 
from the ceiling and walls. In the main chamber, an iron 
smell of blood underlies the grave-like scent of the earth. 
A torture rack stands in the center of the room beneath a 
pulley system hanging from the ceiling, clearly visible in 
the light from flaming braziers. Cruel pokers, blades, and 
other implements of torture hang on the back wall.
Gyve jailers extract confessions, true or not, from 
prisoners in this torture chamber that was designed 
to prey on all the senses of its victims. Victims hang 
from manacles in the antechamber (K13a), where 
they’re forced to listen to others’ screams, while others 
wait in the main area (K13) and are forced to see what 
awaits them. Two Hellbreaker captives are here, both 
hanging from chains in the main chamber while their 
torturer prepares for another interrogation session.
The area is kept well-lit both so prisoners can 
see what awaits them and also as a contrast to the 
darkened cells above. The strange echoing properties 
enhance noises here—any effect that does sonic 
damage does an additional 1 point of sonic splash.
Creatures: In addition to the shackled Hellbreakers, 
the prison’s head interrogator is here with an assistant, 
planning for another session with her victims. If she 
hears PCs approaching in the antechamber, she moves 
to the northwest side, forcing them to enter the 
main chamber, where she enters melee. She fights to

MISSION: RIDE OR DIE
Once the PCs have rescued all of their fellow 
Hellbreakers from the Gyve, they must make their 
way out of the chaotic prison, avoiding guards and 
prisoners to reach the army stables through a winter 
storm that has gathered over the city. Once they make 
it to the stables, they can steal mounts both to speed 
their passage out of the city and prevent pursuit.
Chase: This encounter uses the chase subsystem 
(GM Core 192) as the PCs try to avoid falling into 
Caeto’s clutches in their rush toward freedom. Each 
round of this chase takes 15 minutes. Because the PCs 
are fleeing and trying to avoid pursuit, they act first. 
On their turn, the pursuers gain 1d4 Chase Points. In 
addition, the pursuers get a bonus to the roll equal 
to the PCs’ Suppression Point threshold (up to 4) and 
a penalty equal to the PCs’ Uprising Point threshold 
(up to 4), though these might cancel each other out. If 
the PCs were successful Placing Bombs earlier, remind 
them they can use those to help during their escape.
If the pursuers catch the PCs, a patrol cuts off their 
path and they must fight their way past it before they 
can resume their pursuit. When this happens, the PCs 
are presumed to be mounted unless they indicate 
otherwise (likely because they have a Speed greater 
than 30, or they’re too large to ride a horse). If they 
dismount, assume some of the other Hellbreakers catch 
their horses and they can remount freely after the fight.
Creatures: A number of army units rush to stop the 
PCs’ escape. Because they are not well organized, these 
are low-threat encounters. Because they can happen 
multiple times, you can mix and match who catches 
the escapees, drawing from the creatures below so 
the encounters feel different each time. You can build 
an encounter using the XP budget (GM Core 75) or 
use one of the following combinations: One adiutor 
and two elite infantry soldiers, one unsanctioned 
sheriff and two elite infantry soldiers, two equestrian 
constables and a conscript squad, two elite infantry 
soldiers and two watch officers.

MISSION: THE DRUMA ROAD GATE	
SEVERE 6
The massive wooden doors that form the Druma Road Gate 
rise above the city walls, a point of defensive construction 
meant to keep the city safe from any external threat.
Unfortunately for the PCs, one more obstacle stands 
between them and freedom: Caeto and most of the 
army are busy dealing with the chaos caused by the 
PCs’ actions (and perhaps literally putting out fires), 
but the Hellknights also responded to word of the 
prison break by sending units to secure the exits from 
the city. Use the map on page 114 for this encounter. 
The PCs notice the enemy as they approach the gate, 
and can begin this encounter mounted or on foot.
Creatures: Caeto sent a brigade of his Hellknights

the Hellbreakers traitors and murderers, and fight until 
slain or knocked unconscious to prevent their escape. 
While the PCs must deal with the primary threat here, 
you can describe smaller battles between other guards 
and the escaping Hellbreakers.
