Once upon a forgotten time, a king now nameless 
inherited the crown from his deceased younger 
brother, Grand Prince Cyricas, who had perished as a 
result of his own hubris in lands far away from home. 
The King-Now-Nameless demanded a tribute worthy 
his arrogance: the subjugation of the lands between 
the mountains. For centuries, the king’s ancestors had 
coveted these lands and bit and clawed at them to no 
avail. The Twelve Tribes of the Seasons, which had 
protected the region as one since before the sun was 
swallowed, were an impassable wood of birch, maple, 
and oak.
But even a great wood is nothing compared to the 
forest of swords and armor the King-Now-Nameless 
sent to do his bidding. Many of his warriors fell, some to 
spears and swords and others to schemes and deceit. An 
entire generation forgot what it meant to live in peace, 
knowing only fear, fighting, and fleeing. Capturing the 
land was not enough to satiate the King-Now-Nameless; 
he demanded the tribes be slaughtered, for he hungered 
for more than the title of conqueror.
Hunted, starving, and hiding, one desperate tribe 
painted their skin with the ashes of their dead. 
Through the ways of the Speakers of the Pale, they 
called upon their predecessors, the spirits of the land, 
and the patron deities of the Twelve Tribes. In the bleak 
silence of winter, one voice answered. Feast upon the 
harvest your enemies have wrought, the voice soothed. 
Become the herald of my winter and survive in spite of 
death—forever.
Eventually, the tribe was caught. Those who survived 
scattered to the winds like leaves in fall, but those who 
didn’t rose as wights. Before long, an immortal army 
stood ready to liberate the land and destroy those who

had slaughtered them. In fear, Taldor deposed their 
nameless, bloodthirsty grand prince, but it was too 
late—in a little over a decade, the undead drove the 
invaders out and made plans to march south.
Unwilling to let their legacy become that of 
bringing undeath to others, what remained of the 
Twelve Tribes allied with the Taldane army for one 
last war. They were so few in number that by the time 
the last wight was destroyed, so too was the culture 
of the Twelve Tribes of the Seasons. In tribute to the 
lost, Taldor commemorated the tribes as the Isgeri, a 
name some say means “those who were sacrificed,” 
or perhaps “those who sacrificed themselves.” The 
definitive meaning is unfortunately lost to time.
For some Isgeri descendants, such as the Alonnors 
and their fellow cultists, the ending of this story did 
not matter—if they considered the tale to have ended 
at all. They held the ancient pledge to their savior as 
sacred, but Isger was not freed from its conqueror. It 
fell to Taldor’s rule, after all, and then to Cheliax’s. 
Isger is, therefore, yet destined to become the realm of 
the Pallid Princess.
Illcayna Alonnor has believed since youth that she has 
a pivotal role to play in this grand destiny. Her feverish 
visions and transformation into a Child of Urgathoa 
only strengthened that sense of self-importance. For the 
past century, she has secretly sowed discord throughout 
the nation, instigating the Goblinblood Wars through 
Ezio Gaeta and cursing a merchant to afflict Gillamoor 
with a deadly curse. Her plots would have required 
another century to reach proper culmination, but the 
return of Tar-Baphon and the descent of warshards 
during the Godsrain accelerated her plans.
While most in Isger regard Illcayna as an exaggerated 
urban legend, the Wight Mother of Isger and her cult 
know they are close to reaching their goals and finally 
claiming the land for their goddess. With the murder 
of Hedvend VI distracting the political movers in 
Elidir, she is on the cusp of victory. Should she manage 
to curse the entire nation and deliver the land to 
Urgathoa, her goddess shall gain a place on Golarion 
where she is singularly revered, not reviled.
Warnings on the Horizon
The Hellbreakers have been busy since their explosive 
exit out of Elidir. During the party’s downtime, they 
have settled into a new headquarters at Highfort, 
an abandoned hobgoblin fortress once used during 
the Goblinblood Wars. As it is only a few days’ trek 
from Saringallow, Highfort’s location enables the 
two Hellbreakers branches to cooperate even as they 
remain isolated from one another. This foresight 
becomes very important in Chapter 8.
As Abadius comes to an end, reports of undead 
activity surface in southern Isger. At first, the 
troubles sound typical, but then the attacks increase 
exponentially. Settlements are overrun, and their 
residents flee for safety. The PCs can get a glimpse of 
the developing threat through the following methods, 
if they are available:
•	 Grizzo the goblin forager delivers a letter from 
the gnome official Ioan Marblemug. While Umok 
doesn’t require assistance yet, Captain Ioan 
finds it prudent to alert the PCs that undead 
are becoming an issue. If Fesimwyth “Fessy” 
Finwinkle, the Abadaran cleric from the gala, is 
alive and friendly, she co-signs the letter.
•	 One of the founders of Stumpfield, Erk Oilfingers 
the goblin painter, passes by Saringallow while 
leading refugees north. Erk is angry that their 
requests for aid to the official Isgeri army were 
ignored.
•	 If Lezinia, the human singer from the gala, is 
alive, she crosses paths with the party as a guest 
performer at the Fiend’s Finale. Lezinia urges the 
PCs to leave Isger, for she has heard that Caeto 
Vulaunex has ordered his forces to ignore the 
undead problem in favor of catching Hellbreakers.
Dampened Celebrations
With the Elidir Hellbreakers settled in at Highfort, 
Saringallow’s Hellbreakers host a celebratory dinner 
on the 1st of Calistril at Rhokrag’s house. At the 
gathering, the PCs see familiar faces ranging from 
Rhokrag to Maire to Xerra; even Gram (see the 
Saringallow gazetteer on page 200) makes a rare 
appearance. Phoebe and Alceo graciously host the 
celebrations, while Jenvirick represents the Elidir 
Hellbreakers with Sarevial and Otton.
THE CHITTERWOOD OFFENSIVE
A few days after he declared martial law in Elidir, 
Caeto Vulaunex directed his Hellknights to seize 
Logas. This unfortunately placed his comrades 
in the line of fire when undead rose in southern 
Isger. The Hellknights in Logas were ultimately 
routed, and the survivors who stumbled into 
the Chitterwood were captured by goblins who 
acquired their gear and modified it for their own 
purposes. In Calistril, these goblins with Hellknight 
gear successfully repel an undead invasion on the 
Chitterwood, then liberate Logas in what will come 
to be known as the Chitterwood Offensive.

===== Page 119 =====
118
Despite the dinner’s celebratory intent, a sense of dread 
lingers over the guests. Maire ultimately broaches the 
subject and asks if people have heard about the undead. 
The PCs can share what they know, and Jenvirick sadly 
mentions how she heard that Logas fell to an undead 
incursion some days ago. Phoebe, however, shares a letter.
“This is a copy of the reply Vulaunex sent to Logas after 
the city requested aid. Begins much as expected. ‘We are 
aware of the situation developing…’ and ‘I understand your 
concern…’ Bureaucratic speak. I’ll skip to the good part.
“‘Isger has greater problems than a few undead. The 
Hellbreakers are a pest that must be nipped in the bud 
before their dissidence spreads like a plague, though their 
self-righteous act may still be of some use. Your concerns 
are noted.’”
Alceo sighs. “The Hellbreakers have worked hard in 
the past months to earn the people’s trust and show that 
we’re an organization that takes action. With officials 
doing nothing about the crisis, people are frightened 
and desperate for help. We need to do all we can to 
help civilians find refuge against this undead entity and 
empower them to fight for themselves… and if the so-called 
leaders of Isger won’t protect its people from the undead, 
we’ll deal with it ourselves.”
PCs can attempt a Perception check to Sense Motive 
or a Society or Warfare Lore check to Recall Knowledge 
at DC 23 to suss out Caeto’s intent. On a success, they 
discern that the Hellknight hopes the Hellbreakers will 
play heroes. If they perish, it saves Caeto the trouble 
of hunting them, but if they live, they might still be 
weakened, making them easier to catch and dissolve.
The Hellbreakers have earned a reputation as an 
organization that fights for the people, and with no aid 
coming from government officials, civilians are itching 
to act and looking for guidance. The Hellbreakers 
just need to rally those ready to fight. Helping 
people secure their settlements or relocate to safety 
would make recruitment even easier. In fact, if the 
Hellbreakers solve the undead crisis once and for all, 
that in itself would cement their standing in the heart 
of the populace. With past successes like Hellknight 
Hill and Elidir under the Hellbreakers’ belt, Alceo is 
confident that tackling the undead head-on is within 
the organization’s capabilities. It’s time to prove to 
Caeto how much he has underestimated them.
NEW ASSIGNMENTS, OLD PLACES
The Riotmongers, Rhokrag, and Jenvirick quickly 
divide tasks up for the Hellbreakers. They charge the 
PCs with aiding and recruiting from the familiar area 
south of Saringallow and north of the Chitterwood. 
This also puts the party in charge of negotiating with 
Thorngrip—an 
exceptionally 
important 
task, 
as 
Thorngrip’s elders represent the Chitterwood much like 
how the Hellbreakers wish to represent the Isgeri outside 
the woods. Any promises the PCs make may become 
political obligations once the Hellbreakers free Isger.
As for solving the undead crisis, Alceo mentions he 
heard a rumor when he first came to the nation that a 
curse was the source of the undead. Phoebe chimes in 
and explains that the tale originated from merchants 
who traded in southern Isger. After all these years, 
however, present day trade caravans only know which 
routes are safe, not what or where they are avoiding. 
If the Hellbreakers ask the right questions and observe 
the undead, though, they should be able to triangulate 
the curse’s location by process of elimination.
CHAPTER TIMELINE
Below is a proposed timeline for specific events 
or deadlines featured in this chapter, though GMs 
are welcome to make adjustments to it as they 
see fit. Alceo shares any information that the 
Hellbreakers learn or any actions they take during 
the night of the day indicated via dream message. 
Meeting the suggested deadlines often gives extra 
rewards. Though missing them doesn’t impact the 
overall questline, this can limit the PCs’ options 
until they make up for them later.
CALISTRIL 4726 ar
1st: The celebration dinner takes place.
4th: Deadline for seeking Thorngrip aid.
6th: The Chitterwood Offensive successfully 
retakes Logas. Alceo negotiates an alliance 
with the Hellclad Goblins who saved Logas 
from the undead. Hellbreakers League recruits 
should convene in Logas from here on.
7th: Maire discovers Gillamoor is the source of 
the undead curse if the PCs haven’t.
9th: If the PCs have yet to investigate Gillamoor, 
the Riotmongers visit instead and discover 
that Illcayna is behind the rising undead. They 
fail to break the curse. This is the deadline to 
reconvene in Logas.
10th: The Hellbreakers army leaves Logas and 
marches toward Finder’s Gulch.
13th: The Hellbreakers army arrives on the 
outskirts of Finder’s Gulch.
19th: If she isn’t interrupted, Illcayna completes her 
curse and sacrifices Isger to Urgathoa at dusk.

Below are questions the PCs might ask after they are 
given their tasks and the answers Alceo provides.
Which settlements are we covering? “From closest 
to furthest from Saringallow, you’re in charge of 
Swiftrun, Stumpfield, Umok, and Vordia. Oh, and add 
Wolfpoint. There might be redeemable bandits hiding 
there from the undead.”
What should we do for the settlements? “Most will 
likely need fortifications, and some might have unique 
requests based on their situations. You can always 
escort folks to safety otherwise. Oh, and you can 
also send any recruits to Saringallow, though if that 
changes, I’ll let you know.”
Do we have to search for the curse? Rhokrag perks 
up. “I’ll bet you 100 gold that Maire and I can beat 
you lot to finding the hole these things are crawling 
out of while we’re in the north.”
Make it 100 gold each and it’s on. “So, 100 gold 
from each of you if we win? Deal!”
How much time do we have? “I’d like to know if 
Thorngrip will join us within three days from today,” 
Alceo says. “It’s tight deadline, but the sooner we know, 
the more time we have to ease others into accepting 
them as allies. As for recruitment, let’s reconvene on 
the 9th, though probably not in Saringallow. I’ll update 
you about that later. As for the curse…” Alceo’s voice 
drops to a whisper. “Rhokrag usually only bets if he 
believes he can get it done in a week. No pressure.”
What can we expect Thorngrip to demand? “I truly 
can’t say. It’s always difficult to guess what would help 
achieve reconciliation. I imagine Brakknap will help 
keep the terms reasonable.”
What are the rest of you doing? “Jenvirick will 
lead the Elidirans to recruit from around the capital. 
Rhokrag and Maire are headed to Breachill first, 
but they’ll recruit as they return. Phoebe and I are 
bound for Logas; there’s contradicting information 
about what happened there, so we need to see for 
ourselves how things are. Gram will be holding down 
Saringallow while we’re away.”
How do we contact each other if we’re all on the 
move? “…I knew I was forgetting something,” 
Alceo sighs. Gram presses a wand of dream message 
(4th-rank) into the cleric’s hand with a wink.
If the PCs have other means of helping the 
Hellbreakers communicate, they can offer solutions. 
Otherwise, the Hellbreakers settle on contacting Gram 
(mysterious female halfling candler 4) in Saringallow, 
who will update Alceo daily. Alceo will then send a 
dream message each night to 11 individuals of his 
choice; the PCs should pick two in their party to be 
designated contacts. They can update Alceo on who to 
contact if need be.
Undeath in Southern Isger
After the mission briefing, the game opens into a 
slight sandbox that proceeds mostly in downtime 
mode, with exploration and encounters in between. 
While the PCs have objectives with prospective 
deadlines, where they go and when is up to them. 
They might need to retreat and recuperate before 
heading out again after encounters with the undead 
roaming the lands.
Random Encounters: As they travel, the PCs are 
likely going to be ambushed by Illcayna’s minions, who 
grow bold as her plan approaches fruition. Once per 
day, whenever the PCs travel more than 1 mile from 
their point of origin, make a secret flat check against 
a DC of 5 + the number of days into Calistril (or the 
number of days passed since this chapter started). On 
a failure, the PCs encounter a group from the Undead 
Random Encounters table below within the next 24 
hours. Use appropriate Flip-Mats that match the 
PCs’ location, or reuse maps from previous chapters. 
If the PCs or the area they are in are under an effect 
that would suppress the rise of undead, conceal their 
presence from undead, or provide any similar benefit, 
the DC of the flat check decreases by 4.
Each time the PCs defeat a random encounter, 
you can forgo the flat check for 2 days. Once the 
curse in Gillamoor has been broken (see The Curse 
of Gillamoor on page 122), the DC of the flat check 
is reduced and fixed at 5 (and possibly reduced to 
1 with further protection). Once Illcayna has been 
destroyed, these encounters stop entirely except 
within 10 miles of Gillamoor if the curse there has 
not been dispelled.

HOW TO RECRUIT AN ARMY
From here on, the PCs can use the Assist a Settlement 
downtime activity and Recruit for the Cause 
exploration activity (page 120) to recruit troop units 
to use in skirmish encounters. For Chapter 7, access 
to different troops gives PCs options in an upcoming 
skirmish encounter. In Chapter 9, the number of 
troops the PCs have recruited matters slightly more. 
The PCs can continue using these activities during 
and after this chapter, either to make up for a failed

===== Page 121 =====
120
recruitment or to obtain the stronger advance troop. 
When running these activities, GMs can reintroduce 
past NPCs to provide roleplay opportunities.
Settlement Units: The troops recruitable from each 
settlement are as listed in the Settlement Units table 
above. The PCs should keep track of what and how 
many units they have recruited.
•	 Swiftrun’s Erastilian clergy are difficult to 
persuade, while the apprentice mages are eager to 
prove themselves.
•	 The nature of Stumpfield’s art makes some 
residents natural saboteurs.
•	 Stumpfield’s local spoken word association easily 
picks up warchanting.
•	 Umok can request that the wolves among their 
animal defenders aid the Hellbreakers.
•	 The gnome beastspeakers who communicate with 
the animals join if Umok is secured.
•	 While Vordia doesn’t have enough people to offer 
troops, they do know a few mercenaries they can 
hire instead.
•	 There are bandits hiding around Wolfpoint who 
can be persuaded—or intimidated—to join.
Treasure: Succeeding at the Assist a Settlement 
activity during Chapter 7 also rewards the PCs with 
items, as listed in the Settlement Skills and Rewards 
table above. Succeeding at Assist a Settlement outside 
of Chapter 7 does not yield these treasures, though 
GMs can give the items out for other accomplishments 
later at their discretion.
Reward: If the PCs successfully recruit troops from 
three different settlements, they gain 2 Reputation 
Points and 30 XP. If they manage to recruit troops from 
all five settlements, they instead gain 5 Reputation 
Points and 50 XP. This reward can be earned at any 
point, even outside of this chapter.
ASSIST A SETTLEMENT
CONCENTRATE
DOWNTIME
You spend a day helping a settlement prepare for 
incursions or defend against dangers. This is a Crafting, 
Society, or Survival check to fortify the location, or a 
Religion, Scouting Lore, or Stealth check to guard those 
leaving. The DC for these checks is a hard DC based on 
your current level (DC 25 for level 7). The GM can accept 
other skills as they see fit.
As part of this activity, the party can travel up to their 
Speed or the Speed of their mount or vehicle per day. 
Each settlement has additional skills you can use that are 
listed on the Settlement Skills and Rewards table above. 
The DC for these skills is an easy DC for your current level 
(DC 21 for level 7). You can only Assist a Settlement once 
per month.

for the Cause as one step better than what you rolled.
Success For a week, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to 
Recruit for the Cause or to Aid another PC to Recruit for 
the Cause at the settlement you assisted.
Critical Failure As success, but you gain a –2 circumstance 
penalty instead.
RECRUIT FOR THE CAUSE
EXPLORATION
You spend an hour speaking or corresponding with 
potential recruits, urging them to join the Hellbreakers’ 
cause. You can do this once per week per settlement 
or target as defined by the adventure. Once you have 
recruited a troop, you cannot recruit them again from the 
same settlement until the next chapter begins.
The DC to recruit is a very hard check for your level 
(DC 28 for level 7) using Diplomacy or Society. If more 
than one PC takes this activity at the same time, they can 
choose to roll separately or have one PC attempt the roll 
while the others Aid.

HOW TO DISCOVER A SOURCE
Some PCs might be more comfortable with academic 
pursuits, such as determining the location of the 
curse, than they are with attempting recruitment. This 
mission is conducted through the Locate the Curse 
downtime activity. To discover that Gillamoor is the 
curse’s source, the party needs to obtain 10 Tracking 
Points with the Victory Point system (GM Core 184).
LOCATE THE CURSE
CONCENTRATE
DOWNTIME
You spend the day pursuing rumors or tracing undead 
movements as you travel to triangulate the source of the 
undead scourge. You can take this activity once per day. 
Attempt a DC 25 Arcana, Diplomacy, Occultism, Religion, 
Survival, or suitable Lore check to Gather Information. 
GMs can allow other skills as they see fit and award 
circumstance bonuses for appropriate supporting actions 
or activities. If Brakknap is with the party, all DCs in this 
activity decrease by 5.
If the PCs don’t reach 10 Tracking Points by the 
7th of Calistril, Maire beats them to the punch. Alceo 
shares the news with everyone that night through 
dream message. As he and Phoebe can’t step away 
from Logas for a day or two yet, those closest to 
Gillamoor—likely the party—should investigate the 
place.
Treasure: Rhokrag put a lot of gold on the line to 
motivate the party. Should the PCs discover the location 
first, they can pick up their reward of 100 gp each when 
they next return to Saringallow. If they lose and pay up, 
Rhokrag gives them two jars of warding paste (page 
210) and a restful salve (page 210) each as consolation.
Reward: The PCs receive 30 XP if they locate the 
curse before Maire.
NEGOTIATING WITH GOBLINS
Recruiting Thorngrip is a more delicate 
matter given the lingering sentiments 
from the Goblinblood Wars. The 
new Hellbreakers army makes many 
goblinoids wary that it might become 
a threat to them in the future. While the 
PCs don’t meet any resistance when they 
arrive in Thorngrip, the atmosphere is tense 
and their reception cold. Brakknap is the 
only one who greets the PCs warmly.
“You come in difficult times to make a difficult request. 
The voices of my ancestors say this took place quite often 
over fifty-ten generations ago. I wonder why it stopped. 
Death has come for us all; prematurely, in many cases. I, 
for one, do not want to see the Chitterwood lifeless, so 
let us speak openly of the peace we both desire beyond 
all this death.”
After the PCs and Brakknap have caught up, they 
can begin negotiations with Thorngrip. This is an 
Influence challenge (GM Core 187) against the council 
of elders. The PCs have six 10-minute rounds to make 
their discovery and influence checks.

Weaknesses The elders love rhymes. One PC can attempt a 
DC 26 Performance or Theater Lore check at the start of 
each round to compose offers in limerick. On a success, 
all Influence DCs decrease by 2 for that round.
Background Council members have fancy or simple titles 
like “Master of the Communal Mud” or “Two.”
Appearance Six goblinoids make up this leadership council. 
All are considered elders, though this might be due to 
experience rather than age in some cases.
Personality The council is chaotic yet cohesive, each doing 
their best for this part of the Chitterwood.
Penalty The elders mistrust the written word. If the 
PCs mention or engage in the practice of writing, all 
influence DCs increase by 2 until the PCs and Brakknap 
forgo a round to assure the council that the party won’t 
bind their souls through text. Making this cultural error 
a second time increases the DCs permanently.
Development: After negotiations, Brakknap asks 
to join the party. He says he wishes to aid the PCs, 
particularly in locating the curse. The elders insist 
their advisor take two bodyguards with him (a goblin 
commando and a goblin pyro, Monster Core 174). 
While these goblins can’t participate meaningfully in 
combat, they do help drag Brakknap out of combat if 
a fight starts.
In truth, Brakknap has learned of a way to break the 
undead curse from his ancestors, but they cautioned 
that it might come at the cost of his life. The goblin 
oracle faces his end bravely for the greater good. He 
keeps this to himself, thinking the PCs and elders 
would reject his aid or prevent him from leaving if 
they knew of his impending death.
Treasure: In celebration of reaching an accord, the 
council of elders gifts Bounty’s Light (page 214) to the 
PCs.
Reward: Regardless of how well they negotiated, 
the PCs gain 80 XP.
L. The Curse of Gillamoor
After the Goblinblood Wars ended, Illcayna placed a 
curse she was testing on a merchant who was scouting 
out new trade routes. The unfortunate merchant later 
passed from sickness and was buried in Gillamoor. The 
curse on his body desecrated the settlement, and both the 
bodies previously buried in its graveyard and its living 
villagers transformed into undead. For a while, this curse 
was misidentified as a plague. The town was quarantined, 
and the steward put up a bounty for a cure. When none 
could find the nonexistent disease, however, the bounty 
was rescinded and Gillamoor forgotten… until now.
The curse is but a trial run of the ritual Illcayna 
wishes to inflict on Isger. With the true ritual underway, 
Gillamoor has become a conduit—one of many helping 
the ritual take root in the nation’s very soil. While 
dispelling the curse here does not stop Illcayna’s ritual, 
it can reduce the rate at which the undead spawn.
Village Condition: In the wake of the Goblinblood 
Wars but before the curse took hold, Gillamoor quickly 
recovered, becoming a vibrant village in the post-war 
economic boom. It was popular with caravans under 
Druma’s Mercenary League, who preferred homely 
bed-and-breakfasts to the crowded inns of larger 
settlements. Once the curse took root, the inhabitants 
left the village for the undead and weather to ravage. 
Today, Gillamoor is a decrepit ruin full of collapsed 
huts and houses. It’s devoid of the nature that usually 
reclaims such sites, and any trees still standing have an 
unhealthy wilt to them, their leaves spotted yellow and 
black. In the unsettling silence, the way to the graveyard 
is clear.

L2. KEEPER’S HUT
The grave keeper’s home was one of the last buildings 
to be left behind. The windows and doors are 
well-fortified. The interior is covered in a layer of 
dust but is otherwise suitable for an overnight 
rest… if the curse is no longer in effect.
Dying Erinyes: If the PCs spared Sister 
Endreah, the leader of the Golden Erinys from 
Chapter 2, they find her here with 1 Hit Point 
left, succumbing to the curse. If Endreah 
died, the PCs find Sister Sylve instead.
The Erinys sisters are not here for 
the curse; they were led here to hunt 
whoever disturbed the graves of their 
deceased. In truth, the missing dead 
have risen as wights loyal to Illcayna. 
The newly undead lured their past 
compatriots to Gillamoor in hopes of killing 
them to fuel the curse here.
Treasure: If the PCs manage to lift the curse before 
the 10th of Calistril, the sister here survives and takes 
shelter in Saringallow. She gifts the PCs the token of 
salt and earth (page 212) that saved her and points 
them to a disturbed grave where she saw a calamity 
(page 212) sticking out.
L3. THE CURSED GRAVE	
MODERATE 7
The merchant Illcayna cursed was an aiuvarin man 
from rural Druma named Dottol Harpier. Though 
his future with the caravan looked bright, Dottol’s 
life was cut short when he caught dysentery and died. 
Without a will to execute and not wanting to transport 
a possibly infectious body back to Druma, the caravan 
opted to bury him in a respectable grave in Gillamoor, 
unknowingly dooming the town.
Gillamoor’s graveyard is up on a 10-foot-high hill, 
surrounded by a brick-and-iron fence that’s 5 feet tall. 
All of the graves look like they’ve been dug up and 
desecrated. Dottol’s grave has been dug up as well, but 
his gravestone is still intact. Other than his name, the 
gravestone notes the year of his death (4702 ar) and a 
single sentence that reads, “Forever in the memory of 
the 27th contingent of the Mercenary League.”
The PCs can deduce Dottol’s ancestry and cause 
of death with a successful DC 28 Medicine check. If 
they succeed at a DC 23 Religion or Occultism check, 
they also learn that his bones are saturated with void 
energy that’s bleeding into the surrounding soil. If the 
PCs surpass this check by 5, they notice that there’s an 
even deeper well of undeath feeding and amplifying 
the curse on the body. In fact, an entire ocean’s worth 
of void energy rumbles beneath Isger, which can only 
be observed here because the body is tapping into it.
L1. THE ORDER OF THE PIKE	
TRIVIAL 7
The Hellbreakers aren’t the only ones seeking the 
curse’s source. A Hellknight contingent from the 
Order of the Pike, which is dedicated to slaying 
monsters that threaten society, broke off from 
Caeto’s forces after he ordered them to ignore 
the undead. They then located Gillamoor and 
came to see if they could solve the problem.
Creatures: Unfortunately, the undead 
thinned the Hellknights’ ranks as they 
traveled. Only Hecatinia and Hestlebeth 
Remsaine (determined female human 
Hellknight twins 3), nieces to the lictor 
of the Order of the Pike, managed 
to reach Gillamoor. When the PCs 
arrive, the twins are about to be 
overwhelmed by skeletal giants.

Lifting the Curse: If Brakknap isn’t with the party, 
the PCs can break the curse with rituals such as 
consecrate or divine keystone of 4th rank or higher. 
Other than the cost of time, the PCs might need to 
head to Logas or Saringallow to obtain ingredients if 
they don’t have any on hand.
If Brakknap is with the party, however, he reveals 
he knows of a faster method to break the curse that is 
made possible with the help of his ancestors. Unlike the 
rituals, which require greater preparation, Brakknap 
only needs to chant for 5 consecutive rounds. During 
these, he is slowed 2 each round and must remain 
within 5 feet of the grave.
Creature: While having Brakknap break the curse is 
efficient, it also marks him as a target for the undead 
to eliminate, as they can sense that his power would 
spell their doom. When the PCs or Brakknap start the 
ritual, four deathless acolytes and a Godclaw hellcrown 
stealthily rise to surround them. The acolytes come 
out from the graves, remaining close by so their aura 
can prevent healing and keep the PCs occupied. The 
Godclaw hellcrown rises outside and tries to pick 
off the ritual’s primary caster from behind the fence. 
Breaking the curse doesn’t disrupt these undead; they 
must be destroyed even if the curse is broken.
If Brakknap falls unconscious, his soul immediately 
rises and continues chanting over his own unconscious 
body. The goblin dies if he remains at 0 Hit Points 
for 3 consecutive turns. This sacrifice automatically 
breaks the curse, as his body sprouts into a tree over 
the grave with the statistics of a 4th-rank protector 
tree. Before his soul departs, Brakknap makes sure to 
comfort the PCs, saying that his death was his choice 
and wasn’t their fault, and that he’s glad to give back 
to those who gave so much for his people. Brakknap 
then joins his ancestors for his eternal rest, finally 
at peace. In the years afterward, more trees grow in 
Gillamoor in the direction of Chitterwood until the 
two woods become one.

hobgoblin battalions to the PCs’ forces.

M. The Mystery of Finder’s 
Gulch
The town of Finder’s Gulch suffered a fate similar to 
Gillamoor’s over a century ago, though rather than a 
curse, it was Illcayna herself who brought ruination. 
She didn’t discover the significance of her lair until 
she explored the twisting tunnels beyond the cave of 
Urgathoa’s temple. Though most led to the Darklands, 
there was one that led upward, ending at a grotto that 
featured a pool clearer than crystal. While observing 
the ancient murals on the walls and drinking from its 
waters, Illcayna learned this chamber was the site where 
her ancestors first accepted Urgathoa’s grace.
It was also here that the last warband of the Twelve 
Tribes of the Seasons gathered before they took up arms 
against their undead brethren and became the Isgeri. 
The truth was in the settlement’s name all along: this 
valley was the place where Isger was founded, spiritually 
and philosophically, in both undeath and death. Most 
would have been humbled by such revelations, but 
when Illcayna gained this knowledge, it only solidified 
her belief that she was the chosen ruler of Isger.
Scouting Finder’s Gulch: Illcayna’s name is 
whispered as an urban legend; learning that she’s the 
mastermind behind the current undead horde shocks 
the Hellbreakers’ recruits. Many begin to despair, 
as they were expecting to fight cultists or destroy a 
cursed item, not take up arms against a being of legend 
and nightmares. As the Riotmongers do all they can 
to repair the nascent army’s morale, they ask the PCs 
to scout out Finder’s Gulch and prove that Illcayna’s 
forces are not invincible.
After she obtained a warshard, Illcayna believed she’d 
become untouchable and decided that her strongest 
servants would be of more use fueling the undead 
reservoir needed for her nationwide curse than they 
would protecting her. Some of these servants readily give 
their existence, while others futilely attempt to resist her. 
Finder’s Gulch is therefore low in security for the first 
time in decades—an opportunity the PCs must seize.
M1. TOWN ENTRY ROAD	
TRIVIAL 7
The abandoned farms that flank the path into town 
used to house an acolyte and a necromancer who 
served as lookouts. Both have been sacrificed to the 
curse unwillingly.
Creatures: As she still needed someone to keep 
watch, Illcayna infected the redcaps on the outskirts 
of town with a fungal affliction known as the red drip. 
She held the disease in remission and threatened to 
withdraw her protection should the fey refuse to serve 
her. The redcaps grudgingly accepted, as they preferred 
to continue their murderous ways here instead of back 
in the First World.
While the redcaps are more than happy to make 
the PCs their latest victims, any offer to cure the 
visibly infected fey makes them hesitate. If the PCs 
successfully cure the redcaps, they decide to look away 
for a few minutes and let the PCs pass. They warn that 
if the PCs return this way, though, they’ll view it as a 
sign that the PCs wish to be murdered and will fight 
to the death.

MODERATE 7

The scale of the Finder’s Gulch’s town map makes it 
more suitable for the skirmish encounter on page 126 
than for individual encounters. GMs should use 
appropriate settlement Flip-Mats or maps of their 
choosing to better represent the area the PCs are in.

killed her and had them track down their makers. She 
made sure to capture the head priestess of the Ashen 
Church, Cileidia Iomandi. Illcayna always thought 
Cileidia was unworthy to serve Urgathoa, as the old 
Ustalav woman was more focused on planning how to 
attack her homeland than enacting the Pallid Princess’s 
will. Much like how she fed herself to the undead, 
Illcayna cut Cileidia and let the wights devour the 
priestess. While it was technically a proper final sacrifice 
in honor of a servant of Urgathoa who completed their 
task, Illcayna was personally glad to rid the cult of what 
she considered to be an embarrassment of a worshipper.
Haunt: The echoes of Cileidia’s gruesome end 
manifested as a haunt in the years after her death. The 
cultists serving Illcayna tolerated it, especially since 
she was fond of rewatching Cileidia’s demise. Since the 
curse ritual began, however, echoes of Illcayna’s own 
death have resurfaced as well. The similarities between 
the two priestesses’ deaths caused the two spiritual 
echoes to resonate until they merged.
When the haunt is active, creatures trained in 
Perception and not caught by the haunt notice a feminine 
figure flickering in the center of the haunt, which throngs 
of undead descend upon and devour. The visage of the 
figure changes rapidly, alternating between images of 
two different priestesses. The young priestess cries tears 
of joy as she holds out her arms to accept her fate, while 
the elderly priestess cries out in pain and panic, her arms 
bound to pillars with ropes. Both appear to be bleeding 
from long cuts made to the body.

M3. SACRIFICIAL SITE	
LOW 7
Worshippers of other faiths were sacrificed at this 
patch of scorched earth in the past. There used to be a 
haunt here, but with Illcayna’s ritual underway, it has 
dissipated to allow something else to take its place.
Creature: The most recent sacrifice of Illcayna’s 
own servants created an incendiary undead known as 
a sulfur zombie. Illcayna considers dealing with these 
residues to be beneath her. She appointed three newly 
risen erinys sister wights to keep the fiery undead in 
check. Having been defeated by the PCs in the past, 
the undead sisters fight until destroyed. Note that the 
erinys sister wights only have a claw and a dart Strike 
instead of the usual attacks of a wight.

M4. DESECRATED CHURCH	
SEVERE 7
The Urgathoans have thoroughly desecrated this 
former temple to Pharasma. All windows are broken, 
and the walls have been graffitied with praises to the 
Pallid Princess. Attempts to fully tear down the building 
have always failed, so the structure was eventually 
left alone. When the delegation from the Whispering 
Way requested a permanent residence, the Urgathoans 
arranged for them to move into this building as a 
stealthy insult. The map of the interior of this church 
is on page 128.
The Whispering Way’s assistance is naturally not 
altruistic, as Tar-Baphon would not mind having 
another Child of Urgathoa as a servant. If that servant 
came with a piece of territory, all the better. There’s 
also the concern that a warshard-empowered Illcayna 
could become an enemy, as she would soundly reject the 
idea of serving anyone but Urgathoa. The Whispering 
Way thus sent the dhampir witch Varlario Demicci 
(carefree agender dhampir witch 8) to Isger as both a 
goodwill ambassador and a spy. Varlario has furthered 
Illcayna’s plans and in the process learned many of her 
weaknesses. The witch has even developed a spell to 
deprive the Wight Mother of Isger of her warshard 
should the need arise.
Creatures: With Illcayna busy with her ritual, 
Varlario found time to invite a sarcovalt and two 
skavelings from the Whispering Way over as guests. 
Varlario doesn’t mind the PCs overhearing their 
conversation, finding it amusing that anyone might 
consider taking Illcayna down instead of fleeing. In 
their opinion, the wannabe-heroes are a few months 
too late; if Illcayna hadn’t gotten the warshard, they 
might have stood a chance. If they converse with 
Varlario, the PCs easily get the sense that the spy 
wouldn’t mind establishing a secret alliance. While 
Varlario can assist the PCs in learning Illcayna’s 
weaknesses, making a deal with the Whispering Way 
greatly harms the reputation of the Hellbreakers, 
causing the PCs to lose 5 Reputation Points.
In combat, the sarcovalt and the skavelings fight to 
the death, while Varlario fights until they are below 50 
Hit Points. Once they hit this threshold, Varlario begs 
for mercy, offering anything the PCs wish in exchange 
for their life. If the PCs don’t give up, Varlario distracts 
them by throwing their items at them before using 
their translocate spell to flee.

Treasure: Other than loot from the enemies, the PCs

Varlario’s notes that Illcayna’s final ritual is set to take

gives way to night. To finalize the curse, Illcayna must 
return to a location in Finder’s Gulch that Varlario 
hasn’t been privy to. The location in question is the 
Grotto of the Sacrificed (page 130).
M5. WEST TOWN
Before Illcayna’s transformation, the Ashen Church 
lived and operated in the west part of town. The secret 
basements and rooms here remained in use to create 
undead after the cult’s annihilation. A brief exploration 
of the buildings reveals paperwork and correspondence 
left behind by Illcayna’s servants, some half-finished 
before their authors were sacrificed to the growing 
curse. A PC who succeeds at a DC 24 Religion, Undead 
Lore, or Warfare Lore check can use the information 
here to research the types of troops they might face in 
the Siege of Finder’s Gulch (page 133). On a critical 
success, they can also estimate the number of troops 
they’ll run up against.
Treasure: Searching through the buildings, the PCs 
can uncover 220 gp worth of onyx left behind from 
create undead rituals. There’s also enough information 
here for them to learn the ritual if they wish.
M6. SARCOVALT HIVE	
MODERATE 7
North of the town center lie several buildings that used 
to be the political center of Finder’s Gulch. The largest 
building served as an open town hall beside which the 
mayor lived. There are also two community gardens: one 
for herbs and one (surprisingly) for poisonous plants.
Creature: Where there is fervent Urgathoa worship, 
there are sarcovalts. Occasionally, when Illcayna 
deems a person so unworthy that she wouldn’t even 
give them the privilege of becoming undead, she 
summons sarcovalts to dispatch the eyesore. It’s been 
a while since Illcayna sacrificed servants worthy or 
unworthy, and the hungry sarcovalt hive in the area 
pounces on the PCs the first chance they get.

M7. EMPTY ROAD
LOW 7
This straight path used to be the 
commercial heart of town, filled with 
businesses that were small but essential. 
Now, the shopfronts are devoid of goods, 
and the residences above them are empty.
Creature: A skeletal Hellknight bonesinger 
patrols these streets in a mockery of 
Cheliax’s supposed grip on the nation.

M8. FROZEN RIVER
This part of Finder’s Gulch has been flooded since a 
rockslide downstream (northeast of area M2) slowed 
the flow of the stream. As it’s currently winter, the 
water has frozen in slippery ice. The ice is considered 
difficult terrain, though a creature can attempt to 
move on it at full Speed. To do so, they must succeed 
at a DC 28 Acrobatics check to maintain their balance. 
On failure, they fall prone.
Hazard: The river’s ice is thin. If two or more PCs 
walk onto the ice, they hear a series of metallic cracks, 
indications that the ice is about to break.
THIN ICE
HAZARD 8
ENVIRONMENTAL
Stealth DC 28 (expert)
Description The white-and-blue ice is less structurally 
sound than it looks.
Disable DC 31 Nature or Survival (expert) to spread out 
and prevent the ice from cracking further, or DC 31 
Acrobatics or Athletics (trained) to get off the ice safely 
as it cracks.
Crack [reaction] Trigger Two or more creatures step onto the ice 
in area M8; Effect The ice beneath the party cracks. All 
creatures in area M8 must attempt a DC 30 Reflex save. 
On a failure, they fall into the freezing water, whereupon 
they must succeed at a basic DC 30 Fortitude save 
against 4d10+22 cold damage. On a critical failure, the 
creature must start holding their breath or risk drowning 
as their muscles lock and they begin to sink. A creature 
must spend an action to Swim to the shore and must 
then succeed at a DC 30 Athletics check to Climb up out 
of the water.
Reset The river freezes over every night, 
restoring this hazard. The hazard disappears 
once the vernal equinox passes.
Treasure: If a PC Searches the bottom 
of the riverbed, they find a delaying aeon 
stone and a greater devilwing badge (page 
211) that were dropped by adventurers 
who fell to Illcayna.
M9. TEMPLE OF URGATHOA
This cave used to be a shrine to another 
goddess until Illcayna claimed it. The 
cultists destroyed the original reliefs 
and covered what remained with 
depictions of Urgathoa’s hedonism. 
The interior is draped in chains of phalanges 
connected with sinew, a way for Illcayna to display of 
the number of creatures she has recruited into her fold 
over the years.
Fortunately for the PCs, Illcayna is out surveying 
her work. She has left the temple unguarded out of 
arrogance, believing she and her plans are untouchable. 
The PCs have plenty of time to Search the location and 
discover the secret entrance to the tunnels that lead 
to the Darklands. If the PCs have Bounty’s Light or 
Lifebloom in their possession, fluorescent stencils of 
hands and feet appear along the walls of the tunnels, 
guiding them to the Grotto of the Sacrificed (page 
130). The journey takes only 10 minutes, though the 
winding path makes it feel much longer.
Treasure: In a treasure box behind a good lock 
(five DC 30 Thievery checks), the PCs find a potion 
of flying, a pallid crystal (page 199), and a discarded 
greater staff of healing.
CLEARING FINDER’S GULCH
It takes the Hellbreakers army 3 days to travel from 
Logas to Finders Gulch. After arriving, they camp 
on the outskirts, which allows the PCs to rest safely 
outside the town without fear of being attacked. As 
the army needs time to recover from their march 
and conduct some last-minute training, the task of 
clearing out the town of Finder’s Gulch falls to the 
PCs. Once the ruins are cleared, the army moves into 
the town itself and Finder’s Gulch effectively becomes 
a level 3 settlement.
Treasure: The army arrives with two catapults 
(Guns and Gears 75), which Rhokrag eagerly gives 
Varlario

130
a demonstration with. The PCs are given control of 
these and can put them anywhere in Finder’s Gulch. 
Moving the siege weapons into place takes an hour 
each time.
Reward: If the PCs manage to clear the town of 
hostiles before or on the day the army arrives, they 
gain 50 XP and 5 Reputation Points. If they clear it 
after the army arrives, they only receive 30 XP and 2 
Reputation Points.
N. The Grotto of the 
Sacrificed
The walls of this 20-foot-high ellipsoid cave are 
fully decorated with murals whose magical pigments 
survived the ravages of time and weather. Despite 
Illcayna’s influence, the plants here remain lush, 
though they frost over in winter. A large opening 
about the same size as the pool within the grotto 
allows the natural light in.
As perhaps one last attempt to record who they 
were, the last of the Twelve Tribes painted the walls to 
depict their culture, icons, and beliefs. There are four 
major murals, each dedicated to a season, and since 
there were three tribes per season, every season is also 
associated with three patron deities. This connection 
partially survived to modern times in the names of the 
months of the modern Avistani calendar.
Reward: The PCs receive 80 XP for fully exploring 
all areas of the grotto.
N1. MURAL OF SPRING
Flowers blooming upon branches without leaves make up 
the border of this mural. Members of the Twelve Tribes 
in varied clothing and body paint holding their sacred 
implements gather around a warrior who raises Lifebloom. 
On the trees and field flanking this image, animals rouse 
from sleep. A butterfly bearing the moon on its wings and 
a flock of whip-poor-wills stand out in particular. There are 
also sprays of petals that suggest wind blowing.
A PC who succeeds at a DC 23 Religion or Nature 
check recognizes the favored animals of Desna and 
Pharasma. If their result is at least 28, they also discern 
that the animals and wind likely represent Gozreh.
Spring Awakening: If a PC holding Lifebloom 
touches the mural outside of combat, all in the 
grotto find themselves in a nightscape version of the 
grotto. Specters of the Isgeri surround them. If any 
PCs speak Hallit, they recognize a few words as the

N2. MURAL OF SUMMER
Though the border of this mural depicts flames, the painting 
is welcoming rather than intimidating. The center depicts 
the Kellid tribes on one side and a group of goblinoids 
emerging from a forest on the other. Bounty’s Light sits 
between the two, ambiguous in which direction it’s passed. 
A dove with a sun crown flies above the exchange, and a 
stag and rhinoceros flank the image as witnesses.
PCs who succeed at a DC 23 Religion or Survival 
check to Recall Knowledge recognize the favored 
animals to be those of Sarenrae, Erastil, 
and Gorum. If a PC rolls 28 or higher, 
they intuit that the message is about two 
peoples at peace, but that the chances 
of war breaking out are ever present.
Midsummer 
Dreams: 
When 
a PC holding Bounty’s Light 
touches the mural, everyone in 
the grotto must attempt a DC 28 
Will save against a 4th-rank sleep 
spell. PCs who sleep for 1 minute 
from the spell wake as if they had taken 
a full long rest. Any daily preparations 
necessary are included in this effect. A PC who 
benefited from this nap must wait a week before they 
can benefit from it again. They can accept the sleep 
effect any number of times.
N3. MURAL OF AUTUMN
A large wheat field serves as the mural’s backdrop. 
Some people are harvesting, while others are hunting 
on horseback. There is a disconcerting aura despite 
the serene image, as scorpions and jackals leer at the 
bountiful harvest.
It’s here that the PCs notice that 
there’s a faint carving of a serpent 
that wraps around the entire 
grotto. PCs who succeed at a 
DC 23 Farming Lore or Religion 
check to Recall Knowledge 
recognize the favored animals 
of Rovagug and Lamashtu, with 
the serpent likely representing 
Asmodeus. If they roll 28 or 
higher, the PCs recall that there’s 
an ancient calendar system where a leap 
month would be inserted at different times of the year, 
and that Asmodeus might symbolize that “rogue” 
month. This is highly ironic as Taldor, the odd army 
out in the war against the wights, ended up splintered, 
and the province that broke the empire later dedicated 
itself to the Prince of Hell. It’s as if the Isgeri predicted 
Cheliax’s infernal future.
The Rightful Goddess: One of the feminine figures 
seated on a horse holds a black scythe (Reaper’s Sigh, 
page 214), though the distinct lack of flies and rot 
suggests she is not Urgathoa. Every time the PCs fall 
asleep to the effect in area N2, this woman visits them 
in their dreams. Other than traditional Kellid attire, 
she wears stripes of white ash. As she approaches, the 
woman bleaches as she becomes a wight and her 
steed rots to a skeleton.
This is a spirit much like those 
encountered in area N1, except she 
speaks from the perspective of 
those who became the wights that 
defended Isger. As Illcayna’s direct 
ancestor, this spirit knows Illcayna’s 
backstory. If questioned about 
Illcayna, the spirit laments that their 
ill choice condemned her and how 
their holy implement, Reaper’s Sigh, 
was corrupted as punishment. The spirit 
urges the PCs to “evoke the true goddess of 
the harvest” to cleanse the scythe; a PC who succeeds 
at a DC 34 Religion check knows that the spirit is 
referring to Jaidi.
N4. MURAL OF WINTER
In a rather unusual choice, perhaps to represent 
themselves walking to their deaths, the artists painted 
the mural of winter surrounding the entrance. The border 
of painted frost and snow can almost be mistaken to be

the real thing. Few creatures are depicted except for 
three humanoid figures. They huddle in a hut, making 
handicrafts by a hearth. One is draped in gold and 
silver. The other two wear clothes of many colors, 
and their handicrafts are just as bright.
PCs who succeed at a DC 23 Religion or Society

to be Shelyn. If they roll at least 28, they 
presume by process of elimination that

he looks nothing like the Midnight Lord. This 
is because the image is of the god Zon-Kuthon 
used to be, called Dou-Bral in the days before

N5. POOL OF MEMORIES
Were it not for its reflective surface, 
one might not even realize this is a pool of 
water. The water is surprisingly thin and does not impede 
movement at all.
Any PCs who drink the waters here receive a rush of 
ancient memories in flashes, mostly involving the past 
inhabitants’ struggle against the four-centuries-long 
Taldane incursion. How this pool formed is sadly a 
magical art lost to time.
Each time the PCs drink, they gain the ability to 
understand the spirits in the grotto for 1 hour. However, 
they must also succeed at a DC 28 Will save or become 
stupefied 1 for the same duration. The DC of the save 
increases by 2 for each subsequent drink, and the 
condition also increases by 1, up to stupefied 3. Upon 
three failures (a critical failure counts as two), the PC 
is permanently slowed 1 as they become burdened 
by ancient memories. The stupefied condition can be 
reduced by appropriate spells, but the permanent slowed 
condition requires effects like wish or stronger to remove.
Winter’s End
While Illcayna left Finder’s Gulch unguarded more out of 
overconfidence than strategy, it does put the Hellbreakers 
in an odd position. Instead of attacking Illcayna in her 
home, they must now keep her from reaching the Grotto 
of the Sacrificed to complete her ritual and enact her 
curse. It’s more likely, therefore, that the Hellbreakers 
will find themselves under siege soon. Simply throwing 
their troops at the undead would be ineffective, but 
luckily, the Whispering Way has been plotting against 
Illcayna, seeking to weaken her through her very own 
curse via a counter-ritual they call Wight Queen’s thaw. 
The PCs can learn about this counter-ritual through 
Varlario Demicci or her notes (area M5).
Once the PCs have cleared Finder’s Gulch of threats, 
they have time to research this counter-ritual 
and other ways to weaken Illcayna until she 
returns on the 19th. Alceo suggests that they 
look into how to stop Illcayna if none of the 
PCs think to engage in this research on their 
own. This investigation uses the Research 
subsystem on page 190 of GM Core. Most 
of the research takes place in Finder’s Gulch, 
but the PCs might need to venture out to other 
settlements to find answers. Each research check 
takes 4 hours, but this doesn’t include any 
travel time to go to other places.
Meanwhile, under the direction of 
the 
Riotmongers, 
any 
assembled 
Hellbreakers and their allies begin 
fortifying Finder’s Gulch in preparation 
for 
Illcayna’s 
return. 
Instead 
of 
researching, PCs can use the intervening time 
to perform downtime activities and continue 
to help settlements, recruit troops, or break the curse 
in Gillamoor if they haven’t yet.
AREAS OF RESEARCH
The PCs can perform research checks in the following 
areas to learn how to stop Illcayna.
Search Finder’s Gulch: The town has been Illcayna’s 
base of operations for years, so lingering traces of her 
energy and other information should help the PCs 
uncover her weaknesses; Maximum RP 10; Research 
Checks DC 18 Urgathoa Lore to recall information 
about related undead creatures, DC 21 Occultism or 
Religion to examine sacrificial sites, DC 23 Diplomacy 
or Intimidation to get information from Whispering 
Way cultists.
Commune in the Grotto: The Grotto of the Sacrificed 
holds mystical and spiritual energy that could help 
direct the PCs’ research; Maximum RP 10; Research 
Checks DC 20 Isger Lore or Society to decipher the 
many murals; DC 23 Diplomacy to commune with 
the resident spirits; DC 25 Occultism or Religion to 
extract meaning from visions provided by the pool of 
memories.
Field Research: By scouring the remains of 
Gillamoor or by sneaking back into Elidir to find 
treatises on undeath, the PCs might learn about 
Illcayna’s methods and her grasp on existence; 
Maximum RP 5; Research Checks DC 23 Occultism 
or Religion to glean knowledge from any discoveries, 
DC 25 Perception to find specific books or clues, DC 
25 Stealth to stay hidden from lingering threats.

3 	 Research Points The PCs find an inert sample of the 
disease carried by all children of Urgathoa: the pallid 
plague. They can then concoct a temporary vaccine 
against it, granting them a +2 circumstance bonus to 
their saves against Illcayna’s pallid plague.
5 	 Research Points The PCs learn that the illumination 
of Bounty’s Light empowers those who stand against 
undead like Illcayna. PCs and allies within the bright 
light shed by that relic gain a +2 status bonus to all 
saving throws against Illcayna’s spells.
10 	Research Points The PCs uncover stories of how 
Lifebloom is enchanted to strike fear into the hearts of 
wights who beheld the blade. A PC who wields that relic 
can spend a single action to brandish it like a religious 
symbol. Illcayna and any wights who can see this 
become frightened 3 (DC 23 Will save) and can’t reduce 
the value of their frightened condition for as long as a 
living creature wields Lifebloom in their line of sight. At 
this point, Illcayna’s undead minions sense that the PCs 
are learning how to defeat their progenitor and move to 
ambush them. If the PCs are outside Finder’s Gulch (or 
the next time they leave the town), roll on the undead 
encounter chart.
12 	Research Points The PCs understand that Varlario’s 
occult magnet in area M4 might be used to extract 
Illcayna’s warshard from her body and master its usage. 
How to do so and its effects are described in Warshard 
Extraction on page 135.
15 	Research Points The PCs learn the full details of the 
Whispering Way’s counter-ritual, Wight Queen’s thaw. 
Alceo volunteers to perform the counter-ritual when 
Illcayna arrives to ensure the PCs can take the fight to 
her. Before each of her turns in the encounter with her, 
Illcayna must attempt a DC 10 flat check. On a failure, 
she is slowed 1 for that round.
20 	RP The echo of Cileidia’s death (as seen in the haunt 
in area M2) can be turned against Illcayna if she’s 
damaged by Reaper’s Sigh. What happens if the PCs 
successfully turn the weapon against her is described 
in Final Feast on page 135. How they might disarm 
her of the scythe remains a challenge, especially as 
it’s melded into her arm. Learning this information 
produces another echo of Cileidia’s death wherever the 
PCs are. They encounter the haunt from area M2 again, 
even if it has been deactivated.
25 	RP The Urgathoan temple in Finder’s Gulch (area 
M9) used to be a shrine to Jaidi, the Azlanti goddess 
known as the Blessing and Bounty and spouse of 
Erastil. Urgathoa replaced her as the tribe’s patron 
after Earthfall took place. Evoking Jaidi’s name and 
prayer is the key to purifying Reaper’s Sigh; when in 
Illcayna’s presence, a PC can spend an action with the 
concentrate trait and attempt a DC 25 Farming Lore, 
Nature, or Religion check to implore Jaidi to reclaim 
the scythe. On a success, Reaper’s Sigh glows, dealing 
2d6 spirit damage with the holy trait (double on a 
critical success) to Illcayna, who is then disarmed of 
the weapon. In such an instance, she can’t pick it back 
up again.
Reward: The PCs receive 80 XP for completing 
their research on the topic. Otherwise, the PCs gain 
30 XP.
The Siege of Finder’s GulchLow 7
This event occurs on the afternoon of the 19th of 
Calistril. Illcayna and her army descend upon Finder’s 
Gulch to complete her curse. Luckily, Hellbreakers 
scouts spot their approach, and the PCs have time to 
prepare against the undead.
This encounter uses the skirmish warfare rules 
found on pages 158–169 of Battlecry! GMs should 
read up on these rules before running this encounter. 
The objective of this encounter is to destroy Illcayna’s 
armies. This encounter begins in area M1, the town 
outskirts, and the buildings here are intact enough to 
be impassable for troops. Use the Finder’s Gulch map 
from page 126. 
Picking Troops: For combat, each PC takes 
command of a 7th-level troop from the following 
list: bandit gang (NPC Core 22), elite hobgoblin 
battalion (NPC Core 5, 194), gnome cannon corps 
(Battlecry! 182), Stumpfield war chanters (page 
218), Umok beastspeakers (page 221), and a weak 
Hellknight cavalry brigade (NPC Core 5, 92). A 
troop is available only if the PCs have recruited them 
earlier in the chapter, though enough elite hobgoblin 
battalions arrive from Logas to give each PC a troop 
to command.
Creatures: Illcayna has an army of undead at her 
command, and the PCs and their troops face off 
against two skeleton mobs and two wight battalions. 
Other groups the Hellbreakers recruited hold the rest 
of the undead army at bay in other parts of the town, 
succeeding if the PCs do well but faltering if the PCs 
are also being routed.
Illcayna remains out of the fray for now, believing 
her army to be enough to crush the living who have 
invaded her town. She spectates in amusement until the 
PCs vanquish her troops. Then, she flies in the direction 
of the grotto, where the PCs can confront her.

Drain Life (divine) When the warshard wight damages a

attack or its bound weapon, the warshard wight gains

a spawned wight after 1d4 rounds. This spawned wight 
is under the command of the warshard wight that killed 
it. It doesn’t have drain life or warshard wight spawn 
and is clumsy 2 for as long as it’s a spawned wight. If its 
creator dies, the spawned wight becomes a full-fledged, 
autonomous warshard wight; it regains its free will, 
gains drain life and warshard wight spawn, and is no 
longer clumsy.
ILLCAYNA ALONNOR
CREATURE 9
Page 242
Initiative Perception +23
Though this is an extreme encounter (as Illcayna is 
still very powerful), the PCs have several ways to turn 
the tide in their favor. What they’ve learned through 
their research comes into play now!
Warshard Extraction: A PC who understands how 
to remove Illcayna’s warshard using Varlario’s occult 
magnet can perform an Interact action while adjacent 
to Illcayna and wielding the magnet. Illcayna must 
attempt a DC 29 Fortitude save. On a failure, the 
warshard is pulled forcibly from her body and into 
that PC’s possession. Illcayna loses her ability to use 
the Bleeding Heart of Urgathoa as a greater symbol 
of conflict. She also loses her bonus to saves against 
holy effects and her ability to make warshard-tipped 
entrail melee Strikes.
Final Feast: The PCs can either disarm Illcayna of 
Reaper’s Sigh or use the prayer they learned through 
research to force it to fall from her body. Once she 
loses Reaper’s Sigh, Illcayna cannot use her Reaper’s 
Sigh Strikes. Should the PCs retrieve the scythe and 
successfully hit Illcayna with it, the Strike deals 
an additional 2d6 persistent bleed damage. Each 
time Illcayna takes bleed damage from this effect, 
each undead creature within 60 feet (even undead 
summoned by Illcayna) must succeed at a DC 27 Will 
save or spend its next turn attacking only Illcayna. 
Illcayna’s share blessing ability doesn’t trigger if she 
is destroyed this way. As she is once again devoured, 
Illcayna wordlessly cries, her tears drawn to the pool.
Treasure: The PCs receive all items under Illcayna’s 
item entry, including Reaper’s Sigh and the Bleeding 
Heart of Urgathoa, which reverts to a greater symbol 
of conflict and a blood-red lump of warshard.
Reward: The PCs gain 5 Reputation Points for 
defeating the Wight Mother of Isger, stopping her curse, 
and ending the undead scourge she brought about.
Boon of the Isgeri Spirits: The first time the PCs 
take a long rest after their battle with Illcayna, they 
collectively experience a dream. A swarm of flies 
washes over a frozen land like snowflakes, while 
a stag stands opposite on lush grounds. A voice in 
their heads, booming yet soothing, asks which they 
choose. Those who once protected these lands made 
their choices. What would those protecting the lands 
now choose?
If the PCs pick the stag and its warm spring, they 
wake to find clawed bracers by their side. If they 
pick the flies and its desolate winter, they receive a 
runestone with a decaying rune instead. Refusing 
to pick or being split in opinion results in the PCs 
being jolted out of the dream to find a standard-grade 
duskwood shield.
Concluding the Chapter
The PCs are hailed as heroes by the Hellbreakers and 
their army for defeating Illcayna in combat. Maire 
spreads tales about the party’s exploits, giving them 
titles like “Spring’s Herald” or “Wight Mother’s Bane.” 
She takes care to leave out identifying details; the PCs 
can encourage or discourage her or maybe even get a 
say on their epithet. 
With this triumph, the Hellbreakers have cemented 
their place not only in Isger’s politics, but also the 
nation’s history. What’s not likely going to be recorded 
in the books is the whereabouts of the warshard 
Illcayna had. The Hellbreakers’ leadership decides to 
keep it safe in their headquarters.
The Hellbreakers also decide it best to collapse 
Urgathoa’s temple to hide the grotto’s entrance from 
those with ill intent. The PCs have a chance to study it 
fully beforehand and can always access it from above 
with flight if necessary. There’s also a bottle of shared 
memories among Illcayna’s possessions, which hints at 
the last Wonder of the Seasons, the wintry Woe. The 
mystery of Woe is outside the scope of this adventure, 
however, and is best explored after the PCs have 
liberated Isger.

In traveling throughout the country and bolstering 
the populace to join their rebellion, the Hellbreakers 
League has exposed itself—never have its members 
and leadership been so widely known. With many 
who joined the League eager to share stories of their 
contribution, there’s bound to be an absent mind or slip 
of a tongue.
Aided by powerful friends, Caeto carefully tracked 
down the League’s leadership to Saringallow. The fear 
of being watched seemed almost forgotten in the high of 
victory and the frenzy of returning to normalcy. Caeto 
allowed that complacency to grow, even fueling it by 
acting like he was cowed. In reality, the Hellknight was 
preparing a strike force, one pointed at the very heart of 
the rebel organization and waiting to stab.
Opportunity arrived on the sacred Day of Bones, a 
Pharasmin holiday where the community comes together 
to pay respects to the recent dead. As the first of such 
major holidays after the undead scourge, this Day of 
Bones is particularly significant, serving as a milestone in 
both resetting the pace of peace and acknowledging those 
who lost their lives. Though many were buried in their 
home settlements, the Hellbreakers agreed that honoring 
those who died shouldn’t be bound by the whereabouts 
of the living, and the organization’s leadership promised 
to observe the holiday together in Saringallow.
In this moment of vulnerability, Caeto’s forces struck. 
At noon on the Day of Bones, when the Hellbreakers 
had agreed to assemble, Hellknights and Chelaxian 
forces seized Saringallow’s entries and exits and 
searched for dissidents. On the top of their list were 
the Riotmongers and the PCs. As chaos descended 
in the town, a mile away on the Conerica River, the 
PCs are helping to upgrade the Witchfire for potential

DESPERATE ESCAPE	
CHASE 8
Escaping Caeto’s forces is played out as a chase using the 
chase subsystem (GM Core 192). Each obstacle lasts 1 
round, meaning the PCs can only attempt to overcome 
them once. The Penalty entry in each obstacle happens 
automatically. Many obstacles ask the PCs to make a 
hard choice and choose an NPC to rescue. While the 
captured NPCs will get roughed up, make it obvious 
that the enemies want to capture the Hellbreakers alive. 
Should a PC reach 0 Hit Points during the chase, they 
automatically stabilize, and the GM can assume any 
unconscious PCs are carried onto the next obstacle by a 
party member, NPC, or a sympathetic citizen.

expected, arriving there in 4 days instead of 2.
Special If there are Hellbreaker NPCs with the party, 
reduce the DC of this obstacle by 1 for each NPC.
Development: The Elidir Hellbreakers are relieved 
to see the PCs and any rescued NPCs arrive. Any 
PCs in need of medical attention are treated 
immediately. Currently, Highfort only knows that 
Saringallow has been seized and that all captured 
Hellbreakers seem to be alive. There are reports of 
forces scouring the rural areas for escapees, making 
travel high risk. No one has figured out how the 
headquarters was discovered and to what extent 
they’ve been exposed.
Jenvirick informs the PCs that she has sent for 
help, and the Eagle Knights are sending Ethran 
Howell to aid them. The Hellbreakers should take 
some mandatory downtime until they arrive. The PCs 
can use this downtime however they wish, so long as 
they remain in Highfort.
The PCs receive 100 gp as a stipend toward 
equipment. As the city of Logas remains an ally, 
the PCs can access common items up to their level, 
though delivery might take time. Quoster can also 
attempt to obtain uncommon resources for them 
with a flat DC 15 check.
Reward: The PCs receive 80 XP for completing the 
chase. If they escaped with four or more Hellbreaker 
NPCs free, they receive an additional 30 XP for the 
massive accomplishment. If a Riotmonger escaped, 
that Riotmonger grows more resolute, and the GM 
can add the elite template to the rescued Riotmonger 
from here on.
Picking Up the Pieces
Ethran Howell arrives in the afternoon of the 10th 
of Pharast, heavily disguised as a wandering druid. A 
meeting is called, during which Ethran and Jenvirick 
share the following intel.
•	 The day after Saringallow was seized, new forces 
moved in to secure the city. While most are loyal 
to Caeto, some Isgeri soldiers hold grudges 
over the inaction against the undead, a parallel 
to Isger’s neglect of the countryside during the 
Goblinblood Wars.
•	 A strict curfew has been enforced on Saringallow. 
Even merchants haven’t been able to enter the 
city, and those at the docks have only been 
allowed to briefly resupply under the watchful 
eye of Caeto’s forces.
•	 The captured Hellbreakers are still alive. Ethran 
suspects Caeto intends to interrogate them 
HANDLING LOSS
While the chase is meant to create a low point in 
the Adventure Path, GMs are free to modify the 
chase’s penalties as necessary for their table, as 
not everyone might stomach losing so many NPCs 
in a single moment. The PCs might wish to sacrifice 
themselves during the chase, which the GM can 
accept at their discretion. As the adventure doesn’t 
have room to cover the journey of any PCs who 
are captured, players should discuss with their GM 
on how best to handle the story going forward. 
The player can consider playing an NPC or a new 
character, so long as their level is appropriate.

MANOR MATTERS
The PCs can attempt to Recall Knowledge with a DC 
24 appropriate Lore or Society check to know that 
Sarini Manor was once the home of the noble house 
of Sarini. The Sarinis were found guilty of kidnapping 
and murdering many of their own servants’ children 
for fiendish sacrifices, and the noble family was 
subsequently lynched for their offense. Their surviving 
servants then founded Saringallow. The manor is also 
the source of the demon bile incident over a decade 
ago. While that corruption was cleared, no one has 
been back to inspect it.
Unfortunately, 
Jenvirick 
reports 
that 
after 
Saringallow was seized, Caeto allowed the diabolist 
Sephone Haugini (uptight female human diabolist 9) 
to claim the manor, reportedly for private research. As 
Sephone’s mission is secondary, Caeto provided her 
with security that’s sufficient but not impeccably tight. 
From Ethran’s assessment, an infiltration might be 
possible, though the exact method is to be determined.
Ethran says they have a place close to the manor 
for the PCs to work from. A sympathetic rancher has 
expressed that he’s willing to take the PCs in. If the 
PCs leave with Ethran by midnight (Pharast 10th 
going to 11th), they can get to the ranch by the early 
morning of the 12th. While the PCs undertake this 
mission, any Saringallow NPCs rescued will stay in 
Highfort to gather the army in secret.
VULAUNEX RANCH
After two days and nights of floating down the Clover 
Stream, Ethran takes the PCs to meet a rancher with 
a mild resemblance to Caeto. The man, Fierdo 
Vulaunex (grizzled male human rancher 3), 
is in fact Caeto’s eldest brother. The ranch 
the PCs are hiding in is the Hellknight’s 
childhood home, which he left and never 
visited again. His family isn’t happy 
about the man Caeto has become, and 
while guilt is a motivator, Fierdo says the 
family is helping because the Hellbreakers 
are doing what’s right.
Meeting Fierdo is an opportunity for 
the PCs to learn more about who Caeto 
was before he became a Hellknight. 
More details on Caeto’s life can be found 
in his NPC entry on page 238. The PCs’ 
focus in this chapter remains on Sarini Manor 
otherwise.
Development: After the PCs settle down in one of 
the ranch’s dormitories and learn how to disguise 
themselves in both appearance and vocabulary as 
ranch hands and rovers here for the upcoming calving 
season, Sarevial arrives on Quoster’s cart, ready to 
pass the PCs and Ethran new intel so they can begin 
their infiltration. The infiltration of Sarini Manor 
uses the infiltration subsystem on pages 196–199 of 
GM Core.
Infiltration Day 1: An Ambush 
in the Dark
Sarevial reveals there are two groups headed toward 
Sarini Manor who’ll be camping near the ranch 
tonight: a unit of Isgeri infantry and a mercenary crew. 
Those at Sarini Manor likely haven’t met these new 
hires yet, so if the PCs successfully infiltrate, intercept, 
or replace one or both of the groups, they can gain free 
access to the manor.
Working to take over the manor from within over a 
few days is unlikely to alert those in Saringallow that 
something is wrong at the manor, and being part of 
a larger group would also help the PCs blend in. The 
party will also need to keep Lifebloom out of sight 
since it’s easily identifiable, though the other Wonders 
of the Seasons aren’t known to the Hellknights.
Between replacing or infiltrating the group or 
bribing and recruiting them, Ethran thinks it’s better 
for the Hellbreakers to choose the former because 
there’s no risk of betrayal. The choice is ultimately 
left up to the party, and Ethran reminds the PCs that 
no matter what happens, they should use nonlethal 
force. Killing will give Caeto ammunition to paint the 
 Fierdo

Hellbreakers as dangerous insurgents. For each non-
fey creature the PCs kill in this chapter, they lose 1 
Reputation Point unless stated otherwise.
Open Plans: The PCs have a lot of flexibility on 
how to handle the two groups, from their approach 
to how many enemies they want to take out. The 
two units are camped in clearings that are adjacent 
to each other, separated by a forest trail. Relations 
between the two groups are strained after several 
poor interactions between them on the trip from 
Elidir to Saringallow.
Whatever the plan is, the PCs should complete it 
within the next 24 hours, as the groups are scheduled 
to report to Sephone after this time passes. With a 
day to prepare and act, the PCs can spy on the groups 
to gather information and plan out their strategies. 
While they only need to replace or infiltrate one 
group, they should think of strategies to handle the

a group dismissed is a boon in itself since it’ll thin out 
the number of enemies during the secret takeover of 
Sarini Manor.
ISGERI INFANTRY	
MODERATE 8
The tents in the northern clearing are uniform and 
orderly, with guards regularly patrolling both within 
the camp as well as on the periphery. This group of 
Isgeri infantry is led by Nixa Volsetti (loyal female 
human captain 7), a soldier native to Saringallow. 
After 10 years in the military, Nixa has seen for 
herself how the army has failed the people of Isger 
time and again due to the ineptitude and willful 
inaction of the ruling elites, and she’s desperate 
for reform. Whatever hope she had in Caeto’s 
decisiveness quickly soured when he ordered the 
army to ignore the undead uprising. Her resentment 
only increased with the seizure of Saringallow and 
Caeto’s willingness to work with fiends. Many of her 
soldiers share this sentiment and openly discuss their 
frustrations as they walk about the camp.
The PCs can easily overhear these conversations 
without a check while spying on the soldiers. Despite 
rumors of disgruntled fey, the soldiers don’t care to 
keep their voices down, believing their captain Nixa 
knows tricks to pacify the fey if issues arise. A PC

THE CAUSTIC AND CAUTIOUS	
MODERATE 8
In comparison to the other contingent, the southern 
clearing is disorganized. These mercenaries came 
together at the last minute for this assignment, so they 
don’t work very well together nor make great company. 
Some are Isgeri Slayers, while the rest used to work for the 
unscrupulous Azri family. The mercenaries spend their 
time huddled by the fire, playing games, and drinking. 
Most keep their voices low out of fear of offending the 
fey rumored to be in the region. Any PCs who succeeds 
at a DC 26 Perception check can hear them share gossip 
about the kinds of fey appearing in Sarini Manor.
Creatures: What the mercenary band lacks in 
coordination, they make up for in numbers. If attacked 
outright, those hurt raise the alarm. Mercenaries swarm 
out into a single troop that does its best to keep the PCs 
in their squares. The drill sergeant leading them stay in 
the distance, picking off targets with ranged attacks. 
Both flee and seek help from the Isgeri infantry when 
they fall below 30 Hit Points.
If the Isgeri army is attacked, the mercenaries assume 
they were attacked by fey for failing to keep their voices 
down. They only check on the camp once things fall 
quiet again, though they’re doing so more to scavenge 
for valuables than to help. Like the Isgeri army, if the 
PCs capture the mercenary band and commander, 
they’re held at Highfort.

Fear and Greed: The PCs can exploit the band’s fear

The successes between scaring and persuading the

Impact on Infiltration: Take note that an alliance

DISHONORABLY DISMISSED
Should the PCs replace or ally with one group and

AWARENESS POINTS
Anytime the PCs roll a critical failure on a 
skill check during their infiltration, they gain 1 
Awareness Point. If the roll was for a check under 
a complication entry, they gain 2 Awareness 
Points instead. The PCs can get a maximum of 25 
Awareness Points. Upon reaching this threshold, 
infiltration immediately ends. The party is caught 
and thrown into the stables in the southwest 
corner of the manor grounds. Ethran arrives with 
some Hellbreakers (use the statistics of a line 
infantry [Pathfinder NPC Core 90]) within the hour 
to free the PCs, after which they must deal with 
the security and researchers via combat.
VERSATILE EDGE POINTS
While Edge Points are usually used to succeed at a 
failed roll against an obstacle or complication, for 
this chapter they can be expended to improve the 
result of any failed skill check to a success, providing 
the PC attempted the check while on Sarini Manor 
grounds and they’re outside of combat.
