IN CASE OF FAILURE…
If the PCs end up failing both encounters, they can get 
hired as independent contractors by Sephone, who’s 
short on hands. The PCs must spend 8 hours each day 
taking the Earn Income downtime activity and will 
need to explore the manor to know what each room 
does. On the other hand, they do get a room of their 
own (area O9) and have more flexibility in where and 
when they go. You should run the rest of this chapter 
more as a dungeon crawl if the PCs go this route. The 
same applies if the PCs choose Stealth to sneak in and 
out through area O5.
Infiltration Day 2: Joining the 
Rotation
The second day of infiltration is dedicated to feeling 
out the exact number of enemies and their whereabouts 
over the course of a day. The PCs have 6 rounds to 
obtain as many Victory Points as possible. Each round, 
they can attempt a DC 22 Perception check to Seek, a 
DC 24 Warfare Lore check to Investigate, or a DC 26 
Diplomacy or Deception check to Gather Information. 
Once they’ve reached 6 Victory Points, the PCs can 
also attempt a DC 24 Isger Lore or Nature check to 
learn more about the fey that was here before Sephone 
took over. Any time the PCs critically fail a check, they 
gain 1 Awareness Point.
0 Victory Points: The lighting conditions for the 
outdoors depend on the time of day (bright for day, 
dark for night), while the interior is generally well lit 
except when an area isn’t in use. The soldiers try to 
avoid having dim light, as that’s the optimal lighting 
conditions for fey. Most doors, except those to area 
O10, are poor in quality.
2 Victory Points: There are three shifts per day, 
named morning (8 a.m. to 4 p.m.), afternoon (4 p.m. 
to midnight) and night shift (midnight to 8 a.m.). 
Most guards have only a single work shift a day. They 
generally eat before and after work. Most return after 
a shift to sleep, though it’s not unknown for slackers to 
return late and end up needing an extra shift off before 
they work again.
4 Victory Points: The PCs learn that during each 
shift, there’s one line infantry and one elite watch 
officer guarding areas O3 and O4, and another line 
infantry and watch officer guarding areas O11 and the 
corridor on the second floor. A draconic fumecrux and 
a watchmage guard the exterior at the front entrance 
and in the garden (area O7). The dormitory for the 
troops is beyond the map. If necessary, the GM can 
use the ambush site on page 140 to represent the 
encampment. The GM should keep these creatures 
visible on the map for the PCs at all times.
6 Victory Points: Sephone has a private research team 
of two kylixes, three zealots of Asmodeus, and two 
demonologists (NPC Core 100). These researchers are 
in the library (area O1) during the day and afternoon 
shifts and in their sleeping quarters (area O8) at night. 
Every other day on the even dates, Sephone calls half 
of the team (one of each NPC type) to meet with her in 
area O10 during the afternoon shift. The GM should 
keep these creatures visible on the map for the PCs at 
all times.
8 Victory Points: There’s quite a bit of dangerous 
flora around. The PCs learn about the poisonous 
plants in area O7 and breathless thickets in area O13. 
They also learn that Sephone has put up a bounty for 
anyone willing to do pruning.
10 Victory Points: Some fey seized Sarini Manor 
shortly after Illcayna’s death, calling it an “overdue 
payment.” Bitter and vengeful after Sephone drove 
them off, these fey might make good allies. That said, 
the Hellbreakers will likely need to negotiate with 
the fey too… or send them back to the First World 
permanently.
12 Victory Points: The ancient Kellid tribes used 
to commune with the fey. The fey probably don’t 
understand that the tributes stopped with the tribes’ 
extinction. While fey such as the empress katroome, 
draxies, and pixies are unfriendly but likely to let the 
PCs explain or retreat, the redcaps and elananxes are 
hostile and attack on sight.

post. The same applies to the research team.
If a troop loses their commander NPC, they become 
frightened 1. If two or more researchers go missing 
or are defeated, the other research staff become 
frightened 1. Any point a creature reaches frightened 
4, it flees from the area and manor altogether; the PCs 
can consider the creature permanently defeated and 
remove it from the map.
Day 3 to Day 6: Shift by Shift
The third day begins with a commotion in the garden; 
the excavation has finally uncovered the rumored 
corrupted basement. The guards complain that with 
Sephone’s habit of sleeping in the morning, some poor 
sods are going to be up in the night as prime targets 
for the fey to attack. The PCs can learn where in the 
manor fey have been spotted and at what times if 
there’s a restriction.
From this day onward, the PCs can decide what they 
wish to do shift by shift. The obstacle in each room 
is generally the creatures in it. Each area also details 
if there are opportunities or complications and the 
requirements or trigger for them, such as time of day. 
The PCs can visit up to three areas per shift without 
drawing attention. For each area after the third, the 
party gains 1 AP.
Focus by Day: For easier encounter management, 
you can have the PCs focus on befriending or 
removing the fey on Day 3 (areas O1, O6, O9, and 
O12), seeking out opportunities and learning about 
complications in advance on Day 4 (areas O1, O7, O8, 
and O10 in particular), then taking out the enemies on 
Days 5 and 6. The PCs should know that the night of 
the 18th of Pharast (or Day 7 of their infiltration) is 
when the Hellbreakers must take the manor, by force 
if necessary.
O1. LIBRARY	
MODERATE 8	
As Saringallow took away most books of value, there 
remained a lot of empty shelves for Sephone to fill 
with her own collection. Any PC who succeeds at a 
DC 26 Arcana or Religion check to Recall Knowledge 
recognizes that most of her collection is about 
teleportation, conjurations, summoning, and Hell. In 
the day and afternoon, the room is kept brightly lit. 
At night, all fires are put out, though the visiting fey 
bring a small lamp that makes it dim light instead.
Creatures: During the morning and afternoon 
shifts, Sephone’s research team gathers here. Every 
other day on odd dates, Sephone calls half of the 
team (one of each NPC type) to report to her in area 
O10 during the afternoon shift. At night, draxies and 
pixies appear, discussing how best to evict the humans. 
If the PCs express that they also want to remove the 
people here, the fey’s attitude automatically becomes 
indifferent, and they can be further influenced from 
there. If they become helpful, the PCs can convince 
them to help with the opportunity here. Evicting the 
researchers from this room is enough for these fey 
to consider any past debts paid, and they become 
willing to help the PCs tackle any enemy on the first 
floor. They refuse to touch the katroome in area O6 
and don’t go upstairs since that’s redcap territory.

O2. MESS HALL
This room, once meant for recreation, has been 
converted to a dining room for staff and security to have 
their meals. The fireplace is used as the stove. There’s 
at least a couple of guards posted in this room at all 
times, though they are usually slacking off and take a -2 
circumstance penalty to their Perception checks.
Complication: If the PCs have 5 or more AP, the 
watch officer leading the troop on the first floor 
guards this area themselves. They’re quick to call for 
assistance from any of the nearby rooms if attacked.
Opportunity: There’s usually a stockpile of 20 
or so minor elixirs of life (Player Core 2 288) here, 
replenished daily. If the PCs hide, take, or steal the 
entire stash twice, the privilege is withdrawn, and all 
of Sephone’s staff and security become permanently 
drained 2. The PCs gain 1 EP.
O3. BALLROOM
The east half of this ballroom has collapsed and is 
mostly covered in rubble, except for a corridor that’s 
accessible over a 3-foot-tall railing. The area is brightly 
lit by both standing torches and the fireplace, though 
it’s not unusual for the fey to put these fires out to 
spook the soldiers.
The rubble reaches 10 feet high and requires a 
successful DC 26 Athletics check to Climb. The PCs 
can reach area O6 by succeeding at this check to Climb 
over the rubble in the southeast. Doing so attracts the 
attention of the troops guarding this area. If the PCs 
haven’t allied with the Isgeri army or mercenaries, 
climbing the rubble in view of the troops increases 
their AP by 5 if the PCs are observed climbing.
The troops guarding the first floor are mostly 
concentrated here. They pay attention to what’s going 
on in area O4 but ignore noises from areas O5 or O6 
unless they’re absolutely certain an ally (the PCs count 
if they’ve infiltrated as hired hands) is calling for help.
Complication or Opportunity: Every time the PCs 
reach 10 AP and every 5 points above 10, all troops 
are gathered here to be searched. If the PCs are hiding 
among the troops, they must succeed at a DC 26 
Deception, Diplomacy, or Thievery check to conceal 
suspicious items and keep up their disguise. The PCs 
can also attempt a DC 28 Stealth check to sneak out of 
the search. If they’re allied with Nixa’s army, the DC 
decreases by 5. If they’re allied with the mercenaries, 
the DC increases by 5. The search lasts an entire shift, 
which gives the PCs 1 EP each if they evade, pass, or 
otherwise escape inspection. This EP expires at the end 
of the next shift.
O4. ENTRANCE
What was once a beautiful sitting room is now armed 
to the teeth like the interior of a guard’s tower. At least 
a third of the guards on the first floor of the manor 
are situated here. The watch officer leading the line 
infantry usually passes time in the cloak room off to 
the left, unless the PCs have 5 or more AP (area O2).
Treasure: Someone left a greater devilwing badge 
(page 211) in the cloak room.
O5. FORGOTTEN BEDROOM
This dark bedroom full of moss used to be a guest 
bedroom on the second floor. It survived the fall 
relatively intact and now rests on the first floor. Only 
the windows were shattered. 
This room is a security blind spot. So long as the 
PCs successfully Hide from the troops in the garden 
(area O7), they can Sneak into this room by succeeding 
at a DC 22 Athletics check to Climb on the outside. 
The PCs can even take a long rest here so long as they 
make no noise and stay in the dark.
O6. A FEY’S THRONE 	
TRIVIAL 8
The only way to enter into this unlit area of the manor 
is by climbing over the rubble from area O3. While the 
dining room remains relatively intact, the breakfast 
room and pantry have been crushed by the study 
above. The alchemy set that used to be in the room 
is in shambles. The floors creak when stepped on, 
imposing a –4 circumstance penalty to Stealth checks 
to Hide, Sneak, and conduct other similar activities.
Creature: An empress katroome by the name of 
Spring’s Crown (haughty agender empress katroome

“throne room.” This magical beast is an advanced

O10. DIABOLIST OFFICE AND QUARTERS
Sephone converted the bathroom to her private office 
and quarters. Other than a hefty desk taken from the 
main bedroom, very few furnishings decorate this area. 
Sephone even opts for a bedroll instead of a proper bed.
Opportunity: Sephone is usually here and sleeps in 
the morning. This changes once the excavation in the 
garden (area O7) unearths the basement (area O14). 
From the 14th and onward, Sephone spends her time 
in area O14 except for meetings and sleep. Each door 
has a good lock, and Sephone expects the security to 
keep people out of her room.
If the PCs are allied with Nixa’s army, they get a 
+2 circumstance bonus to Stealth checks to get into 
the room. If the PCs allied with the mercenaries, the 
number of checks needed to unlock the doors decrease 
by two each. Access to Sephone’s room allows the 
PCs to tamper with her items; if the PCs succeed at 
three DC 26 Arcana, Occultism, or Religion checks, 
Sephone loses a spell of each rank from her prepared 
spell list, determined by the GM. Unless a PC rolled 
a critical failure, which causes the PCs to gain 2 AP, 
Sephone assumes the tampering to be due to vicious 
fey pranks. If a PC critically succeeds, they also learn 
that Sephone has contracted an instillo and coartis 
to serve her.
Sephone is away for the entire day on the 16th of 
Pharast. She doesn’t reveal why she was gone, only 
that she headed into Saringallow. PCs who Investigate 
this room on the 16th can attempt a DC 28 Arcana 
or Religion check to Recall Knowledge to recognize 
preparations for a resurrect ritual.
Forgotten Connection: While she mainly follows 
Caeto into Isger to secure a recommendation for her 
to become a Hellknight signifier of the Order of the 
Gate, Sephone has an ulterior motive: she wants to 
know if Caeto knew who her parents were. Sephone 
was a Goblinblood orphan, only a few months old 
when Caeto’s contingent rescued her from goblinoids 
who’d raided a village and kidnapped its villagers. 
Despite being told to leave the child behind for the 
rescued folks to take to safety, Caeto then personally 
cared for Sephone until he found an orphanage in 
Haugin’s Ear that was willing to take her in. Caeto has 
forgotten about this small act of kindness completely, 
while Sephone hasn’t. She attempted and failed to 
write a letter to him a number of times, leaving a 
stack of drafts behind. The PCs can find out about this 
motivation of hers if they succeed at a DC 24 Arcana 
or Society check to Decipher Writing.
Reward: If the PCs discover Sephone’s past 
connection with Caeto, they gain 30 XP.
Treasure: Among Sephone’s belongings are a jade 
bauble (Player Core 2 305) and a greater emerald 
grasshopper.
O11. RUINED MASTER BEDROOM
The manor’s once-splendid master bedroom has an 
unfortunate hole in it from the collapsed roof. The 
commander NPC usually stands out on the balcony 
of the master bedroom, while the troops are inside 
and also stationed along the walkway and area O12 
during the day and afternoon.
Complication: If the PCs successfully tamper with 
Sephone’s items, she moves to sleep here during the 
morning shift under the watch of the guards.
O12. STUDY REMNANTS 	
MODERATE 8
The study’s remains are a ruin of its former self. All 
furniture, broken or whole, are pushed into the rotunda.
Creatures: The troops move out of this area at 
night to avoid the elananx and redcaps under the 
command of a pukwudgie named Rustflesh. He would 
rather like to evict both humanoids and other fey out 
of the manor, and an alliance with him is unlikely. 
Fortunately, Rustflesh fights to the death against the 
PCs, unaware of how powerful they are. If the PCs 
defeat Rustflesh and befriend the redcaps, they recruit 
a weak redcap brigade (Battlecry! 189).

BREATHLESS THICKETS (3)	
HAZARD 6
UNCOMMON
COMPLEX
ENVIRONMENTAL
 PLANT
Stealth +15 (expert; or –10 and no minimum proficiency if the 
thicket has been recognized)
Description A 10-foot-wide patch of dead shrubs with wilted 
flowers steals the breath of the living.
Disable DC 28 Nature (expert) or Survival (expert) to 
recognize the thicket for what it is and avoid it
AC 21; Fort +18, Ref +11
Hardness 15; HP 58 (BT 29); Immunities critical hits, object 
immunities, precision damage; Weaknesses fire 15
Branch Ambush [reaction] Trigger A creature that breathes steps 
within 5 feet of a thicket; Effect The thicket makes a 
sinewy leaves Strike against the triggering creature. The 
hazard then rolls initiative.
Routine (3 actions) The breathless thickets patch attempts 
to Strike a creature in its reach. It then uses Suffocate if 
it has any creature grabbed; otherwise, it continues to 
Strike.
Melee [one-action] sinewy leaves +20 (reach 10 feet), Effect branch 
grab
Branch Grab If the breathless thicket hits a creature with 
its leaves, that creature becomes grabbed by the thicket. 
Unlike with a normal Grab, the creature isn’t immobilized, 
but it can’t move beyond the reach of the thicket’s leaves. 
A creature can sever a branch by Striking against AC 18 
and dealing at least 12 slashing damage. A branch doesn’t 
have the thicket’s Hardness, and damaging it doesn’t deal 
damage to the thicket. The DC to Escape a branch is 26.
Suffocate [two-actions] (incapacitation, nonlethal) Requirements The 
breathless thicket has grabbed one or more creatures 
that breathe; Effect The dead flowers of the breathless 
thicket begin pulling oxygen from its victims’ lungs. Each 
creature grabbed by the breathless thicket takes 4d6 
nonlethal bludgeoning damage and must attempt a DC 26 
Fortitude save.
Critical Success The creature takes no damage and can 
immediately attempt to Escape (DC 26) as a free action.
Success The creature takes half damage and is stupefied 
1 for 1 round.
Failure The creature takes full damage, is stupefied 
1 for 1 round, and is stunned 1. For as long as it’s 
grabbed by the thicket, the creature must hold its 
breath or suffocate.
Critical Failure As failure, but the creature also falls 
unconscious and starts suffocating. If it’s no longer 
grabbed, the creature stops suffocating.
Reset The thicket goes back into hibernation 1 round after 
there are no more targets to Strike in its reach. It then 
remains dormant for 24 hours.
Opportunity: A PC who succeeds at a DC 29 
Nature or Survival check can remove a thicket 
without triggering it and unleash it in an area of 
their choice. If Sephone knows the PCs removed the 
breathless thickets, the PCs must succeed at a DC 
25 Deception check before or after they unleash the 
breathless thickets or gain 3 AP.
Treasure: Sephone has put up a reward for anyone 
who can get rid of all the orchard patches. If the PCs 
destroy or remove all the breathless thickets, she 
rewards them with a pair of armbands of athleticism. 
The PCs also find a pair of boots of bounding 
entangled in one of the thickets.
Day 7: Confrontation
The PCs must end their infiltration on the night of 
the 18th of Pharast, as the Hellbreakers expect Caeto 
to return by tomorrow. This confrontation can be 
triggered earlier at your discretion, particularly if 
all the troops and NPCs guarding the manor and 
Sephone’s staff have been defeated. When infiltration 
ends, for each troop or NPC they haven’t permanently 
removed, the PCs gain 2 AP. Sephone and fey creatures 
are excluded from this calculation. The GM should 
tally up the total number of AP the PCs have at this 
point. For every 5 points, the PCs gain 1 Liberation 
Point, which will apply in Chapter 9 (page 158). 
Location: If the basement hasn’t been excavated, 
Sephone sends the instillo to intercept the PCs at 
area O3 while she waits in area O10. Otherwise, the 
encounters take place as indicated below.

This room has been left dark. The pentagram at 
the room’s center is still fresh, as if someone has 
retraced it.
Creature: Sephone secured the service of an instillo 
to delay the PCs. They fight to the death.

Concluding the Chapter
Once the PCs defeat and capture Sephone, the other 
forces at Sarini Manor also submit. Prisoners are 
taken to Highfort, where the Hellbreakers’ army 
slowly assembles. The morning after they captured

delayed in his return by a series of “unforeseen 
circumstances.” This development has bought the 
Hellbreakers precious breathing room; the liberation 
of Saringallow awaits.

Interrupted Celebrations
The PCs are due for a rest after taking over Sarini 
Manor. Ethran and Jenvirik take over the duty of 
setting up the command post so the party can get 
some downtime. Since they’re now free on the vernal 
equinox, Fierdo asks if they would like to participate 
in the local celebration of Firstbloom on the night of 
the 19th. The PCs can accept or decline as they see fit; 
this decision only has a small impact on their starting 
location for the next encounter.
Firstbloom: For those who work in agriculture, 
Firstbloom is often considered the start of a new 
year. The holiday is celebrated on the evening before 
the vernal equinox, which keeps the celebration from 
overlapping with the numerous tasks required during 
Planting Week. While the PCs likely missed much of 
the setup, they are nevertheless welcome to join in the 
feasting, dancing, and exchanging of flower crowns.
Development: As midnight draws near, Nolaria 
stumbles into the celebrations, seeking sanctuary. The 
fact that Nolaria escaped from Saringallow with intel 
on the city’s current state makes her an important asset.
SKIRMISH AT THE RANCH	
LOW 9
One of the strategic advantages of the ranch is that one 
side of it is higher in elevation than the other. The road 
leading to the entrance of the ranch was dug right into 
the hill that creates that height difference, meaning 
there’s a 5-foot overhang on each side. Currently, the 
entire land is bathed in darkness save for the festival 
site, which is well lit with torches and a giant bonfire. 
Near the center of the ranch, there’s a small artificial 
pond that’s 5 feet deep.
This is a skirmish encounter that uses the rules 
starting on page 158 of Battlecry! The objective of 
the encounter is to rout the two Hellknight cavalry 
brigades. This will be easier if their commanders 
are defeated or flee. If half of the PCs are knocked 
unconscious, the Hellknights have free rein to tear 
the ranch apart.
PC Troops: Given the urgency of the situation, the 
PCs must rely on the troops readily available at the 
ranch. They have four troops—two line infantries 
(NPC Core 91) and two phalanx formations (NPC 
Core 91)—ready to fight, but the PCs don’t have time 
to form skirmish bonds with them. Since they know 
the enemies are coming in advance, the party can 
decide where they and their troops start.
Creatures: Two groups are pursuing Nolaria. One 
consists of 2 Hellknight cavalry brigades, each led 
by a Chelaxian knight. The second group is actually 
Saringallow’s own city guard led by Captain Jordis, 
who volunteered to join the search. While they put on 
a grand display of pretending to be loyal to be Cheliax, 
the captain and the guards are hoping to find Nolaria 
first so they can hide her in the barracks. The PCs 
recognize the captain and the city guards on sight.
Being more familiar with the area, Captain Jordis 
arrives at the ranch first. While Jordis never liked the 
Hellbreakers on principle, they know the rebels can 
hide Nolaria better than the city squad ever could. They 
give the PCs a chance to talk before attacking, allowing 
them to attempt two DC 25 Deception, Diplomacy, or 
Intimidation checks. If the PCs succeed at both, they 
convince Jordis to leave and act as if they didn’t find 
anyone. If any check is a critical success, Jordis tells 
the PCs that the Hellknight troops are coming. If the 
PCs don’t succeed at both checks, Jordis apologizes and 
informs the PCs that the guards have to search the area.
Fifteen minutes later, the cavalry brigades arrive and 
immediately initiate combat. If Jordis is there, their troop

The Calm Before the Storm
The adventure returns to a slight sandbox again from 
the 21st of Pharast to the 4th of Gozran. During this 
time, while the army continues to come together, the 
party can head out again and attempt to recruit any 
troops they didn’t manage to unlock in the previous 
two chapters. They can recruit up until the 31st, as 
it’s suggested the 1st to 4th of Gozran be used for the 
armies to train and strategize together.
PREPARING FOR WAR
For the next several days, the PCs should make 
preparations for the battle ahead. Saringallow isn’t 
an easy target to besiege, but that doesn’t mean it’s 
impossible. Perhaps there’s a weakness or two the PCs 
can exploit if they wish to infiltrate the city instead. 
The PCs should also take a day to form a skirmish 
bond with one of the recruited troops, preferably 
one of 8th or 9th level; they won’t always be fighting 
alongside this troop, but once the siege begins, they 
won’t have time to form this bond, so they should do 
it now. The PCs can also take the time to craft items 
and retrain, if they so desire.
Recon
Using stealth, deception, and perhaps a bit of magic, 
the PCs can investigate occupied Saringallow to 
discover any weak points in its defenses and discover 
where their comrades are being held. They might also 
receive a bit of insight on who or what they’ll likely 
face when they storm the walls.
This investigation uses the Research subsystem 
(GM Core 190). Each research check takes 8 
hours, so any PC who attempts one won’t be able 
to do downtime activities that day. The PCs can use 
the following methods to gain reconnaissance on 
Saringallow. At the GM’s discretion, the use of an 
appropriate spell (such as a scrying spell to look into 
the city from a distance) gains the PCs 1 or more 
Research Points.
Questioning the Locals: The PCs can make inquiries 
about what’s been going on behind the walls by 
speaking with the citizens who are allowed to come 
and go and those who live just outside the city; 
Maximum RP 5; Research Checks DC 24 Isger Lore or 
Society to determine which people to approach, DC 26 
Diplomacy to win the citizens over, DC 27 Intimidation 
to scare the locals into divulging information.
Spying on the City: Reconnaissance from afar is the 
best way to learn about Saringallow’s current situation 
without being spotted; Maximum RP 5; Research 
Checks DC 23 Engineering Lore or Warfare Lore to 
notice weak spots in the city’s defenses, DC 24 Stealth 
to observe unnoticed, DC 26 Perception or Society to 
follow enemy movements within the city.
Trading Secret Messages: The Hellbreakers League 
had lots of allies within Saringallow, and those 
who haven’t been captured might be able to get 
information to the PCs if contacted; Maximum RP 5; 
Research Checks DC 22 Scribing Lore to hide requests 
in the margins of normal documents, DC 24 Society 
to encode and decode messages, DC 26 Deception or 
Stealth to keep the correspondence secret.

Strategy and Logistics
By this point, the Hellbreakers have multiple armies 
under their banner. The PCs have already engaged 
in a bit of skirmish warfare, but the upcoming siege 
on Saringallow will see them fully implementing 
their troops to their full abilities against other large 
troops. How the PCs direct the troops under their 
command will affect the overall outcome of 
the battle.
As such, the PCs should choose 
four troops with which to gain 
skirmish bonds. Each PC forms 
a skirmish bond with one troop, 
and that bond will be active for 
the entirety of the siege. Should a 
PC’s troop be killed in the line 
of duty, they can command a 
new troop of the same level 
in the next skirmish encounter, 
but unless the PCs retreat from 
the city and take an entire day of 
downtime to train with their troops, 
that PC doesn’t have a skirmish bond 
with this new troop. The ramifications of 
stepping away from the battle for a day are explained 
in Liberation Points on page 158.
The PCs choose two level 8 troops and two level 
9 troops for the battles ahead. No matter who 
else they’ve recruited, the level 8 troops available 
to them include an elite bandit gang (NPC Core 
5, 22), an elite gnome cannon corps (NPC Core 5, 
Battlecry! 182), a Hellknight cavalry brigade (NPC 
Core 93), and a troop of woodland scouts (NPC 
Core 179). Similarly, the level 9 troops include a 
hobgoblin veteran regiment (Battlecry! 183), a 
mercenary band (NPC Core 84), a weak dwarf 
longshot squad (NPC Core 5, Battlecry! 179), and 
a weak watchmage squadron (NPC Core 5, 120). 
You can provide the PCs with other options at your 
discretion.
The lower-level troops the PCs have been 
recruiting will also be helpful in the war effort, as 
described in The Western Feint on page 159.
Sabotage
A city under siege is at the mercy of its current level 
of supplies and an ever-shrinking morale. While 
most of the occupiers of Saringallow are devils 
and highly disciplined Hellknights, the PCs can 
nevertheless attempt to sabotage the city’s defenses 
in preparation for their eventual attack using the 
Sabotage Saringallow downtime activity described 
below. This activity takes 8 hours (and so precludes 
any other downtime activities) and grants Liberation 
Points (which are described on page 158). The PCs 
can earn a maximum of 5 Liberation Points from 
sabotage.

SABOTAGE SARINGALLOW
DOWNTIME
Through espionage and similar underhanded tactics, you 
weaken the occupying Hellknights’ defenses and morale. 
Attempt a DC 26 Deception, Thievery, or Warfare Lore check.
Critical Success You cut off external supplies or sow chaos 
in the city from afar. You gain 1 Liberation Point and the 
next check attempted to Sabotage Saringallow gains a 
+2 circumstance bonus.
Success You manage to noticeably sabotage an aspect or 
function of the city. You gain 1 LP.
Critical Failure Your efforts backfire, causing the occupying 
forces to dig in. You lose 1 LP (minimum of 0).
COUNTERSPY	
MODERATE 9
Espionage is a common tactic in warfare, especially 
during revolutions and protracted sieges. While 
the PCs are doing their own reconnaissance, the 
Hellknight forces stationed in Saringallow are on 
the watch for them. Their interim leader Nayren 
Allurajix is expecting the Hellbreakers League to try 
to rescue their captive comrades, so the Hellknight is 
on guard for the rebels’ approach. To that end, as the 
PCs continue to amass their forces by Sarini Manor 
and perform their own spying, a group of devils is 
watching them.
When the PCs accrue 8 Research Points in the 
Saringallow Reconnaissance research challenge above, 
an allied lookout catches a glimpse of one these devils 
near the manor late one night. Alternatively, you can 
use this encounter at any time before the Hellbreakers’ 
attack on the city begins to show that their enemies 
aren’t complacently waiting around.
This encounter can take place on any map used to 
represent the lands near Sarini Manor. It’s nighttime, 
but the lookout drops their lit lantern after spotting 
the devil, providing some light to see by.
Creatures: While the lookout spotted only one devil, 
the counterespionage unit consists of four coartis, 
using their wings and their ability to teleport to remain 
out of sight until now. They descend upon the lookout, 
who cries out for help before they’re swarmed. While 
the PCs don’t have enough time to muster any of their 
allied troops, they can arrive on the scene before the 
coartis escape. The devils take this opportunity to 
engage in battle instead of fleeing, either mistakenly 
believing the PCs will be as easy to kill or recognizing 
them as important Hellbreaker leaders.
One coarti casts darkness at the beginning of 
the fight to prevent allied NPCs at the manor from 
interfering. Two of the devils stand firm against the 
PCs, using Despairing Shriek if the other coartis aren’t 
in range. The other two swoop in to strike before 
flying out of melee range each turn. The coartis fight 
until defeated.

OTHER STRATEGIES
Your PCs might have a different idea about 
infiltrating Saringallow, and that’s fine! Ethran or 
another Hellbreaker can steer them toward the 
methods presented in this chapter, but ultimately, 
the players are in charge of the liberation. Use 
the missions and Liberation Points rules provided 
to adjudicate their method, and be sure to stress 
the importance of rescuing captives and taking 
out key enemy figures like Gredress Tilnanos and 
Nayren Allurajix.

damage to off-guard creatures.
Wing Snap [one-action] Frequency once per turn; Effect The coarti 
makes two wing Strikes, then falls if they’re flying. They 
can’t Fly until the end of their turn.
For Saringallow!
On the morning of the 5th of Gozran, the temporary 
Hellbreaker leadership calls upon the PCs. Ethran 
gives each PC a standard bearing the Hellbreakers’ 
insignia, which officially puts them in charge of 
leading this battle. The PCs can easily notice that no 
other Hellbreaker, not even a Riotmonger, is holding 
a standard. The PCs have truly been given the reins 
of command for the upcoming battle to free the city. 
The Eagle Knight muses how less than a year ago, the 
PCs were but recruits running errands. They’ve since 
grown into capable leaders with more than a hundred 
under their command. It’s a heavy burden, but one 
that the PCs wear well.
Speech! Speech! The gathered army clamors for the 
PCs to say something encouraging. This monumental 
moment requires each PC to attempt a DC 26 
Diplomacy, Intimidation, or Performance check. If 
they achieve at least one success, the army erupts into 
rousing cheers. For the remainder of the chapter, each 
troop commanded by a PC can reroll a single check 
during the first skirmish encounter they are part of; 
this is a fortune effect. If the PCs achieved at least three 
successes, each troop commanded by a PC gains this 
benefit for all skirmish encounters they are part of.
LIBERATION POINTS
The success of the retaking of Saringallow is measured 
in Liberation Points. The PCs might already have 
gained a few Liberation Points from earlier actions, 
but the majority of Liberation Points will be garnered 
through their efforts on the field of battle and within 
the city walls. Keep a running tally of the total 
Liberation Points, as this will also determine how 
quickly Caeto Vulaunex learns that the Hellbreakers 
have retaken the city.
Momentum is important. Once the attacks begin, 
if the PCs retreat from the city to take a full night’s 
rest, they lose 2 Liberation Points, plus 1 additional 
Liberation Point for every day they don’t resume 
the attack, as the Hellknight forces use the respite to 
bolster their defenses.

AID LIBERATION
EXPLORATION
You briefly deviate from your planned missions to find 
a spot where your allies could use some help, either 
defeating an evenly matched force or planning a route to 
proceed through the city. This takes 10 minutes. Attempt a 
DC 28 Warfare Lore check.
Critical Success Through your words or your deeds, you 
give an allied troop much-needed tactical advice or help 
them vanquish a foe. You gain 2 Liberation Points.
Success You lend a hand to an allied troop in battle. You 
gain 1 LP.
Failure As you fight your way through the streets, you 
have an unplanned skirmish. You handily win the fight, 
but each PC loses a number of Hit Points equal to their 
level.
Critical Failure You make a tactical blunder, engaging an 
enemy you weren’t prepared for. You lose 1 LP, and each 
PC loses a number of Hit Points equal to twice their level.
Special Once a PC performs this exploration activity, no 
other PC can attempt it until the PCs have gained or lost 
Liberation Points through another means.
THE WESTERN FEINT
With advice from Ethran (and Rhokrag if he hasn’t 
been captured again), the Hellbreakers have a plan 
that will distract most of the occupying forces long 
enough for the PCs to take their own troops and 
infiltrate the city. Several of the armies the PCs have 
recruited over the past few weeks will march on 
Saringallow’s two western gates with the seeming 
intent of breaking through. This should draw enough 
Hellknights and devils to that side of the city, allowing 
the PCs to take Noble’s Folly Gate to the north. This 
won’t be simple, however, as the Hellknights have 
armies to spare!
The strength of the forces sent to this feint will 
determine its success. The players should choose six 
troops from the troops they have recruited (three for 
each gate). They shouldn’t choose any of the troops 
they’ve already formed a skirmish bond with; those 
soldiers will be accompanying the PCs as they march 
on the northern gate. Then, add up the levels of the 
three troops assigned to each gate. If the PCs assign 
an NPC commander to a group of three, add 1 to that 
total. If the total for a group is 15 or lower, the PCs earn 
1 Liberation Point. Otherwise, they earn 2 Liberation 
Points. The PCs can earn a total of 4 Liberation Points 
for this feint.
When these armies attack the western gates, the 
PCs can proceed to Noble’s Folly Gate, starting with a 
skirmish outside the walls (see below).
OUTSIDE THE WALLS	
MODERATE 9
Though most of the Hellknight troops have shifted 
their focus to the western walls, the PCs have to 
deal with one patrolling army before they can reach 
Noble’s Folly Gate. This entails taking the troops 
they’re commanding and smashing through the line to 
reach the gatehouse entrance.
This is a skirmish encounter, using the rules outlined 
starting on page 158 of Battlecry! The objective of 
the encounter is for all PCs to reach the gatehouse 
entrance (as indicated by the dotted lines on the map 
on page 158). For more than one PC to enter that 
space, the PCs will have to relinquish command of 
their troops at just the right moment, leaving them 
vulnerable to being routed. However, once all PCs are 
in the designated area, they can move on to Mission 1 
(page 160) while their troops finish the battle outside 
the gate. If the half of the PCs’ troops are routed 
before they can enter the gatehouse, the PCs will have 
to either flee and try again with different troops or 
finish the fight.
PC Troops: The PCs command the troops they 
chose to form a skirmish bond with before the siege 
begins (see Strategy and Logistics on page 156).
Creatures: The patrol consists of two Hellknight 
cavalry brigades, each led by a Hellknight field-
maralictor. They are accompanied by a legion of 
vordines commanded reluctantly by an experienced 
docent devil named Besunas. The docent devil hopes 
that the throng of vordines will protect her while she 
casts her spells, and only drives them forward into 
melee combat when left with no other choice.

MISSIONS INSIDE SARINGALLOW
Once the PCs have made it inside the Noble’s 
Folly gatehouse, their journey to liberate 
Saringallow begins in earnest. They must 
first defeat those occupying the gatehouse 
to allow their troops inside the city, but 
after that, they can complete most of the

Mission 1: Noble’s Folly Gate
Moderate 9
The feint against the western gates does draw 
most of the city’s attention there, but as the PCs 
might have learned, the Hellknight signifer Gredress 
Tilnanos isn’t easily fooled. Her paranoia pays off 
when she spots the PCs marching on Noble’s Folly 
Gate. To begin their infiltration of the city, the PCs will 
have to take the gatehouse where Gredress is holed 
up. They must do so alone, as the troops they brought 
to the city remain in the field to battle the Hellknight 
brigades. To represent the interior of the gatehouse, 
use an appropriate Flip-Mat of your choice.
Creatures: Gredress has three warmonger devils 
with her to protect the gatehouse. They protect her 
as frontline fighters while she casts spells at the PCs. 
These foes fight to the death or until unconscious, not 
realizing how powerful the PCs are.

Mission 2: Armory Sabotage
Moderate 9
Saringallow’s town hall complex is close to the center 
of the city. Most of the buildings are administrative, 
but the area also includes a small garrison and armory 
for the city’s guards. Since Saringallow’s occupation, 
this area has been overrun by Hellknights and devils as 
Caeto and Nayren work to keep their forces supplied. 
A calculated strike against the armory while most of 
the occupying forces are fighting at the western wall 
would help undermine their strength and make the 
liberation of Saringallow that much easier.
Once inside the city proper, the PCs can 
approach the town hall garrison from almost 
any direction. When they arrive, they find it nearly 
empty. The mayor and other bureaucrats are still 
within, hunkering down as the siege commences, but 
even if they spot the PCs approaching, they don’t try 
to stop them.
To sabotage or destroy the armory, the PCs can 
use any means at their disposal, whether that be with 
devastating spells, using demolition equipment, or by 
smashing and stealing everything in sight. That last 
method takes about an hour.
You can use part of Pathfinder Flip-Mat: Bigger 
Keep for this encounter.
Creatures: Before the PCs can examine the garrison 
armory, they have to deal with the few individuals 
left behind: a pair of Hellknight drill sergeants and 
a warmonger devil called to keep watch over the 
building. The devil fights until destroyed, but the drill 
sergeants flee the scene when reduced to 20 or fewer 
Hit Points.

there are five generic members of the Hellbreakers 
League imprisoned here.

Mission 4: Headquarters Rescue	
Moderate 9
After 
some 
consideration, 
Caeto 
decided 
the 
Hellbreakers’ elusive headquarters would make the 
perfect bait for capturing those who got away. He 
therefore imprisoned more important Hellbreakers 
NPCs of 3rd level, such as Gram, Rhokrag, and 
Maire, in the rooms on the second floor. If there are no 
captured NPCs that fit that description, there are three 
generic senior Hellbreakers here instead. Use the map 
on page 158 for this encounter.
Creatures: Three assassins await on the first floor,

ASSASSINS (3)
CREATURE 8
Pathfinder NPC Core 23
Initiative Perception +16
Liberation Points: Freeing the Hellbreakers here 
grants the PCs 1 Liberation Point.
Treasure: The Hellbreaker captives give the PCs a

Development: The Hellbreakers here aren’t sure

Mission 5: Temple Entrance
Moderate 9
The entrance to the city’s Temple of Erastil faces 
Saringallow’s massive graveyard. In better times, the 
building was visited by dozens of people daily, seeking 
blessings, medical attention, or emergency housing. 
Now, it serves as a makeshift prison for the former 
head priest Ildris Ruvarra. As such, it is well-guarded, 
and the PCs have to fight through the force stationed 
on the steps (at the only entrance) if they want to 
rescue those inside.
Creatures: A trio of sarglagons have been called to 
watch over the street in front of the temple. They’re 
upset about the lack of water here and would rather 
be down near the docks. Also, they’ve been forbidden 
to join the fighting at the gates to the west; the sounds 
of that close battle are driving them to distraction. 
They don’t notice the PCs approach, but fight until 
destroyed when the heroes get too close.

Mission 6: Temple Rescue	
Moderate 9
The main chamber of the temple would usually be 
filled with worshippers attending a sermon or the 
occasional devotee making a small offering to Old 
Deadeye. At the moment, most of the pews have been 
destroyed and much of the Erastil iconography has 
been defaced. Rooms past the main temple hold the 
most important prisoners of Saringallow’s occupation.
Creatures: With Caeto out of the city, Nayren 
Allurajix oversees the occupation from here. The 
recently revived and now fiendish Viro is also at the 
temple, hoping to have a final showdown with the PCs. 
While the two have not known each other for long, 
they work seamlessly, flanking to take down opponents, 
covering each other’s back. Nayren fights until they fall 
below 20 Hit Points. They know that if they’re killed, 
Caeto is going to be in danger, so they attempt to flee. 
Viro, on the other hand, fights to the death, as he just 
doesn’t know when to quit his vengeance.

Mission 7: Stop that Pigeon!	
Low 9
As the PCs rush toward Saringallow’s Sundries only 
a few blocks away from the temple, they can hear the 
continuing sounds of the battle at the western gates. 
The three-story-tall aviary attached to the building is 
easy to spot. Thirty feet in diameter, this tower has one 
continuous spiral staircase that runs along the wall 
from the ground floor to the top.
Creatures: Four vordines guard the base of the 
aviary stairs, while the message runner heads up to 
attach the note to a carrier pigeon. The length of the 
staircase to the top of the aviary is 100 feet. Catching 
a pigeon then takes an Interact action with a successful 
DC 22 Acrobatics check. Attaching the missive and 
throwing the pigeon out the window takes an Interact 
action each. The message runner does their best to 
remain on task, but engages any PCs that reach the 
same floor as them. Should the pigeon fly off, the PCs 
have until the beginning of the runner’s next turn to 
take the poor bird out; a carrier pigeon has an AC of 
15 and 7 Hit Points.

Mission 8: At a Crossroad	
Moderate 9
Within an hour of the PCs liberating the Temple of 
Erastil, the occupying forces of Saringallow grow 
desperate. Some Hellknight signifers get together to 
perform a last-ditch summoning at Crossroad Plaza in 
the center of the city. These spellcasters are consumed 
in hellfire when the ritual goes awry, creating a semi-
stable portal to Hell through which fiends begin to 
emerge. The PCs are immediately informed of the 
situation by a fellow Hellbreaker (or they might even 
witness a destructive plume of flame rise over the 
city rooftops) and must gather their troops to face 
whatever has come through.
This is a skirmish encounter, using the rules starting 
on page 158 of Battlecry! Use the map on page 162 for 
this encounter. The object of the encounter is to close 
the portal at the center of the plaza. An individual PC 
adjacent to the crater can attempt a DC 28 Arcana, 
Occultism, or Religion check as a two-action activity; a 
PC gains a +2 circumstance bonus to this check if they 
wield one of the Wonders of the Season. The PCs must 
succeed at three of these checks to fully close the portal.
PC Troops: The PCs take command of the troops 
with which they formed skirmish bonds before the 
attacks began. Though they’ve been fighting in the city 
all day, they haven’t received any additional wounds 
from their skirmish outside the city walls. However, 
if this encounter takes place on a different day than 
the skirmish outside the city walls, the troops are fully 
healed. The PCs can approach the plaza from any 
direction they wish.
Creatures: The portal has already disgorged 
dozens of hell hounds, which have formed into two 
hell hound packs. They were followed by a single 
greater hell hound and a rust devil. While ferrugons 
usually prefer corrupting mortals to fighting them, 
this one is angry that it’s been pulled through the 
portal to the mortal realm and begins smashing 
nearby structures. A few iron lampposts have been 
turned to rust when the PCs arrive. All these fiends 
fight until killed.

FIGHTING ONE-ON-ONE
At your discretion, Caeto can accept a demand 
from the PCs that they fight without involving 
any troops. The battle still takes place in Traveler’s 
Square with the allies of both sides looking on. For 
an easier bout (though still a severe encounter), 
the PCs face Caeto and the elite coarti. For a more 
challenging fight (halfway between a severe and 
an extreme encounter), the PCs face Caeto and his 
Hellknight signifer ally.

Liberation Points: If the PCs fail to close the portal

War Yet Won
Once the PCs have closed the portal at Crossroad 
Plaza, they can perform any rescue operations in the 
city they have yet to perform. Smaller battles continue 
to rage through the streets for the next couple of days, 
but the Hellbreaker army is ultimately victorious in 
freeing Saringallow.
Afterward, celebrations commence throughout the 
city. During these festivities, the PCs get word that 
Caeto Vulaunex is on his way back to Saringallow with 
a large entourage. Scouts believe he will arrive on the 
10th of Gozran, only 2 days from now. Depending on 
how efficiently the PCs liberated the city, Caeto might 
not be aware of the extent of the Hellbreakers’ success. 
In any case, the PCs have an opportunity to ambush 
Caeto, stopping him from retaking Saringallow. The 
Riotmongers suggest that luring him into the city 
before springing the trap is likely the best bet, as the 
surrounding buildings give plenty of room to hide 
Hellbreaker forces. However, the 2 days are barely 
enough time to prepare. The PCs can perform any 
downtime activities they wish while the Hellbreakers 
and allied citizens of Saringallow establish facades to 
make it appear as if the Hellknights are still in control 
of the city.
The effectiveness of this ambush depends partially on 
the number of Liberation Points the PCs accumulated.
5 or fewer LP: Caeto isn’t fooled by any deception 
and confidently walks into the trap. The DCs to 
Influence him increase by 1 and the PCs have 1 fewer 
round to attempt influence checks. In addition, he and 
all his allies gain a +2 circumstance bonus to their 
initiative in the ensuing fight.
6 to 12 LP: Caeto is wary that something isn’t right 
when his army approaches Saringallow. The PCs have 
1 fewer round to attempt influence checks against him. 
In addition, he and all his allies gain a +1 circumstance 
bonus to their initiative in the ensuing fight.
13 to 20 LP: The PCs can successfully spring the 
ambush on Caeto, but he didn’t get to his position 
in the Hellknight by being a fool. No bonuses or 
penalties apply.
20 or more LP: Caeto is taken completely by surprise. 
The PCs have 1 additional round to attempt influence 
checks against him. In addition, he and all his allies 
take a –1 circumstance penalty to their initiative in the 
ensuing fight.
Reward: If the PCs gain at least 13 Liberation Points, 
award them 10 XP. If they gain at least 20 Liberation 
Points, award them 30 XP instead.
DAWN ON THE HORIZON
The army marching with Caeto is small compared 
to the forces the PCs faced in retaking Saringallow. 
It enters the city through the northernmost gate on 
the western wall, passes the cemetery, and arrives in 
Traveler’s Square. The Hellbreaker forces emerge from 
the woods to the west and from within the city to trap 
Caeto’s army in a pincer. However, the fighting doesn’t 
commence right away.
While Caeto is seething that the PCs have defeated 
his forces and reclaimed Saringallow, it also empowers 
him in a way, as it confirms for him the amount of 
damage the Hellbreakers can do when they fully 
disregard the law. If anything, he’s more certain than 
ever that the rebels must be defeated. Caeto gives the 
PCs one last chance to defend themselves verbally. The 
PCs can flip the opportunity on Caeto to make him 
defend his own actions since they’ve met him.
This brief pause before the battle uses the influence 
subsystem (GM Core 187). The PCs have 3 rounds 
(each of which lasts about 5 minutes) to shake Caeto’s 
confidence in his convictions.

THE CLAWS OF ISGER	
SEVERE 9
After 15 minutes of tense discussion, Caeto signals for 
his troops to attack. He wants to end this revolution 
once and for all, and knows that the PCs are the face 
of it. Caeto’s forces are at the northwestern part of 
the map, while the PCs are directly opposite. As the 
PCs fight Caeto, the other Hellbreakers engage with 
the bulk of Caeto’s army just outside the square. Use 
the map on page 164 for this encounter.
This is a skirmish encounter, using the rules 
starting on page 158 of Battlecry! The objective 
of the encounter is to defeat Caeto or cause him to 
surrender; once this happens, Caeto’s forces lay down 
their arms. However, if all the PCs are reduced to 0 Hit 
Points or killed, Caeto’s forces run roughshod over the 
remainder of the Hellbreakers army.
The Gallows: Traveler’s Square features an old 
gallows as a reminder of the city’s bleak history (as 
marked on the map). It hasn’t had a noose for years, 
and the platform shakes with each step taken on it. A 
troop can’t occupy the same space as the gallows, but 
when a Large or smaller creature steps onto one of the 
two 5-foot-by-5-foot trapdoors, the entire structure 
falls apart. Each creature on the gallows falls 10 feet 
and takes 3d8 piercing damage (DC 28 basic Reflex 
save) from splintering wood. The space of the gallows 
then counts as difficult terrain.
PC Troops: The PCs command the same troops they 
led during Saringallow’s liberation. Since a few days 
have passed, these troops are fully healed.
Creatures: Caeto commands one of the Hellknight 
cavalry brigades, while the signifer who accompanies 
him commands the other. He secured an intimidating-
looking aurocan to bolster his forces, and the construct 
stomps through the PCs’ troops when possible. An 
elite coarti is also part of Caeto’s entourage; they fly 
above the combat and swoop down to strike at the 
most vulnerable.

Concluding the Adventure
Defeating 
Caeto, 
whether 
by 
knocking 
him 
unconscious, killing him, or accepting his surrender, 
results in his allies and forces surrendering immediately 
or fleeing. With the Hellknights no longer threatening 
the Hellbreakers’ existence, the rebellion can finally 
operate out in public in peace. It’s time to begin the 
long political road of fully extracting Isger from 
Cheliax’s rule and establishing its new government.
In a gesture to walk away from the past, the 
Hellbreakers implore those who would join them to 
seek them out not in Elidir, but in Saringallow. For 
now, the PCs should savor their victory as the rays of a 
spring sun shine ever hopeful down upon the highlands 
between the Aspodell and Menador Mountains.

Adventure Toolbox
The PCs should be level 10 at the end of the 
Hellbreakers Adventure Path, having faced the many 
political and supernatural crises of Isger. The players 
are primed to continue their PCs’ adventures in the 
next Adventure Path, Hell’s Destiny, but there’s plenty 
to be done if the players wish to continue in Isger.
Campaign Consequences
The following scenarios happen if the PCs fail to 
defeat certain enemies or achieve their objectives.
REIGN OF THE WIGHT MOTHER
Should Illcayna succeed in her ritual, she becomes the 
mortal herald of Urgathoa and restores the might of 
the warshard embedded in her chest. This turns her 
into a powerful mythic being who quickly takes over 
Isger as she weaves a curse of undeath into the very 
bones of the nation, transforming it into a tribute state 
for Urgathoa. The goblins of the Chitterwood burrow 
deep underground, while those above ground are 
forced to flee or perish as fodder for Illcayna’s endless 
army of wights. Isger is at last free from Cheliax’s 
devilish grasp only to find itself bound by a different 
type of tyrant.
Ironically, Illcayna’s greatest enemy might be 
another terrible force of undeath: the Whispering 
Tyrant, Tar‑Baphon. Tar-Baphon is displeased to find 
a rival for world domination, especially since they use 
similar methods of manipulating undeath, and plots to 
raise Whispering Way supporters against Illcayna. He 
also sends spies and infiltrators into the camps of his 
own enemies to manipulate them into taking down the 
Wight Mother for him, hoping his foes will weaken 
each other enough to allow him to destroy them all in 
one fell swoop.
Kinza (passionate female human cleric 6), a 
descendant of the original Isgeri tribes, suggests 
seeking warshards to aid in striking down Illcayna. 
The Hellbreakers League knows the approximate 
location of one: the very warshard they gave the Eagle 
Knights in exchange for their alliance, which went 
missing along with its carriers in the town of Falcon’s 
Hollow in Darkmoon Vale.
An unexpected ally is Caeto Vulaunex himself. 
Horrified and chastened by the chaos unleashed by 
his refusal to prioritize the people over his ambitions, 
he dedicates himself to Illcayna’s defeat in repentance. 
The Hellknight has little support from Cheliax, which 
is cutting its losses to focus on other parts of the 
growing war, but he’s stalwart in his devotion to seeing 
Illcayna’s downfall and more open to compromise 
than previously. Caeto is able to utilize his Chelaxian 
connections to learn of other warshards rumored to 
lie in the Iron Rose palace in the Menador Mountains 
and one embedded in a mysterious aquatic creature in 
the Conerica River.
THE KNIGHT STEWARD
In the event that the PCs fail to defeat Caeto in 
Saringallow, he quickly amasses the forces and 
authority to crush the Hellbreakers League leadership 
in one swift blow. Saringallow is swept up in a wave of 
brutal interrogations, weeding out anyone with even 
the slightest sympathy for rebels. The most prominent 
leaders are transported back to Elidir, where a public 
execution is held for each individual rebel leader every 
week so as to draw out anyone foolish and loyal 
enough to attempt a rescue. The Riotmongers are 
saved for last and executed together in a small show 
of kindness from Caeto.
Ardano Grizzi III (exacting male human governor 
12) is chosen as the new steward of Isger. Unlike 
Hedvend, Ardano is ruthlessly efficient and has little 
love for finery or the spoiled elites. He quickly purges 
the government of anyone he deems too soft and 
promotes officials of his own choice such as Reverine 
Hallowell (cunning female human politician 9) and 
Justiro Adama (precise male gnome machinist 10). 
His rule is severe to make up for the recent chaos and 
even the elites of Elidir find themselves stifled under 
his iron hand.
The Hellbreakers are broken, but their story doesn’t 
end. The numerous allies they made and the people 
they helped remember who it was that truly cared 
for and defended Isger in its time of need. The image 
of a rose growing through Abrogail Thrune’s broken 
crown becomes a widespread symbol of resistance, 
along with an anti-Caeto version popular in the 
countryside that depicts his cracked face with thorny 
roses bursting through it. In this bleak present, hope is 
still alive, as are the PCs, and it will persevere as they 
continue to fight oppression.

Campaign

Further Adventures
The following scenarios are potential storylines 
contingent upon the PCs successfully completing the 
objectives of the adventure.
HELL’S DESTINY
While Isger still has plenty of adventure left, PCs 
who wish to continue the fight against Cheliax can 
transition into the next Adventure Path, Hell’s Destiny. 
In this campaign, the PCs join various factions such as 
Andoran and Ravounel to directly confront Cheliax 
and mount an attack against its hellish forces as their 
enemy prepares their most diabolical plan yet.
REPAIRING THE CAPITAL
Elidir suffered great damage from the PCs’ escape and 
is still in the hands of Hellknights. The Hellbreakers 
League must negotiate a surrender from maralictor 
Lucia Devona (serious female human Hellknight 
10), whom Caeto left in charge in his absence. Even 
if Caeto survived and surrendered, Lucia refuses to 
give in and must be persuaded via a thorough legal 
battle or trial by combat. Killing Lucia is an option, 
but this foments deep fear and resentment among the 
pro-Cheliax elites and makes them more likely to stage 
their own eventual rebellion.
Even without Cheliax’s direct intervention, there are 
plenty of loyal Chelaxians determined to bring down 
the Hellbreakers League and restore fiendish order 
so they can continue to benefit off a government that 
cares more about appeasing its patrons than helping 
its people. Cygnetus Frawn (flamboyant nonbinary 
human dandy 9) prances about the city bemoaning its 
fall from glory, lamenting the lack of riches Elidir once 
had and besmirching the name of the Hellbreakers as 
much as they can. Nerina Halfsong (spoiled female 
dromaar socialite 10) demands reparations for all 
the destruction the Hellbreakers wrought on the city, 
starting with throwing her a birthday ball since hers 
was canceled thanks to Hellbreaker-inspired riots. 
Priest Vindictus Ricci (fanatical male human priest 
8) protests daily outside the cathedral of Asmodeus, 
crying out that the Hellbreakers have sinned against 
their patron deity and will bring destruction to Isger. 
These elites, while petty and frivolous, hold most of 
Elidir’s (and therefore the nation’s) wealth and have 
substantial influence over the direction of the city.
SEEKING WOE
When Illcayna is defeated, the PCs find a potion of 
shared memories in her possession. Drinking the 
potion reveals a memory of Illcayna finding a magically 
hidden message in the mural of winter in the Grotto of 
the Sacrificed, leading to a vision of the fourth Wonder 
of the Seasons, Woe.
The vision details an icy figure in the mountains 
wearing a mantle of snowflakes. The PCs can seek 
Woe in the Menador Mountains, where it’s currently 
in the possession of a powerful winter hag named 
Zamoranna (artistic female hag 10). Zamoranna 
desires to preserve the beauty of the world and ignore 
the ugliness of humanoid societies. Believing people are 
most beautiful when they’re happy, she visits villages 
and takes in travelers, lavishing them with gifts and 
working to help people gain their heart’s desires only 
to freeze them into solid ice sculptures at the height 
of their happiness. Her icy mountain lair is filled with 
dozens of such frozen art pieces.

THE IRON QUEEN
Lady Kaltessa Iyis has made Isger her domain for 
centuries, biding her time to perfect her plans. She 
isn’t pleased to learn the nation has been taken by a 
group of rebellious upstarts. While she doesn’t directly 
intervene, she sets her agents to work on unraveling 
the authority of the Hellbreakers League, forcing them 
into a position that better serves Mammon’s desires.
The first of these agents is Niceforo Zikka (stern 
male human champion of Mammon 12), a financier 
who petitions for a seat in government as the treasurer. 
Niceforo is upfront about his intentions to see Isger 
profit off its new independence and won’t take no 
for an answer, swaying citizens to support him lest 
Isger fall into financial disaster after detaching from 
Cheliax. His true motive is to disseminate coins 
from Erebus throughout Isger’s population via the 
bank, organically spreading his master’s influence 
throughout the region through trade and market.
Petricca Segracci (ostentatious female nephilim crime 
boss 10) is another lackey of Kaltessa’s, paid to attack 
shipments and starve the nation of incoming resources 
to keep the Hellbreakers busy while the priestess sets 
up her plans. Kaltessa also has connections to the 
Druman merchant Silgrey Dawnsleeve (ambitious 
female dwarf capitalist 9), who owns swaths of Isgeri

FRACTURED ARMY
Not all are eager to accept 
Isger’s new direction. Its 
official military splinters 
into several factions, with 
only one electing to accept 
Isger’s 
new 
leadership. 
Commander Nil Harovin 
(militaristic male human 
soldier 12) leads one such 
faction, the Blazing Sword, striking 
at Elidir before the Hellbreakers can cement their 
position there. Nil believes that the Hellbreakers are 
too soft to properly lead the country and determines 
that military governance is the only appropriate 
answer. He is backed by the noble Vittoria Legoto 
(churlish female human aristocrat 10), who hopes to 
become Isger’s new governor. Vittoria’s funding and 
social status keeps Elidiran socialites in check as the 
Blazing Sword attempts to take hold of the capital and 
declare itself the new leaders of Isger.
Other factions become bands of roving bandits, 
preying on the chaos of change, while others yet turn 
to vigilantism, untrusting of the new order. Captain 
Carista Frey (charismatic female human soldier 9) 
leads the largest vigilante group, the True Army, and 
refuses to join any forces led by revolutionaries.
HELLISH REMNANTS
Though Cheliax is formally detached from Isger, its 
hellish claws dug deep into the very bones of the nation’s 
structure and society, and its influence remains strong. 
Most notably, the Sisterhood of the Golden Erinys has 
an impeccable reputation and holds substantial social 
power. Even if Isger is free, these nuns have a mission: 
to spread the faith of Asmodeus and care for orphans 
in need of their deity’s strict and vengeful guidance. In 
fact, there are plenty of new orphans for them to care 
for in the aftermath of the undead uprising that Caeto 
neglected to address.
PCs may wish to oust the Sisterhood from Isger, 
along with all traces of Asmodeus, or they might 
partner with them. Sister Marcella (pious human monk 
6) comes forward as the Sisterhood’s representative 
and beseeches the PCs to allow the Sisterhood to 
continue their charitable work, swearing the Sisters’ 
allegiance is to Asmodeus and not to Cheliax. She is 
willing to sign a (non-magical) contract to formalize 
the agreement and concedes to most stipulations 
unless they directly interfere with her faith’s 
practices. In return for the 
Sisterhood’s 
continued 
existence, she offers a prize: 
the location of a small 
warshard at a nunnery in 
the Aspodell Mountains, 
where the stone’s presence 
has mutated a herd of stony 
goats in the Sisters’ care 
into living dawnsilver.
Should the PCs prefer to 
oust the Sisters, most go 
without protest except for 
Sister Kavinna (fanatical female human 
nun 10), who rallies pious Asmodeans against the 
new governors of Isger and demands that Asmodeus 
be formally named the patron deity of Isger. If her 
demands aren’t met, she begins kidnapping children 
to indoctrinate them to the ways of Asmodeus, 
determined to fulfill her duties to her deity no matter 
the cost.
SCORCHHOME RELATIONS
As the dust settles, the goblins of the Chitterwood 
formally 
name 
their 
region 
Scorchhome 
and 
declare it a free and independent nation. There are 
tensions amongst the goblinoids on whether to trust 
humanoids and establish a formal alliance or keep to 
themselves. Brakknap prefers to see all ancestries unite 
and suggests the PCs destroy the bigoted and violent 
organization of the Isgeri Slayers as a show of good 
faith. The PCs can easily track down disparate groups 
of Isgeri Slayers to stamp out the organization, but the 
real issue lies in resolving the wounds of the past that 
have manifested into such a hateful response.
Some goblins request that the PCs establish a 
formal holiday to celebrate the alliance of goblinoids 
and humanoids in Isger, as goblins did much to fight 
against both Cheliax’s forces and the undead invasion. 
The passing of Bounty’s Light between the two groups 
could be reestablished as a tradition, or a new way to 
highlight peace might be implemented. Here are some 
suggestions.
•	 A festival (the goblins suggest a pickle festival)
•	 Replanting trees in the Chitterwood
•	 A day of reconciliation
•	 Educational reforms
All in all, peace is still a work in progress for 
Isger as it recovers from the undead scourge and the 
aftereffects of Cheliax’s neglectful rule.

Known throughout the Inner Sea Region as a vassal 
state under the thumb of Cheliax, Isger is poised on 
the brink of a major milestone. With recent events, 
the nation could either gain its full independence or 
have its spirit thoroughly crushed by those who claim 
to be its betters. After centuries of being controlled 
by one nation or another, many of the Isgeri people 
are just one small push away from rising up en masse 
against House Thrune. But such an event wouldn’t be 
without bloodshed, and Isger is still healing from its 
recent internal conflict with the goblinoid residents 
of the Chitterwood. Another war could leave Isger a 
broken husk, ripe pickings for yet another nation to 
consume.
History
Like many areas of Avistan, the land that would 
become Isger was occupied by Kellid tribes for 
thousands of years. These hardy people roamed the 
plains, hunted in the hills, and fished in the rivers as 
a way of life. There were 11 tribes in all, collectively 
known as the Isgeri, who lived off the land between the 
Menador Mountains and the Five Kings Mountains. 
When these tribes met regularly with one another to 
trade and intermingle, they did so at the confluence of 
rivers close to where the city of Elidir would be built. 
When conflicts between the tribes couldn’t be settled 
at this moot, they would occasionally result in battles, 
though one tribe never fully conquered another.
This all ended in 2133 ar when Taldor’s Seventh 
Army of Exploration marched into the region and 
claimed it as their own. The Isgeri fought back, but 
their tenacity was no match for the sheer size of 
Taldor’s army. The land was conquered and its people 
subjugated, though the newfound country was named 
Isger in their honor—no consolation to the Kellids 
killed in battle. Taldor ruled over Isger for almost 
2,000 years until Cheliax won its own independence 
in the Even-Tongued Conquest of 4081. Shortly after, 
Cheliax acquired Isger by force as the first vassal state 
of a burgeoning empire.
Isger experienced relative peace for the next few 
centuries, but the Chelaxians eventually got greedy 
and encroached upon the Chitterwood in an attempt 
to take it for themselves. What initially began as 
self‑defense soon grew into all-out war as bloodthirsty 
hobgoblin warlords, who only needed an excuse for 
conflict, used the goblin tribes of the Chitterwood to 
form a massive army. Fed up with their mistreatment 
at the hands of humans, many of these goblinoids 
were happy to enlist, but an equal number were 
conscripted by force.
The Goblinblood Wars began in 4697 and lasted 
for four years. The deaths of thousands of Isgeri 
citizens were accompanied by untold property 
damage as the goblin hordes moved north across the 
Conerica River and toward the foothills of the Five 
Kings Mountains. Only an unlikely alliance between 
Cheliax’s Hellknights, Druma’s Mercenary League, 
and Andoran’s Eagle Knights halted the offensive. 
These groups set the edges of the Chitterwood aflame, 
and though the forest wasn’t completely burned down, 
its size was greatly reduced. Since that time, many 
goblins have reemerged from the caves they hid within 
to reclaim their forest.
In the aftermath of the war, the Church of Asmodeus, 
with the support of House Thrune—the current rulers 
of Cheliax—enacted programs to help those affected 
by the fighting. These acts weren’t of pure charity; 
the wounded were cared for by Asmodean priests in 
exchange for future favors. Orphaned children were 
placed in newly built orphanages run by a group called 
the Sisterhood of the Golden Erinys that has spent the 
last two decades indoctrinating those children into 
their faith. Many Isgeri citizens felt grateful for this 
support and became more loyal to Cheliax while their 
prejudice against goblinoids waned and waxed.
The Godsrain ignited a spark of revolution in the 
hearts of some of Isger’s citizenry. They saw how even 
the mightiest of gods could be laid low and began to

wonder if it was possible to throw off Cheliax’s yoke. 
A group called the Hellbreakers League became the 
forefront of this dissidence, having 
discovered a warshard—a piece of 
the dead god Gorum—and used it as 
a rallying symbol. This displeased 
Her Infernal Majestrix Abrogail 
Thrune II of Cheliax, who’s been

It eventually led to a massive clash in the fields near 
Citadel Altaerein that has come to be known as the 
Battle of Hellknight Hell. Some say it’s the first salvo 
of an all-out war between Cheliax and Andoran.
At a Glance
Isger is a temperate country bounded by the River 
Keld and the Aspodell Mountains to the south, the 
Menador Mountains to the north, and the Five Kings 
Mountains to the east. It shares borders with Cheliax, 
Andoran, Druma, and Molthune, though the most 
direct routes to Molthune must pass through the 
northern mountains. Its geography is mostly plains 
and hills, with the Chitterwood being the nation’s 
largest forest. The Conerica River, a major corridor 
of trade, runs through the center of Isger and forms 
a major part of its western border. The Conerica is 
fed by the North Conerica River, which joins with the 
Summerun River at the capital of Elidir.
Isger is a vassal state of Cheliax and must abide 
by its laws and decrees. Hedvend VI (sniveling male 
human aristocrat 9) is the latest in a long line of 
stewards appointed by the Chelaxian government to 
oversee Isger. The nation is required by Cheliax to 
maintain a standing army to protect the important 
routes but receives little money, material support, 
or training from Cheliax to do so. The Isgeri army 
consists of volunteer recruits and watches over travel 
on the Conerica River as well as the borders of Druma 
and Andoran. Since the Battle of Hellknight Hill, most 
soldiers have been pulled back to protect Elidir.
Most of the people of Isger are human, the majority 
being either of Taldan or Kellid descent. The next 
biggest bloc of population are goblins, with most of 
them residing in the Chitterwood. Surprisingly, gnomes 
are plentiful in Isger, thanks in part to the gnome 
settlement of Umok. Other ancestries and ethnicities 
are present throughout the nation, concentrated 
mostly in the riverside cities.
Government
Isger is ruled by a steward appointed by Cheliax 
who oversees the nation and its trade. However, 
the elites of Isger are often preoccupied 
with the trade along the Conerica 
River and neglect any settlements 
outside the capital. Therefore, 
most 
towns 
and 
villages 
are self-governed with little 
interference from the wider 
government. Sheriffs, mayors, 
and guards take up civic duties for 
those forgotten by their own rulers.
Religion
As a vassal of Cheliax, Isger’s patron deity is 
Asmodeus, but other deities are quietly worshipped as 
well. Abadar has the second greatest following, and 
Milani has grown popular with rebels and freedom 
fighters who chafe against Cheliax’s boot. Urgathoa 
has a small but strong presence thanks to her servant 
Illcayna Alonnor (malevolent female daughter of 
Urgathoa 9) making a stronghold for undead forces in 
the countryside. Her servants work in the shadows of 
the nation to bring about her nefarious plans.
Asmodeus is popularly worshipped by those loyal 
to Cheliax, but otherwise, Erastil is popular among 
the Isgeri countryside. His edicts of taking care of 
community resonate with those who lost so much and 
wish to rebuild. Many towns have shrines to Erastil, 
though they always have a larger one for Asmodeus just 
in case the authorities ever come around.
In the capital, an old temple of Nocticula has become 
a focal point in the great clash between Nocticula’s old 
followers from her incarnation as a demon and her 
newer converts who revere her current incarnation as 
the Redeemer Queen.
Culture and Society
Isger is a land full of contradictions. The ultrarich 
dwell in the capital city, where they live lavishly at the 
height of excess. More about Elidiran culture can be 
found on page 192. Most of those who dwell outside 
the capital are humble, rustic people still struggling to 
recover from the Goblinblood Wars and deal with the 
consequences of that terrible conflict.
