Adventure Toolbox
O. Moil: The former slave market attached to the 
Gyve was shut down following the Emancipation 
Edict, only to reopen a short time later as a labor 
camp. Those who can’t pay their debts or who commit 
other minor crimes work here in difficult conditions, 
creating munitions for use by the army or goods sold 
to benefit their creditors.
P. Myrogy’s Menagerie: This showcase of exotic 
animals and bizarre creatures was once a star 
attraction of the city but has fallen into disrepair. 
While ordinary citizens still enjoy the occasional tour, 
the wealthy elites have grown bored of the mainstay 
animals and demand variety if the menagerie wants 
their patronage. Bulric Soddentough (frazzled male 
human zookeeper 3) has turned to paying adventurers 
to bring him new creatures, no matter how dangerous. 
He hopes to keep the menagerie fresh and interesting 
to attract the high-end clientele.
Q. New Dream Designs: This tattoo shop is the secret 
meeting place of Nocticula’s remaining followers who 
survived the violent schism among the city’s faithful 
after the goddess turned her back on her demonic past. 
Sevizoy, who leads the shrine’s small congregation, 
is developing magical tattoos to sell so he can hire 
mercenaries to help in a bloody struggle against his 
former companions.
R. Night Market: This street market spills out of the 
Druma Road Gate, offering produce, goods, and crafts 
by day or night to city residents and passing caravans. 
After the sun sets, the merchandise inevitably includes 
items lifted by workers and thieves from cargo on 
its way through the city that were never intended to 
remain in Elidir.
S. Rampways: The network of roads that runs 
around Elidir allows traders to bypass the city and the 
army to easily navigate the Conerica Straits. Because 
the Rampways are more difficult to protect than the 
river itself, the bulk of bandit activity in the region 
occurs on them, with raiders striking and quickly 
retreating back into the hills.
T. Spellbinder’s Stage: This small theater has 
become celebrated by the city’s elite for its minimalist 
performances, often little more than spoken pieces 
or stage readings. Completely oblivious to the truth 
that the theater lacks the resources to put on grander 
shows, its patrons praise it as avant-garde—a uniquely 
Isgeri take on drama. The theater’s owner, Theletch 
(subversive male kayal playwright 4), has taken to 
presenting ever more searing shows, convinced that 
his audience will continue to overlook what’s right 
in their face. It’s rumored that the theater plans to 
perform the infamous play Abrogail I when the 
timing is right.
U. The Succubus’s Sash: Ignoring the fact that 
succubi aren’t devils, this high-end boutique specializes 
in devil-themed fashion and the “latest” (really 
months behind) Egorian fashion trends. Owner Felice 
Gregoria (savvy genderfluid halfling tailor 6) isn’t 
actually a Chelaxian loyalist but knows catering to 
those who are will bring the most gold to their hands. 
The boutique also provides special enchantments for 
their most expensive items, such as illusory scents or 
glimmering images of dancing nobles. Those who pay 
extra can gain access to the store’s rarest merchandise, 
magically battle-ready clothing designed for both 
aesthetic and practicality.
V. Sweet Embrace: This unassuming wooden tower 
for years held a low-end brothel and, secretly, the 
city’s temple of Nocticula, home to an assassin’s guild 
operating in her name. Following the former demon 
lord’s ascension as the Redeemer Queen, Mistress 
Erity (charming female human assassin 9) won control 
of Sweet Embrace and continues both of its trades 
while battling to eliminate the remnant of the cult 
that accepted Nocticula’s changes. She and her fellow 
assassins have found a new divine patron to answer 
their prayers, but it isn’t clear if even they know who 
grants them power.
W. Trade House: The city’s tax and customs 
office, which oversees Conerica Landing, the city’s 
caravanserai, and all other trade matters, fills a 
sprawling labyrinth of buildings near the docks. 
Its wide purview leaves it rife with opportunities 
for corruption, which generally gets ignored until it 
becomes too egregious. Even so, punishment is often 
light, leading to a certain fearlessness among those 
who fill their coffers with the city’s gold.
X. White Stag Inn: This large, bustling inn a short 
walk away from the docks serves all those who make 
their living from the river, from the richest merchants 
to the meanest stevedore. It’s a common place to find 
work or workers, depending on which side of the 
divide a person falls on.
Y. Xerlidia Park: Named for Elidir’s founder, this 
park has survived through the centuries thanks to an 
ironclad pact she made with the early Isgeri tribes. 
It’s tended by a handful of animists who channel the 
spirits of the ancient Kellid Speakers of the Pale faith; 
these animists also welcome visitors to walk its paths, 
interact with nature, and commune with the dead at 
the city’s Memorial to Lost Soldiers, a gleaming steel 
sculpture made from broken swords and armor. This 
site is one of the few spiritual places in Isger that 
remains untouched by Cheliax, and many flock to it 
not out of faith but out of hope, seeing something that 
isn’t tainted by Hell’s fiendish presence.

Adventure Toolbox
Urgathoa was a mortal woman who so loved indulging 
in the pleasures of the body and mind that she tore 
herself from the Boneyard and ascended to godhood. 
As the goddess of disease, gluttony, and undeath, 
Urgathoa invites her followers to endlessly feast on all 
the sensations and experiences Golarion has to offer 
with little regard to morality or mortality. Hedonists, 
gluttons, necromancers, and undead all follow in 
her bloody footsteps, chasing after a life where their 
desires never go unfulfilled.
Prominent Figures
Urgathoa’s most influential worshippers are revered 
by some, reviled by many, and feared by all. Driven 
by hunger and delighting in the freedom of undeath, 
they’re handful of the most gruesome, grotesque, 
and glorious paragons who faithfully serve the Pallid 
Princess.
BARASTHANGAS
Barasthangas (studious female fleshwarp mage 11) 
was obsessed with the machinations of destruction 
and anti-life, and so she traveled to the Void and was 
transformed from an elven mage into an undead one. 
Her powers are now entwined with the Void, and her 
flesh is stretched so tautly that bones and tissue are 
visible through her translucent skin. Now back in the 
Universe, Barasthangas experiments with the creation 
of new forms of undead infused with entropic energy, 
viewing Urgathoa as both patron and co-parent to her 
profane children. She regularly fuels her magic with 
the life force of foes, allowing her to stupefy them and 
turn them into new test subjects.
FJARN
Fjarn (veteran male ghoul commander 12) has a 
hulking form, corpse-gray skin, and an unnerving 
rictus smile that strike fear in the hearts of anyone 
unlucky enough to cross his path in battle. Once an 
Ulfen Linnorm King who died by suicide after he was 
forced to murder and eat his own honor guard, Fjarn 
rose from the grave with the taste of forbidden flesh 
on his tongue. He now wages endless war against 
Urgathoa’s enemies, devouring the corpses of his 
fallen foes to grow his power. Paladins and warriors 
devoted to other gods whisper about the horrifying 
sight of a once regal figure stooping low to gnaw on 
carrion like a common beast.
MOTHER’S MAW
As the divine representative of Urgathoa, Mother’s 
Maw (enigmatic agender herald 15) soars through the 
air on leathery bat wings to enact its goddess’s will. 
Surrounded by swarms of buzzing flies and adoring 
undead thralls, the giant winged skull ferries allies into 
battle, creates new undead, and shoves enemies into 
its endless gullet. It does everything and anything that 
the goddess commands, no matter how destructive 
or bizarre the task is. When it isn’t busy fulfilling 
Urgathoa’s wishes, Mother’s Maw searches for 
novel sensual experiences and partakes in passionate 
conversation about food, wine, perfume, and the other 
pleasures of life.
MANY-LIMBS KIMMATO
Formerly a physician devoted to Sarenrae, Kimmato 
(sorrowful nonbinary halfling herexen 5) had their 
faith shattered when their spouse died in childbirth. 
Desperate to be united with their spouse, Kimmato 
spat in the face of everything they once believed and 
grafted the still-warm remains of their loved one onto 
their own body with gruesome surgical precision. This 
act of blasphemous defiance delighted Urgathoa, who 
blessed them with undeath and a new title. Many-
Limbs Kimmato now vengefully carves a bloody path 
through Sarenrae’s temples and worshippers in the 
name of Urgathoa, their profanely amalgamated body 
growing with each new victim, hundreds of arms and 
legs moving in uncanny unison.
Plots of the 
Pallid Princess
CONTENT WARNING
This article explores the many manifestations of 
Urgathoan worship. It includes themes of body 
horror, cannibalism, disordered eating, vomiting, 
alcohol, eugenics, disease, intentional transmission 
of disease, medical negligence, death in childbirth, 
mass murder, suicide, human experimentation, 
desecration of the dead, undead, and involuntary 
reanimation.

===== Page 199 =====
198
URRA LYNEDON
Urgathoa gave Urra Lynedon (experimental female 
vampire count 9) a new purpose in an otherwise boring 
immortal life: cultivating diseases like one would rare, 
exotic flowers. Using the bodies of her devoted mortal 
consorts, Urra nurtures and breeds strains of bacteria, 
fungi, and viruses from all across Golarion. She offers 
the results of her experiments to fellow Urgathoan 
faithful who seek new sensations or the fever-driven 
visions from their goddess.
Practices
Urgathoa demands that her worshippers put personal 
gratification before all else and cast off the constraints 
imposed by morality, society, and the mortal body. 
Many of her followers indulge in extreme hedonism, 
defying taboo to satiate their appetites of the body 
and the mind. Casting away self-restraint, worshippers 
feast upon everything Golarion has to offer, whether 
that’s rare delicacies, poisonous rot, or the flesh and 
lifeblood of sapient creatures. They experiment with 
the sensual limitations of their bodies, mixing pleasure 
and pain as they chase increasingly bizarre and 
grotesque hungers.
Other followers willingly contract and endure 
illnesses. By allowing disease and infection to ravage 
their bodies, Urgathoa’s faithful can prove their 
dedication to a life of limitless indulgence while 
experiencing novel sensations. Urgathoa often gives 
visions and divine insights to her followers during 
the fevered dreams of affliction, and her favored 
messengers exist in a perpetual sickly state. 
Urgathoa’s worshippers view undeath as the 
ultimate transcendence of the mortal body’s limitation. 
Many dream of becoming undead, when they can 
forever fulfill their desires without the pesky limit of 
mortality. The more magically gifted practice the art 
of necromancy, learning how to raise the dead and 
spit in the eye of the natural order to fulfill their own 
ambitions. Those unable to realize their post-death 
fantasies venerate the undead, sometimes to the extent 
of willingly feeding themselves to their more ravenous 
peers if only to experience the rapture of death in 
service to Urgathoa.
The more bloodthirsty of Urgathoa’s followers 
satisfy their cravings for violence by torturing and 
killing in her name. They seek out congregations 
who worship Urgathoa’s enemies and take delight in 
massacring them, savoring the symphony of screams 
and the splatter of warm blood upon skin. The victims 
who were most adamantly against undeath are then 
reanimated and sent after their surviving loved ones in 
a final act of perverse and ironic pleasure.
Cults
Festering in the darkness of Golarion like a hungry rot, 
Urgathoan cults gather in secrecy to worship the Pallid 
Princess. Whether they act in their own self-interest or 
in misguided selflessness, no matter if they follow her 
divine aspect of disease, gluttony, or death, all these 
cults seek to serve Urgathoa’s insatiable will.
THE SAVORING SOCIETY
On the surface, the Savoring Society is an eccentric and 
exclusive club made up of the wealthiest politicians, 
merchants, and nobility of Absalom. However, behind 
gilded doors is a cult that allows the upper class to 
freely indulge in the pleasures that privilege provides. 
For these hedonistic aristocrats, gluttony and luxury 
are their given due, and Urgathoa is their patron who 
ensures the party never stops.
Members boast of tasting every living thing that 
has existed across Golarion while sipping wine aged 
for a thousand years. Opulent gatherings can last 
for weeks, as the cult’s rules proclaim that members 
must not only indulge in material joy but also savor 
it, taking all the time one could ever need and more 
to enjoy such extravagance. The Savoring Society 
lures in new members from the rich and powerful 
elite, plying them with their vices and convincing 
them that Urgathoa is the only goddess they should 
revere—for who else understands that to enjoy the 
benefits of impossible wealth, one must consume the 
poor?
THE ASHEN CHURCH
Cults dedicated to proliferating and venerating the 
undead are plentiful among Urgathoa’s worshippers, 
but none are as successful as the Ashen Church. 
Appearing across Golarion where war, natural 
disaster, or extreme poverty have struck, the Ashen 
Church bears witness to the ways people become 
fearful, cruel, and desperate when faced with their 
own mortality. Members seek to alleviate this cycle of 
suffering by sharing the comfort their goddess offers: 
that one doesn’t have to fear death, as Urgathoa 
ensures that death isn’t the end. Through gentle acts of 
kindness and empathy, they teach people that undeath 
is Urgathoa’s mercy to all mortal kind, a way to save 
them from their mortal dread with the promise that 
immortality awaits all who accept it.
The Ashen Church’s compassion isn’t limited to the 
living. While most people look upon an undead creature 
with revulsion or terror, the Ashen Church sees a being 
that deserves respect and affection. Their very presence 
can quell the aggression of otherwise malevolently 
ravenous undead. It’s through this peaceful conduct

THE SHEPHERDS OF AFFLICTION
The Eye of Dread’s residents have 
experienced firsthand how powerless 
mere mortals are in the face of 
godlike threats. While some people 
cower behind the shields of 
heroes or sequester themselves 
away in ruins, the Shepherds 
of Affliction believe that the 
path to civilization’s survival 
is to nurture the strong and weed 
out the weak. They worship Urgathoa 
as the pinnacle of survival and utilize 
disease as the ultimate test to see who’s worthy to 
inherit the world in her name.
Going from town to town, the Shepherds of 
Affliction infect entire villages with devastating 
illnesses and deprive them of medicine. Those who 
survive are brought into the fold, given plenty of 
food, military training, and necromantic secrets to use 
against anything that threatens them. Those unworthy 
enough to die are reanimated as undead servants, used 
as tools rather than given the dignity of peaceful rest. 
The rare few who are gifted with visions of Urgathoa 
are revered as prophets, granted great privilege though 
forced to stay in a perpetual fever state. Each day, the 
Shepherds of Affliction grow in number and strength, 
marching forward with the unshakable belief that the 
disease-ravaged world they seek to build will be worth 
the sacrifice.
THE ETERNAL EATERS
Some say you are what you eat, and the Eternal Eaters 
take that saying to its most literal extreme. Members 
come from all across the Golden Road, united in 
the belief that everything they consume becomes an 
inextricable part of their soul and will be brought with 
them to their final destination in the afterlife. Food 
is eaten not just to sustain mortal bodies but also to 
fill otherworldly feast tables. Teeth crunch against 
coveted heirlooms and precious gems to fill coffers, 
and throats raggedly swallow down stone and metals 
to build personal palaces. In the most extreme cases, 
members will even consume beloved pets and family 
members to guarantee they’ll be united in eternity. 
Every bite is dedicated to Urgathoa in the hopes that 
she’ll accept their piety and provide them a home 
within her domain.
The Eternal Eaters suffer greatly as their bodies 
struggle to digest this unusual diet. However, they 
accept the pain as a minor price to pay for everlasting 
happiness after death and refuse any medical treatment 
to alleviate their symptoms. After an Eternal Eater 
dies, their last act of devotion is to give their body 
to Urgathoa so that it can continue to serve 
her on the mortal plane while their soul 
moves on to their carefully crafted 
afterlife.

PALLID CRYSTAL	
ITEM 7
UNCOMMON
DIVINE
INVESTED
Price 360 gp
Usage worn; Bulk —
Requirements You’re a follower of Urgathoa.
This finger-shaped crystal on a thin strip of leather bridges 
the worlds of life and undeath, shifting from a pale opaque 
pink when worn by a living creature to a deep translucent 
purple when worn by an undead creature. While wearing 
the necklace, rotten food and drink taste as if they were 
fresh and can be eaten with no ill effects. If you’re healed 
by healing vitality effects, you gain void resistance 5, but

Adventure Toolbox
Isger’s status as a mistreated vassal state of Cheliax 
overshadows much of the nation’s past. For seven 
centuries, Chelaxian and Isgeri noble houses plundered 
what resources the land had to offer. What wealth 
was gained from the lumber, minerals, and gems 
harvested, generations of ruling stewards squandered. 
Though threats rose and dangers imperiled, the rich 
and powerful cared only for the flow of coin on the 
waters of the Conerica River. And so, whenever the 
common folk of Isger suffered strife—be it famine, 
disease, or war—they often faced it alone.
The Goblinblood Wars from nearly three decades 
ago exemplified this neglect. The Chitterwood hordes 
razed entire rural communities while the Isgeri 
army failed to make a timely response. Hedvend 
VI, then only a couple of years into his stewardship, 
issued token military orders to protect assets of the 
upper class and the capital. As more settlements 
succumbed, waves of soldiers deserted their posts, 
further lowering morale and straining resources. The 
violence of the Goblinblood Wars thus inevitably 
spread beyond the nation.
By the time Isger’s neighbors intervened, both 
banks of the Conerica were overrun. Miraculously, 
the riverside town of Saringallow stood relatively 
unscathed amid the wreckage. Protected by its historic 
ramparts, this defense attracted not only refugees but 
also soldiers looking to recuperate. That the town’s 
location by the river expedited travel to all corners of 
Isger was another strategic boon for retreating action 
or reinforcements.
Convenience, 
however, 
didn’t 
automatically 
translate to support. Saringallow was but a small 
settlement back then, with plans to shelter 2,000 
denizens at most. Without official resupply channels 
from the government, the town’s food stores shrank 
quickly from the influx of people. Alarmed, the then-
mayor passed a highly controversial ordinance upon 
the foreign forces. Each soldier was allowed a meal 
and a night of rest per week. Those wounded could 
stay a fortnight but would consequently be barred 
from town for a month.
Predictably, many locals disagreed with the 
absurd rules and began circumnavigating it. They 
took strangers into their homes, claiming them to 
be distant cousins or similar relations. Some even 
risked foraging, fishing, or hunting outside the walls 
to privately resupply the troops. However suspicious 
they were of outsiders, the inhabitants of Saringallow 
knew Isger needed help. If there was a time to defy law 
and culture for the good of the nation, it was then or 
never again.
Allegedly, sheltering foreign troops in secrecy was 
how the unlikely alliance between the Eagle Knights, 
Hellknights, and Mercenary League started. Claims 
purport three commanders awkwardly discovered 
each other’s true affiliations while hiding under the 
same false identity and roof. After coming clean, 
the three recognized their shared goal. Even when 
their generals refused to ally over philosophical 
differences, the commanders tacitly coordinated their 
troop movements anyway. Several victories later, the 
reluctant higher-ups acknowledged the effectiveness of 
cooperation and established a formal alliance… or so 
the Saringallow folklore whisper.
The famed alliance saved Isger at an immense cost. 
Death took with it many who witnessed how the 
coalition formed. Capitalizing on the uncertainty to 
hide his incompetence, Hedvend VI insinuated he was 
the one who secretly brought the heroes together. When 
Saringallow attempted to suggest otherwise, the steward 
warned he might direct recovery efforts and future 
protection toward more “important” locations. Yet full 
of refugees, Saringallow held its tongue to survive and 
rebuild. For years, it reverted back to the town known 
only for its grim name, tragic past, and superstitions. 
The past Saringallow hides from—be it the city’s 
own founding or the role it played in the Goblinblood 
Wars—speaks a simple truth: the settlement was 
always meant to be a stage on which rebellions against 
establishments, dogma, or tyranny played out. What 
manifests as paranoia was at its heart a wariness 
toward power.
Since recovering from a demonic corruption 
crisis, a renewed growth has revived a spark of that 
destiny in Saringallow. While the young city yet 
maintains the tradition of exclusive social circles, the 
spaces in between have allowed those who would’ve 
been enemies in the past to reconcile. People now 
maintained the traditional social distance not out of 
fear, but rather to abstain from superficial judgment. 
For the modern Saringallow, actions in times of 
Saringallow

crisis measured one’s trustworthiness most truly. 
As the red haze of a nascent war approaches from 
the horizon, Saringallow once again readies itself to 
bear witness to what’s to come next in Isger’s future, 
whether it be a turn for the better or one for the 
worse.

History
Everyone knows Saringallow as the place founded on 
the lynching of the Chelaxian noble house of Sarini. 
The noble house’s servants would go mysteriously 
missing until residents had enough and dealt with the 
Sarinis themselves. Witch hunts mired the settlement’s 
first decade of self-rule. Those in the rural regions 
recall it as a time of dogma. Their ancestors risked 
cultivating the wilderness outside the walls, for to live 
in Saringallow then was to live in intense paranoia. 
The settlement struggled financially, as without 
a manor to serve, there were no goods coming in 
through the docks.
The 
Conerica 
River 
ultimately 
saved 
the 
settlement 
from 
dissolution, 
for 
Saringallow 
managed to stabilize its economy by serving as a 
rest stop for those traveling north and south. In 
time, those traveling by road began using it as a stop 
as well, sometimes as passersby, sometimes to trade 
with those on the river.
Saringallow’s growth was slow for the next two 
centuries, fueled mostly by those who left to find 
fortune and returned upon success. Most who tried 
returned empty-handed if they returned at all. Things 
changed as the town’s third century rolled in, for 
the Goblinblood Wars were on the horizon. During 
the wars, Saringallow persevered. Though the locals 
called their walls the Pauper’s Roof, the ramparts 
were anything but poor in quality. Surviving the war 
intact gave Saringallow a head start on recovery.
Unbeknownst to most, the site where Saringallow is 
today was known as the Crosspaths in older, ancient 
days. Lying almost at the heart of Isger, it was a regular 
place where those who lived on the lands between 
the Aspodell and Menador mountains met, usually to 
reaffirm their alliance. The Sarinis specifically chose 
to construct their manor here, 
for it allowed their guests to 
entertain themselves with some 
amateur archaeology. At one point, 
a beautiful glaive was unearthed 
from the village. The pristine 
historical artifact was sent to 
Elidir, where it stayed ever since.

started before the death of 
the Sarinis and continued

terms were for life. After the first century, Saringallow 
switched to terms of 5 to 10 years, with the exact 
number being part of the mayor’s proposal during 
their campaign. This made it easier for Saringallow 
to see large infrastructural projects through under 
a single leader. It’s tradition for new candidates to 
start campaigning about two years before the term is 
up, though there have been occasions when it starts 
earlier.
While the settlement elects its mayor, Saringallow 
does answer to Elidir and the Steward of Isger. While 
most of the city enforces the law by Isgeri standards, 
there are some times when Saringallow decides to 
evoke their right to the Old Book. This set of laws is 
reportedly based on an ancient copy of the Abadaran 
Manual of City-Building, so ancient that its title 
actually translates to Laws of Civilization-Building. 
Some Saringallow locals believe the Old Book to be 
more friendly for the disenfranchised, especially if 
they live off the land. Critics of the Old Book point to 
this reason as to why it shouldn’t be used in modern 
times since its considerations are often unsuitable for 
an urban environment.
It’s undeniable that Saringallow is almost a proper 
city; it just needs to properly divide itself into 
districts, name its streets, and number its buildings. 
While Mayor Trinelli has less than a full year left 
in her term, she has significantly increased the city 
hall’s administrative capabilities to prepare for this 
project. This preparation accidentally ended up being 
a boon when the Steward implemented a new tax 
for the ongoing war. Many needed it to be deferred, 
and without the increase in staff to complete all the 
paperwork, Saringallow might have been squeezed 
dry.
Residents
Within the walls, Saringallow is home to over 
2,500 people. Another 800 or so live beyond the 
walls in the rural regions, some of which are almost 
the size of small towns. The population has three 
major demographics: those who descended from the 
Sarini servants, those who immigrated here before 
the Goblinblood Wars, and those who immigrated 
after. The first group is distinguished by their last or 
family name as well as their strict adherence to many 
traditional practices in prayers and superstitions. 
Some Saringallow laws once gave these families 
specific privileges in areas such as land or home 
ownership. Most of these discriminatory laws have 
been phased out in the recent years.
Saringallow was considered a human settlement 
before the Goblinblood Wars; nearly all residents 
without human ancestry today came to reside 
hereafter. For some, it was because their home 
was destroyed and beyond salvage. For others, 
Saringallow’s proven safety gave them peace of mind. 
Halflings and gnomes were among the first to move 
into the city, while goblins and hobgoblins only 
started settling in within the last few years. The first of 
the goblinoids were even paid to move to the city, as 
Saringallow realized the best way to prevent conflict 
with the Chitterwood was to accept its people first.
Age is usually a better determiner of how 
a Saringallow resident acts nowadays. Older 
residents are more distant, superstitious, stoic, 
and hardworking. Younger residents and newer 
immigrants are opportunistic, direct, and open-
minded. Those in their teens and under are almost 
universally mischievous and curious. Regardless of 
age, nearly all Saringallow folk despise nobility and 
aristocracy. Even the kindest of noble runaways need 
to prove themselves before they find acceptance here, 
which resulted in these scions forming their own 
private community like everyone else in Saringallow.
Culture and Society
Closed social circles remain an integral part of 
Saringallow culture. Folks used to believe that one

could live their entire life in the settlement and never 
meet the soul that will become their neighbor in 
the graveyard. In some ways, this might be true. As 
schooling is primarily conducted by one’s own family 
and apprenticeship remains the best path to a career, 
there isn’t a lot of social mobility in Saringallow. 
One’s class and status are often decided upon birth; 
only adventuring and a decorated military career can 
predictably break those expectations.
While magic was once greatly feared, that attitude has 
changed significantly after the Godsrain. Saringallow 
once saw divine powers as the most reliable—or at 
least predictably good or evil. Witnessing the death of 
a god has made many reconsider. Most settled on the 
sentiment that the intent of the magic user mattered 
most, not the magic itself. People should be judged by 
who they are, not what powers they wielded. Anti-
magic signage has been taken down, and magic users 
have been emboldened to be more open about their 
abilities when they once might have hid them.
One thing that does unite Saringallow is its holidays. 
While many are observed in Avistan at large, a few 
are local attractions. There’s the Nightgallop, a horse 
race in rural Saringallow that takes place at night on 
the first full moon of spring. Succession, on the other 
hand, is a day when apprentices receive their badge 
of approval from their teachers in a literal torch-
passing ceremony.
Many of the local holidays are then related to 
agriculture, such as Shearwalk, a week chasing 
down sheep to shear; Oaksplit, a time when lumber 
is processed; Snowsow, blessing of the grains that 
will be used for winter wheat; Harvest Feast, a time 
of communal meals; and Loomgather, a localized 
version of the Shelynite Crystalhue. Gallows Day, 
which commemorates the city’s founding, was a 
somber day of religious observance in the past but 
has been commercialized recently in an attempt to 
attract tourism.
Notable People
No one knows where Elleri “Gram” Smalltoes 
(mysterious female halfling candler 4) came from; 
some say she’s as old as Saringallow itself. The candler 
mostly keeps to herself except to nag her customers. 
In truth, Gram was a runaway slave before the 
Emancipation Edict and harbors a grudge against 
Cheliax for all its sins against her.

Old Hawk (stubborn male human fearmonger 4) is 
one of the oldest residents of Saringallow and holds to 
various superstitions, including lining his house with 
salt and eating tons of garlic. He’s convinced that, one 
day soon, the Sarinis will descend upon Saringallow to 
reclaim what was once theirs, and he’s determined to 
be ready for it. Many of the younger folk humor his 
ravings by accepting garlic garlands and promising to 
train in fighting, but the older folk are getting tired of 
his constant fearmongering.
Mayor Sandra Trinelli (prudent female human 
mayor 6) believes in modernization and reform. This 
outlook clashes with some of the older residents, who 
cling to superstition and are wary of change. Slowly 
but surely, the mayor hopes to pave the way for growth 
in Saringallow as it teeters on the edge of becoming a 
potentially major city.
Maire Phelan (jovial female human storyteller 3) 
has lived in Saringallow for only a short time, settling 
there after traveling as a storytelling bard. She has 
witnessed firsthand the neglect and atrocities of the 
Isgeri government (and implicitly, the Chelaxian 
government) and knows the people need hope. Using 
her stories, she works to uplift the people.
Relationships and Conflicts
Saringallow’s reputation is quite pristine these days, 
and the city maintains good relations with many 
settlements within Isger, particularly the nearby town 
of Swiftrun. Within the city, however, there have been 
more and more interpersonal conflicts. Some are more 
private in nature that inadvertently spill over into the 
community, while others are of the public interest. 
The most likely conflict though is from a source 
Saringallow has likely not faced before, in recent 
memory at least: the fey.
Many mourn that the simple settlement has lost its 
rustic charm, and the fey are no different, chafing at 
the influx of people and structures. While it isn’t the 
city’s fault that no one has communed with the fey 
in centuries, Saringallow might find itself under attack 
again if its people don’t come to realize the growing 
grudge of their primal neighbors.
Places of Interest
As a burgeoning city, Saringallow has a mix of old, 
new, and even historical locations of interest to visit.
A. Gallow Farms: The six Gallow Farms have been 
responsible for maintaining Saringallow’s emergency 
ration supply since the settlement’s establishment. 
Some are family-run and passed down through the 
generations, while others have been bought and 
sold. With the recent formation of slums along the 
north wall and a rise in theft of crops, the farms are 
campaigning for a change in mayorship. Gerudina 
Mezeret (meticulous female halfling farmer 4), the 
most senior of the owners, is their candidate of choice. 
Though Gerudina has plans for social housing and 
punitive measures against unregulated construction, 
her lack of opinion on other issues is criticized.
B. City Watch Barracks: After the demon bile 
incident, Saringallow expanded its security. The city 
watch barrack was established within the Noble 
Folly’s gate. Despite the obvious move to deter youths 
from sneaking out, guards continue to catch children 
of all ages attempting the traditional dare of going up 
the Noble Folly’s path.
The barracks is fully equipped with its own watch 
towers, a training yard, stables, a dormitory for two 
dozen guards, and a mess hall. Captain Jordis Serelli 
(determined nonbinary aiuvarin human guard captain 
5) runs the squads as tightly as the orphanage they 
grew up in. Under Jordis’s command, the city watch 
handles matters from pickpockets and nightly rounds 
in the graveyard, to frequent noise complaints against 
the new resident band. While Jordis is no Chelaxian 
sympathizer, they dislike insurgents, believing no 
matter how noble the organization’s intent might be, 
they would do more harm than good.
C. Gallow’s Graveyard: With graves as old as the 
city, Saringallow’s graveyard is a place most avoid 
except when necessary. Nolaria Wintren (adventurous 
female human cleric of Erastil 5) surprised many when 
she volunteered to become the new groundskeeper. 
Rumors say that she might have taken up the post 
in an act of adulthood rebellion against her adoptive 
father, Ildris. Others suggest her attachment to the 
place is sentimental.
Since taking over the graveyard, Nolaria has 
cultivated a large canopy of mistletoe as a ward on 
the area against evil. She prunes the patches frequently 
to prevent overgrowth. The cuttings are then used by 
both her and many other artisans in Saringallow to 
create wearable charms in the form of bracelets or 
wreathes.
D. Traveler’s Square: As its name suggests, Traveler’s 
Square is surrounded by inns, eateries, and stores that 
cater to those who are passing through Saringallow, 
usually by the Conerica Highway. The gallows here 
are a popular attraction despite it being forebodingly 
functional and guarded by menacing-looking (but 
polite) city guards. When the weather is pleasant, 
performers like Maire Phelan often line the perimeter 
of the square in the morning, both to earn their keep 
and to serve as a convenient alarm clock for travelers 
who have overslept.

===== Page 207 =====
206
E. City Hall: Realizing that Saringallow would 
require a larger administration soon with its growing 
population, Mayor Trinelli bought this mansion by 
the triangular Crossroad Plaza several years ago. The 
old town hall was given to the city guard to use as a 
second office. Much like before, the building contains 
the mayor’s residence, office, and also Saringallow’s 
town records. New additions include a large registry 
office that keeps track of paperwork, from census to 
deeds, as well as a cartography department dedicated 
to surveying rural Saringallow. A courthouse is 
currently being furnished, though a judge has yet to be 
officially hired or appointed.
Trinelli’s former secretary, Lupia Marietti (curious 
female human historian 3), has been promoted to City 
Historian. While her research has uncovered curious 
records about the Saringallow region before Isger 
was founded, Lupia has reservations on whether the 
information should go public during such politically 
turbulent times.
F. Temple of Erastil: This temple to Old Deadeye is 
likely the oldest structure in Saringallow, second only to 
the half-derelict Sarini Manor. While it has undergone 
many expansions and renovations over the centuries, 
the building remains dedicated to serving the public. The 
temple’s contribution in health, nutrition, and shelter 
is the predominant reason why most in Saringallow 
consider Erastil to be their patron god. Other faiths, 
especially those popular in Cheliax, have found it rather 
difficult to establish a foothold in the city as a result.
Ildris Ruvarra (kind male human cleric of Erastil 
6) has served as the head priest to the temple for 
nearly 20 years. With recent political developments, 
he’s distanced himself from associating with any side, 
stating he wishes to focus on ensuring the city’s food 
security and agricultural needs. That said, no one—
even Hellbreakers who disclose their affiliation—
has ever been refused treatment or assistance by the 
temple’s staff or Ildris.
G. Hellbreakers’ Headquarters: This two-story 
residence is difficult to locate unless one has a 
guide. The Hellbreakers obtained the property at 
a slight discount after helping the original owners, 
the Vazarros, restart their life elsewhere. On paper, 
the property is under Rhokrag’s (hardened male 
hobgoblin warrior 3) name, though Phoebe and Alceo 
are known “tenants.” The three regularly consecrating 
the house has endeared them to their neighbors, who 
respectfully keep quiet whenever Captain Jordis is in 
the neighborhood.
H. Saringallow’s Sundries: The city’s co-op venture 
supplies travelers with general adventuring gear and 
basic weapons and armor. The store also occasionally 
sells silver and cold iron weapons, though the demand 
has long exceeded the supply. Last year, an aviary 
was added to start a courier pigeon service to major 
settlements in and out of Isger. Abdil Nestthew (discreet 
male human scribe 3), hired directly from the partner 
aviary in Logas, acts as both caretaker to the birds and 
letter-writer-in-proxy. While the Hellbreakers would 
love to have Abdil as an ally, Maire’s probing so far 
suggests the young man has an intense dislike for 
conspiracy and intrigue.
I. Saringallow Orchard: This apple orchard 
unfortunately suffered from repeated infestations 
after the demon bile incident. The land was ultimately 
donated to the Temple of Erastil and consecrated 
for years to end the vermin problem. After its first 
successful harvest, a new co-op venture took off.
Today, gallow apple preserves and dried slices have 
become popular gifts to buy in Saringallow, available at 
the sundries store and several dockside stalls. The temple 
intends for the funds to ultimately go toward building 
a school, though whether that will prevent the youths 
from skipping their chores, classes, or apprenticeship to 
hang out in the orchard remains to be seen.
J. Witch’s End Tavern: This tavern managed by 
Alicie Kruptin (tough female human tavern keeper 4) is 
especially popular with more conservative Saringallow 
residents, as it implemented a heavy “no magic unless 
of divinity” policy after the demon bile incident. The 
entire tavern is under a strong magic suppression field, 
which has caused a number of issues to even those who 
might have simply passed by. Exactly who or what 
Alicie has employed, she refuses to say, other than it’s 
safer than whatever is being prevented on her premise.
K. Dependable Drummady’s: Once a simple 
cobbler shop, Dependable Drummady’s is a full-on 
haberdashery and boutique these days. Drummady 
Laterna (ambitious female human cobbler 4) 
expanded her business over the past decade with 
good word-of-mouth and a sharp eye for fashion that 
picks up trends faster than Elidir. Though not a full-
on member, Drummady has helped the Hellbreakers 
with disguises many times in the past. Even her 
staff knows little of her activities since she often 
conducts them outside of shop hours. As one of the 
stockholders behind Saringallow’s Sundries and the 
Saringallow Orchard, Drummady holds quite a bit of 
influence in the city’s economic circles.
L. The Lucky Anvil: Ludoff Smeltbristle (boisterous 
male dwarf blacksmith 5) first visited Saringallow as 
a tinkerer for his family’s caravan from the Five Kings 
Mountains about a decade ago. He immediately fell 
in love with Saringallow’s surroundings, both nature 
and urban. After moving to the city proper, he slowly

established himself as a reliable smith. A rebel at heart, 
Ludoff secretly supports the Hellbreakers and crafts 
items for them in his spare time.
M. 
Mashnom’s 
Mercs 
and 
Mortar: 
When 
the Stonechewer goblinoid tribe first moved to 
Saringallow, they had a difficult time finding those 
willing to provide housing to the clan. Ultimately, the 
goblins and hobgoblins decided that, if people won’t 
lease, then they’ll just build their own homes. Under 
the leadership of Mashnom (mute female goblin union 
leader 5), a vibrant goblinoid community was born in 
Saringallow. While the unofficial “Chitterstone Road” 
has many regular businesses that cater to daily needs 
(with products especially beloved by goblinoids), it’s 
most famous for its construction companies, excellent 
masons, and mercenary associations.
N. Gerty’s Hearty Breads: Claiming “the heartiest 
damn breads this side o’ the river,” this bakery’s 
signage has an additional piece hanging underneath 
that reads, “Now with Pastries and Pies!” The bakery’s 
owner, Gerty Keronna (stern male human baker 4), 
spends more time chatting with customers nowadays 
than at the oven. The chronic pain from his old leg 
injury from the Goblinblood Wars prevents him from 
standing for long. Fortunately, his past apprentice 
Noemi Tauralio (squeamish female human baker 3) 
has become a baker in her own right. Xerra Bluebottle 
(kind genderfluid halfling baker 2) is a joy to work 
with too. The halfling likes to take home leftover 
bread for the Hellbreakers at the end of the day.
O. Merchant’s Square: The Merchant’s Square 
regularly holds auctions for various goods and wares 
at different hours of the day. Those in the day are a 
cacophony, while those at night are pleasantly quiet so 
the nearby residents can rest. Petrello Pindlion (greedy 
male human fur trader 6), who schedules the auctions, 
is pretty well known for being willing to move time 
slots around and “forget” to inform a seller of a 
schedule change if his commission rates are upped by a 
percent or two. Petrello has also been making political 
endeavors, promising to provide tax cuts and establish 
trade deals with cities outside of Isger through his 
children. While it’s known his son and daughter are in 
Druma and Cheliax respectively, Petrello’s campaign 
remains speculative for most.
P. Pricknettle’s Potions and Poultices: Majara 
Pricknettle (curt female gnome alchemist 4) is 
often overworked these days with custom orders 
for remedies. Rather than take on an apprentice, 
Majara insists on hiring contract workers instead, 
especially those who are working hard to establish 
themselves in the city. As an immigrant from Umok, 
she knows all too well the struggles of integrating 
into Saringallow, even if that barrier has lowered 
considerably in recent times.
Q. Queenly Quriosities: As one of the first shops 
dedicated to the purchase and sale of magic items, 
many visitors are decidedly nervous to step beyond 
the beaded curtains of the front door. To make the 
experience more entertaining than anxious, the store’s 
proprietor, Lukus Melchian (resolute male gnome 
harrower 4), adopts the persona of a motherly fortune-
teller by the name of “Mama Yaga.” In addition to 
suggesting the best lucky charms for the season, Mama 
Yaga always mentions that her extensive private 
collection of books on all things magical is available 
to peruse for any whose heart is in the right place.
R. The Fiend’s Finale: Once known as the Fortnight 
Inn, this establishment is a popular spot to dine late 
into the night. Morvinarr Albusin (superstitious male 
human innkeeper 3) bought the place a couple of 
years ago and refurbished the historic inn with his 
savings. As Alicie’s apprentice, Morvinarr’s dishes are 
famously delicious. The innkeeper, however, considers 
his food a bonus to the real attraction: Saringallow’s 
new resident band, Oasis Rain Showers (outspoken 
male anadi, male human, female knoll, female elf, and 
agender aiuvarin human bards 3).
Made up of five Magaambya graduates—one 
of each branch—Oasis Rain Showers haven’t only 
been influencing Saringallow’s cultural scene, their 
understanding and willingness to explain magic is 
one of the reasons why Saringallow has softened its 
attitude toward magic considerably in recent years. 
That and the famous “sing a Chelaxian loyalist out of 
town” incident, of course.
S. Beacon Candles Workshop: After the Hellbreakers 
bought this abandoned warehouse, they discovered 
it wasn’t as inconspicuous as they’d hoped for a 
headquarters. Gram (mysterious female human 
chandler 4), one of the oldest Hellbreaker recruits, 
suggested that they keep it anyway as a decoy. The 
result is the Beacon Candles Workshop, whose carved 
candles help fund the Hellbreakers. Gram even worked 
out a way to pass secret messages by the colors of the 
candles she makes as well as their carved patterns and 
shapes.
T. Conerica Docks: Though more boats are 
docking in Saringallow these days than ever before, 
Bartle Rudderport (skeptical male human wharfinger 
4) keeps meticulous track of all inventory passing 
through. He’s ever concerned of smugglers ruining 
the reputation of the city. Despite this, Bartle has 
given the Hellbreakers several second chances and 
sometimes even points out how the organization 
could improve their subterfuge.

Usage held in 1 hand; Bulk L

Atrophy bombs contain powerful chemicals developed by 
Urgathoan alchemists that sap a living creature’s strength 
and drain their energy. A primary living target that takes 
damage from an atrophy bomb becomes enfeebled until 
the start your next turn. Many types of bombs grant an 
item bonus to attack rolls.
Type lesser; Level 1; Price 4 gp
The bomb deals 1d4 persistent void damage and 1 void 
splash damage, and the target is enfeebled 1 until the start 
of your next turn. 
Type moderate; Level 3; Price 11 gp
You gain a +1 item bonus to attack rolls. The bomb deals 
2d4 persistent void damage and 2 void splash damage, and 
the target is enfeebled 1 until the start of your next turn.
Type greater; Level 11; Price 255 gp
You gain a +2 item bonus to attack rolls. The bomb deals 
3d4 persistent void damage and 3 void splash damage, and 
the target is enfeebled 2 until the start of your next turn.
Type major; Level 17; Price 2,550 gp
You gain a +3 item bonus to attack rolls. The bomb deals 
4d4 persistent void damage and 4 void splash damage, and 
the target is enfeebled 2 until the start of your next turn.

ITEM 6
RARE
ALCHEMICAL
CONSUMABLE
Price 50 gp
Usage held in 1 hand; Bulk —
Activate [three-actions] (manipulate) 
Silver filings to ward off fiends, cold iron filings to repulse 
demons and fey, and powders made from garlic, peppers, 
and wort to repel undead creatures are combined into this 
gritty paste. A container of warding paste contains enough 
to cover one suit of armor or set of clothes. For the next 
hour, creatures with the unholy trait take a –1 circumstance 
penalty to melee attacks against the affected outfit’s wearer.

Usage held in 2 hands; Bulk L
Activate [one-action] (manipulate)
A restful salve is a compound that can be applied to the skin 
to prevent undeath. If applied to a fresh corpse, the corpse 
doesn’t decay, nor can it be transformed into an undead or 
otherwise controlled until the sun rises the next morning. If 
applied to a living creature, this salve lasts for only 1 hour due

wards off effects that would cause undeath upon dying.

ITEM 3
UNCOMMON
CONSUMABLE
EXTRADIMENSIONAL
MAGICAL
Price 50 gp
Usage held in 2 hands (see text); Bulk L
Activate 1 minute (manipulate)
This padlock exists in a dormant state while it’s closed and 
its associated key is in the keyhole. To activate this item, 
you remove the key, which causes the keyhole to become 
a portal to an extradimensional space. This space can hold 
a single object of up to 1 Bulk by pressing it against the

can be used to open the lock with an Interact action, which 
safely releases the item onto the ground in your space. 
If the lock isn’t opened within the next 24 hours, the key 
disintegrates, and from then on, a creature who succeeds at 
a DC 16 Thievery check can Pick the Lock open to release 
the item. On a critical failure, the padlock is destroyed and 
its contents are lost forever.

LAZYBONES PENDANT	
ITEM 5
UNCOMMON
INVESTED
MAGICAL
Price 130 gp
Usage worn; Bulk —
A lazybones pendant is a six-sided die pendant carved from 
the regretful bones of Work-Too-Hard Whappa, a goblin 
unusually industrious in life and said to be making up for a 
long-overdue rest in his afterlife. Depicted on the five sides 
of this six-sided die are representations of Whappa engaged 
in various acts of slothful mischief, while the remaining 
side is utterly blank; apparently, he’s so engrossed in his 
indolence that even his image has forgotten to show up on 
that side of the die.
When you wear and invest in this pendant, you gain a +1 
item bonus to checks when you Follow the Expert.
Activate—Can’t Someone Else Do It? [three-actions] (concentrate, 
manipulate, occult) Frequency once per day; Effect 
You cast phantasmal minion, summoning an ephemeral 
version of yourself. When you Activate the pendant and 
each time you Sustain the spell, your phantasmal minion 
gains a reaction that can be used only to Aid an ally. 
It uses your skills for any skill checks and can’t Aid an 
attack.

THE WONDERS OF THE SEASONS
Long before Taldor’s conquest of Isger, the Kellid 
and early Isgeri created or perhaps retooled powerful 
magical artifacts to mark the seasons of their creation. 
One was Firstbloom, a glaive said to be carved of 
natural and native woods from the Arthfell Forest yet 
stronger than any steel weapon of its like. Another was 
Harvest Feast, a scythe meant to usher in harvest and 
bounty yet rumored to be burdened with a dark past 
and darker present. A summer wonder, Bounty’s Light, 
was said to be a magical torch that could light a field as if 
kissed by sunlight and was a gift traded back and forth 
between the Isgeri and their goblin neighbors as a sign 
of mutual friendship long before any wars fomented 
resentment. The final wonder was known only as Woe, 
but records of its construction and use have long since 
disappeared along with any information about where 
it might reside. See Continuing the Campaign (page 
168) for more on Woe.
These wonders are relic seeds, and the full rules for 
relics and descriptions of the listed gifts, including 
when to advance a relic, appear starting on page 308 
of GM Core.

This +1 vitalizing striking glaive is said to have been carved

in the Arthfell Forest. The grain of the weapon’s blade 
is especially tight, giving the weapon both incredible 
durability and a finish that resembles silver and steel 
folded by a master smith.
Minor Gifts: apothecary’s garden, healing wave
Major Gifts: inextinguishable, petal dance
Grand Gift: life everlasting
REAPER’S SIGH	
ITEM 7
UNIQUE
MAGICAL
 RELIC
VOID
Aspects death
Usage 2 hands; Bulk 2
This +1 wounding striking scythe is a weapon of intricately 
embellished blackened metals and polished surfaces. It 
was originally intended to venerate Urgathoa in her role as 
the herald of autumn in pre-Taldor Isger but has recently 
found more malevolent meaning. With the scythe in her 
hands, Urgathoa was said to cull the harvest for feast to 
usher in the cold, bleak winters. As Urgathoa’s legends 
took a darker tone, the scythe’s own legend was reclaimed 
to venerate Erastil and Pharasma as part of the holiday for 
which it now claims a name.
Minor Gifts: death gaze, living death
Major Gifts: pierce the veil, tide of death
Grand Gift: grim specter
THE STEADFAST KEYSTONE
The divine keystone ritual first appears in the 
Pathfinder Society Adventure #4-02: Return to the 
Grave. This ritual was the invention of a gifted 
Acadamae wizard turned Pharasmin priest named 
Elios. He sought to protect Steadfast, a small 
settlement of refugees in the Gravelands, from 
oncoming hordes of undead under the control of 
a fallen Ivory Reaper. Unfortunately, Elios found 
that the Whispering Tyrant’s influence was too 
great for a common consecration ritual. With the 
instructions Elios left before his own demise, the 
Pathfinder Society successfully imbued a keystone 
from Steadfast’s old Pharasmin temple with the 
divine touch of Pharasma herself, sending a team 
of Pathfinders to bring it to the besieged town and 
rescue the refugees. Since then, the ritual has been 
used to protect several other refugee settlements 
in the Gravelands from becoming overrun by the 
hungry dead.

Isgeri Boarhound
UNCOMMON
Through training and selective breeding, the gnomes 
of Umok found ways to capitalize on the native Isgeri 
boarhounds’ exceptional scent abilities and sturdy frame 
to patrol against extraplanar predators and other enemies 
regularly found in the region.
Size Small
Melee [one-action] jaws (finesse), Damage 1d8 piercing
Str +2, Dex +3, Con +2, Int –4, Wis +1, Cha +0
Hit Points 6
Skill Survival
Senses foe scent (precise, 40 feet), low-light vision, scent 
(imprecise, 40 feet)
Speed 40 feet
Special As part of daily preparations, the Isgeri boarhound 
can be offered a sample of an enemy with the fiend or 
undead trait, such as a bone, piece of flesh, or similarly 
scented sample that has been acquired within the last 
24 hours. For the next 24 hours, either fiend or undead 
becomes the boarhound’s designated foe. The Isgeri 
boarhound’s foe scent enables it to smell the presence 
of a creature designated as its foe as a precise scent at 
a range of 40 feet.
Support Benefit Your boarhound is a faithful hunting 
companion. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your 
next attack roll to Strike a foe within your boarhound’s 
reach. This bonus lasts until the first time you use 
it or until the beginning of your next turn, whichever 
comes first. If you damage a creature with the trait 
corresponding to your boarhound’s designated foe with 
that Strike, the creature takes an additional 1d6 piercing 
damage from the boarhound. If your boarhound is 
nimble or savage, the damage increases to 2d6.

LOCK JAW [one-action]

jaws Strike.

New Ritual
The following ritual appears in this adventure.
DIVINE KEYSTONE	
RITUAL 4
RARE
CONSECRATION
HOLY
Cast 4 days; Requirements cornerstone from the structure 
of the casting area used as a locus; Cost holy water, 
powdered silver, and purified chalk worth 200 gp; 
Secondary Casters 1
Primary Check Arcana (master) or Religion (expert); 
Secondary Checks Architecture Lore, Crafting, or 
Engineering Lore
Area 100-foot emanation from the building’s keystone
Duration 1 week
You magically remove and consecrate the cornerstone 
of a building or ruin in the center of a settlement before 
returning the stone to its structure to spread its divine 
protection into the settlement around it. Once the final 
hammer strike returns the stone to its structure, the area 
protected by the sanctified stone becomes a sacred space, 
protecting the living from undead. Within the protected 
area, the consecrated site is holy, undead creatures can’t 
be created or raised, and living creatures are invisible to 
the undead. 
A successful dispel magic used on a specific effect 
removes only that effect (such as the invisibility effect). 
However, destroying or removing the keystone ends the 
entire ritual and all its effects.
Critical Success You create the effects described above, 
and the keystone’s consecration effect doubles its 
radius.
Success You create the effects described above.
Failure The ritual has no effect.
Critical Failure The area becomes a font of power for 
undead for the next month. All undead creatures in the 
ritual’s area gain fast healing 3 and resistance 3 to holy.
Heightened (+1) The emanation protected by the keystone 
increases by 20 feet.

Hellbreaker (Archetype)
Founded in Isger to protest against the injustice 
and apathy of their faraway rulers in Cheliax, the 
Hellbreakers League is a young but growing rebel 
organization determined to make its mark. Members 
of the League swear themselves as agents of rebellion 
to topple the Chelaxian regime and free its vassal 
states from its oppressive rule, starting with Isger. 
The Hellbreakers League knows it’s at a heavy 
disadvantage in its war against Cheliax as a still-
developing group challenging one of the world’s most 
powerful nations. Hellbreaker tactics rely on wit and 
daring as well as knowledge of the fiendish forces their 
enemies might use against them. Through sword, spell, 
and subterfuge, they work tirelessly to liberate the 
oppressed and remove tyrants from power.
Additional Feats: 4th Combat Assessment (Player 
Core 140), Lightning Swap (Player Core 141); 10th 
Blind-Fight (Player Core 145), Felling Strike (Player 
Core 146)
HELLBREAKER DEDICATION	
FEAT 2
UNCOMMON
ARCHETYPE
DEDICATION
Access You’re a member of the Hellbreakers league.
By joining the League, you’ve taken on the responsibilities 
of a Hellbreaker. You gain the Additional Lore general feat 
for both Devil Lore and Hellknight Lore. If you were already 
trained in one or both of those Lore skills, you also become 
trained in a Lore skill of your choice.
When you roll initiative, you can attempt a Devil Lore, 
Hellknight Lore, or Society check to Recall Knowledge 
about one enemy you can see as a free action, if that skill 
would be applicable. The GM is the final arbiter of whether 
or not one of those skills would be appropriate to Recall 
Knowledge about the enemy.

FEAT 4
ARCHETYPE
SKILL
Prerequisites Hellbreaker Dedication, expert in Devil Lore 
or Hellknight Lore
Your knowledge of your enemies gives you an advantage 
against them, granting you a swift reaction to their 
devilry. If you know you’re fighting against any devils or 
Hellknights at the beginning of an encounter, you can roll 
the respective Lore skill for your initiative roll. 
In 
addition, 
whenever 
you 
successfully 
Recall 
Knowledge about a creature using Devil Lore or Hellknight 
Lore, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your next skill 
check against that creature before the end of your next 
turn. If you’re a master in Devil Lore or Hellknight Lore, the 
bonus increases to +2.
HELLBREAKER’S RESOLVE [one-action]	
FEAT 4
ARCHETYPE
Prerequisites Hellbreaker Dedication
Frequency once per hour
You gird yourself in both mind and body for danger, 
steeling your resolve. You gain a number of temporary 
Hit Points equal to your level that last for 1 minute. While 
you have those temporary Hit Points, you gain a +1 status 
bonus to Will saves.
HIGH ALERT [one-action]	
FEAT 6
ARCHETYPE
Prerequisites Hellbreaker Dedication
You’re constantly on guard, keeping watch over your allies 
against fiendish forces—no one can get the jump on your 
group while you’re around. Choose an ally you can see 
within 30 feet. They gain a +1 circumstance bonus to their 
AC and Reflex saving throws against devils and creatures 
allied with the Chelaxian government (as determined by 
the GM) until the beginning of your next turn. This action 
gains the visual trait, the auditory trait, or both, depending 
on how you alert your ally.

RETURN TO THE PIT!	
FEAT 12
ARCHETYPE
Prerequisites Hellbreaker Dedication
You can send the fiends who have vexed you back to their 
home plane where they belong. You can cast banishment 
once per day as a divine innate spell. When you take 
this feat, you craft a personal symbol of the Hellbreakers 
League that’s anathema to devils. If you wield this symbol 
in one hand when you spend an extra action while casting 
banishment on a devil, you don’t need to pay the extra cost 
to give that creature a –2 circumstance penalty to its save.
THORN IN HELL’S SIDE	
FEAT 12
ARCHETYPE
Prerequisites Defy Hell
Your devotion to the ideals of justice, freedom, and 
revolution allow you to truly punish those who stand in 
your way. When you critically succeed at a Hellbreaker 
Strike, the target must succeed at a Fortitude save against 
your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher, or become 
stunned 1 (stunned 2 on a critical failure). This effect has 
the incapacitation trait.
HELLBREAKERS’ REGIMEN
Hellbreakers work around the clock, as they 
know their opposition won’t be taking a moment 
off either. Training is vigorous and frequent, 
constantly testing Hellbreakers’ abilities and 
almost always bringing them to the brink of 
exhaustion. That being said, discipline in a 
Hellbreaker station is certainly less painful than in 
their Chelaxian counterpart’s.

HELLBREAKER TROOPS 
AS ENEMIES
While the four troops presented 
here are meant to ally with the PCs 
during this Adventure Path, a GM 
can find use for them outside of this 
campaign as enemy combatants. A 
goblin village could field a choir of 
war chanters to protect itself or to 
bolster a raiding party, represented 
by the war saboteurs. 
Hellbreaker Troops
The Hellbreakers League stared with just a few recruits scattered across Isger, 
performing small acts of rebellion against Cheliax and demonstrations of 
support for everyday Isgeri. During this Adventure Path, the organization 
grows to become the center of the revolution, gathering allies from every 
corner of the country. When the time comes to fully go to war, the Hellbreakers 
can hopefully count on many Isgeri citizens to rise up and give their all for 
the cause. The following troops are just four of the many allies that the PCs 
can recruit for their skirmish encounters against Hellknights and worse.
STUMPFIELD WAR CHANTER CHOIR
The goblin artists of Stumpfield love a good song, as most goblins do. 
While they aren’t primarily warriors, these goblins have taken up their 
dogslicers to fight for the liberation of Isger. Their main advantage as a 
troop asset in skirmish encounters, though, is their ability to bolster their 
allies and flummox their enemies with their chants.

HELLBREAKER TROOPS 
AS ENEMIES
The Swiftrun clergy could easily 
represent a hostile group that only 
cares about its own community. 
The gnome beastspeakers could 
represent a circle of druids more

than protecting nature. 
SWIFTRUN CLERGY
Swiftrun is a small settlement dedicated to Erastil, barely large enough to 
be considered a village. Its priests are devoted to community and peace, 
nature and nurture. And yet, sometimes the time comes when one must 
take up arms to protect their community, when words and gentleness 
aren’t enough.
The Erastilian clergy is known more for their farming techniques than 
their magic, but their rural ways shouldn’t fool anyone into thinking they 
can’t defend themselves. Each priest is equipped with the divine power 
of Old Deadeye as well as sharpshooting skills conducive to Erastil’s 
favored weapon, the longbow. These priests are prepared to defend their 
homes with their skills when they must, though they are never eager to 
shed blood and would rather spend their days tending their crops and 
community.

Troop Spellcasting When the Swiftrun clergy Casts a Spell, their

feet (a burst with a smaller radius is not affected). Add 5 feet to the

UMOK BEASTSPEAKER CIRCLE
The gnomes of Umok have a reticence to fire after the pyrrhic wildfire 
that razed the Chitterwood during the Goblinblood Wars. To help protect 
their home from unwanted arson, many gnomes of Umok have learned to 
communicate with animals, whose instincts can quickly sniff out unauthorized 
smoke or flame. The two groups work together to keep the town safe, with 
the animals serving as an early-warning system when threats approach.
Several Umok beastspeakers have joined the war effort, harnessing their 
primal magic and their connection with animals against the armies of 
Cheliax. Their powerful magics are used to summon beasts of the wild 
to defend Isger from forces that threaten the peace of their home, pitting 
primal power against fiends.

WANNABE DEVILS
The process by which the adiutors 
are created is supposedly one 
engineered by the iconoclastic 
archfiend Barbatos, who’s rumored 
to not be of true devilish heritage. 
While none would dare do so in front 
of the Bearded Lord, true devils take 
a joy in lording over the adiutors, 
who are neither of Hell’s elect nor 
its elite, and in sending them on 
dangerous tasks to earn some 
unwinnable respect.
Adiutor
Adiutors, while nicknamed auxiliary devils, are not truly devils, but 
mortals invested with infernal power. These mortals gain a taste of Hell’s 
might as rewards for their loyalty to the cause of tyranny and oppression. 
Hungry for power, an adiutor ruthlessly enforces Hell’s will at any cost in 
hopes of fulfilling their fiendish ambitions. They’re most commonly found 
in Cheliax and its territories due to the nation’s relationship with the forces 
of Hell, serving as spies and informants for both the Thrunes and powerful 
devils invested in meddling with mortals.
While some adiutors climb the ranks of mortal society to become 
Hellknights and other supporters of tyranny, most have higher ambitions 
and desire to become devils themselves. To this end, they seek to serve more 
powerful devils and make deals that will benefit them so that they can 
ensure their transformation. There’s nothing an adiutor despises more than 
their own mortality—a sign of weakness, when beings like devils walk the 
Universe in their perfect Hellish vision.
Although they’re most likely to be found in places or near people with 
existing links to Hell, adiutors can be found anywhere, quietly plotting 
to gain power and status so they can become the lieutenants of Hell they 
desire to be.

MODE OF TRANSPORT
The aurocan’s chest hull is large 
enough to carry up to five Medium 
or smaller creatures. The creatures 
benefit from total cover and can 
leave the aurocan with an Interact 
action to open a hatch and slide 
out. Some aurocans are designed 
specifically as protective tanks for 
ranged soldiers like snipers and 
spellcasters, with slots built into 
their sides for weapons and spells to 
shoot out of.
Aurocan
One can predict what foes are on the battlefield by how they sound. Foot 
soldiers clang weapons on shields as they march. Cavalry is marked by 
a rapid drumbeat of hooves. Armies with great monsters under their 
command don’t try to silence their hair-raising screeches.
No sound prompts as much caution as the steady clicking of gears and 
hiss of billowing steam, for the only thing that accompanies that chorus 
is an aurocan: a mechanical creature created in the shape of a massive 
six-legged bull prone to exploding when destroyed. The aurocan’s greatest 
strength is how its head can detach from its body to rain down scalding 
steam from above.

SPIDERY INCLINATIONS
The insidiator often takes after 
specific spiders, even bearing 
webbed markings on their face, 
which shows in their tactics. Those 
inspired by jumping spiders are 
quick to hunt down their prey, 
attacking relentlessly with every 
tool they have, while those closer 
to the patient trapdoor spiders 
integrate deeply into the society 
they infiltrate.
Devil, Insidiator (Entrapment Devil)
These devils from the first layer of Hell serve their betters by ensnaring those 
who are easily tempted and weaving plots that lead to the fall of mortal 
souls. Insidiators are commonly recruited to set up sting operations that 
entice mortals into committing terrible sins or lay bare the machinations 
of fiendish rivals. They delight in seeing their victims fall prey to their well-
crafted schemes and might spend years on the perfect plan, though the 
most efficient are more likely to rise through Hell’s ranks.
An insidiator’s talent for subtlety extends to their physical form. Their 
bat-like wings appear gossamer but, like the spider webs they resemble, 
are excellent for catching prey, sticking to enemies and trapping them 
in melee. When the mood strikes or circumstances warrant, entrapment 
devils can alter the color of their skin and wings to avoid detection.
Insidiators generally seek to avoid physical combat, preferring to toy 
with their targets in games of subterfuge and mental manipulation. Their 
specialty is leading a target down a convoluted path that ends with the target 
incriminating or damning themselves, forcing them to agree to the insidiator’s 
demands. Should a would-be victim see through the insidiator’s 
schemes, the devil concedes temporary defeat and 
leaves to begin plotting anew. When all else fails 
and physical tactics become necessary, entrapment 
devils are capable fighters who use their spiderlike webs and 
camouflage abilities to their advantage, employing sneak 
tactics to throw their opponents off-guard.

ANTI-INTELLECTUALISTS
Instillos know the importance 
of diverse thinking and media 
literacy, which leads them to target 
educational institutions and free 
thinkers. They seed organizations 
with false information and selfish 
intellectuals who use their 
knowledge for themselves instead of 
others, plying them with power and 
information before exposing their 
corruption so society turns against 
them.
Devil, Instillo (Docent Devil)
Wherever learning and instruction is called for within the burning shadows 
of Hell, from the bureaus of Dis and coffers of Erebus to the war colleges 
of Malebolge and Caina’s courtrooms, docent devils ply their unassuming 
and perspicacious trade. The instillo, so named for their creativity and 
talent in instilling a respect for Hell’s ways and legitimacy to captive 
audiences, are valued for their ability to transform recently conquered 
lands into compliant, even loyal, client-states. The conquered are taught 
to be ashamed of their origins; the despairing are issued philosophies 
that displace blame and uncertainty upon the mistakes of history and 
geography; the orphaned are taught to respect those who orphaned them.

MINIONS AND VASSALS
Powerful kylixes use their goblets 
not just as accessories but weapons, 
animating them to pour acid onto 
rivals and batter opponents from 
afar. Though all cupbearer devils are 
charming, only the strongest can 
fully use their seductive charisma 
to capture victims’ minds and send 
them off to do the devil’s bidding, 
all while their bewitched “friends” 
believe they’re acting of their own 
accord.
Devil, Kylix (Cupbearer Devil)
The elegant and mortal-appearing kylixes, or cupbearer devils, rarely 
hide their infernal nature, preferring to dress tastefully and immaculately 
to accentuate the beauty and symmetry of their forms. Theirs is the 
dance of idle speech and clever chatter, half-promises of friendship amid 
smiling hints of dalliance. They make friends swiftly wherever they go, 
and their presence alone seems to prevent insurrection and conflict. The 
cupbearers are the face of occupation; with their devilish charms, they 
can rob a rebellion of its revolutionaries, waylay spouses from their 
partners, steal children from cradles, and get thanked for it all. 
The cupbearers shape art and culture, wielding their talents in hospitality 
and merrymaking to seduce their guests and entourages toward the 
glamour of evil. Hell is, after all, a bastion of civilization; the cupbearers, 
with their twinkling vessels and carelessly sincere flattery, remind that Hell 
is the best place to be, and you have nothing to fear from its laws.

FANATICS OF HELL
Odvolos love to engage foes in 
debate, even if they’re ill-suited to 
the arts of logic and rhetoric; their 
passion is to engulf their opponents 
in fallacy and flame. In their eyes, 
anyone who dares to disagree with 
them or their archdevil idols is but 
a straw man, and they’ll do their 
damnedest to ensure the straw man 
burns.
Devil, Odvolos (Censorship Devil)
As empires posture amid decline and demagogues preside over republics, 
censorship devils scatter the burning ash of ignorance as a comforting 
veil over the complications of history and causality. These devils are 
feverishly devoted to Hell and find anything that could be interpreted 
against Hell’s doctrines to be anathema and deserving of immediate 
destruction. Inconvenient accounts of the past, truths that draw the 
faithful away from the ways of Asmodeus, words that bring hope to 
those who might otherwise fall into a devil’s temptations—these are fuel 
for the odvolos’s hateful torches, burning bright on the cinders of ink 
and vellum.

MIND OVER MATTER
Velavis have long, birdlike legs, pallid 
skin, and piercing black eyes that 
unnerve many who look upon them. 
When angered, one glare is enough 
to intimidate troublemakers into 
compliance. Despite their imposing 
demeanor, velavis aren’t especially 
strong physically. When they need 
to move heavy tomes, they tend 
to do so with the aid of magic and 
conjured servants. These devils are 
accomplished spellcasters whose 
intellect, speech, and quills are their 
most powerful weapons.
Devil, Velavi (Librarian Devil)
Knowledge is power, and no one is more keenly aware of this truth than 
velavis. These scribes and junior scholars are tasked with maintaining the 
unfathomably vast collections in Stygia’s Academies of Lies. Velavis are 
the front faces of the library, greeting visitors and determining whether 
to grant their requests. Their organizational skills are among the best in 
Hell, and their memories are long, allowing them to easily navigate their 
home library with astonishing speed. Velavis provide another vital service 
for Hell: should another devil make a valuable discovery, they’re expected 
to report to an Academy to have a velavi record it on a scroll or book the 
velavi crafts out of living flesh.
Each velavi is intimately familiar with the collections in their library, 
and they have unfettered access to other Academies’ archives. Those 
seeking information in Hell might be tempted to seek a velavi’s aid, but the 
velavi will demand a high price before conceding any information—even 
then, the flow of knowledge almost always goes one way, as velavis are 
tricky with what they share. Librarian devils are custodians, gatekeepers, 
and guardians; it’s exceedingly rare for velavis to share their knowledge 
with anyone but a devil of higher rank, and even then, it must be bought 
or threatened out of them.

FUMECRUX VARIANTS
As devastating as draconic 
fumecruxes are, they’re uncommon 
sights to behold. Common 
fumecruxes are made from horses, 
large birds, and other mundane 
beasts. All fumecruxes display an 
apathy toward living creatures, 
including their makers, making them 
difficult to control. A necromancer 
who unleashes a fumecrux made 
from something as untamable as a 
dragon is either incredibly powerful 
or incredibly foolish.
Fumecrux
By studying the phenomena of hellcrowns (page 232) and beheaded 
(Monster Core 2 56), Chelaxian mages have created a fusion of the two. 
Years of experimentation culminated in the creation of fumecruxes, 
brimstone specters capped with the decapitated and rotting heads of great 
beasts. The process is being attempted more frequently as yet another 
weapon for the war against Andoran.
DRACONIC FUMECRUX
This creature is the result of the fumecrux ritual performed on the head of a 
young adamantine dragon. Unlike most fumecruxes, draconic fumecruxes 
retain some of the unique magic of their living counterparts.

SECRET SIGNALS
Gliding river snakes sometimes 
migrate between nests depending 
on weather conditions and the 
movement of prey, which has 
led some villages to use them 
as messengers. Once a snake is 
domesticated, it’s trained to locate 
specific nests based on scent, and 
messages are tied to its body. When 
the snake arrives, it’s rewarded with 
live prey.
Gliding River Snake
Wise travelers keep watch for snakes along their path, but few expect 
them to attack from above. When threatened, the gliding river snake takes 
to high ground and launches toward its target, gliding through the air by 
flattening its ribs and controlling its flight by moving sinuously. If unable 
to make an aerial attack, the gliding river snake simply attempts to bite 
its target and snap off a finger or two. The snake’s jaws are extremely 
powerful, able to bite clean through bone and flesh.
The mildly venomous gliding river snake prefers to keep to itself but 
reacts harshly to potential threats with a vicious bite. Its mouth is filled 
with serrated teeth that tear into its prey rather than piercing like a 
typical snake. Using these teeth, the gliding river snake rends its food into 
chunks before swallowing, allowing it to target larger prey. Sometimes 
an unfortunate animal is beset by multiple gliding river snakes, covering 
it with writhing serpents. These group meals have been mistaken for a 
singular monster before, as only the snakes’ tentacle-like bodies can be 
seen as they feast.
The gliding river snake often lives in pairs, staying together with its 
mate through the mating season before separating in the off season. They 
lay their eggs either in trees or underwater, sometimes even stealing bird 
nests for their own uses once they’ve devoured the birds’ eggs. Many a 
birdwatcher has been taken aback by the sight of hatching snakes up in 
the treetops, occasionally even laid side by side with bird eggs for easy 
access to a meal.
